- ONE PER ROUND (`_tod_golden_zombie.gsc`, `TOD_GOLDEN_PER_ROUND` 1 replaces the 1% roll): at each round's first ordinary spawn the round picks its target, the Nth ordinary spawn with N from the first 60% of the round's zombies (`TOD_GOLDEN_SPAN`; stock `get_zombie_count_for_round`, the same count the luck bar reads), so it always turns up with most of the round left to hunt it. ## 2026-09-29 13:36 - THE SIGN'S REAL BEARING: the first play of the jump reveal found the sky, not the camera, was wrong (docs/196 §3)
- User, after the first play: "your cinematic jump actually looks pretty good ... the way you're facing doesn't have the actual Tower of Doom sign ... rotate the skybox so it fits your exact measurement. You can work with the other agent who's actually working on the ... sign". The log proves the scene did its job (`CINE_TURN to_yaw=180 pitch=-11`, `CINE_REVEAL angles=(-10.0, -172.2)`).
- CAUSE: nobody had ever measured where the sky image lands in the ENGINE. docs/166's "centre column = +Y" was Blender's frame, and test_jumppad's lockstep (`yaw = 90 - roll`) was built on it, so it passed while the sign sat behind the crown.
- THE PROOF: the engine's own sky shader, decoded (the toolsgfx DXBC of techsetdef_sky_latlong_hdr, LZ4 + D3DDisassemble). The pixel shader's `u = 0.5 - atan2(y, x)/2pi` puts the image's centre column at world +X (yaw 0), NOT mirrored. The vertex shader turns the view by `gScene.skyRotation` (a float2, packing unproven; Treyarch's Sector sun fits "clockwise" within 3 deg, the Giant and the default templates fit nothing). So the built roll -90 put the sign due NORTH and the image seam due west, right in the reveal shot.
- THE FIX, as a team: session 22 finishes its new render (sign +25%, brighter, static ships gone) at `--roll 0`; session fd set `"skyRotation" "180"` in mtl_skybox_tod_cybercity (tod_skybox.gdt) in its brightness pass; fd's one FULL build carries both. 180 is the one turn whose direction cannot matter, and it keeps the sign at the image centre, off the seam. Session 9c told (its reveal wing already targets due west).
- GATE: `tools/test_jumppad.js` section 3c now SIMULATES the decoded shader. It reads stats.json roll + the material's skyRotation, and the camera's yaw must sample the sign's column under BOTH turn directions (only 0/180 pass). Self-checks cover roll -90 -> north (the user's finding), roll 0 + 180 -> west, and a 90 turn -> refused. The deployed pair (-90, 0) only warns while in flight; a half-landed pair fails with the roll it needs.
- Memory `bo3-sky-latlong-mapping` (the engine fact); the old sky memory's "+Y" line corrected. docs/196 §3 + status; CLAUDE.md top note.

## 2026-09-27 00:12 - NECROMANCER: THE HELPER MANGLER WALKS - variant_type 0 (the real cause; rides the next build)
- User: "Mangler still doesnt walk around. You should have logs to detect this and I should have to tell you." The log did show it (HELPER_TICK moved=0), and two builds went out on guesses (rev 8 ignoreMelee, rev 9 the per-tick rate). NOTE: the user's last play was build 16 (rev 8); rev 9 was never played.
- ROOT CAUSE, traced tree -> ASM -> selector: stock `set_zombie_run_cycle` (called from `init_zombie_run_cycle`) re-rolls `variant_type` = RandomInt(zm_variant_type_max) for archetype `zombie`, which the Mangler aitype is. `animtables/hb_mangler.ai_ast` has ONE move@zombie row, `_variant_type 0`, so any other roll leaves the tree in zombieMoveAction (has_path=1, asm running, cant_move set) with no walk clip, and it moves 0. The enemy `_tod_mangler::initialize_actor` sets `variant_type = 0` right after the run cycle; `mangler_init` (a copy of it) had dropped that line.
- Fix (`_tod_necro_summon.gsc` rev 10): `variant_type = 0` after the run cycle, re-asserted every 0.25 s in `mangler_chase` (logs `MANGLER_VARIANT_FIX was=` if anything re-rolls it). HELPER_TICK now also logs `variant=` and `speed=`. Gates: arity 112 OK, native API OK. UNPLAYED.

THE GRAPPLE (user, after the Archer playtest: "not really bringing me into the air ... stuck on the ground"):

Two of the hall pulls only lifted once the player ran off a 16-unit tier edge; on the crown's bell floor (z 18224, outside the hall) it never lifted.

Stock's own jump pad pays it with `self SetOrigin( self.origin + ( 0, 0, 1 ) )` right before its per-frame velocity loop (_zm_jump_pad.gsc:484). `_tod_archer.gsc` `floor_release()` is that idiom; the attach and every grounded lift in `grapple_step` call it before the write. `GRAPPLE_END` logs `floor_releases=`.
- THE STRANDING: the same log showed the rope carrying the Archer over the hall's wall (anchors on the wall top, z 19974) onto the crown's bell floor outside every zone, where they stood for 45 s with stock's out-of-bounds kill blocked only by god mode (`OOB ... spared=0` x10). `playable_area_cb` now RETURNS a stranded Archer to stock's last navmesh point (`self.last_valid_position`, +8) once the grace is spent and the rope is down; kill brushes stay lethal. Log `OOB_RETURN from= to=`.

White marker on any damaging hit, gold on a headshot hit, and on a kill a RED PUNCH: the marker lands 1.7x its size and snaps down in 80 ms (ScaleOverTime + MoveOverTime on stock's crosshair element), then fades. Elites keep their bigger punch + the ding via boss_kill; a boss gets the biggest. - GAUNTLET: stock _zm_weap_dragon_gauntlet hits everything within 96 u every 0.1 s DURING the juke and within 128 u on the swing; the copy had only the engine's single hit at the end of the dash.

- SWORD SLAM: Hellbound's slam is a proxy weapon (hb_gold_sword_cast_zm, raise = the slam clip) + a leap; it was installed at the tools root and never zoned.
- BASH: one damage sample at 250 ms, straight ahead.

Fixes:
- NEW `_tod_warrior_melee.gsc` (started by `_tod_class_kit::init`): on every swing of a Warrior blade (`weapon_melee` / `_power` / `_charge`) the PUNCH hits a 35-degree cone to 100 u (half damage past 64 u, stock's), the GAUNTLET everything within 128 u of the fist plus, on `weapon_melee_juke`, everything within 96 u of the body every 0.1 s for 1 s, the SWORD a 53-degree arc to 120 u and again 0.40 s later (the clip's second blade pass). Blade damage (tod_classes::melee_dmg) through the normal melee chain; the engine's own target is skipped on the first pass. Ordinary zombies a Warrior blade kills are FLUNG (stock's launch numbers); elites never. Extra targets get the blade's impact FX + hit sound.
- gen_tod_twins LADDER (regen = the lead's): cc_punch `lunge: true`, meleeChargeRange 100 (the bat's stock reach), meleeChargeAnim = the punch's charge clip (_upgraded on PaP). cc_gold_sword fireTime/meleeTime 1.033 (Hellbound's); damage per swing stays the MELEE_TIER_DMG pin, the second stroke is the second hit.
- GRAVITY SMASH with the Gold Battle Sword plays Hellbound's slam: the cast proxy, Hellbound's leap (up to 128 u forward, 56 u high; `SetOrigin( +1 )` then SetVelocity, stock's jump-pad release), the hit on the clip's impact frame (967 ms) + hb/gold_sword smash FX + sound. The hit is the same Gravity Smash (stock knockdown + elite hit). Fists / gauntlet keep the instant slam. A refused switch still slams.
- BASH turns toward the nearest zombie within 360 u ahead (30 degrees), hits everything within 64 u of the body on every tick of the dash, then the 175 u cone; one hit per zombie per cast. Its impact FX is the blade's own burst (the electric Raz shockwave is gone).

## 2026-09-25 - Power scale: map 1's power structure at one tenth (damage and enemy health)

- THE FRONT DOOR: wraps `level.callbackActorDamage` (stock's one entry for every actor hit)
  so every hit a PLAYER or a partner robot lands on an ENEMY is x0.1 BEFORE anything reads
  it - cards, headshots, Panzer armor pools, the crosshair number and the kill feed all see
  the new value, each hit divided once. Guns, melee, lethals, tacticals, perks, partners.

  / tod_wisp_hit / tod_mage_chain_hit / tod_mage_hit_ms marks, a new neutral `tod_ps_exempt`
  (Thor's Thunder, PhD), the Gift of Death (xmas gun), Gravity Spikes lift kills, kill-intent
  (health + 1/100/666/1000/10000); no-attacker and enemy-on-enemy damage never scale.
  Rounding carries the fraction on the victim: exact on average, a steady number on screen.
- THE HORDE CURVE: map 1's exact integer curve (135 / +90 / +10% from r10) / 10, rounded:
  r1 14, r10 94, r20 243, r30 630, r50 4238. Held on `level.zombie_health` every 0.05 s and
  written onto every fresh spawn by `_tod_zombie_speed::apply_health_scale` (now also solo);
  stock's own inputs are 13.5 / 9.
ENEMY HEALTH at map 1 / 10: Protector 400, Panzer 1500, Fury 1500, Hellhound 1120, Warden
King 1M per player; Panzer part pools and caps (faceplate 150 +10, cover 75 +5, powercap 50 +5,
armor 35 +2.5; caps 1750/1600/750/500/350), claw cancel 50; Doppelghast/Mangler floor 50.

## 2026-09-16 (v19.19) - THE SKY'S SMOOTH SOLIDS: Tower II's profile-solid pass ported to Cybercity

User: *"In Tower of Doom Hellbound we had a math and geometry enhancement to
the skybox, so not everything is so blocky. I want to apply that to our skybox
too ... make it look better and more sharp."* That pass is Hellbound's v0.7
SMOOTH SOLIDS (its docs/63, `tools/gen_hb_sky.js` `drawSolid`); v18.87 had
already taken its v0.5/v0.6 QUALITY pass (2x paint, Lanczos resolve, cubic
noise, three sharpen passes) but not this one.

**THE PRIMITIVE.** `tools/gen_tod_sky.js` gains `drawSolid` / `addSolid`: a
PROFILE SOLID whose cross-section is a function of height, `sec(z) -> {cx, cy,
hx, hy}`; each column marches z at ~2.5 samples per screen row and solves the
section analytically - a circle when `round` (no faces, no face-flip shading,
a cylindrical falloff), a rectangle otherwise - with FRACTIONAL column
coverage so a thin taper thins out instead of snapping to whole pixels. The
shading is drawBox's own (haze fill, window cells, the neon cell grid, corner
and cap rims, the veil, the bloom emit), so a solid sits in the same light as
the box under it. `drawBox` is untouched. Constructors: `roundBody` (radius
profile), `spire` (concave cone), `hipCap` (rectangular slope), `setback`
(the sloped band between a box and the smaller box on it).

**WHAT STOPPED BEING BOXES.** Every antenna mast (a round taper, round
collars); every setback tier in the lattice, the far-ring mega-towers, the
arcologies, the megablocks and the tether anchor (a sloped band, not a flat
ledge); the ziggurat (sloped gold bands between its tiers, a round finial);
the floating platform's mast; the arcology masts. **AND SHAPES THE CITY NEVER
HAD:** a fifth of the lattice is ROUND (cylinder towers with cone-frustum
setbacks; per-lot hash roll OFF the rng stream, so every other roll is
unchanged), a fifth of the untiered box towers wear a PYRAMID crown, a third
of the far mega-towers are round drums, half the arcologies carry a DOME, and
each far twin tower a concave spire. 2048 preview: 1,225 solids (258 round
towers, 96 crowns, 5 domes); city pass 3.5 -> 4.6 s; seam 0.08x (unchanged).

⚠️ **A NaN DISTANCE BREAKS THE PAINTER SORT FOR THE WHOLE CITY.** The first
cut gave round lots no `base.d` (they never went through `addBox`), the tiers
inherited `undefined - 1`, and `items.sort((a, b) => b.d - a.d)` with NaNs in
it scrambled the order of EVERY item - the near towers drew before the far
ring and read as cut off at the mist line, across all 360 degrees. Found by
`TOD_SKY_PIXDBG`; both `addBox` and `addSolid` now THROW on a non-finite d.
Bisect aids: `TOD_SKY_SKIP=round,crown,slope`.

## 2026-09-15 (v19.15) — THE KEY IS THE TILE, AND IT IS ONE CHARACTER

User, on the v19.14 screenshots: *"The key should overlay the ENTIRE ability. Why
did you make it smaller and to the top right? Also I already told you about the
long string text and also you didnt use the correct typography."*

**THREE COMPLAINTS, ONE MISS.** The screenshot shows `G OR MIDDLE MOUSE` spelled
ONE LETTER PER LINE down the side of the lethal tile. That is the untrimmed
multi-bind expansion: `+frag` sits on both G and MOUSE3 and the engine returns
every key. v19.12 handed that to `CoD.TodKeycap.Name` to trim at the separator —
and in a Lua 5.1 harness that function returns `"G"` correctly, which is why
nothing caught it. In game the full string reached the element anyway, missed
our 42-glyph set, fell through to the LUI-text fallback, and WRAPPED inside an
18-unit box. Long string, wrong typeface and bad fit were all that one failure.

⚠️ **A FUNCTION THAT PASSES IN A HARNESS IS NOT A FUNCTION THAT RAN.** The test
proved `Name` works; it could not prove the value ever reached the row. The fix
is not to debug the trim, it is to STOP NEEDING ONE.

- **`TutKey` takes the FIRST CHARACTER of the expansion**, in this file, off
  `Engine.Localize` directly. That is what the user asked for in the first place
  ("the first letter of what key you have binding") and it is a string that
  cannot be long, cannot miss the glyph set for any ordinary key, and cannot
  wrap. A first byte >= 128 means a controller BUTTON PICTURE — multi-byte, no
  baked alphabet can draw it — and that alone is handed whole to the engine's
  font. The `TodKeycap` require is gone; nothing here depends on it now.
- **The badge IS the tile**: a plate over all 46x32 of it at alpha 0.80, with one
  character at cap 20 centred on it, in the map's typeface. v19.12 put a band
  across the top, v19.14 shrank that to a corner pill; both were wrong in the
  same direction and this is the opposite of both.
- Retirement and the owned-and-ready gate are unchanged (v19.13).

`test_mage_hud.lua` now feeds `"G OR MIDDLE MOUSE"` — the exact string that
reached the screen — and asserts a single `G` in OUR row with the engine font
dark. It also pins that a multi-byte picture takes the other lane whole. ⚠️ The
harness's own bug is worth the note: a chunk-LOCAL `Engine` shadowed the global
stub, so the first version of these assertions was localizing nothing.

## 2026-09-15 (v19.14) — TWO THINGS THAT LOOKED LIKE "TOO SMALL" AND WERE NOT

Both from screenshots, and both had a measured cause that resizing would have
papered over.

### 1 · Quick Revive was not clipped by its card. It was clipped by a POOL

User: *"I think QR needs a larger prompt to fit everything."* The card showed
`...REVIVE YOURSELF 3 TIME` and `...REVIVE TEAMMATES FAS`.

**Both lines came back cut at EXACTLY 34 characters** — 35 and 37 in, 34 and 34
out. That is `POOL_DESC`, the description row's glyph pool: `TodGlyphText` draws
until the pool runs out and then simply stops, with nothing said. Rendering the
two real strings over the real chassis through `tmp/render_card.py` shows them
fitting the 147-unit box with room to spare, because the row SHRINKS ITS CAP to
fit the width. **Width was never the constraint and the card did not need to
grow.** `POOL_DESC` 34 -> 40.

⚠️ **A CLIP AT A ROUND NUMBER IS A POOL, NOT A BOX — COUNT THE CHARACTERS
BEFORE RESIZING ANYTHING.** 40 and not 50 on purpose: every card carries two of
these rows, so each slot is ~12 elements across the prompt set, paid once at
construction, and the element pool is exactly what tonight's crash work was
about.

### 2 · The key badge is placed from the tile's own measurements

User: *"the button overlay doesnt fit on the ability cleanly. Lets be more
careful and better."* v19.12 dropped a full-width plate across y568..586 — **56%
of a 32-unit tile** — straight over the icon.

Read off the three elements rather than eyeballed, the tile is: **icon**
x0+5..x0+29 (the LEFT), **count** right edge x0+43 in the lower half (the
RIGHT). So the free ground is the TOP RIGHT, and that is where the badge now
sits, **right-aligned to the count's own edge** so the key and the charge number
share one vertical rule.

**IT SHRINKS BEFORE IT SPREADS.** One and two character binds — G, E, RT, LT, F,
which is nearly all of them — sit entirely in the corner and touch nothing. A
long one may grow left as far as `BADGE_MAX` 38 (the tile's content width), and
past that the cap shrinks to fit by exact arithmetic rather than iteration.
Measured, never estimated, which is the rule `TodKeycap` was rewritten for.
Cap 9 against the count's 12, so it reads as secondary; plate alpha 0.62.

`test_mage_hud.lua` pins the geometry: the row sets on the count rule, a short
bind keeps the full cap, and an over-wide one shrinks to exactly the content
width. Build: -GscOnly. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-15 (v19.13) — THE KEY BADGE NEEDS THE CARD **AND** A CHARGE

User: *"Key cards should only show when you actually have the ability and its
ready to use ... You need the actual upgrade and it needs to be ready."*

v19.12 gated the badge on OWNERSHIP alone (`everHad`), so an owned ability that
was spent or recharging still advertised its key while the tile sat dimmed at
40%. Now it needs both.

**THE TWO CONDITIONS ARE GENUINELY DIFFERENT STATES.** `everHad` is ownership —
the first upgrade card taken, which is what makes the tile draw at all; a
never-owned tile is hidden outright, so a badge on it would float over nothing.
`charges > 0` is readiness. Prompting a key that would be refused is worse here
than in most maps, because **every refusal in this class is SILENT by design**
(2026-09-09) — the badge would be the player's only feedback, and it would be
wrong.

**READINESS IS NOT RE-DERIVED IN LUA.** It rides the count the server already
sends: `abil_send` clamps the heal count to 0 for the aura's own 5 s lock
(`ready()` false) and re-sends when it lifts, and blink reports
`blink_charges_now()`. So `count > 0` IS "this cast would succeed", with no
cooldown arithmetic duplicated on the client. The one new line is in
`slot.setCount`, which records the number — `slot.count` is the GLYPH ROW, not
the value, so nothing else could answer the question.

`test_mage_hud.lua` covers it: spending the last charge takes that badge and
only that badge, and both return when the charges do. Build: -GscOnly. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-15 (v19.12) — THE KEY SITS ON THE ABILITY, IN OUR TYPEFACE; QUICK REVIVE STOPS ASKING WHICH PARTY IT IS

Two user calls on the v19.11 pass, both narrowing it.

### 1 · The ability hint is a badge ON the tile, key only

User: *"I wanted that ON TOP of the actual abilities, not to the side ... until
they've used that ability three times ... I don't want it to use any text ...
the first letter of what key you have binding, and if you're on controller ...
left trigger or right trigger"* — then: *"they should use our typography and not
the aetherium HUD letters."*

v19.11 drew three captioned lines beside the tiles. Gone. Each ability tile now
carries ONE badge on its top band (y568..586, the charge count keeps the bottom
right), showing the KEY AND NOTHING ELSE — no verb, no ability name.

- **The key comes from the live bind, trimmed.** `CoD.TodKeycap.Name( token )`
  localizes and cuts at the separator, so `+frag` — bound to BOTH G and MOUSE3,
  which the engine expands to the literal `G OR MIDDLE MOUSE` — reads **G**.
  That is the user's "first letter of what key you have binding", taken from the
  binding rather than from a table, so a rebind is right at the next refresh.
- **It is set in the map's own typeface**, the same baked glyph sheets as the gun
  name and the ROUND readout, centred by MEASURING the row first (it sets
  right-aligned) rather than by guessing a character width.
- ⚠️ **THE ONE EXCEPTION IS NOT A SHORTCUT: A CONTROLLER BIND DOES NOT EXPAND TO
  LETTERS.** The engine returns a BUTTON PICTURE (memory
  `bind-token-is-never-a-string`), and a 42-glyph baked alphabet cannot draw one.
  A pad therefore falls back to the engine's own font, which is the only thing
  that can render that icon — and it is also the *right* answer, correct on every
  pad layout without us writing "LT" anywhere. A keyboard never takes that path.
  A `measure` of -1 (a character we have no glyph for) takes the same lane, so a
  missing glyph degrades to readable and never to a gap.
- **No device branch.** One reader; what the engine returns IS the device's
  answer. `CoD.TodPad` is not consulted (v16.81: it is not a device proof).
- **ARCHMAGE has no badge** — it has no tile to sit on. It keeps the mana bar's
  own PRESS AIM BUTTON cue, which already exists and already flashes on a full
  bar. The server still counts its casts; only the third line is gone.

### 2 · Quick Revive states both prices and stops guessing

User: *"quick revive moving forward should not be dynamic at all. It should give
all the information for solo and co-op on one panel ... the solo price, co-op
price, and then what it does in solo and co-op."*

The card reads **SOLO $500 - REVIVE YOURSELF 3 TIMES** / **CO-OP $1500 - REVIVE
TEAMMATES FASTER**, and the price row is cleared **for this perk alone**. Every
other perk is a fixed price and is untouched.

**WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND THE PREVIOUS THREE WERE NOT.** Each earlier
attempt had to answer *"which party is this?"* from the client, and each got it
wrong in turn: a `tod_party` read that returned CO-OP whenever it failed
(v18.99l), then a hint parse that is only ever as right as whatever the server
last stamped — and tonight's own v19.11 fix exists because the server stamped 500
in co-op. **A card that states BOTH prices cannot be wrong about the party,
because it no longer asks.** ⚠️ The CHARGE is still per-party and still correct:
`solo_qr_price_fix` sets the trigger cost after stock settles the party. This
changes what the panel SAYS, never what the machine takes.

⚠️ **NOT AN EARLY RETURN**, though it reads like one: the perk ICON is set at the
END of `UpdatePerkInfo`, so returning at the price would have left Quick Revive
wearing the previous machine's picture — the same shape of bug as the price it
replaces.

### 3 · A gate that had been failing silently

`tools/test_perk_prompt_price.lua` modelled a widget with a `perkCost` member.
The v19.3 refactor moved every prompt onto `CoD.TodPromptCard`, whose price
element is `todPrice` — so since then **every assertion in that file was
comparing `nil` to a string** and the file could not have caught anything. It
now models the real element names (and the real `"$" .. digits` output),
auto-vivifies any `tod*` element the card reaches for, and answers `measure` /
`getText` with real values so the card's own layout arithmetic runs. Both suites
extended: the Mage HUD test covers badge show/retire per ability, the pad
fallback and the class swap; the price test asserts the empty row for Quick
Revive whatever the hint carries, and that the copy carries both prices.

**A TEST THAT PASSES BECAUSE IT CHECKS A FIELD NOBODY WRITES IS NOT A GATE** —
same family as `check-passes-wrong-question`. Build: -GscOnly. UNPLAYED.

### Same build — QUICK REVIVE PRICED 500 IN CO-OP (user: "QR is broken ... For coop it says 500. We just need two prices 500 solo and 1500 coop")

`_tod_perk_lights::solo_qr_price_fix` decided "solo" with `GetPlayers().size != 1`
the instant the FIRST player existed. In co-op the host exists alone for a
moment before the second client finishes connecting, so a two-player game
passed the solo test and the fix then re-asserted 500 onto the trigger (cost
AND hint) for 20 s, over stock's correct 1500. The party size is not known
until stock says so: `_zm.gsc` waits for every expected player, sets
`all_players_connected`, and only then decides `solo_game` from the settled
count. The fix now waits for that flag and reads that decision — two prices,
`500` solo / `1500` co-op, both asserted through the same loop, the mesh
relight kept solo-only. Dev log `[TOD_QR_PRICE]` records the settled party,
the chosen price and any re-assert that found a different cost on the
trigger. The prompt side (v18.99l) is untouched: it reads `[Cost: N]` off the
hint, so it shows whatever the server now stamps. UNPLAYED in co-op; solo is
the unchanged path.


### Same build — THE KING'S SYNC BURST IS SPREAD OVER FRAMES (crash suspect, NOT a proven fix)

Workshop, barn: *"we finally got to the warden king and immediately crashed"*
(co-op). NO CAUSE IS PROVEN — there is no log, it has never been reproduced,
and the King fight has never had a native co-op run at all. What follows is the
strongest suspect found by reading, and it is cheap enough to take on suspicion.

`king_max_player` sent one `LuiNotifyEvent( "tod_upg_sync" )` per eligible
domain with no yield (43 domains), then called `refresh_upgrade_list`, which
sends another per OWNED domain plus the tier row: **~87 scriptNotify writes per
player in ONE server frame**, and `king_max_out` looped every player with no
yield between them — ~174 in a frame for a duo, ~350 for a quad. Nothing else
in normal play is close: the only other 40-at-once sender is `dev_grant_maxed`,
which is dev-only and nothing threads it in a ship build, and
`refresh_upgrade_list` alone runs once per card pick. The burst lands at
precisely the moment barn describes.

It now yields a frame every `TOD_SYNC_BURST` (8) sends, and gives the list
refresh its own frame. The whole max-out runs inside `king_run`'s world pause,
so the extra fraction of a second is spent on a frozen board — the cost is
invisible and the caller releases the freeze after the dark deals either way.
Player validity is re-checked after each yield.

**What was RULED OUT this pass, so nobody re-runs it** (the element-pool crash,
PostiveMentalAttitude 2026-09-10 round 19, and Buffsee's "random crashes after
this last update"): a scan of every `.lua` under `ui/` found **ZERO** element
creations inside a subscription / notify / event-handler body — the leak
signature. Glyph rows are pooled and closed (`TodGlyphRow`), every prompt card
is Built once and closed by `ZMCursorHintNew`, and the pause menu's close now
walks and closes every direct child (the v18.x fix is present and correct). So
the Sep 14-15 prompt-card rebuild did not introduce a per-hint allocation leak.
The `AetheriumPerkItem` / `AetheriumPerksContainer` pair allocates through a
stock `UIList` + `updateDataSource`, which is the one lane not proven either
way here and is the next place to look if the pool crash persists — the spire's
`perma_perks_give` re-gives every perk after every revive and respawn, which
drives that refresh hard.

⚠️ **AND THAT "RULED OUT" IS NARROWER THAN IT SOUNDS — READ IT AS ONE
SIGNATURE, NOT AS "NO LEAKS".** The scan above looks for an element CONSTRUCTED
inside a callback. It cannot see the other leak shape: an element constructed
once and never closed because **LUI does not cascade `close()` to children** — a
parent's close leaves every child allocated unless something calls theirs.
`TodGlyphRow` says so in its own header and closes its pool for exactly that
reason, but a row is only released if its OWNER's close calls it. A concurrent
session found three such owners at 21:01:57 tonight (`AetheriumPerkItem`,
`AetheriumPerksContainer`, `TodPromptCard`) and added `close` overrides to them
in the repo — **five seconds after this build's sync, so they are NOT in this
`.ff`** and belong to whoever builds next. Do not read this entry as clearing
the element pool.

### The element-pool crash: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND QUANTIFIED (implemented by a concurrent session, not by this one)

User: *"UI clean up is typically the issue we have if you look at abandoned
cybercity as well."* Correct, and this is that bug.

**THE MECHANISM.** LUI does **not** cascade `close()` to children —
`TodGlyphRow.lua` states it in its own header and every widget in this tree is
expected to close its own by hand. The kit HUD's whole menu lifecycle is re-run
by the engine **PER LIFE**: `_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc` says so three separate times
("the engine closes a player's LUI menus on death -> spectate and the HUD is
rebuilt per life"). So every element a HUD widget owns but never closes is
abandoned on each death and freshly allocated on the respawn — a permanent,
per-life drain on a fixed pool. That is what "failed to allocate from element
pool" reports when it runs dry (PostiveMentalAttitude, round 19).

**THE SIZE, from `tools/test_ui_lifetimes.lua`'s own negative controls:**

| widget | unclosed per rebuild |
|---|---|
| `AetheriumLoadout` | **129 of 130** |
| `AetheriumScoreboard` | **74 of 75** |
| `AetheriumPlayerInfo` | **49 of 52** |

~252 elements from three widgets alone, every life. `AetheriumHud`'s close
override also names its children and omits six of them (`AetheriumLoadout`,
`AetheriumPlayerInfo`, `AetheriumRoundCounter`, both powerup widgets, the
crosshair) — the same stale-named-list defect `AetheriumStartMenu` was fixed
for. Glyph rows are the bulk of the Loadout figure: seven pools of 16/2/26/3/
32/4/7 = 90 images, all real children (`todMakeGlyphRow` calls
`owner:addElement`) held in a plain table with no `self.*` member, so a named
list can never reach them and only a child walk can.

**THIS SESSION DID NOT SHIP THE FIX.** A concurrent session owns this lane —
it added `close` overrides to `AetheriumPerkItem`, `AetheriumPerksContainer`
and `TodPromptCard` at 21:01:57 and extended `test_ui_lifetimes.lua` at
21:07:31 with HUD-owner and menu-rebuild suites plus the negative controls
quoted above. A child-walk version was written here and **reverted whole**:
two implementations of one fix in one working tree is how both get corrupted,
and the duplicate hook made that session's own negative control stop firing
("missing ownership hook must fail for AetheriumLoadout"), which would have
failed the build gate for both of us. The tree is left green for them.

⚠️ **ONE TRAP FOR WHOEVER LANDS IT:** a generic child walk on
`AetheriumPlayerInfo` closes the same wrapper `TodHealthTint.Attach` already
closes, and `test_ui_lifetimes.lua` catches it as *"element closed twice"*.
Those two overrides have to be reconciled into one owner, not stacked.

**UPDATE, 21:25 — THE CONCURRENT SESSION'S FIX IS COMPLETE IN THE TREE, and it
is the same shape.** `CoD.TodUIOwnership.Attach( owner )` in
`ui/uieditor/widgets/HUD/AetheriumWidgets/TodUIOwnership.lua` is one shared
child-walk close hook, **zoned** at `zm_tower_of_doom.zone:1574` (a `require` of
an unzoned rawfile fails SILENTLY, so that line is the difference between a fix
and a no-op), wired into nine owners — `AetheriumHud`, `AetheriumLoadout`,
`AetheriumPlayerInfo`, `AetheriumScoreboard`, `AetheriumRoundCounter`, both
powerup widgets, `tod_upgrade` and `tod_class_select` — and proven load-bearing
by the negative controls quoted above. Its header also solves the double-close
trap by ORDERING rather than by guarding: it installs immediately after
construction so feature hooks (`TodHealthTint`) run FIRST and it then closes
only what is left attached.

⚠️ **AN AUDIT THAT GREPS FOR `X:close()` CANNOT SEE THIS FIX** — the ownership
hook names no child. The audit run earlier in this entry reported Loadout /
Scoreboard / PlayerInfo as uncovered when they were already wired; the numbers
it produced are the size of the ORIGINAL leak, not of anything still open. Read
the constructor for an `Attach` call before calling a widget uncovered.

Publish build for the first Workshop upload since Sep 13 3:30 pm. No gameplay authored here — this
entry is the ship state and the notes reconcile.

### THE LEDGER WAS WRONG AND ONLY THE LIVE PAGE COULD SHOW IT

The user pasted the two newest Workshop sections. They proved row **#38 sat PENDING through its own
upload** — exactly the failure CLAUDE.md warns about and the one no gate here can catch:

- The upload went out **Sep 13 15:30 Eastern** carrying the **15:09:40 `-CleanPak` publish build**

- That evening `stage --version v19.0` **overwrote the still-pending row IN PLACE** — swapping the
  `.ff` to 23:11:50 and growing the section from 5 bullets to 7.
- So two bullets were recorded as shipped that **players have never seen**: *"RAMPAGE can now be
  switched on or off at any time"* (v19.0, built 23:11:50) and *"Solo Quick Revive now shows the
  price it actually charges"* (v18.99l, built 22:47:17). Both were built HOURS AFTER the upload.

Row #38 is closed `uploaded 2026-09-13 15:30`, `confidence: reconstructed`, version **v18.99d**, with
the whole story in its `note`. docs/68's section is cut back to the 5 bullets that actually shipped
and re-labelled with the 3:30 pm upload; the two orphans move into this release, where players meet

it had also swallowed the entire rampage-inducer rebuild.

⚠️ **THE LESSON IS THE ORDER, NOT THE TOOL.** `stage` overwrites a pending row and `check` only
compares it to the CHANGELOG, so neither can notice an upload that happened in between. **Stage ONLY
at publish time, and run `uploaded` the moment the upload lands.** Nothing in the repo can
reconstruct a missed upload; only the live page can, and only if someone asks for it.

## 2026-09-14 (v19.8) — THE UI ART WAS 79% OF THE MAP'S MEMORY

A Steam comment: *"I received a catastrophic freeze after reaching the top of the tower that
resulted in me having to restart my entire PC."* One report, no logs, never reproduced. The user
asked for a quick optimization check, not a three-hour hunt, and then for the findings to be fixed
with **"0 regressions"**.

### WE DID NOT FIND A BUG THAT EXPLAINS THE FREEZE, AND THAT IS THE HONEST HEADLINE

Seven angles, 27 candidates, 21 killed by an adversarial verify pass. What got ruled out matters
more than what survived, because each of these is the obvious theory someone will re-open:

- **No runaway script loop.** A scanner over every `for(;;)` / `while(1)` in all tod GSC **and** CSC
  found exactly one hit and it was a COMMENT, not code. Every boss director opens `for(;;){ wait 3; …}`.
  This was the leading hypothesis (a spinning game thread is what "my whole PC froze" usually is) and
  it is dead.
- **The crown cannot drive a GPU hang.** Also: **the "crown is 84% of the map's lit area" figure in
  CLAUDE.md is STALE — it is 67%** (`measure_lit_area.js` prints 949M of 1409M u²), and lit area is a
  LIGHTMAP-BAKE number, not a per-frame draw number. The tool says so in its own header. It must never
  again be cited as evidence about runtime rendering. Corrected in CLAUDE.md in this pass.
- **310 of 310 map lights ship `PRIMARY_NOSHADOWMAP 1` + `shadowUpdate Never`** — audited in the
  compiled `.map`, not inferred from the generator.
- **Zero looping or ambient FX anywhere at the crown, terrace or causeway.**
- **The sky and all 46 reflection probes are at stock parity** — our 8192x4096 EXR is the same
  resolution as stock Cold War skyboxes with field-for-field identical conversion flags.
- **The finale is the map's LIGHTEST elite phase, not its heaviest** — ~36 actors solo / ~51 quad
  against a 60 limit, bosses capped at `TOD_FINALE_BOSS_ROOF` 4.

So the freeze is unexplained and most likely host-side (a display-driver hang, or a machine already
under memory pressure). **Do not tell a player this build fixes their crash.** What it does is remove
a very large standing memory cost, which makes a memory-pressure failure less likely on a weak
machine. That is a real improvement and a different claim.

### THE REAL FINDING: 731.0 MiB OF THE MAP'S 920.6 MiB RESIDENT WAS UNCOMPRESSED UI ART

Measured from the linker's own ledger (`zone_source/all/assetinfo/zm_tower_of_doom.csv`), which is
the only honest source — it is the linker reporting what it PACKED, not what we asked for:

| | resident |
|---|---|
| upgrade cards (177) | **596.0 MiB** |
| other `i_tod_*` UI art (511) | 135.0 MiB |
| everything else in the entire map | 189.6 MiB |
| **total** | **920.6 MiB** |

All 687 image blocks in `source_data/tod_ui_images.gdt` shipped `compressionMethod "uncompressed"` —
raw RGBA8, 3.38 MB per 768x1152 card. **After: 377.8 MiB. Saved 542.8 MiB, a 59% cut.**

**ONLY THE DIVISIBLE-BY-4 IMAGES WERE FLIPPED — 487 zoned of 637.** Block compression works on 4x4
blocks and the converter's behaviour on a non-div-4 source (pad? resize? refuse?) is unproven here.
The 150 excluded images total 7.2 MiB, so the caution costs ~1% of the win. **Bigger is also SAFER,
not riskier**: a 768x1152 card draws into 351x526 physical pixels at 1080p (the LUI canvas is
1280x720 and scales 1.5x), so the GPU downsamples 2.19x per axis and averages block artifacts away;
a 32x32 icon drawn at 32x32 has no such headroom. (Related correction: the "186x279" in CLAUDE.md is
CANVAS UNITS, not 1080p pixels — the real class card is 279x418.5 px.)

### THE IN-REPO OBJECTION WAS REAL, AND IT WAS AIMED AT A DIFFERENT CODEC

v16.97, docs/89 and docs/61 all argue against compressing this art — *"DXT5 quantises 4x4 blocks,
which is worst exactly on"* smooth gradients, thin strokes and soft alpha — and docs/61 says outright
*"keep the 138 cards uncompressed if the user's art bar demands it."* **That objection targets
`compressionMethod "compressed"`. This pass used `"compressed high color"`, which is a DIFFERENT
codec at the IDENTICAL 1.0 bpp.** Proven by reading the converted `.iwi` headers: the Aetherium kit's
art is format byte **0x1e**, our flipped cards are **0x1f** (BC7). BC7 was designed for exactly the
gradients and alpha DXT5 mangles. **Before re-opening this, read the format byte, not the word
"compressed".**

Precedent, measured across the whole tools root (1,062 GDTs, 29,873 image blocks): 20,592
`compressed`, 6,030 `compressed high color`, only 1,287 `uncompressed` — and **1,227 of those 1,287
are this author's own GDTs**. Of the 60 that are not, not one is UI colour art. Stock BO3 compresses
UI art carrying legible baked text (the ESRB logo with its descriptor paragraph, the 1024x1024
credits screen, twelve 64x64 QR codes). The vendored Aetherium kit is **103/103 compressed** — and
**this map ALREADY shipped a compressed 1024x1536 pause-menu background in the same fastfile, which
is literally the surface the cards are drawn on top of.**

### TWO TOOLS, BECAUSE A REVERSIBLE CHANGE AND A REAL GATE ARE WHAT "0 REGRESSIONS" ACTUALLY MEANS

- **`tools/set_image_compression.js`** — selects div-4 only, biggest first, writes a manifest,
  `--restore` returns the GDT. Round-trip proven byte-identical (md5 before == md5 after restore).
  It reads the linker ledger so its projection counts only ZONED images; projecting from the GDT
  alone overstates the saving by ~17% (50 of 687 blocks are retired-domain art the zone never takes).
- **`tools/verify_image_compression.js`** — diffs two ledgers. Fails on a vanished image (a white
  square the linker never mentions), a flip that did not take, a resize masquerading as a compress,
  and drift in anything untouched. Negative controls for two of those are proven to fire.

⚠️ **THE VERIFIER CRIED WOLF TWICE AND BOTH WERE ITS OWN CALIBRATION.** A flat 3.2–4.8x ratio band
flagged the two 24x24 pause pips at x2.94 — because a fixed `.iwi` header survives while the pixel
payload shrinks 4x, so small images can never hit 4x. And a percentage-based drift rule flagged 12
untouched images that moved 16–224 bytes. **Both were settled by reading the `.iwi` header directly**
(format byte at offset 22, dimensions at 28–31): the pips are BC7 still at 24x24, the 12 are still
raw RGBA8 at their original dimensions. The gate now predicts the block payload from the manifest's
own w/h and uses ABSOLUTE bytes for drift, because the faults it exists to catch are never small — a
resize moves an image by a factor, never by 96 bytes.

### TWO BUGS FROM THE SAME SWEEP

- **THE PACK-A-PUNCH CLIENT-MODEL LEAK.** `zm_cwpap.csc` spawned a `tag_origin` host with
  `util::spawn_model` at all three FX handlers, kept it in a LOCAL, and only ever `DeleteFX`'d the
  effect — so every PaP field change leaked an empty client entity for the rest of the match. Stock's
  own `_zm_pack_a_punch.csc::pap_play_fx` keeps its host on `self.mdl_fx` and `Delete()`s the previous
  one beside its `DeleteFX`; the fix copies that idiom. **THREE SEPARATE HOST FIELDS, NOT ONE** —
  `papFXIdle(0)` and `papFXInUse(1)` fire in the SAME FRAME on the same machine (`zm_cwpap.gsc:293-294`),
  so a shared host would kill the in-use FX the instant it started. All eight `PlayFXOnTag` argument
  lists are byte-identical after the patch, so the render is unchanged by construction.
- **A FALSE COMMENT ABOUT PANZERS ON THE CAUSEWAY.** Two comment blocks claimed rampage's second
  Panzer "does NOT follow the party onto the causeway". `finale_beat_panzer()` and the hold-out top-up
  do read the raw constant — but only to decide whether to BANK a debt. `director()` at :1575 SPENDS
  every finale debt under `panzer_max_alive()`, which answers 2 while the inducer is on, and nothing
  clears that flag for the last mile. **So the causeway and the sealed crown hall CAN carry two.**
  v19.0 did not cause it; it only widened when the switch can be thrown. Comments only — whether a
  rampage finale SHOULD stand two is an open design question and nothing was changed to alter it.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.99g) — THE DEAD TRIGGER, THE MIRROR DOOR AND THE DOORWAY SLOTS

User, on playing v18.99f: *"I guess that isnt the inducer. WHat else could it be. It has to be an asset.
ALso fix this door. It has a reflection bug, and the inducer is way too high to even trigger."* Three
reports, three different causes, and the one they named LAST turned out not to be a height problem at all.

**1. THE INDUCER DID NOT "FAIL TO TRIGGER BECAUSE IT WAS HIGH" — ITS TRIGGER ORIGIN WAS BURIED.** v18.99f
left the trigger at the device's own x/y while cutting a 72-tall plinth around it, so the origin sat inside
a solid brush, and a `trigger_radius_use` whose ORIGIN is inside any solid **never prompts**. This is the
map's FOURTH payment on that exact trap (extraction obelisk, hall crate clip column, crown altar; memory
`trigger-origin-under-decal`). Fixed properly rather than nudged:
- the pedestal, the device and the trigger all come from ONE set of constants in `gen_tower_map.js` and are
  emitted into the generated `_tod_breather_data.gsc` as `base_inducer_org/_trig/_yaw/_trig_r` — the base
  ammo crate's own no-drift contract. `_tod_rampage.gsc` reads them; nothing is hand-typed any more.
- the trigger is **56 units out in FRONT** of the pedestal on open floor (`CRATE_TRIG_OUT` grammar), and the
  generator now **THROWS** if that point ever lands back inside the plinth.
- pedestal **72 -> 32 tall** and re-materialled to `MAT.pilaster` (plain cyan). The device top now sits at 61
  against a ~60 eye line. The old plinth was `dark_blue` — black tiles, dim grid — so it vanished against a
  black floor and the canister read as stuck to the wall in mid-air.

**2. THE DOOR'S "REFLECTION BUG" IS TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS.**
- **It is a mirror, not glass.** Nothing in the vertigo pack is transparent (`transparent 0`, zero
  `blendFunc` in the whole GDT). Every one of its 30 materials is instead a polished flat mirror:
  `$white_diffuse` albedo, `$white_specular`, `specAmount 1`, a gloss map measured **97% white**,
  `reflectionProbeAmount 1`, `envMap*` 1 with no fresnel, and **no normal map at all** — so a flat brush
  face reflects the skyline undistorted. The door shows it worst because it is the dimmest rung
  (`scaleRGB` 5 vs a wall's 15) and the filled texture with no grid lines to break a reflection up.
  FIX: five matte clones `tod_door_<hue>` in our own `source_data/tod_materials.gdt`
  (`tools/gen_tod_door_materials.js`), identical to their donors but with the specular and reflection
  zeroed, wired through a new `doorMatOf()` that touches **door slabs only** — deliberately not an edit to
  the shared pack, which would also strip the reflection off every landing, breather floor, the terrace,
  the causeway deck and the extraction pad.
- **There was also a real hole.** The arena cornice is emitted per WALL RUN, and the south and east walls
  are split around their doorways, so the 20-tall cyan cap simply stopped at each opening — leaving an open
  320x20 slot above the teleport-bay door and 120x20 above the power hallway, through which you saw SKY.
  New `base doorway lintel S` / `_E` close them. Collision is unchanged; the anti-vault clip already ran
  through that band.

**3. THE MODEL IS STILL WRONG AND IS NOW KNOWN TO BE WRONG.** `t10_zm_aether_canister` was picked in
v18.99e on a name match. Measured off its mesh it is **12.0 x 12.2 x 29.4, constant ~6-unit radius in all
22 z-bands, mirror-symmetric, one mesh** — a plain hazmat drum, charcoal with yellow/black chevrons
(2 orange pixels in 262,144), whose `_on` glow is **blue-violet** and 87% one fluid-level gauge. The real
Rampage Inducer is a lab containment canister: glass cylinder, brass ferrules, floating yellow crystal
shards in amber gas, red lamp, gauge, bail hoop, flex hoses, splayed base with a radiation trefoil. It is
in **no installed pack** (3,333 models checked across every GDT in the tools root) and `rampage` / `induc`
return **0 of 272,642** loaded BO6 assets, so it must be found by fiction — canister / essence / aetherium
/ crystal / vessel — and exported through Saluki. That needs one administrator approval, which was declined

## 2026-09-14 (v19.8) — THE FOOTER SITS IN ITS OWN SECTION, AND READS AT ONE SIZE

User, with three screenshots: *"okay your footer is the main issue. Its doesnt fit in its section
properly."*

### THE SECTIONS WERE MEASURED OFF THE ART, NOT EYEBALLED

`i_tod_prompt_chassis.png` is 924x304 drawn at canvas 544..775 x 444..520 — exactly **4 px per canvas
unit** — so every structural line in it has an exact canvas position, and none of this had to be a
judgement call:

| band | canvas | holds |
|---|---|---|
| header | 446.4 .. 460.6 | the title |
| cyan underline | 460.6 .. 462.1 | — |
| body | 462.1 .. 500.6 | the description rows |
| **divider rule** | 500.6 .. 501.1 | — |
| **footer** | 501.1 .. 516.6 | HOLD / key / verb + price |

The footer box was **499.35..508.75**. Its baseline is `top + 0.94h`, so the caps ran 500.7..508.2:
they STARTED above the divider and stopped **8.4 units short of the section's floor**. The line was
jammed against the top of its own band with a void beneath it and the rule running through the top of
the letters — which is precisely what the screenshots show. Now **503.8..513.2**, caps 505.1..512.6,
centred in the band. The price shares its baseline.

### "HOLD" WAS BIG AND "TO ACTIVATE" WAS TINY — ONE LINE, TWO TYPE SIZES

`TodGlyphText` fits each row to its OWN box. The verb had 40.6 units for a string that measures 60.7,
so it clamped to **cap 4.56** while "HOLD" beside it — which fits its box easily — drew at **7.52**.
Three changes, all needed:

* **The key slot was 30 units** for a button PICTURE that draws about 13 wide beside a one-character
  default keyboard bind. 30 -> **22**; `FOOT_HOLD_W` 28.1 -> **24** ("HOLD" measures 23.2, so 24 is
  the smallest box that never clamps it).
* **The verb's right edge is conditional now.** The price shares this row, so with a price the verb
  stops at 723 and without one it runs to the card's inner edge at 771. "TO ACTIVATE" — the longest
  verb in the map, on the power switch, which has no price — now fits at **full size**.
* **One cap for the whole line.** `LayoutFooter` measures the verb BEFORE anything draws and pushes
  the cap it can actually have into both rows. They already shared a baseline; now they share a size.

Measured against the real metrics, the only verb that still clamps at all is Pack-a-Punch's
"TO UPGRADE" (**cap 6.87**), the one long verb that shares its row with a price — and "HOLD" goes
with it.

⚠️ **THE MEASUREMENT COMES FROM THE TYPEFACE, NOT A CONSTANT.** `CoD.TodGlyphRow.measure` walks the
GENERATED metrics, so a re-sliced sheet re-spaces every string. `TodGlyphText` kept that private; it
now exposes `measure( str, cap )`. Hard-coding "~0.81 x cap per character" in the card would have been
a second source of truth that nothing regenerates.

### THE DESCRIPTION GOT THE SAME TREATMENT (v19.8b)

Moving the footer down made the other void obvious: the body band is 38.5 units and the two rows sat
at 466.65..487.1, hugging the cyan underline with 13.5 units of nothing beneath them. On a ONE-LINE
card — Pack-a-Punch, and every one of the 53 doors — a single line sat at the top of the band with
**25 units of void under it**. `LayoutDetail` centres a pair as a block and a single line on its own;
the rows keep the v19.7 size (8.4) and pitch (12.05). This is the user's standing *"ton of empty space
under the description"*, fixed from the side the art defines rather than by moving the footer up.

### VERIFIED BY RENDERING THE CARD, THEN BY THE GAME

`tmp/render_card.py` walks `TodGlyphRow.set`'s own arithmetic over the generated metrics and
composites the real glyph cells onto the real chassis. Run against the OLD numbers it reproduces the
user's three screenshots — the rule through the footer text, the tiny verb, the price crossing the
line — which is what makes it trustworthy for the new ones.

## 2026-09-14 (v19.7) — THE SIZE INCREASE, CUT TO 35% OF ITSELF

User, on seeing v19.5/v19.6 in game: *"lets cut the size increase we did on everything by 65%. I
think its too big."* Every number here is `v19.3 + 0.35 * (v19.5 - v19.3)` — arithmetic, not a
re-judged layout, so what ships is exactly 35% of the growth that went out.

| row | v19.3 | v19.5 | v19.7 | drawn cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompt title | 10 | 14 | **11.4** | 8.00 → 11.20 → 9.12 |
| prompt detail ×2 | 7 | 11 | **8.4** | 5.60 → 8.80 → 6.72 |
| prompt footer | 8 | 12 | **9.4** | 6.40 → 9.60 → 7.52 |
| prompt price | 9 | 13 | **10.4** | 7.20 → 10.40 → 8.32 |
| left player HUD | 1.00 | 1.10 | **1.035** | — |

The box height IS the type size (`cap = h * capFrac`, capFrac 0.80), so there is no separate font
number anywhere. **The fractions are deliberate**: this is the 1280x720 virtual canvas, and rounding
448.3 to 448 would have quietly made the cut 75% on that row instead of 65%.

### THE DEAD BAND IS THE ONE THING NOT INTERPOLATED BACK

The same playtest that produced *"the text is very small"* produced *"there's always a ton of empty
space under the description"*, and only the first of those two has been revisited. Interpolating the
footer's POSITION would have put 8 of those 22 units back on screen with nobody asking for them. So
the footer keeps the v19.5 lift and takes only the size cut, and the 6.5 units the shrink frees are
split evenly above and below it — dead band 9 → 12.25, bottom margin 6 → 9.25. Against v19.3's
22-unit hole that is still less than half.

### THE FOOTER VERB BARELY MOVES, AND THAT IS THE EXPECTED RESULT

`TodGlyphText` fits to the box, so a long verb in the 153-unit bottom row is WIDTH-clamped, not
height-clamped: "TO UPGRADE" already drew at cap ~4.7 and a height change cannot reach it. "HOLD" is
the height-bound half, so `FOOT_HOLD_W` comes down 32 → 28.1 (v19.3 was 26 — the same 35%) or the
glyph would clamp at the new cap and the word would stay big while everything beside it shrank.

### THE LEFT HUD SCALE, AND WHY NOTHING ELSE HAD TO CHANGE WITH IT

`TOD_PLAYER_HUD_SCALE` 1.10 → 1.035; the anchor (45, 678) does not move. A smaller factor about the
same measured corner keeps all four widgets in register exactly as 1.10 did, and every overlap
figure only gets safer as the factor falls: the tightest content gap (the portrait, 7.0 at 1.00 and
7.7 at 1.10) is 7.2 here, and the cluster's top goes 415 → 431.

Unchanged from v19.5/v19.6: the footer key, the money glyph's baseline and advance, the Endless
Spire door naming, the icon table, and `TOD_MOCK_PARTY` (still ARMED — `-Publish` refuses while it
is).

## 2026-09-14 (v19.5/v19.6) — THE BLANK KEY, THE TYPE SIZE, THE COIN, AND THE LEFT HUD

User, after walking every prompt: *"it says hold blank to buy ... there's always a ton of empty
space under the description, and the text is very small ... the money sign alignment with numbers is
still off"*, then *"the Endless Spire says Spire on each door"*, then *"the player HUD on the left
can be increased by 10% all around ... and we need to double check that a full game of players dont
have overlapping HUDs."*

### 1. "HOLD ___ TO BUY" — MY REGRESSION, AND THE WRONG COMPONENT

v19.3 drew the footer key through `CoD.TodKeycap`, the widget that renders a bind INSIDE the pale
keycap art for the class draft and the pause legend. On a prompt card it drew NOTHING on every card
in the map. Two causes, both mine: `make( owner, fallbackText )` was handed a **nil fallback**, so
every failure path inside `paint` resolved to an empty element; and that widget expects the CAP ART
drawn behind it by its caller, which a prompt footer has no room for.

**It is one element holding `[{+activate}]` again** — which is what v14.58..v19.2 already had right,
and what the user said out loud: *"this should already be taken care of. The other had this figured
out."* The engine expands the token into the device's own key or button picture. No device branch,
cannot come back blank, correct after a rebind.

### 2. THE TYPE SIZE IS THE BOX

A glyph row's size is `cap = h * capFrac`, so the box IS the type size. Title 10 -> 14 (+40%), both
detail rows 7 -> 11 (+57%), and the 22-unit dead band under the description is 9.
⚠️ **THE FOOTER IS WIDTH-BOUND AND COULD NOT TAKE IT.** The bottom row is 620..773 = 153 units and
must hold "HOLD <key> TO UPGRADE" AND a price; at the letters set's own metrics "TO UPGRADE" alone
wants ~73 units at cap 12. Widening it means moving the price, and every row it could move to
already carries copy of varying length. The size went where the user could not read.

### 3. THE COIN WAS SIX PIXELS BELOW THE BASELINE — MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED

`TodGlyphRow` scales each glyph by `cap / S.cap` and places it so `S.baseline` lands on the row's
baseline. The letters set is **cap 89, baseline 103**, so its cap box is y 14..103. The v19.2 coin
was ink **y 37..109**: 73 tall against a 89 cap, with its bottom **six pixels BELOW the baseline**.
That is exactly the two things on screen — a fifth short, and sitting low. Cause: v19.2 bottom-
aligned it on the DEAD AMPERSAND's ink (y110) instead of on the set's baseline.

Recut to sit **exactly on 103**, 75 tall (85% of cap — the coin art is square and the cell is only
80 wide, so a full 89 would overflow into its neighbour). `slice_hud_sheets.js` re-cut the cell and
**re-measured the advance from the art**: `$` went `{adv 72, x 5, w 72}` -> `{adv 74, x 4, w 74}`.
⚠️ THE SLICER READS `_images/` BY DEFAULT — the master lives in `_sheets/` and needs `--src`.

### 4. THE SPIRE'S DOORS NAMED THE WRONG BUILDING

`Open Door to the Spire` titled every one of the 70 doors "SPIRE", and PromptDoors' generic detail
told the player they would "CLIMB HIGHER INTO THE TOWER" — a different tower entirely. Now
`the Endless Spire` + "DEEPER INTO THE ENDLESS SPIRE".
⚠️ **RENAMING A HINT ORPHANS ITS MULTIPLICITY ROW.** `lint_tod_hints.js` keys each variable hint on
its TEXT, so the reword dropped the spire door template out of the budget entirely (43 -> 42
templates, 95 -> 94 strings) and failed the build. Re-keyed; its `why` also still claimed "all 100
spire doors (flat 3000)" when the spire has been 70 doors at 6300 since v17.70.

### 5. THE LEFT PLAYER HUD, +10% — A SCALE, NOT RE-AUTHORED BOXES

Opposite shape to the prompt card, and therefore the opposite technique. The left HUD is FOUR
widgets (the local row + three party rows) that must keep their exact relative positions, sharing
one text column at x=90 and a 43-unit pitch. `TodScaleAt( el, ax, ay, scale )` scales about a
measured anchor and `TodScalePlayerHud` pins all four to the same one.

⚠️ **THIS IS NOT THE SCALE v17.9 REVERTED.** That was 1.15 on the LOADOUT about a bottom-RIGHT
anchor, and the loadout parents the perks row, which is bottom-CENTRE — one anchor could not serve
both, the row walked off centre and the plate ran 117px past the right edge. The left HUD is
single-anchor by construction. Anchor **(45, 678)**, measured from the widgets' own boxes
(local row x90..250 y636..678; party rows x45..198 y439..611).

**THE OVERLAP QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY LOOKING.** Computed from the rows' own
offsets, content-band gaps are portrait 7.0, name 30.0, health 32.0, points 30.0 — and because the
anchor sits BELOW the cluster, a uniform scale SPREADS them: 7.7 / 33.0 / 35.2 / 33.0 at 1.10. Zero
overlaps before or after. Cluster at 1.10: top 415, right 270.5 — clear of every edge. (The row
BACKGROUNDS overlap by design, 87 tall on a 43 pitch; the visible content does not.)
`TOD_MOCK_PARTY` is ARMED so four rows are testable solo — `-Publish` refuses to build while it is.

User, two minutes into a playtest: *"the teleport bay, the power switch. These don't even use the

### THE ARCHITECTURE — `Prompts/TodPromptCard.lua`

Six prompt cards were six independent copies of one design: same five chassis rects, same
title/detail/price boxes, same footer, each with its own fonts and its own hardcoded copy. v19.1
reskinned the art in all six; v19.2 converted the typeface in ONE. That half-and-half state is
what the user hit — the ammo crate drew the map's letters and the power switch three feet away
drew the kit's.

`CoD.TodPromptCard` now owns the chassis, the icon well **and the icon table** (which was `local`
to PromptDefault, so five cards could not reach it), the typeface, every box, the footer and the
price. All six cards plus `TodTeleportFeedback` are thin shells over it. **Zero `setTTF` calls
remain on any reachable prompt surface**; the single survivor is one element that exists only to
carry a controller BUTTON PICTURE, which is not typography and must match the player's hardware.

**THE CASE COMPLAINTS ARE FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION.** `TodGlyphText`'s cleaner runs `string.upper`
(the sheet has 42 glyphs and no lowercase), so "the Teleport Bay" cannot reach the screen in mixed
case once a card routes through the owner. The leading article is stripped for the TITLE only —
the hint still has to read as a sentence, a title band does not.

### ⚠️ THE 42-GLYPH SET SILENTLY DELETES WHAT IT CANNOT DRAW

Measured on the live perk table: `( ) , / : ;` all appear in strings that now route through the
typeface. `"Faster revives in co-op / Self-revive up to 3 times in solo"` would have drawn with the
divider GONE and the clauses fused. `CoD.TodPromptCard.Sanitize` converts every mark we can say
without a glyph and runs on every setter, so no card can bypass it by accident. The perk card also
gets purpose-written short copy (the shared table's lines are up to 83 chars against a 34-glyph
row); the long copy stays untouched for the perks container, which has the room and the font.

### THE COPY

`"Powers various things around the map"`, `"Buy to unlock new areas"` on all 53 doors, `"You must
find and activate the power first"` — all kit filler, none written about this map. Rewritten. Doors
now name what is through them. Power Required says WHERE the switch is.

### THE PRICE LOCKUP

User: *"the money icon on the ammo prompt is tiny and not aligned with the cost."* One cause for
both halves: the coin was a separate `UIImage` in a hand-numbered 15x12 box beside a text box, and
`i_tod_hud_points_icon.png` carries transparent padding, so the visible coin was far smaller than

price is ONE glyph row, `"$2500"`, right-aligned to the card edge: same cap height, same baseline,

## 2026-09-14 (v19.2) — THE PROMPT CARDS: the bind was never a string, and the typeface was never swapped

User, on five screenshots of the v19.1 reskin: *"Some dont have titles some have overflowing names.
SOme are missing assets completely and its not using the typography for the map liek I asked."*
Four faults, four different causes, and one of them was mine.

### 1. THE EMPTY TITLES WERE THE RESKIN'S OWN REGRESSION

The kit's outer layer was a FRAME with a hollow centre, so it did not matter that FIVE of the six live
cards `addElement` their title BEFORE it. v19.1 replaced it with one OPAQUE plate (meanAlpha 255,
measured), and it painted over them. The chassis block moves above every text element in
`PromptDoors`, `PromptPerks`, `PromptPAP`, `PromptPowerSwitch` and `PromptPowerRequired`; `PromptDefault`
already ordered it correctly, which is why only the door cards showed a blank band.

### 2. "Hold (X)" IN THE TITLE — THE BIND TOKEN IS NEVER A STRING BY THE TIME LUA READS IT

**Proven from the live console, not inferred:** the client caches the cursor hint as
`<localization ref> 0x15 <args>` — `[BGCACHE] Client: Registering configstring index 506 with data
<0x15>Hold ^3[{+activate}]^7 ^1RAMPAGE^7 - currently ^1OFF^7` — and RESOLVES that pair (localize,
substitute, expand `[{+bind}]`) before publishing the result to `hudItems.cursorHintText`. So by the
time `PromptDefault` reads it, `[{+activate}]` is already an Xbox button PICTURE. Its
`string.find(t, "%[{%+[%w_]+}%]")` test therefore **never once fired since v14.58**, the "Hold " strip
it gated never ran, and the prefix rode into every title. **THE SAME FALSE FLAG ALSO HID THE FOOTER**
on every PromptDefault card — two unrelated-looking symptoms, one cause. And it is why
`HEAVENLY GIFT ALTAR` wrapped: ~44 canvas px of prefix in a 134 px box.

**THE FIX ANCHORS ON TEXT THE MAP AUTHORED, AT BOTH ENDS.** Every pressable hint is
`Hold ^3[{+activate}]^7 <TITLE> - ...`, so the word "Hold" and the `^3`/`^7` pair are OURS and only the
middle is the engine's: swallow the middle whole, whatever it became. Device-independent by
construction — a pad glyph, `F` and `MIDDLE MOUSE` are all just "between our two colour codes".
**Do NOT replace this with a byte-range test**: v18.47 shipped exactly that next door in `TodKeycap`
and turned every keyboard player into a controller player. Title box also 754 -> 770 (the art's band
runs to 773; the 16 px were unused).

### 3. THE FIFTH SCREENSHOT WAS NOT A FAULT

The ammo-crate shot is timestamped **22:51:56**, against a `.ff` from the 22:47 build — BEFORE the
reskin linked at 00:19/00:24. It shows the OLD kit chassis and the stock documents glyph because that
is what the card was. **Check a screenshot's mtime against the `.ff` before diagnosing from it.**

⚠️ **AND THE PEER SESSION WAS WRONGLY NAMED.** This session told the user a peer's ZMCursorHintNew
rewrite was "a prime suspect", on a `git diff --stat` of 635 lines. That figure is against commit
57f565f (v14.16, weeks back) — every UI file in the tree reads like that (`tod_upgrade.lua` shows
3001). The bug predates both sessions. **A `--stat` against an ancient cutoff is not evidence of a
recent edit.**

### 4. THE TYPOGRAPHY, AND THE MONEY SYMBOL

*"its not using the typography for the map liek I asked"* — correct, and v19.1 could not have: it
replaced images and left all 21 `setTTF` calls alone. **"Our typography" is a NAMED ASSET here**, not a
font: `CoD.TodGlyphText` over a 42-glyph baked sheet with GENERATED metrics, which already draws the
gun HUD, the ROUND counter, damage numbers, points, the kill feed and every keycap since v17.34 — on
this same user's earlier ask. The prompt cards were the LAST live-text surface still on the kit's two
TTFs. `PromptDefault`'s title, both detail lines and the price are converted (a constructor swap by
design — the element takes the same box). **THE FOOTER KEEPS ITS TTF ON PURPOSE:** it carries the live
bind, which on a pad is a picture, and our 42 glyphs contain no button icons.

**THE MONEY SYMBOL IS THE HUD'S OWN, IN A CELL THAT WAS GOING TO WASTE** (user: *"Our HUD usies this
symbol in the player HUD when showing amount of money you have. You can reuse that"*). The letters
sheet is 15x2 = 30 cells for 30 characters — full — but cell 28 was DEAD: the delivered ampersand reads
as an "8", so it was never zoned, never sliced, and `AetheriumLoadout` expands "&" to " AND ". The
points icon is composited there, cropped to its own ink and bottom-aligned on the ampersand's ink
bottom so the row's baseline check is untouched; `$` joins the four other marks exempt from the
cap-height median (a coin is no more cap-height than "." is); and its advance is **MEASURED from the
art** by `slice_hud_sheets.js`, not typed. So `$` now draws the player's own money symbol **anywhere
the map's typeface is used**, and the reword this was going to need never happened.

## 2026-09-13 (v19.0) — RAMPAGE IS A FREE SWITCH: the round-9 seal is retired whole

User: *"I want to remove the round 9 rampage lock. It will be toggleable throughout the game."*

**The lock was smaller than its reputation: ONE predicate and ONE constant.** `locked()` was
`level.round_number >= TOD_RAMPAGE_LOCK_ROUND` (9), read at exactly three sites — the use loop's
refusal (the only functional one), `lock_watcher` (cosmetics + the banner) and `hint_for_state`.
**The device already toggled BOTH WAYS** (`level.tod_rampage_on = !IS_TRUE( ... )`, and the module
header lists a one-way toggle as map 1 failure mode F2), so "toggleable throughout the game" needed
nothing added — only the refusal removed.

**RETIRED WHOLE**, because half a retirement is dead weight or a white square: the constant,
`locked()`, `lock_watcher`, `seal_banner`, the `tod_rampage_sealed` eventstring precache, the
`CoD.TodRampageSealed` Lua widget with its SEAL_* geometry, the `image,` zone line and the baked
1024x512 plate. Zoned images 627 -> 626.

**TWO PERMANENT ENGINE SLOTS CAME BACK.** `hint_for_state` was four constant strings, two of them
the sealed forms; it is two now. The hint lint reports **94 distinct strings of 190 budgeted**, down
from 96 — in a map whose hard engine cap is 250 and whose overflow crash blames an innocent object.

**THE ARGUMENT FOR A LATE SEAL WAS ALREADY DEAD BEFORE THIS ASK.** The header justified round 9 by
the inducer sitting behind the `enter_tpbay` door at a co-op price of 1,909 / 2,727 / 3,545 — but
**v18.99f moved the device onto the open arena floor** at (-280, -516), where it is reachable from
spawn for nothing. Two comment blocks still argued the old map a day after it changed; both are
rewritten.

### What a free toggle actually means, because the levers are not uniform

Established by reading every consumer, and it is unchanged behaviour — only now it can happen twice:

- **Most levers revert live.** The elite roof, zombies-at-once, the spawn floors and the director's
  reads are all `IS_TRUE( level.tod_rampage_on )` evaluated per use, so OFF is felt within a couple
  of seconds or at the next round rollover.
- **Spawn-time HP is not retroactive, in either direction.** An elite, an armored sprinter or a
  horde zombie banks its multiplier as it spawns. Flipping OFF does not soften what is already on
  the deck; flipping ON does not harden it.
- **The Warden King latches at `king_setup`** — his HP, his sprint thread and the per-zombie sprint
  stamp are taken once when he lands. Toggling during the summit fight does not change HIM; it still
  changes the adds around him.

lane shipped with no diagnostics at all): the toggle with player, new state and round, and the one

## 2026-09-13 (v18.99d) — THE ICE STAFF FIRES EVERY 0.8 s

User, on being told the cadence and the post-shot weapon-switch pause are the same field: *"Move the
ice staff to 0.9s per shot then"*, then *"0.8s actually"*.

Native `fireTime` **1.1111 -> 0.8** on `tod_staff_ice` and both regenerated twins. One number, and it
buys two things at once, which is exactly why the call was theirs to make:

- **The cadence.** 0.90 shots/s -> 1.25 shots/s, a **~39% rate increase**. The ice staff's damage per
  hit is untouched, so this is a **~39% DPS buff** and the biggest single change to the staff since
  v18.77 halved its way through a balance pass. It lands on the three-missile volley, so every pull
  still throws three full-damage projectiles — just more often.
- **The switch pause.** The engine holds the weapon switch for the firing state, so the pause after a
  shot drops 1.11 s -> 0.8 s with it. That was the complaint v18.94 tried and failed to fix with a

## 2026-09-13 (v18.99c) — TWO REGRESSIONS THE USER CAUGHT: the ice staff's rate of fire, and the riot shield card

### 1. THE ICE STAFF FIRED AS FAST AS YOU COULD CLICK — v18.94's fix did not transfer

User: *"We also broke the ice staff rate of fire. We tried to fix the fact that when you shoot, you
can't switch, and instead we made the rate of fire super super fast. They worked for the fire staff
because it had a charge up shot where the ice staff doesn't. So we need to fix this. They should still
be able to switch after shooting, but the shot timing should still be one point one seconds, which it
was before."*

**Their diagnosis is the whole cause, and it is a `fireType` difference.** v18.94 cut ice's native
`fireTime` 1.1111 -> 0.1 and moved the cadence onto the fire staff's script cooldown
(`DisableWeaponFire` on a deadline). That works for FIRE because fire is **`Charge Shot`**: the engine
fires on RELEASE, so every shot needs a fresh press and the flag is read on that press. ICE is
**`Single Shot`**. With the engine's own gate down to 0.1 s, the script flag did not hold the next
press, so the cadence became however fast the trigger could be clicked.

**The cadence is the engine's again: ice `fireTime` 1.1111** (source + both regenerated twins), and ice
comes OFF the script controller entirely — `TOD_MAGE_ICE_RECOVERY_MS` and `tod_mage_ice_ready_ms` are
gone, so `fire_recovery_*` is the fire staff's alone. One owner, no race, exactly the 1.1 s the staff
shipped with for months.

**THE COST IS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: the post-shot weapon-switch pause comes back with the timing**, because
the engine holds the switch for the firing state and that state IS the cadence. The two requirements
are in tension through one field. The only native lever that could separate them is a short `fireTime`
plus `shotsBeforeRechamber` 1 and `rechamberTime` ~1.01 — the bolt-action split; both fields exist on
this `projectileweapon` asset and both are 0 today. It is **unproven** on this asset type, so it is not
being guessed at inside a publish build; it is a one-line experiment whenever the user wants it tried.

`verify_staff_animations.py` now asserts ice `fireTime` 1.1111 AND that `TOD_MAGE_ICE_RECOVERY_MS` is
absent, so the v18.94 shape cannot come back by accident; `test_mage_fire_swap.js` asserts ice is never
gated by that controller. GDT change = FULL build.

### 2. A RIOT SHIELD CARD DID NOT BRING A BROKEN SHIELD BACK

User: *"I had no riot shield, and I got a riot shield upgrade card, and it didn't refill my riot shield
when it should. That is the requirement. I thought we fixed this before. Sometimes it seems to work,
but this time it didn't."*

**They did fix it before — a different case.** v17.10's `swap_shield` refill covers a card taken while
you are HOLDING a shield. A card taken while the shield was **broken and recharging** fell into
`reconcile()`'s recharging branch, and the only thing that branch did was re-derive the deadline at the
new, faster rate. So it appeared to work exactly when that new deadline had already passed (a big level
jump, or a break most of the way through the wait) and did nothing at all when it had not. **That is
the reported intermittency, precisely.**

Now a card **ENDS** the recharge: the deadline and the break stamp are cleared, `recharge_loop` is
stopped by notify BEFORE the give (two owners handing out one shield is the inventory-overflow trap),
and the reconcile falls through to the give — the shield is back in hand at its new strength.

**The recharge still means something.** The test is `improved` — the shield's HP NUMBER went up since
the last reconcile — which no routine caller can cause. The 2 s maintain loop, every respawn and every
reload of the lane still fall through to the old shortening, so a broken shield still has to wait
unless the player earned a card. `improved` also already covers the DARK rung, which raises HP without
moving the level.

### 3. AND THE NOTES HAD TO BE NETTED

Three bullets came OUT of the pending release by the house netting rule, and the first one had gone
actively false: *"No more delay switching weapons after an ice staff shot"* was v18.94's promise, and
this entry reverts it. Against the LAST PUBLISHED build (v18.85) the ice staff's cadence and switch
behaviour are IDENTICAL — 1.1111 s then, 1.1111 s now — because the break and the fix both happened
inside this unreleased window. The shot-flash bullet went for the same reason: the flash it promised to
remove only ever existed in v18.89-92, which nobody ran. What players actually receive is a new-looking
ice staff, which the New section already says. **A window that contains both a regression and its fix
must report NEITHER**

⚠️ **CORRECTED 2026-09-13, SAME DAY: THE PREMISE ABOVE WAS WRONG AND THE TWO ICE BULLETS WERE RIGHT TO
SHIP.** They went out in the 13:59 upload, which carried the **v18.98** build (13:45:51) — the one with ice
`fireTime` 0.1 — so "no more delay switching weapons" and "no flash or puff" were both TRUE of the binary
players received. The break and the fix were NOT in one unreleased window; the break shipped. What made this
look otherwise was a three-hour timezone error (see the v19.0 notes and `patch_notes.js`
`STEAM_TO_LOCAL_HOURS`), which placed the upload after builds that came later. **The real consequence runs the
other way: v18.99c/d TAKES BACK a behaviour players were promised in writing** — the ice swap is 0.8 s again,
not free — so the next notes have to say so out loud rather than quietly reverting it — and the moment a revert lands, re-read the staged notes for a promise it just
broke.

New gate `tools/test_riotshield_card_refill.js` runs the real `reconcile()` body: the card-mid-recharge
case (the bug), the start-of-a-long-recharge case that used to do nothing, plus negative controls that a
routine reconcile does NOT hand a shield back and can only ever shorten a wait. It fails against the old
code. Wired into `build_map.ps1`.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.99b) — THE POWER SIGNS: six glowing decals from the base to the switch

User: *"I downloaded a power switch decal that we can add, or decals that we can add to the power
hallway, and maybe one decal or two right outside the door. So players know where to turn on power,
and they'll see it and they know to open the door. Abandoned cyber city already uses this download."*

It does, and that made this a port rather than an authoring job. The pack is **"Images arrow coldwar
dogcanary"** — Treyarch BOCW dark-aether wall scrawl, ripped by DOGCANARY — and it has been installed
in the **shared** Mod Tools root since 2026-07-12, already in `gdtdb`, with four of its images already
converted. **Map 2 pays nothing to use it: no download, no GDT, no repo file, and NO ZONE LINE** —
a material used only as a brush or mesh face is baked into the `.d3dbsp` by cod2map and resolved out of
gdtdb, which is why map 1 ships eleven of these with no `material,` row either (map 2's own
`tod_hall_crest_*` plaques prove the same rule).

**Which material is which had to be READ, not inferred** — the material numbering and the image
numbering do not line up: `arrow_power_coldwar1` is the word POWER (image `_05`), `arrow_power_coldwar4`
is the thin LEFT arrow (image `_02`), and the bare `arrow_power_coldwar` is a curved RIGHT arrow
(image `_01`). The other eight are ENGINE / VENT / STAIRS / Assemble / PASSWORD / Family / STOLEN and
one more arrow. They are `usage decal`, `lit_emissive_scroll_transparent` at `scaleRGB 16` — they glow,
which is the whole point in a corridor lit by three cyan point lights.

**THE RECIPE IS MAP 1'S PROVEN CHALK-MESH, NOT A BRUSH** (`decalMesh` / `decalSouthWall` in
`tools/gen_tower_map.js`): a flat 2x2 patch mesh, `contents nonColliding`, `DECAL_PROUD` 2 units off
the wall face, texture mapped once (u 0 -> 1024 across the columns, v 0 -> -1024 up the rows), with
map 1's donor lightmap floats copied verbatim. A brush would have given a picture collision, a navmesh
cut and six textured faces. The geometry lint's `parseWorld` needs exactly six planes, so a mesh is
invisible to it — no `MATERIALS` entry, no baseline move; both advisory map tools still parse.

**THE WINDING DECIDES WHICH WAY THE ART FACES, and map 1 already paid for the rule**: normal =
u_dir x v_dir with v_dir = +z, so **-y normal -> columns Xmin->Xmax, +y normal -> columns Xmax->Xmin,
-x normal -> columns Ymax->Ymin**, and u0 is always the VIEWER'S LEFT with the texture unmirrored. Get
it backwards and POWER renders as a mirror image and every arrow points the wrong way. The consequence
that placed every decal here: on a **+y-normal** wall the viewer faces SOUTH, so texture-left is EAST —
which is why the **LEFT** arrow is the one that points a player east, down this hall, at the switch.
All six are on +y faces for exactly that reason, and +y is one of the three normals map 1 proved in game.

Six decals, 64x64 at z[32,96] (clear of the floor inlay at z[0,1] and the cyan cornice at z[128,148]):

| Where | What | Face |
|---|---|---|
| power room north wall, x[376,440] | **POWER** | y=-400, faces the arena |
| arena south wall, x[180,244] | arrow EAST | y=-540, at the door mouth |
| hall south wall, x[300,364] | arrow EAST | just past the door |
| hall south wall, x[760,824] | arrow EAST | |
| hall south wall, x[1120,1184] | arrow EAST | |
| hall south wall, x[1448,1512] | **POWER** | the switch is at x=1613 |

Two outside the door and four in the hall, exactly as asked. The base teddy bear sits at x=1614 on the
same wall and the last decal ends at 1512, clear of it. This continues the v16.11 floor trace, which
exists for the same Workshop complaint: *"having a difficult time finding the power. Where is it?"*
