## 2026-09-13 (v18.99) — THE TWO AMMO DROPS THE LIGHTNING STAFF IGNORED

User: *"We have a few issues on max ammo, the lightning staff. Reload needs to reset, or the lightning
staff clip needs to reset. And then on infinite ammo, it should be able to shoot without needing to
reload."*

**One cause behind both.** The lightning staff's forced reload (every `TOD_MAGE_BOLT_SHOTS_PER_RELOAD`
20 shots, v18.77) is not an ammo state. It is a counter this module keeps (`tod_mage_bolt_shots`) plus
a clip `staff_ammo_watch` pins to **0** while `tod_mage_bolt_reload_due` stands. Every ammo powerup in
the game works by writing ammo or by not deducting it, so **neither drop could see this staff's debt** —
and the mage was the one class in the map for whom a Max Ammo did nothing at all.

- **MAX AMMO RESETS IT** (`max_ammo`, `_tod_mage_elements.gsc`). `bolt_reload_reset()` plus an immediate
  top-up of the held staff's clip, and both sit **above** the ARCHMAGE gate: that card buys the mana
  fill, not the right to have your ammo back. Never written while `IsReloading()` — writing a clip
  mid-reload can finish or cancel it (the v18.71 rule at `staff_ammo_watch`).
- **INFINITE AMMO SUSPENDS IT** (new `bolt_reload_suspended()`). While the drop holds, a shot does not
  count, any standing debt is **wiped**, and `staff_clip_target` never returns 0 — so a reload owed at
  the moment the drop lands is lifted within the watcher's 0.25 s, mid-debt, with no reload. When it
  ends the player gets a fresh 20, not the reload they had stopped owing. It reads the same
  `level.zombie_vars[ "zombie_powerup_infiniteammo_on" ]` the slasher's THOR cooldown reads, guarded
  the same way: no `#using`, and no second copy of the powerup's lifetime to keep in step.

**A MOCK TIGHTER THAN THE MACRO FAILED A CORRECT FIX.** `test_mage_bolt_reload.js` modelled `IS_TRUE`
as `v === true`, but `shared.gsh:251` is `( isdefined( __a ) && __a )` and the stock powerup stores the
**integer** 1 (`_zm_powerup_infiniteammo.gsc:120`) — so the first run of a correct implementation went
red. The mock now models the macro and three controls pin it (1 true, 0 false, undefined false). It
could as easily have passed a broken one: a mock that is stricter than the engine is not "safe".

Tests: `test_mage_bolt_reload.js` (+ the drop landing mid-debt, 60 shots under it owing nothing, a full
count after it ends, the other staffs unaffected), `test_mage_max_ammo.js` (+ reset without the card, no
write mid-reload, non-mage and gun-in-hand untouched — its harness runs the real `max_ammo` body, so it
needed the new calls), `test_mage_reload_mana.js` (the clip helper's new consult). Arity green.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.94) — THE RED DOT COMES OFF THREE PACK-A-PUNCHED GUNS, AND THE ADS POSE COMES WITH IT

User:

> *"Is it possible to remove the red dot sight from the RPD and the MP7 and MP5? Pap
> version has the sight. Without any regressions?"* … *"lets make sure doesnt cause
> issues with aiming down now that we removed"*

### Two facts the request needed before it could be answered

**1. The base guns never had a sight.** On every Skye port in this map the BASE form
ships iron sights and no optic at all; it is the `_up` half that bolts a reflex onto
`tag_reflex` / `tag_aimpoint`. So this was always an edit to three PaP forms, and the
guns a player carries before the machine were never involved. Confirmed by reading the
emitted `tod_weapon_twins.gdt`, not the ports — `t9_mp5_h0` has an empty
`attachViewModel1` and `t9_mp5_up_h0` has `vm_t9_reflex_snappoint_hip_scope`.

**2. There is no RPD in this map.** Nothing named RPD ships — a `skye_t9_rpd.gdt` exists
in the SHARED tools root, but it belongs to map 1. The two belt-fed LMGs here are the
**Stoner 63** (heavy T1) and the **HK21** (heavy T2), and BOTH of their PaP forms carry a
dot, so the name could not be resolved from the repo. Asked; the user meant the **HK21**.
The Stoner 63 keeps its quickdot deliberately — three guns were named, three guns moved.

### AND IT IS TWO EDITS, NOT ONE — the whole substance of "without any regressions"

The `_up` forms also swap in the port's **optic-specific ADS animations**
(`am_t9_mp5_snappoint_ads_up`, `am_t6_mp7_reflex_ads_up`, `am_t5_hk21_reflex_ads_up`),
which raise the gun to the **optic's** eye height rather than the iron sights'. Delete the
attachment and keep those anims and the player aims down an empty rail with the irons
sitting below the eye line — **a worse gun than either state, and it would have looked
perfectly correct in every screenshot of the hip pose**, which is exactly why this class
of change ships broken. The anims go back to the port's own non-optic pair, which the BASE
form of the same gun already uses and already packs, so PaP now aims exactly like base.

Proven by field comparison rather than by argument: after the change, **every**
ADS/zoom/reticle/scope field on the three PaP guns matches its base form except
`adsTransIn/OutTime` (×0.75) and the eight gun/view kick values (×0.75) — the PaP
handling and recoil bonuses, which are supposed to differ. No `adsZoomFov` difference,
no `adsOverlayReticle` (all `none`), and a regex for
`reflex|snappoint|quickdot|aimpoint|scope_rail` over every field of all ten changed assets
returns **zero hits**.

### What changed, exactly

`noOptic()` in `tools/gen_tod_twins.js`, written through the existing per-form `str`
hook so it lands AFTER every ladder scale and no scale can undo it. Ten weapon assets:
`t9_mp5_up_h0..h3`, `t6_mp7_up_h0..h4`, `t5_hk21_up_b`. Per gun it clears attach slots 1
and 2 (hip optic / ADS optic), their tags and offsets, and restores `adsUpAnim` /
`adsDownAnim`. The **HK21 additionally drops `attachWorldModel4`** — the world-model
scope rail the optic was mounted on; clearing only the optic would have left an empty
rail standing on the third-person and dropped gun.

Everything else that makes these forms Pack-a-Punched is untouched: extended mag, heavy
barrel and stock, PaP camo, damage, reload anims, upgraded muzzle flash. A generated-GDT
field diff confirms **exactly 10 assets changed and nothing else** — 247 entries before
and after, none added, none removed.

**Ledger-neutral: 207 generated + 28 fixed = 235 against the guard 235**, weapon-cost
table 238/240 unchanged, `tod_twins.zpkg` and `zm_levelcommon_weapons.csv` byte-identical
to the last build's deployed copies (only the `.gdt` moved). The reflex xmodels simply
stop being referenced by these three guns; `vm_t9_reflex_quickdot_*` still ships for the
MAC-10 and the Stoner 63. Generator double-run is byte-identical.

**GDT change = FULL build.** What cannot be proven here is how the irons *look* on the
three PaP models — that is a native check.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.88) — SCAVENGER: the whole ladder takes another 0.2 off, ceiling included

User, minutes after v18.86 landed:

> *"Lets shift all by another 0.2"*

**ALL**, which is the part that separates this from the pass before it. v18.86 moved the
first three rungs and deliberately pinned Lv4/5/6; this one takes 0.2 kills off every
rung, so the assault capstone moves for the first time since v16.42.

| Lv | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 (assault) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v16.42 | 4.0 | 3.0 | 2.4 | 2.0 | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| v18.86 | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.2 | 2.0 | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| **v18.88** | **2.8** | **2.3** | **2.0** | **1.8** | **1.6** | **1.4** |

Rounds banked per kill: 0.36 / 0.43 / 0.50 / 0.56 / 0.63 / **0.71**.
`TOD_SCAV_KILLS10_*` (tenths) = 28 / 23 / 20 / 18 / 16 / 14.

### Why the shape did not need re-deriving

A uniform shift **cannot** change the step table — subtract a constant from every rung
and the gaps are identical. So the diminishing-step rule v16.40 was written to enforce
(0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2, never growing) came through this retune untouched, without
anybody re-checking it. Worth writing down, because the rule is a property of the
DIFFERENCES, not the values, and the tempting-looking edit — smoothing the three equal
0.2 steps at the top — is precisely the accelerating ladder v16.40 killed.

**The new note at the defines names the floor**, because a third shift is where this
stops being free: Lv6 is 1.4 kills, and no rung may reach 1.0. A round per kill is the
pre-v16.40 Lv5 — effectively infinite ammo whenever a kill costs a round or two — and it
is the exact failure that pass existed to remove. At that point a shift has to become a
re-shape, and the file says so now instead of leaving the next session to rediscover it.

DARK (`×0.6` on the kills you need) follows for free: Lv1 2.8 → 1.6 kills, the assault
capstone 1.4 → 0.8, i.e. a round on nearly every kill at the very top of a dark build.
Note the GSC truncates (`int()` on tenths) where the pause menu's dark row prints the
exact product — a ≤0.1-kill display gap that predates both of today's passes.

Everything structural is where it was: ONE round per shot (the same-frame latch plus the
re-arm-one-kill-short rule in `on_class_gun_kill`), class-primary kills only, capped by
`maxAmmo`, a refund and never a multiplier.

### Lockstep

Same five copies as v18.86, all moved together: the `TOD_SCAV_KILLS10_L1..L6` defines and
`scav_kills10()`'s header, the `add_domain` desc (the card's own text), `DOMAIN[8].desc`
and **both** `SCAV_KPR` tables in `tod_upgrade.lua` (the live pause row and the DARK copy
300 lines below it), and the `docs/armory.html` SCAVENGER row (`lad`, `extra`, `tune`,
`note`). No card re-bake — the art carries no numbers.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.87) — THE SKY: Tower II's quality pass ported, plus an atmosphere pass

User: *"our sky box generator for our tower of doom 2 map found an improvement to make to
enhance the background image. Can we learn from what they did and apply the enhancement to
our cybercity background and on top of that make it even more atmospheric ... more depth
and more cyber type theme art. A deeper dark more detailed sky. People find it beautiful
and I want to expand on that."*

Tower II's `gen_hb_sky.js` is this map's sky pipeline with a different picture; its v0.5–v0.7
passes (its docs/63) changed how the drawing becomes pixels, not what is drawn. All of it is
in `tools/gen_tod_sky.js` now, and the picture grew an atmosphere on top. Full record:
`docs/104_cybercity_sky.md` §4g.

### Ported (same picture, cleaner pixels)
- Painted at **16384×8192** (`--ss 2`) and resolved to the shipped 8192×4096 with a
  wrap-aware **Lanczos-2** — true anti-aliasing on every neon edge, rail, trail and star.
- Noise tables read with **Catmull-Rom** (no linear facets in the gradients).
- **Three clamped unsharp passes** after the resolve (3×3 @0.38, 3×3 @0.45, 5×5 @0.25,
  clamped 0.6..1.5×), Tower II's tuning against the simulated in-game view; the same view
  is written here as `docs/sky_preview/night_ingame_*.png` (1080p, cg_fov 65 → 80.7°,
  0.96 texel/px, bilinear) — **that is the image to judge sharpness on.**
- The EXR is written **directly as half floats** by our own ZIP16 writer — the 12-bit
  LUT → 16-bit PNG → ffmpeg chain banded the dark sky; no ffmpeg in the shipped path.
- **`SKY_GAIN` is SOLVED** for `--target-score 0.478` (the v17.82 light budget) instead of
  hand-held; `--gain` pins it; a solve outside 0.012..0.048 throws. It landed at 0.0175
  (the new picture is ~37% brighter at gain parity, so the gain came down to hold the
  world's lighting exactly where it was).
- Every stage is an IIFE (a top-level function past V8's bytecode limit ran every hot loop
  2–30× slow on Tower II).
- Two scales kept apart: `PXO` (shipped pixel: counts, gates) vs `PX` (render pixel:
  radii); the near-city size gate keyed on `W` and made the 2048 preview draw a
  DIFFERENT city than the ship — it keys on `OW` now.
- **Per-lot RNG seeding**: each lattice lot and far-ring slot seeds its own stream from
  its index, so a composition-lane change re-rolls only the lots inside it (before, fixing
  one covered planet uncovered another — seen live, rust → maelstrom). Lanes test a box's
  angular EXTENT, not just its centre. One-time re-roll of the city relative to v17.87.

### Added
- **GROUND MIST** — a lit fog bank on the city plane (`veil()`, `MIST_TOP` 300,
  `MIST_D` 900): tower feet, the far grid and the reflections dissolve into violet-pink
  haze carrying the glow dome's colour per bearing. Four density steps before it read.
- **HAZE STRATA** — two thin smog layers hanging between the towers (z 560 / 1180),
  crossed once by a ray to anything behind them; patchy in world XY. The strongest depth
  cue in the picture; also drawn against the sky.
- **MOON SHAFTS** — crepuscular rays round the moon through the low deck's gaps.
- **THE STORM** — a cell in the low deck 2.55 rad round from the moon, el 16°, lit from
  inside, with ONE branching bolt (a random walk pulled back to its axis) from the cloud
  base to the far ring; its own lane keeps the skyline low under it.
- **TWO AIRSHIPS** — dark hulls, neon rim, ribs, fins, a lit gondola, a holo billboard on
  the flank, running lights; one close overhead crossing the cyan ring highway, one high
  and far. Depth-tested against the towers.
- **THE ORBITAL TETHER** — an anchor megastructure in the far ring at 19,000, a cable
  toward the zenith with climber lights, a STATION at 47° (hub, lit ring, arms).
- **MEGA-BILLBOARDS** on 40% of far-ring mega-towers (holo glyph walls); signs are
  lights now and carry on `lightFog`, not surface fog.
- **DEEPER DARK** — zenith / high / mid levels ~15% down (the gain solve holds the world
  light, so the lights gain contrast); fine nebula grain from a new `NOISE_D` table.
- New previews `night_view_{tether,station,storm,ship_a,ship_b,mist}.png`;
  `TOD_SKY_PREVIEW_DIR`; `TOD_SKY_SKIP` gained `mist,strata,shafts,storm,ships,tether`.

### 16384x8192 tried and REFUSED (same night)
User: *"I don't mind that size tradeoff."* A 16384x8192 sky was rendered (the approved picture
at 2x the pixels, 139 MB EXR) and the linker refused it — `(image ...exr) unsupported size.`
then `image 'i_skybox_tod_cybercity' is missing` — so the build failed and the sky was
re-rendered at 8192 and rebuilt. 8192x4096 is the converter's ceiling; `--width 16384` now
throws in the generator. At 1080p the 8192 sky is already 1 texel per pixel, so this pass is
the sharpness ceiling; only 1440p/4K would have gained. docs/104 §4g records it.

### The size pass no longer halves the sky
The 2026-09-10 size pass (docs/129 item 9) had shipped the sky as a 4096×2048 2:1
average, and its build gate (`optimize_tod_assets.py --verify`) would have refused a
re-rendered EXR as a "later edit". The sharpness this pass buys is the 0.96 texel/px an
8192 texture gives at 1080p, so the sky ships at 8192 again: new mode
`python tools/optimize_tod_assets.py --retire sky` dropped the two sky rows from the pass
ledger (recorded in `state.json` `revisions`; recovery copies kept; `--verify` reports 260).
Cost ≈ 25 MB of download on a ~2.1 GB item. docs/129 carries the addendum.

## 2026-09-13 (v18.86) — SCAVENGER: the front of the ladder shifts up, the top does not

User:

> *"We need to scale up the scavenger upgrade a little bit ... early on it's, like, almost
> not noticeable, and we don't really want it to be there. But we also don't want it to be
> super, super OP when it's maxed out. So I think we need to shift over the earlier tiers
> ... at least noticeable even on tier one, not super noticeable, but more noticeable."*

Two instructions pulling opposite ways, and the shape of the fix falls straight out of
them: **move the bottom rungs, do not touch the top one.** The domain's ceiling is the
number every other ammo-economy knob in the map has been balanced against since v16.40 —
BULLET FEED, RUN AND GUN's free shots, the crate prices, the `_tod_ammo_crate` header's
whole argument about round ~40 sustain. Raising it would have been a re-tune of all of
them. Raising the first three rungs re-tunes nothing except how long a fresh card takes
to feel like a card.

### The ladder

Kills per refunded reserve round, `TOD_SCAV_KILLS10_*` (tenths, so the bank stays
integer — 1 per 2.5 is not a whole percent):

| Lv | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 (assault) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v16.42 | 4.0 | 3.0 | 2.4 | 2.0 | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| **v18.86** | **3.0** | **2.5** | **2.2** | 2.0 | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| rate change | **+33%** | **+20%** | **+9%** | — | — | — |

Lv1 now pays exactly what Lv2 used to. Rounds banked per kill go 0.33 / 0.40 / 0.45 /
0.50 / 0.56 / 0.63, and the **diminishing-step rule that v16.40 was written to enforce
still holds** — steps in kills 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2, never growing. The three
equal 0.2 steps at the top are not a bug to smooth out; they ARE the v16.40 nerf, and a
comment at the defines now says so, because "the steps should keep shrinking" is exactly
the tidy-looking edit that would quietly restore the accelerating ladder that pass killed.

Nothing else about the domain moved: still ONE round per shot (the same-frame latch and
the re-arm-one-kill-short rule in `on_class_gun_kill`), still class-primary only, still
capped by `maxAmmo`, still a refund rather than a multiplier. DARK (`×0.6` on the kills
you need) rides the new numbers for free: Lv1 3.0 → 1.8 kills.

### Lockstep — five places, four of them prose

The GSC constant is the only truth; everything else is a copy that lies if it is left
behind. All updated in this pass:

- `TOD_SCAV_KILLS10_L1/L2/L3` 40/30/24 → **30/25/22** (`_tod_upgrades.gsc`), the one
  reader being `scav_kills10()`.
- the `add_domain( "reserve", ... )` desc string — **this is the card's own text**.
- `tod_upgrade.lua` `DOMAIN[8].desc` (the same string, duplicated for the pause menu).
- `tod_upgrade.lua` `DETAIL[8]`'s `SCAV_KPR` table — the live pause-menu row, *"1 reserve
  round per N kills"* at the player's current level — **and the DARK `DETAIL[8]` copy of
  the same table 300 lines below it.** Two tables, one ladder; the second is the one a
  grep for the domain name does not find.
- `docs/armory.html` SCAVENGER row: `lad`, the banked-per-kill `extra`, `tune`, `note`.

**No card re-bake.** The SCAVENGER art carries no numbers (docs/33 audit; user 2026-09-02
*"our asset is generic enough"*, restated for this pass), so the three baked rarities and
the pause plate stay valid — which is the whole reason this domain can be retuned in a
`-GscOnly`.

Gates: `verify_armory_constants` (272 constants, 0 mismatch), `verify_armory_domains`
(44 domains, ladder lengths clean), `verify_armory_render`, `lint_tod_lua` (49 files, the
pause-row width check included) and `lint_tod_arity` all pass.

## 2026-09-11 (v18.85) — THREE STRINGS PLAYERS READ THE OTHER WAY

User, on the only copy in the map that reliably confuses people:

> *"The fire rate card ... says truly fires faster. We don't need the word truly there."*
> *"It says hold the crown, but that confuses people. They think they need to hold
> something ... really, they are just defending for a certain amount of time."*
> *"There's a card for perk bottles. It says, like, one perk per level. That's unclear
> because people think that it's per floor level."*

Three unrelated strings, one shared failure: each is precise, and each has a **second
reading this map's own vocabulary makes available**. No behaviour changed anywhere.

### FIRE RATE — TRULY was arguing with a retired domain

`TRULY fires faster` was drawing a contrast with **ECHO ROUNDS** (id 11), the proc that
fired a second bullet instead of raising the rate. ECHO ROUNDS was removed **2026-08-23
(v9.35)**, so for the 19 days since, the word has been distinguishing this card from
nothing a player can see — and an unexplained "truly" reads as a hint that some *other*
card is lying. Gone from the `add_domain` string and `DOMAIN[15].desc`. `DETAIL[15]`
(`-{V}% time between shots` / `MAC-10 only`) was already clean.

**AND THIS ENTRY SAID "v14.11, six weeks" FOR AN AFTERNOON.** The date came from
`tod_upgrade.lua:272` — *"12 REGEN: DOMAIN REMOVED v14.11 (2026-08-30, with
11/22/30/34)"* — which sweeps id 11 into a batch it predates by a week. **The same Lua
file has it right 286 lines further down at `:558`** (*"11 ECHO ROUNDS: domain REMOVED
2026-08-23"*), as does the domain's own `// Was:` block in `_tod_upgrades.gsc`. v14.11
removed REGEN and MOMENTUM. The wrong date reached five live sites — the GSC comment,
the Lua comment, `docs/armory.html`, the `docs/134` brief and this entry — before a
verification pass caught it; all five are corrected, and `:272` is fixed at the source
with a note saying what it cost. **A copy-fix pass shipped the exact defect class it was
written to remove, by trusting a comment instead of the code it described.** When a
retirement date matters, read the domain's own `// Was:` block.

### HOLD THE CROWN — the map spends "hold" on buy prompts

The crown hold-out's status line has said `^3HOLD THE CROWN^7` since v9. HOLD means
*hold out* to anyone fluent in zombies and *press and hold* to everyone else — and this
map says it the second way on **every buy prompt in it**, so players stood on the exfil
pad hunting for the thing to hold. Now:

    ^3DEFEND THE CROWN^7 - survive until extraction arrives

DEFEND has one reading, and the detail line says what the old string never did: this
ends on a **clock**, not on an objective. Still a status line — no `[{+activate}]`
token, so `PromptDefault` hides the footer; the `" - "` splits it into the title band
over one detail line, the grammar every other hint uses. `lint_tod_hints` unchanged at
**96 distinct strings of 190** (one constant swapped for another, no new slot).

`TOD_NOUNS` in `ZMCursorHintNew.lua` carried `"hold the crown"` and now carries
`"defend the crown"` — **and the obvious reason for that is wrong twice over.** First,
`classifyHint`'s last statement returns `DefaultHint` regardless, so a stale noun would
not have misrouted this string; nothing gates the pairing either, verified by reverting
the noun and watching `lint_tod_hints` pass at 96/190, exit 0. Second, `"defend the
crown"` is not even the claimant: the nouns are scanned **in order** and `"extract"` sits
five entries earlier, matching *"extraction"* in the new detail line, so the loop returns
there and never reaches the crown nouns. The pairing stays because the noun tracks the
**title**, which is the half that survives a reword of the detail — drop "extraction"
from the detail and `"defend the crown"` becomes the claimant for real. What the table
buys either way is **claim order**: nouns match at step 3, ahead of the perk-machine and
Pack-a-Punch tests at 4 and 5, so a future reword containing a perk name or the words
*pack* and *punch* is misrouted without a matching noun. **That contract is unguarded** —
CLAUDE.md states it as a rule and no gate enforces it.

And **this was the only hint in the map opening with the word Hold**, which makes
two comments in `PromptDefault.lua` stale: its `hasButton` guard exists so a status line
starting with "Hold" does not lose its first word, and it cited this exact string as the
live example. The guard stays (it defends the grammar); the comments now say the example
is historical. *Players made the same misreading the parser was already being defended
against.*

### PERK SLOTS — "LEVEL" is a word this map cannot spend on card rungs

`+1 PERK SLOT PER LEVEL` is exactly correct and still wrong: **the map has fifty floors**
and a per-player floor high-water that gates class tiers, so "level" already means *floor*
everywhere a player looks. Every other card's `/ Lv` survives because its subject is
obviously a gun stat. This one's subject is a thing the tower also hands out.

Strings now count perks and never say level:

| Where | Now |
|---|---|
| `add_domain( "perkslots" )` | `carry +1 more perk / Lv (base 4, cap 9)` |
| `DOMAIN[40].desc` | `carry one more perk each time` |
| `DETAIL[40].act` | `4 without this upgrade` (was `base 4, +1 per level`) |

`DETAIL[40].eff` (`carry up to {V} perks`) was already the clearest line in the set and
is untouched — it prints the live total, which is the number a player checks against
what they are carrying.

### The cards are the half that needs art — docs/134, requested not delivered

Six re-bakes at the same filenames, zip in Downloads:
`i_tod_card_fire_rate_{regular,super,ultimate}` lose one word to `FIRES FASTER`, and
`i_tod_card_perkslots_{regular,super,ultimate}` take **a different line each** —
`+1 EXTRA PERK` / `+2 EXTRA PERKS` / `+3 EXTRA PERKS`.

**NEITHER `_dark` CARD IS IN THE REQUEST, and the first draft got that wrong.** It asked
for `fire_rate_dark` too, as insurance against a future session zoning a stale bake. The
user caught it — *"I dont think fire rate can be a dark upgrade btw"* — and the block is
structural, not a preference: `set_no_dark( "firerate" )` records it as *"weapon-variant
ladder, +8 registrations, no per-player fire-time call exists"*. FIRE RATE is a TWIN
domain that swaps real gun data, so a dark rung needs eight more weapon registrations
against a ledger at **223/223 with zero headroom**. That kills the insurance argument
outright: the stale PNG can never reach a player, because zoning it would first require
registrations that do not exist. `perkslots_dark` was already excluded (a dark card is not
a rarity, so it has no level count to print). Six files, six prompts.

**That is a deliberate exception to the generic-card-text rule, and it must not be
generalised.** That rule exists because a baked number is falsified by the next retune.
Here there is no rate to retune: a rarity *is* +1/+2/+3 levels, a level *is* +1 perk
(`perk_slot_limit()`), and the **band-honesty clamp** demotes any card that cannot pay
its full rarity — so a card reading ULTIMATE is only ever dealt when it really is about
to grant three. The number is structural, not tuned.

**That proof is only worth anything if the clamp survey is complete, so it was re-run
adversarially.** All **four** shrink sites carry the clamp — `make_option` (:5178),
`guarantee_rarity` (:4991), the overcharge redeal (:5082) and the deferred re-present
after a round takeover (:8648) — and the one documented bypass, `rarity_lock` (:5185,
applied *after* the clamp), is called on exactly two domains, `deadshot` and
`mage_quickhands` (:1853-1854), neither of them this one. The first pass found three of
the four; the conclusion held, but it was resting on an incomplete survey.

`i_tod_card_perkslots_dark.png` is **excluded on purpose**: a dark card is not a rarity,
so it has no level count to print. The FIRE RATE dark card IS included — same one-word
deletion, and both dark PNGs are unzoned/unreachable (`DARK_NONE`), so this is insurance
against a future session zoning a stale bake, not a shipped image.

## 2026-09-11 (v18.84) — THE LIGHTNING STAFF RELOADED TWICE, AND THE GATE SAID IT SHOULD

User: *"There is a bug on auto reload for lightning staff. It forces reload after 15
shots. That should be 20. but the bug is it reloads twice"* — two changes, and only one
of them is the counter.

### The count

`TOD_MAGE_BOLT_SHOTS_PER_RELOAD` **15 -> 20**. Nothing else about the counter moved:
the clip still pins to 0 at the limit, the engine still owns the reload, and ANY
reload start still resets it. `tools/test_mage_bolt_reload.js` asserts the new number.

### The double reload was NOT the counter

All three staffs are `segmentedReload 1` with **`reloadAmmoAdd` 999 against `clipSize`
1000**. A segmented reload repeats until the clip is full, so:

- the OPTIONAL reload starts at the pinned `clipSize - 1` = 999, one segment adds 999,
  clamps full — one animation, which is why this never showed before v18.77;
- the FORCED reload starts EMPTY, one segment adds 999, and the clip is one round shy,
  so the engine runs a **second segment** to top it off. That is the reported
  "reloads twice", and it could only ever happen on the forced reload.

Fix: `reloadAmmoAdd` = `clipSize` = 1000 in `source_data/tod_staff.gdt`, all three
staffs, twins regenerated (generator is idempotent — re-run produced an identical md5).
One segment from either start.

### The gate had the old assumption written into it

`tools/verify_staff_animations.py` asserted `reloadAmmoAdd == clipSize - 1` under the
comment *"one full reload segment"*, and FAILED this build — which is the corroboration,
not an obstacle. That assertion was true when the only reload was the optional one and
the clip always started one short; **the forced empty-clip reload arrived in v18.77 and
nobody revisited the gate that had encoded the old start state.** A gate is a statement
about the world at the time it was written. Now asserts `== clipSize`, with the reason
at the assertion.

### Readouts

"every 15 shots" -> 20 in the staged Workshop notes (both files), `docs/armory.html`
prose AND its tune row (`verify_armory_constants` 272/272), and the CLAUDE.md brief.

## 2026-09-11 (v18.83 PUBLISH) — SHIP STATE, AND A CANDIDATE THAT WAS OVERTAKEN MID-FLIGHT

User: *"Okay recent changes made. Can you prepare a full publish and rewrite the
changelog. Tested and everything is good"*, then *"Are we good for full publish?"* —
and the honest answer to the second question was NO, which is the whole point of
re-running the checks instead of quoting the previous build's result.

### What the re-check found

A v18.82 publish build passed at 23:05:21 (FF 176,322,176 bytes, payload 2,119,291,579
bytes / 48 files, `-CleanPak` + twelve languages, every gate green). **Then a peer
session built v18.83 at 23:44:40 on top of it** — the UI element-pool cleanup for the
round-19 crash report. Three consequences, none visible from the 23:05 result:

- `patch_notes check` FAILED on purpose: the staged cutoff was the v18.82 publish
  header and the CHANGELOG top was v18.83. Working as designed.
- The deployed `.ff` is the peer's 23:44 build, so the 23:05 payload figure no longer
  described what is on disk.
- **The pack had grown, though by less than first claimed — see the correction below.**
  `tools/xpak_report.js` after the peer build: 1,339,326,464 bytes, 60.4 MB of holes in
  1,743 gaps, 2 sun-shadow trees. Eleven of the twelve language `.ff`s were also still
  the 23:01–23:05 set, built from a source revision that predates v18.83 — that part
  stands on its own and is reason enough to rebuild.

**CORRECTION, MEASURED AFTER THIS BUILD (and the reason to measure rather than infer).**
The line above was first written as "60 MB of nothing in every player's download",
reading the whole hole figure and the second shadow tree as the peer build's residue.
A fresh `-Publish` then produced **1,330,642,944 bytes, 52.1 MB of holes in 1,738 gaps,
and STILL 2 sun-shadow trees**. So two trees and ~52 MB of holes are what a CLEAN
publish pack looks like here — neither is peer residue, and the tree count is not the
stale-build detector it was used as. The peer build's actual cost was the delta:
**8.7 MB of file size, 8.3 MB of it holes.** Worth reclaiming with a rebuild that was
happening anyway for the language `.ff`s; not the 60 MB first reported. The user was
told the 60 MB figure in the same breath as the question "are we good to publish", so
the corrected number goes in front of them too. docs/86's own rule applies to this
file as much as to the pack: answer a size question with the report, not with a
reading of one field in it.

**The lesson, and it generalises past this repo's ledger:** a publish result is a
statement about a tree at an instant, and a peer build silently invalidates it. "Are we
good to publish?" is re-run, never recalled — deployed flags, repo-vs-deployed diff,
nothing newer than the `.ff`, the notes gate, AND the pack's own index.

## 2026-09-10 (v18.82) — THE PACK-A-PUNCH TIER ICONS, ROUND 4: THE CHEVRON STACK

User, on seeing round 3 in game with a HUD screenshot: *"Our pap icon looks like ass in
game. But both blink and healing aura look great. Can we zip up an asset request with
those as quality example and get better pap icons? Creative and obvious to the player
what tier pap they are."*

`i_tod_hud_pap_1|2|3` replaced over the same three names — zero wiring. Brief, reference
boards and the acceptance record are `docs/131_pap_tier_icons_art_prompt.md`; the
measurement tool is the new `tools/gen_pap_icon_ref.js`.

### Three rounds had already failed, so the brief changed the MECHANISM, not the subject

docs/125 shipped a capsule with bolts (v17.60), then a pistol with chevrons, then a fist
with a lightning bolt — and docs/125 had itself diagnosed round 1 as reading like *"a
bullet, a rocket or a gravestone"*. Measuring the shipped set against the two offhand
icons on the SAME HUD row, which the user likes, found the real fault:

| | blink | heal | GOOD mean | pap 1..3 | BAD mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ink coverage | 44.2% | 47.5% | 45.9% | 39.3 / 42.4 / 48.1% | 43.3% |
| **bright saturated px** | 20.2% | 38.3% | **29.3%** | 7.2 / 9.2 / 10.7% | **9.0%** |
| tones >=2% of ink | 5 | 5 | 5.0 | 4 / 4 / 4 | 4.0 |

**It was never a size problem, and that mattered most.** The PaP glyph box is 26x26
canvas units (`AetheriumLoadout.lua:1443`) against the offhand icons' 24x24 (:1346) — the
badge already got MORE room than the icons beating it, and ink coverage was effectively
equal. The gap was **colour: 9.0% saturated against 29.3%**, a factor of 3.3. Plus two
half-scale objects sharing one cell, and a tier signal that was a COUNTING task (two small
chevrons versus three, in about 8 px) when the game already prints the level as a digit
beside the glyph.

For calibration on how badly the silhouette read: reviewing round 3 at FOUR TIMES size,
studying it deliberately, this session identified the fist as *"a gun"* and wrote it down.

**A hypothesis tested and REFUTED, recorded so it is not re-derived:** that the good icons
win by being one connected shape, measurable as largest connected ink blob. All five score
100% and a single blob — the fist and its chevron badge touch. Right about the composition,
wrong about the metric.

### What shipped

One flat geometric chevron stack per tier, filling the cell, each stack sized so the group
occupies the same area — so tier reads as shape AND density, not as something to count —
on a three-step slice of the generator's own `DISTRICTS` ladder, which players learn over a
fifty-floor climb:

| tier | hue | hex | shadow step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cyan | `#3FD8E8` | `#1F929E` |
| 2 | gold | `#F5C542` | `#A77C21` |
| 3 | red | `#F0524B` | `#A32D28` |

Tier 1's cyan matches the cyan rule already on the PaP plate. Green is deliberately unused:
it is the healing aura's identity on this same row. No numeral is baked in.

Measured after install: **saturated ink 62.1 / 50.0 / 37.8%** (gate >=20%, bar 29.3%), ink
coverage 49.9% on all three (gate 44-50%), 3 tones (gate <=5), bounding box 80.7% (gate

acceptance test the brief set — and the three tiers are instantly distinguishable at true
size. A "thinnest horizontal run = 1 px" reading is a DIAGONAL ARTIFACT and not a
violation of the 8-px rule; round 3 scored 2 px for the same reason and heal scores 26 px
only because it has no diagonal. Do not chase it.

## 2026-09-10 - Restore elites after same-frame upgrade pauses

A maxed player could enter a round upgrade event through its remaining dark
pool, then receive no hand because the ordinary pool was empty and the dark
card was not guaranteed. The world pause began and ended in the same frame.
It still wrote a 0.05 animation rate onto live elites, but their restore watcher
only checked every 250 ms and required having observed the pause. The normal
zombie speed sweep skips those custom-speed elites, so they stayed almost
motionless with a valid target and path. Dev mode runs this event every round;
normal mode runs it every fourth round.

Native pre-fix evidence: run 20260910_224229_229_a18a10ca, both pause edges at
69550 ms, and hound 54's matching rate-write timestamp immediately before a
25-second stall. Earlier hound 30's 50.55-second stationary window ended in an
explicit watchdog relocation, not demonstrated locomotion recovery. Generic
entity rate=1 / ASM status=running did not reveal the missed rate restoration.

The freeze writer now latches a pending restore on elites with a known base
rate. Their existing watcher consumes it when the pause ends even if it missed
the pulse. Entrance ownership and active pauses retain precedence; unexpired
elite slow effects are preserved. No targets, paths, spawn positions or geometry
changed. The new actual-function test reproduces the old condition leaving
0.05 indefinitely, then passes short/long/repeated pauses, Fury park/unpark,
entrances, live/expired slows and diagnostic release stamps. It gates builds.

The dev recorder now reports exact pause edges, per-actor writes and restores,
including PAUSE_RESTORE missed_edge=1. All five elite families ran the diagnostic
queries in native build e without a script exception in the captured interval.
An attempted shared requested-state hook recorded no calls and was removed;
the native completion-status getter remains. See docs/131 for full evidence
and limitations; earlier first-hall path errors and stock Fury assertions remain
separate observations, not proof of another specific cause.

The initial unwrapped PrintLn fatal and missing devblock launch flag were
mistakes in this diagnostic work. Corrected wrapper, prefix assembly outside
the devblock, and scr_mod_enable_devblock 1 are natively verified. Both launchers
preserve old logs. The separate Mage undefined/lightning comparison guard also
ships; its bolt test now models the native error boundary and passes.

`docs/132_native_game_verification.md`. Persistent focus/screenshot/input helpers
under tools handle Steam's custom-arguments confirmation with foreground/DPI
checks. They were used successfully to start this final verification match.

BBCode block also went: row #33 records that upload.

**THE FAILURE MODE, because a gate cannot catch it:** `check` compares the pending row's
cutoff against the CHANGELOG and `stage` overwrites the pending row in place, so a row
that OUTLIVES its own upload silently re-points the window at a cutoff that is already
public — and every later `window` run then hands back work players have already read.
Nothing in the repo is evidence either way; the only witness is the live Workshop page.
Before writing notes, reconcile the pasted/fetched Workshop text against the ledger's
last UPLOADED row, not against its pending one.

### The notes

**Rewritten SHORT AND PLAIN the same session** (user: *"Lets reduce any jargon and
make it super simple for players to read and understand what changed. This is what we
should do moving forwards. We dont need a billion characters for change notes"*). The
first draft was the old house style — 35 bullets, 5,600 characters, paragraph-long
entries explaining how and why. The section now runs **30 bullets / 2,056 characters**,
median bullet 60 characters, longest 165, covering the same 16-entry window plus the
peer session's v18.81 staff art. **The rule is mechanical, not a good intention:**
`MAX_BULLET` 200 in `tools/patch_notes.js`, checked in `validateNotes`, so `stage` and
`check` both refuse a longer bullet and print the offenders — negative control run, a
211-character bullet is rejected. `window` now prints the rule at the top of every
generated window, and CLAUDE.md's publish flow carries it. Sections before Sep 10 2026
are the older style and are left exactly as they went out.

`Update — Sep 10 (v18.80)`, 35 bullets, netted over the 16-entry window (v18.73 →
v18.80). Dropped as netting to nothing: the floor-10 Sky Lounge (built and reverted
inside the window), the packed-staff-name HUD error (caused by a change inside the
window), and every build / test-session / tooling entry. Numbers that moved twice read
as their final value with the first cut named where players feel both (the staffs took
an across-the-board 15% in v18.73 and ice/fire/lightning took a second pass in v18.77 —
both are stated). No pending row was staged: staging happens with the publish build, so
the ledger never carries a promise the Workshop has not been given.

| `TOD_MAGE_LIGHTNING_VS_PANZER` (the Panzer, the Warden King included) | 5.60 | **4.76** | -15% (user, same day: "Lightning needs 15% nerf against panzers") |

Net ice against its own beasts: 2.85 x 0.68 = 1.94 per missile (was 2.28), at
0.9 of the old cadence — about -23% DPS. Three missiles that pierce a horde is
why the flat cut lands everywhere rather than on one lane.

### Lightning: an invisible counter forces a reload every 15 shots

`TOD_MAGE_BOLT_SHOTS_PER_RELOAD 15`. The staffs pin their clip one round short
so a reload is always OPTIONAL (`staff_ammo_watch`); the lightning staff now
counts `weapon_fired` (`bolt_count_shot`, q0 and q1 on one counter) and at 15
sets `tod_mage_bolt_reload_due`, empties the clip on the spot and the watcher's
pin (`staff_clip_target`) becomes ZERO. The engine refuses to fire an empty
clip and its own trigger-pull auto-reload takes over — no scripted animation,
no forced switch, the reserve is still refilled so ammo stays unlimited.
`reload_start` — ANY staff, ANY reload, finished or interrupted (the user's
rule: "any reload will reset") — resets the count and lifts the pin; a fresh
body starts at zero. Fire and ice never count and are never pinned to zero.
The dry-fire alias on the staffs is the unzoned donor one, so the empty pull
is silent; the reload animation is the tell.

### The armory gets a BALANCE tab (user: "I need armory completely updated. Think about what data I need to properly balance. Lots of classes have stacking abilities")

`docs/armory.html` gains a thirteenth tab, **Balance**, built from four
code-read extractions (enemy health, the gun chain, the mage chain, the
damage-taken chain) rather than from the page's own prose. It is a live
workbench: controls for round, party, rampage, trial tier, card build (fresh /
mid / maxed / maxed+dark), headshot share, sustained-vs-burst, ARCHMAGE uptime,
fire charge and ice missiles on target; then four computed tables — enemy
health by round for all seven enemy kinds (stock curve × party × rampage;
bosses compounding from their anchors × co-op × rampage × trial × elite; the
sprinter as a promoted zombie with its ⅓ armour; the flat King), DPS for every
class × tier × PaP 0–III against every enemy with the whole stacking chain in
code order (the additive card bracket, LOC_NORM head ×3, Panzer body/face
scaling, melee taxes, sprinter armour, reload folding; the mage's matchup table
with the tier step, card ladders, nerfs, script PaP and uptime-weighted
ARCHMAGE), time-to-kill at the chosen round for PaP I and PaP III, and
effective HP per class build with hits-to-down. Below the tables the stacking
rules are written out in code order, and every constant the tab reads is
listed in `tune:` strings — `verify_armory_constants` now checks **272**
constants (198 before) and passes; `verify_armory_render` draws all 13
panels. Assumptions the game decides at runtime (headshot share, uptime, how
many of the three ice missiles land, the 50-damage zombie swing) are controls
or labelled as assumptions, never hidden. The same pass corrected the last
stale figures the 2026-09-10 sweep found (HEALING AURA 10–15 HP/s ×0.50,
ARCHMAGE ×1.30–2.20, ice 3.352 / 2.36 / 1.00, BLINK 4–8 s, the STAFFS ice
row, `MAGE_MU.panzer` 5.60). Republished to the Armory artifact.

## 2026-09-10 (v18.76) — SEVEN PLAYER-REPORT FIXES AND THE FIVE MAGE DARK CARDS

### 2 · No elite behind an unbought door — `_tod_bosses::door_frontier_z`

The v18.9 finding, left out of that pass as its one regression risk: lap zone
volumes overhang the next lap by 200 units, so the sealed flight above an
unbought door reads as an ENABLED zone to `get_zone_from_position`, and
`pick_spawn_point`'s zone gate let an elite land where nobody could reach it.
The doors are now the authority: the GENERATED door table puts door n's org 40
above lap n's floor, so any candidate whose feet are above the LOWEST unbought
door's floor (+4, so the landing itself stays legal and the first 12-high tread
past the slab does not) is behind it. Walks `enter_lap1..50` then `enter_roof`
bottom-up, stops at the first shut flag, spawns at most ONE door-info struct,
runs once per pick BEFORE the budgeted zone checks. TOWER ONLY (the spire is
boxed by `in_spire` / `trial_box`; its doors are another chain). A flag stock
has not initialised reads as NO frontier — a missing reading must never empty
the pick. New `#using` of the generated leaf `_tod_door_data`; no cycle.

### 3 · The King's flame: the RECORD was wrong, not the fight

The sweep repeated CLAUDE.md's line that his flame is "doubled only in
appearance". `king_setup` has replaced the stock 200x50x25 `trigger_box` with a
400x100x50 one on the same tag since v17.70 (this changelog, that entry), and
the pack's burn loop reads `self.flameTrigger` every tick, so the hurt box IS
the doubled one. The brief's paragraph is corrected; no code change.

### 4 · ARCHMAGE ends with the body and with the class — `demigod_guard`

`demigod_run` ended only on disconnect, so dying or re-drafting at the base
station mid-form left `tod_mage_demigod_speed` and the sprint-fire grant on the
next body / the new class until the timer ran out. An `endon` would be no
better (endon is not cleanup), so a guard thread waits on death or
`tod_mage_disarm`, kills the timer loop through its own restart notify and runs
the ONE teardown, `demigod_end( sound )` — the timer's end calls it with the
stance-off cue, the guard without (a corpse or a fresh Heavy should not hear
the mage's stance drop).

### 6 · The lethal tile dims for the aura's own lock — `heal_lock_tell`

`cast_heal` arms a 5 s lock (the aura's duration) that refused a second cast
while the tile still showed 2-3 charges. `abil_send` now clamps the count to 0
while `ready( "mage_heal" )` is false, and `heal_lock_tell` pushes at the cast
and again when the lock lifts; both go through the same gate so the change-gate
sees a real change each way. Blink is untouched.

### 7 · Staff raise / putaway / pickup foley the player can hear

The v18.70 audit: every non-fire staff sound field named the elemental-bow
donor's `fly_shoulder_*` aliases, which no sound table this map ships defines.

and `_pickup_plr` on the shipped `staff_first_raise.wav` (0.98 s under the
0.9 s raise), `_putaway_plr` on `staff_reload_4.wav` (0.28 s) — set on the
three source staffs (`raiseSoundPlayer` / `putawaySoundPlayer` /
`pickupSoundPlayer`) and regenerated into the q0/q1 twins. Reuse, not
authoring: no new WAV. NPC-side fields, ADS (`fly_generic_*`, the class guns'
own family) and dry-fire (never fires: the clip is pinned) are untouched.
GDT + alias edit = FULL build.

### 8 · A fresh Mage is told something

Before the first ARCHMAGE / HEALING AURA / BLINK card the bar was empty, both
offhand tiles were HIDDEN (`abil_send` sent -1) and every refusal was silent
(2026-09-09). `abil_send` now sends 0 for a locked slot, which the Loadout Lua

arm, only while something is still locked: "MAGE: HEALING AURA, BLINK and
ARCHMAGE unlock with their upgrade cards". Constant string, no hint slot; ends
on disarm so a quick re-draft never prints a mage line on another class.

### 9 · The reload reward is paced — `TOD_MAGE_RELOAD_MANA_WINDOW_MS 10000`

`staff_ammo_watch` pins the clip one short so an optional reload is always
available, and each 1.5 s reload paid 5 mana: ~3.3 mana/s against the 0.8/s
passive tick, a full bar in ~30 s of mashing R. The reward now lands at most

## 2026-09-10 (v18.75) — THE WARDEN KING UNDER RAMPAGE: sprint, rage on every summons, +25% health, a hotter deck

User 2026-09-10: *"The final fight against the warden king on rampage should be
super hard. Can we increase the difficulty of that fight on rampage only by at
least 25%? Maybe we can put the panzer in perma rampage sprint mode? That
usually happens when you break their mask. Faster horde, etc."* — then *"Go
ahead without breaking anything."*

### Rampage barely reached him

`king_setup` writes his health flat after `boss_hp`, so v18.74's elite x1.5
skipped him; only the +3 elite roof (his summons) and the horde x1.2 landed.

### Five levers, every one behind `king_rampage()` (= `level.tod_rampage_on`)

| Lever | Off | Rampage | Site |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health | 10M / player | **12.5M / player** | `king_hp` x `TOD_KING_RAMPAGE_HP_MULT 1.25` |
| Locomotion | run | **sprint, permanently**, flame and claw kept | `king_sprint` — blackboard `_locomotion_speed` = sprint, re-asserted every 1 s |
| Rage | mask-break only | **+ ten seconds of berserk on every summons** | `king_summons` -> stock `MechzBehavior::mechzGoBerserk` |
| Summons | every 18 s: 2 Prot / 1 Reaver / 3 hounds / 2 sprinters | **every 13 s: 3 / 1 / 4 / 2** | `king_summon_secs/_prot/_hound` |
| Deck horde | trial floor 0.12; round speed | **floor 0.10; every ordinary zombie in the summit box +10 rounds of sprint** | `king_spawn_floor` + `king_horde_sprint`; `_tod_endless_rounds` lockstep floor |

* **Why not permanent berserk.** The stock mask-break rage IS sprint locomotion
  for 10 s — and while it holds, `mechzShouldShootFlame` and
  `mechzShouldShootClaw` both return 0. A permanently berserk King is a fast
  melee chaser that never burns anyone, which on an open deck with Blink and
  Healing Aura is easier. So the permanent part is the locomotion only, set on
  the blackboard the way the rage sets it (stock's own end-of-rage restores RUN,
  hence the re-assert), and the real rage rides his summons.
* **The horde stamp is the armored sprinter's own lane** (`tod_zspeed_round_add`,
  a signed ROUND offset the keep-alive sweep applies within 1.5 s). Bosses and
  elites are skipped by the speed path's own triad; a zombie that already
  carries an offset (a sprinter) keeps it.
* **The trickle** is a lockstep pair like the trial floor: `_tod_spire` writes
  it into `zombie_vars` at the seal, `_tod_endless_rounds` re-resolves it at
  each rollover (`level.tod_king_active` gains its first reader).
* **New imports in `_tod_spire`:** stock `scripts\shared\ai\mechz` and
  `scripts\shared\ai\systems\blackboard` — both already pulled by the vendored
  Panzer pack; no zone change. The two blackboard literals are copied rather
  than `#insert`ed so the spire takes no AI-system header; the test checks them
  against the stock header.
* Breaker off: every helper returns the v18.74 value and neither thread starts.

### The scoreboard's owned-upgrades panel was nine rows behind (user: "Make sure scoreboard menu is updated as well. Saw some misses there")

`AetheriumScoreboard.lua` draws the same `CoD.TodOwned` rows as the pause menu
off its own plate ceiling, `TOD_UPG_PLATE_MAX`, commented "LOCKSTEP with
PAUSE_PLATE_MAX" since v15 and checked by nothing. It sat at **47** while the
pause menu went to **56**, so on the scoreboard every Mage row (CHAIN
LIGHTNING, FIRE BLAST, ICE SHATTER, HEALING AURA, ARCHMAGE, BLINK, MYSTICAL
HANDS; ids 49-56) and id 48 drew as a plain Orbitron text label instead of its
baked plate, and a dark Mage row could never show its red plate there
(`CoD.TodDarkPlate` returns nil past the ceiling it is handed). Now 56, and
**`lint_tod_assets.js` GATE D fails any build where the two numbers differ**
(the pair is parsed out of both Lua files; the selftest breaks it in each
direction and requires the catch — 19/19). The same lint's row-capacity check
listed four classes and had never counted the MAGE; it does now (14 rows
against the scoreboard's 18 and the pause menu's 18). The rest of the panel was already
right: it takes `o.dark` into `TodDomainDesc`, prefixes "DARK: " off the third
`TodDarkPlate` return, and reads the server-computed `.safe` badge.

### Bookkeeping

The Workshop description and the session brief still said **twenty-five
million** health per player; the code has been 10M since the King's co-op
curve pass. Both now say ten million, and the description names the rampage
King. `tools/test_king_rampage.js` (new) runs the actual helpers and the
resolver branch off and on, checks the lockstep floor pair and the blackboard
literals, and proves every new lane is gated. `-GscOnly` build; **UNPLAYED**
— the blackboard sprint outside berserk is the one lane with no native run.

## 2026-09-10 (v18.74) — RAMPAGE GETS ITS OWN ROOF, ITS OWN CROWD AND A HORDE HEALTH LEVER

User 2026-09-10: *"Why does rampage feel easier recently?"* — then, given the
answer: *"Rampage increases elites at once by 3. And zombies alive at once jumps
10. Elites panzer and zombies health increase by 20%. Carefully do this only
when rampage is on."*

### Why it felt easier

v18.11 made rampage "the hard mode" by holding back exactly two of the Sep 6/7
relief levers (the flat 45 concurrency and the 0.28%/round speed tail). Every
other relief went out to rampage too, because the knobs are shared and no
rampage branch existed on them: the combined elite roof 12 -> 5/7/9/11 (the one
a player feels most), the horde health table 1.15/1.30/1.45/1.60 -> 1.00/1.20/
1.35/1.50, every elite -10% HP, the hound bite -20%, melee +75% on bosses, and
the hound-director fix that stopped hounds sneaking past the roof. The v18.11
entry's own warning ("three solo nerfs in three versions, none played") landed.

### The three levers, all gated on `level.tod_rampage_on` and nothing else

| Lever | Off | On | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Elites at once | 5 / 7 / 9 / 11 | **8 / 10 / 12 / 14** | `_tod_bosses::elite_roof_all` + `TOD_RAMPAGE_ELITE_ROOF_ADD 3` |
| Zombies at once | 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 | **40 / 45 / 50 / 55** | `_tod_corpse_cleanup::ai_limit_for_party` + `TOD_RAMPAGE_AI_LIMIT_ADD 10` |
| Elite + Panzer HP | x1.0 | **x1.5** (was x1.25) | `TOD_RAMPAGE_HP_MULT` 1.25 -> 1.5 |
| Horde HP | x1.0 | **x1.2** (new) | `_tod_zombie_speed::rampage_horde_mult` + `TOD_RAMPAGE_ZHEALTH_MULT 1.20` |

* **"Increase by 20%" is read as a DELTA on the current rampage figure**, the
  same reading as "+3" and "+10" beside it: elites 1.25 x 1.20 = 1.5; the
  horde, which had no rampage health lever at all, gets a new 1.2. If the
  intent was "elites x1.20 flat", that is one constant (`TOD_RAMPAGE_HP_MULT`).
* **Concurrency is ADDED after the party clamp**, not a flat number: v18.11's
  flat 45 was a 15-zombie step at solo and no step at quad. Now every party
  size gets the same +10. 55 + 14 at quad exceeds `TOD_ACTOR_LIMIT` 60; that is
  the overflow the corpse module documents as safe (stock clears corpses and
  waits 0.1 s), so at quad the last few arrive as bodies leave.
* **The ARMORED SPRINTER takes the elite bump ONCE.** It multiplies a horde
  zombie whose HP already carries `health_mult()`, so with the new horde
  factor it would have landed at 1.5 x 1.2 = 1.8. `_tod_sprinter` now divides
  `rampage_horde_mult()` back out (new `#using` of the leaf speed module; no
  cycle — that module imports only shared). Breaker off, every factor is 1.0
  and the arithmetic is byte-for-byte the old one.
* Rampage's other levers are untouched: elite throughput x2, two Panzers on a
  boss round, spawn pacing 0.80 / floor 0.20, sprint maxed by round 10, the
  0.28% tail, the red luck bar.
* Health applies at SPAWN (elite `boss_hp`, horde `apply_health_scale`), so a
  breaker flip mid-round reaches the next spawns, as it always has.

### Verification

`tools/test_rampage_levers.js` (new) runs the four actual GSC helpers and the
sprinter's HP line for every party size with the breaker off and on: the
tables above, the off-state identity, and the sprinter landing at exactly x1.5.
`lint_tod_arity.js` green. `-GscOnly` build; **UNPLAYED.** The Workshop
description's breaker sentence now says what the switch does.

    (`zombie_point_scalar`), rounds up to tens and awards; the HUD popup reads
    the same function through `level.tod_mage_kill_points_fn`. What is
    DIFFERENT about mage money, by design: a staff cannot headshot, so a mage
    kill is a FLAT 80 where a gun class earns 60 on the body and 110 on the
    head (stock's +50 head bonus) — that is the gap a player feels. Per-hit
    money (stock `_zm_spawner` pays "damage" on every non-lethal hit) still
    applies to every splash and chain victim that survives, so a crowd shot
    pays more hit money than a bullet. Dogs and elites keep their own lanes.

## 2026-09-09 — NAIL GUN: -15% DAMAGE, -10% FIRE RATE, -25% CLIP, BASE AND PaP

User: *"The nail gun base and pap need a 15% damage nerf and 10% fire rate nerf
and clip nerf by 25%."* The nail gun is the HEAVY's tier-3 secondary.

SHIPPED VALUES, from a semantic before/after diff of all 247 generated assets:

| | damage | fire rate | clip | DPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 460 -> 391 (x0.850) | 382 -> 344 rpm (x0.900) | 40 -> 30 (x0.750) | 2,930 -> 2,242 (x0.765) |
| PaP  | 575 -> 489 (x0.850) | 478 -> 430 rpm (x0.900) | 50 -> 38 (x0.760) | 4,578 -> 3,505 (x0.766) |

The PaP clip is the one figure off the requested ratio: 50 x 0.75 = 37.5 and a
magazine is an integer, so it rounds to 38. Reserve (11) is untouched.

THE SOURCE GDT WAS NOT EDITED. `skye_t9_nail_gun.gdt` is install-side and SHARED
WITH MAP 1, so all three nerfs ride the generator's per-gun knobs: `dmgMult`,
`clipMult` and `tune.fire`.

ONE SET OF KNOBS COVERS BOTH FORMS, and the pre-nerf numbers prove it rather
than assume it: 460/575 damage, 0.157/0.1256 fireTime and 40/50 clip are exactly
PAP_UP x1.25, PAP_FAST x0.8 and x1.25. `computePapSet` builds the _up block from
the TUNED BASE, so a base nerf propagates by construction and a `tune.setUp`
here would have been wrong.

⚠️ THE FIRE-RATE NERF WOULD HAVE CANCELLED THE DAMAGE NERF. A secondary does not
ship its port's damage: `computeSecondaryOverrides` normalizes it to a DPS
target held against the gun's OWN fireTime — round(2929.6875 x fireTime) for
this rung — so slowing the gun 10% RAISES its normalized damage by the same 10%
before `dmgMult` runs. A naive `dmgMult: 0.85` would have shipped 0.944 damage
and a 15% nerf that was really 5.6%. `NAIL_DMG_MULT` is therefore 0.85 x 0.90 =
0.765, and the generator's own log confirms the landing: `dmgMult x0.765 (after
cap) -> damage 391`. Same trap the PaP +25% case documents at CLASS_DAMAGE_MULT.
The cap did not bind (`under cap 781`), so the ladder value stands.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED. The 247-asset semantic diff reports exactly two changed
assets and exactly three changed fields each; the weapons CSV is byte-identical;
the registration ledger stays 235/235 and the cost table 238/240.

`docs/armory.html:722` hard-coded the old seven numbers and
`verify_armory_constants` does NOT read that table — it passed both before and
after. Updated by hand and re-checked against the GDT field by field. That gap is
worth closing: the armory's weapon rows are a second source of truth nothing
regenerates.

A GDT edit is always a FULL build.

## 2026-09-09 (v18.59) — THE MAGE'S DAMAGE WAS BEING THROWN AWAY, AND THE PUBLISH GATE REFUSED THE CLASS IT SHIPS

`upgrade_damage_cb` ends with a "nothing modified -> return -1" fast path, and
a -1 tells the stock chain to apply the RAW damage. Its test enumerated every
term applied above it EXCEPT two: the mage staff multiplier and the
script-paid Pack-a-Punch tiers.

For a mage that test passed whenever there was no Insta-Kill, no DAMAGE level
and the victim was not an armored sprinter — `gun_balance_mult` has no staff
branch, GIANT SLAYER is assault-only, RUN AND GUN / ADRENALINE are
skirmisher-only, and splash carries no hit location so the headshot clause was
always satisfied. So every mage without the universal DAMAGE card dealt raw GDT
staff damage to almost every victim in the map — no tier ladder, no matchup, no
ARCHMAGE, no fire charge, no FIRE BLAST / ICE SHATTER, not even the first pack
— while `push_dmg_num` had already shown them the multiplied figure and CHAIN
LIGHTNING still chained off it. The same omission stripped the spire's PACK II
/ PACK III from any holder at DAMAGE level 0.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE BUG SHAPE. v13.7's `sprinter_armor_frac` and
v16's `slasher_sidearm_boss_mult` were both fixed in v16.3 with exactly this
reasoning, and the mage arm was added in v18.30 without joining the test. The
v16.3 comment explaining the trap sits four lines above the guard.

Both terms are captured at their application sites (`mage_mult`, `pap_mult`,
defaulting to 1.0 so the guard stays valid with the class gated off) and tested
by the guard. NO BALANCE VALUE MOVED — this restores multipliers that were
already authored, so every published mage number now applies for the first time.

`tools/test_upgrade_damage_guard.js` runs the SHIPPING condition text, not a
copy, over 23 scenarios plus both capture sites, and carries a negative control
that strips the two terms back out and requires the mage and PACK III cases to
regress. It gates every build including `-GscOnly`.

ALSO: the MAGE GATE's `-Publish` refusal in `build_map.ps1` is retired. It Died
on every publish while `TOD_MAGE_ENABLED` was 1 and instructed the operator to
disable the shipping class; the "NEVER publish this .ff" warning went with it,
because a warning that fires on every build from here on trains people past the
next real one. The three consistency assertions stay: GSC/Lua flag agreement,
`TOD_CLS_COUNT` staying derived, and no second Lua flag.

TWO MORE, BOTH USER-SPOTTED WHILE THE ABOVE WAS BEING WRITTEN:

MAGE COOLDOWNS RAN THROUGH THE WORLD PAUSE. Every value in `tod_mage_cd` is an
absolute `GetTime()` stamp — BLINK's recharge deadline and HEALING AURA's
post-cast lock — and GetTime keeps running while the world is frozen. A mage
came out of a card event, a won trial or the King's max-out with charges it had
not waited for: the round event alone is 15 s against a 6-9 s Blink recharge,
and the dark deals run far longer. The player is frozen, invulnerable and unable
to cast, so it was pure profit for standing still. `cd_pause_watch` pushes every
FUTURE deadline forward by the paused elapsed time, so all four existing
`GetTime() >= deadline` reads stay correct as written instead of four call sites
learning to subtract. A deadline of 0 means idle/ready and is skipped by
construction. CHECKED AND ALREADY CORRECT: `mana_watch` skips its tick while
paused and `charge_regen` holds its countdown — the mana half of the report was
not a bug, and both are now asserted so they cannot silently stop being true.

CHAIN LIGHTNING ARCED ONCE PER SPLASH VICTIM. `upgrade_damage_cb` threads
`staff_hit` once per DAMAGED ACTOR and a staff bolt is splash, so one bolt into
a crowd ran the whole arc selection for every body the blast touched — a Lv6
mage paid 4 arcs per victim rather than 4 per trigger pull, and the denser the
horde the further it ran from the card's own text. `shot_id_watch` bumps a
counter on `weapon_fired`; the arc block claims that id and later splash
callbacks for the same bolt return. The claim sits AFTER the `n <= 0 || dmg < 2`
eligibility tests so a trivial splash victim cannot consume the shot and leave
the real hit unable to chain. Which victim seeds the arcs is the engine's damage
order, not a decision made here, and that is stated rather than implied.
STILL OPEN, NOT CHANGED HERE: arc damage is half of the SEEDING victim's final
figure, so it inherits that victim's matchup — a bolt into a Panzer seeds arcs
off a x5.60 hit while one into a hellhound seeds off x0.45. Only the Panzer is
excluded as a chain TARGET; nothing normalises the SOURCE. That is a balance
call, not a defect, and it is the user's to make.

`tools/test_mage_pause_and_chain.js` runs both shipping functions — the pause
watcher over a scripted timeline, `staff_hit` over a 10-body splash — with
negative controls that strip each fix back out and require the old behaviour to
return. It gates every build.

Arity, Lua, asset, hint, weapon, weapon-cost and armory gates pass, as do all
eight mage tests; PowerShell parses clean. Player patch notes for the whole
unreleased window (v18.1 -> v18.59, the Sep 7 section folded in) are written and
staged, and the Workshop store description now sells five classes and describes
the Mage. Not yet played.

## 2026-09-09 - Armory: all twelve tabs re-audited against source

User: *"Please update the armory artifact. Ive asked multiple agents but they
miss multiple tabs every time and its not up to date with latest code and
stats."*

The complaint was accurate and the cause was structural, not carelessness.
**Both existing gates reported GREEN on a page with dozens of stale figures**,
because between them they check only the `tune:` constant strings and the
domain table's structural fields. Everything a reader actually reads — `lad:`
ladders, `eff:`/`note:` prose, the KNOBS descriptions, and every number
computed on the Ceilings / To Max / Verdict / Deal tabs — was unchecked.

### The shape of the drift

The recurring failure is ONE FACT RESTATED ON SEVERAL TABS, fixed in one of
them. The Archmage ladder was rebased on 2026-09-08; the domain row was
updated and four other sites kept saying "17 s ... 27 s". Same pattern for the
staff matchup table (5 sites), GUNSLINGER's retired multiplicative form (4),
and the crown altar's retired "unlimited" (3, one of which fed the To Max
supply arithmetic).

Roughly 90 corrections. The ones that were not just prose:

- **The Verdict tab RENDERED a wrong number.** The wrong-staff boss row was
  `3.95 x 1.5625 x 0.40` — `TOD_MAGE_OFF_PANZER`, retired in v18.56. Fire pays
  its own `TOD_MAGE_FIRE_OFF` 0.83 there, so the row printed a figure ~2x low.
- **The Ceilings tab computed off RUN AND GUN 3 at +50%.** It is max 5 at
  **52%** (`TOD_UPG_RNG_DMG_L5`), and the 0.50 fed three DPS cells.
- **The Executioner's PaP pellet count was 8.** The GDT gives its `_up` form
  **12** (`t6_executioner_rdw_up_b_zm`), so the packed row was a third low —
  and it makes THREE shotguns that gain pellets on PaP, not two.
- **The To Max supply was built on an unlimited crown altar.** Capped at 3
  since v17.37, so 36 picks -> 39, and the tower now has NO unbounded upgrade
  source at all. The pick RANGES were also wrong; re-derived by running the
  page's own `avgToMax( c, bar, 2000 )`: **42-50** on a full luck bar and
  **56-67** without one, against the stated 43-47 / 55-62. The heavy blows
  through both old ceilings.
- **The mage has SEVEN domains, not five.** MYSTICAL HANDS was missing from
  every count; ATTUNEMENT (retired v18.41) was still written up as live in a
  full note. Pool depth 10/11/12 -> **11/12/13**, B-band share 14.3% -> 13.6%.
- **The mage art debt is closed** (docs/120, 2026-09-08) and the page still
  said four mage domains had no card art at all.

### Three new mechanical gates, because prose is not the only thing that rots

**GATE C — an identifier the page names must still exist.** Four DELETED
defines had accumulated (`TOD_MAGE_ARCH_MULT_LV`, `TOD_MAGE_ON_LIGHTNING`,
`TOD_TRAIL_NODE_MS`, `TOD_ATH_EDGE_TOL`) while every gate was green, because
they lived in `note:` prose the harvester never read AND because an unresolved
name landed in a `missing` list that printed "check by hand" and **still exited
0**. A name-with-a-reason allowlist keeps legitimate "X was deleted" mentions.

**GATE D — a domain ladder must have one rung per level it can reach.** Cheap,
and it catches a cap that moves without its ladder. (44/44 clean; `bonusMax` is
a real higher cap for one class, so the expected length is the larger.)

**`tools/verify_armory_render.js` — the page must actually DRAW.** The old
scratchpad shim reported "panels OK (8)" — but the page has **12 tabs and 8
builder functions**, one of which draws five tabs, so that was never the same
claim. It also handed out a fresh fake node per `getElementById`, so a builder
could write into a throwaway object and pass. Nodes are identity-stable now and
every one of the 12 panels must come out non-empty.

⚠️ **That gate immediately earned itself**: an apostrophe I inserted into a
single-quoted JS string literal in a render function (`ice's`) closed the string
and made the whole page a syntax error — every tab blank. In `note:"..."` fields
an apostrophe is harmless; in the render strings it is fatal. Four sites; fixed
to `&rsquo;`. All three gates now run from `build_map.ps1`, still advisory.

### One SOURCE bug surfaced and deliberately NOT fixed here

`add_domain( "mage_ice", "ICE SHATTER", "the ice staff hits harder: **+10% per
level**" )` (`_tod_upgrades.gsc:1666`) while `TOD_MAGE_ICE_DMG_PER_LV` pays
**0.06**. The in-game card text overstates the card by two thirds. v18.58 fixed
the identical lie in the Lua pause row and did not touch the GSC desc. Flagged
rather than fixed: this task was the page, and the fix is a `-GscOnly` build.

**No game files changed. Docs and tools only — no build needed.**

## 2026-09-09 (v18.58) — THE MAGE PAUSE ROWS, MADE TRUE

User: *"Can we make sure pause menu descriptions are accurate for mage upgrades.
fire, ice should be more accurate and instead of using numbers just say what its
good and bad against in a short description."*

The `act` line is the only place a player reads what a staff is FOR — 48..56 sit
above `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX`, so these rows draw as text and the cards bake no
figures. Both staff lines were describing a matchup table two reworks old.

| id | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| 49 FIRE BLAST | `x2 vs robots and armored, x0.45 vs all else` | `melts robots and armor; poor on all else` |
| 50 ICE SHATTER | `x2 vs hounds and Fury, x0.45 vs all else` | `owns hounds and Fury; fine on all else` |

No numbers, and they now say the actual shape: fire is a spike (×3.61 at home,
×0.83 anywhere else), ice is the generalist (×4.19 / ×2.95).

### Two rows were also numerically wrong

**ICE SHATTER read +10%/Lv.** It has been **+6%** since v18.55 split
`TOD_MAGE_ICE_DMG_PER_LV` out of the shared constant — the row kept the old rate,
so the menu overstated the card by two thirds. Now `6 * l`, and the `eff` line
says *"and slows"*, which is where the rest of the level goes.

**HEALING AURA read a rising 40..120% of max HP.** It has been a **flat 10 hp/s**
since v18.38 (a share of max quietly made the aura worth more to a VITALITY heavy
than to the mage). It is 50 hp over 5 s at *every* level; the level buys RADIUS
and USES, so the uses moved into `act` where they belong.

### ⚠️ A change I made and reverted — read the block above the function

`arch_damage_mult` returns `array( 1.0, 1.30, 1.55, 1.75, 1.90, 2.05, 2.20 )`, so
index 0 is 1.0 and index 1 is 1.30. Read against a define comment quoting
"×2.0 at Lv0, +0.20 a level", that looks exactly like a card that makes you
weaker, and it was "fixed" here to `DEMIGOD_MULT + ARCH_MULT_LV * lv`.

**It was not a bug.** A second session had reshaped ARCHMAGE hours earlier on the
user's own instruction — *"No damage should be 130%, etc. Not 230% to start"*
(base ×2.0 → ×1.00) and *"Damage needs a way slower ramp. 30%, 25%, 20%, 15%,
15%, 15%"* (the deceleration) — and had DELETED `TOD_MAGE_ARCH_MULT_LV` with it.
The "fix" therefore also referenced a define that no longer exists, which
`lint_tod_arity.js` cannot catch: it resolves functions, not macros.

Reverted to the peer's array exactly. **The lesson is cheap to state and was not
cheap to learn: the stale thing was the comment I had read hours earlier, not the
code in front of me.** A ladder that disagrees with its own header means one of
them moved — check which, and check the file's mtime, before calling it a defect.

### Armory brought in line with that rework

The page still described the pre-reshape ARCHMAGE (×2.0 base, ×3.2 cap, 15 → 27 s)
and named two deleted defines. Ladder, tune string and note updated to the live
×1.30 → ×2.20 / 8 → 16 s, plus the new MOVE SPEED lane and the dark 7th rung;
the two ARCHMAGE-derived figures elsewhere on the page were recomputed at ×2.20.
`verify_armory_constants.js` green again at 174 checked.

**NOT BUILT.** A second session started a full build (Radiant LED bake) while
this was being verified, and `build_map.ps1` refuses to sync over a live bake.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.56) — FIRE IS THE SPIKE, ICE IS THE GENERALIST

User: *"We need an even bigger nerf. It should also be okay against panzers and
all other enemies. Fire is the one thats pretty bad against anything but its
weakness."* Plus a new ice-staff fire sound.

### One shared off-family number made all three staffs the same shape

`TOD_MAGE_OFF_FAMILY` 0.45 applied to every staff, so each was a spike on one
family and useless everywhere else — the only thing separating them was WHICH
cell they spiked in. Off-family is **per staff** now, and it is the number that
says what kind of weapon each one is:

```
             lightning        fire            ice        best gun
  horde     70,799 r3*     28,146 r5      61,904 r4      DM 77,625
  armour     6,127 r5     122,418 r1*     61,904 r4      AK 84,749
  beast      6,127 r5      28,146 r5      87,925 r1*     AK 84,749
  panzer    76,245 r3*     28,146 r5      61,904 r4      AK 84,749
```

**Read the columns.** Fire is a **4.3× spike** — nothing in the map touches its
122,418, and it is rank 5 the instant it points anywhere else. Ice is **1.4×
flat** — rank 1 at home, and never below rank 4 anywhere, **the Panzer
included**. Ice is the staff you hold when you do not know what is coming; fire
is the reward for knowing. Lightning still owns two families and is nothing
outside them.

Ice also took the matching cut on its own family (`ICE_VS_BEAST` 4.96 → **4.19**),
so it is **72% of fire** rather than v18.55's 85%. It buys breadth with peak.

### Ice's off-family value is a BONUS, and that forced a second change

`TOD_MAGE_ICE_OFF` is **2.95** — above 1.0. It has to be: the staffs' raw damage
sits far below the gun roster and *all* of their competitiveness comes from these
multipliers, so "okay against everything" cannot be written as a number under 1.

That broke the `family_answerable` rule from v18.50, which withheld the
off-family multiplier when the answering staff was not owned yet. Withholding a
BONUS on that rule would make "no choice available" **worse** than "chose wrong".
So the gate now applies to the penalty case only: a bonus always applies.

`TOD_MAGE_OFF_PANZER` retired whole — the Panzer arm reads each staff's own
`off_family_mult()`, which is exactly how ice became okay against him.

### The ice staff has its own fire sound

It was still borrowing a stock port (`pfx_stormbow_arrowhead`). Now
`sound_assets/tod/mage/staff_ice_shot.wav`, cut from the user's download:
**0.70 s**, 48 kHz / s16 stereo, peak-normalised to 0.0 dBFS, 60 ms tail fade,
`fmt`+`data` chunks only. The length is not arbitrary — the ice staff fires every
**0.80 s**, so anything longer would overlap itself; the source had decayed to
−33 dB by the cut point, so the fade is inaudible. Both alias rows
(`wpn_tod_staff_ice_plr` / `_npc`) repointed; nothing else used the stock wav.
