## 2026-09-08 (v18.55) — ICE SHATTER IS THE WEAKER STAFF CARD, ON PURPOSE

User: *"Ice Shatter should not be as good as the fire staff against the weakness
but still solid."*

They were the same card twice. Both ran on one shared `TOD_MAGE_CARD_DMG_PER_LV`
of +10%/Lv, and against their own families they landed **within 0.03% of each
other** — 122,418 and 122,450 — so there was no reason to prefer either.

| maxed, vs its own family | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| FIRE BLAST 6 (×1.60) | 122,418 | 122,418 |
| ICE SHATTER 6 (×1.36) | 122,450 | **104,083** |

Ice is now **85% of fire** and still clears the best gun (the AK's 84,749) by
**23%** — rank 1 against hellhounds and Furies, just no longer the equal of fire
against armour.

### The rate was the only lever that could separate them

The family multipliers are pinned by the *uninvested* half of the contract — each
staff must land rank 3 with its card at zero — so moving `ICE_VS_BEAST` would
have dragged the un-carded ice staff off the roster along with it. Only the card
rate moves the maxed number without touching the baseline. Split into
`TOD_MAGE_FIRE_DMG_PER_LV` 0.10 and `TOD_MAGE_ICE_DMG_PER_LV` **0.06**.

### And it prices what the cards already are

FIRE BLAST buys damage and a burn. **ICE SHATTER buys damage AND CONTROL** — its
level also runs the hit's 45% slow longer, 1.0 s + 0.4 s per level, so Lv6 holds
a target for 3.4 seconds. A card that buys two things should pay less for the one
they share, or the utility is free. That is the honest reading of why the user's
instinct was right.

**No art or Lua owed:** both pause rows are already generic (*"the ice staff hits
harder and slows"*) under the numberless-card rule, so the only places the figure
lived were the GSC and this page.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.54) — THE CONTRACT IS TWO STATES

User: *"His maxed out fire blast should be 1 against their weakness. Easily"* and
*"Fire blast should be quite strong but its fire rate is what will prevent people
from using it."*

### v18.53 priced the maxed card into the baseline

It folded the staff card (×1.60 at Lv6) INTO the rank-3 target, so a fully
invested mage was still third — **six cards bought nothing but parity**. The two
states have to be separate:

| | uninvested | maxed |
|---|---|---|
| Armour (FIRE BLAST 6) | 76,511 — rank 3 | **122,418 — rank 1** |
| Beasts (ICE SHATTER 6) | 76,531 — rank 3 | **122,450 — rank 1** |
| Panzer (ARCHMAGE 6) | 76,245 — rank 3 | **243,984 — rank 1** |
| Horde (ARCHMAGE 6) | 70,799 — rank 3 | **226,556 — rank 1** |

Rank 1 means clearing the AK's 84,749 on elites and the Death Machine's 77,625 on
trash. So: **never worse than third to anything, first at whatever it has paid to
specialise in.** Breadth by default, peak by investment.

`TOD_MAGE_FIRE_VS_ARMOUR` 2.26 → **3.61**, `TOD_MAGE_ICE_VS_BEAST` 3.10 → **4.96**.
⚠️ Both are the UNINVESTED numbers and each is multiplied by its own card later in
`staff_mult`, so raising one raises the maxed figure 1.6× as much — never tune
them against the maxed number alone or the uninvested state slides under the
roster.

**Lightning has no damage card**, so its growth lever is ARCHMAGE (×3.2) rather
than a staff card. That is why the two lightning rows climb further, and why the
Panzer figure pinned "right under death machine DPS" is the UNINVESTED one and
was not raised.

### The fire staff's damage is paid for in rate — and the model already knew

Worth being precise, because the multiplier reads as unpriced and is not: the
fire staff's DPS is computed over its REAL cycle — `fireTime` 1.43 s **plus** the
0.90 s charge hold its ×2.5 payoff requires — so **2.33 s per shot is already
inside every figure the class is ranked on**. The rate then costs a second time
in a way no DPS column can show: a charge is a commitment, and a horde that
closes mid-hold is a shot you never take.

### Build note: the sound banks were poisoned, not the code

Four builds failed with a linker access violation, and the GSC was never the
cause. The game had been open during an earlier build, which locked the alias
bank and left `soundzone` in a state that made every subsequent link AV. The
script diagnoses this itself and prints the ritual — close the game, confirm no
linker is running, **delete `usermaps<map>soundzone` entirely**, rebuild —
and it worked on the first attempt after that. Two false leads on the way: a
concurrency guard tripping on short-lived zombie linkers left by the crashes, and
a `*>&1` in a bash command that glob-expanded into a filename and never ran the
build at all.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.53) — THE CLASS CONTRACT: TOP 3 AGAINST EVERYTHING

User, twice in one sitting, and it is the same instruction both times:
*"you can place him right under death machine DPS"* and *"what makes him OP is
that his best staff is always top 3 against the weakness enemy."*

### The rule

**Against every enemy family, the mage's correct staff lands RANK 3 among the
five classes' PRIMARY weapons — just under the Death Machine.** So the class is
never the best answer to anything and never worse than third to anything. Its
power is that it always *has* the answer, where every other class has an enemy it
is simply helpless against. **Breadth, not peak.**

Tier-3, packed, all cards maxed:

| family | 1st | 2nd | **3rd** | 4th | 5th |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Horde | DM 77,625 | MP7 75,293 | **MAGE 70,799** | AK 68,858 | blade 60,304 |
| Armour | AK 84,749 | DM 77,625 | **MAGE 76,638** | MP7 75,293 | blade 34,826 |
| Beasts | AK 84,749 | DM 77,625 | **MAGE 76,531** | MP7 75,293 | blade 34,826 |
| Panzer | AK 84,749 | DM 77,625 | **MAGE 76,245** | MP7 75,293 | blade 34,826 |

v18.52's ×8.00 Panzer figure (108,921, above every primary in the map) was pulled
back to ×5.60 on the user's call. **The point was never the size of the number —
it was that the number exists at all.**

### It failed on three of four families, and only checking found it

The Panzer landed exactly on target at the first try. Building the checker to
*prove* it then showed the other three families were nowhere near the rule: fire
rank 4, ice rank 4, and **lightning rank 5 on its own horde**. A shared
`TOD_MAGE_ON_FAMILY` of 2.00 cannot express the contract, because the three
staffs have different raw damage — so it is now **one constant per family**:

| | | why it differs |
|---|---|---|
| `TOD_MAGE_VS_HORDE` | 1.30 | + CHAIN LIGHTNING ×4.0 into a crowd |
| `TOD_MAGE_FIRE_VS_ARMOUR` | 2.26 | fire has the highest raw DPS of the three |
| `TOD_MAGE_ICE_VS_BEAST` | 3.10 | ice has the lowest, so it needs the most |
| `TOD_MAGE_LIGHTNING_VS_PANZER` | 5.60 | no damage card of its own, and no crit |

**Retune by RANK, never by copying one of these onto another.**

**Why they look large beside a gun's.** Every gun figure they are calibrated
against carries the engine's flat **×3.0 head crit**, because that is how the
Verdict tab prices guns and it is what perfect play does. A staff hit is splash
and takes no hit-location multiplier at all — so roughly a third of each constant
is buying back a crit the weapon can never land, not buying power.

### A fall-through bug, introduced by v18.50 and invisible

v18.50 gave the off-family penalty a precondition (`family_answerable`) so a
tier-1 mage would not be taxed for a staff it could not own. Written as
`else if ( fam != el && family_answerable(...) )`, the *unanswerable* case then
fell past the penalty and **into the on-family arm below it**:

- a **tier-2** mage pointing the FIRE staff at a hellhound was paid the full
  on-family **×2.00** — for using the wrong staff
- a **tier-1** mage pointing lightning at a Rogue Protector got **×1.25**

Both were meant to be neutral ×1.00. The neutral case has to be its own arm
rather than the bottom of an else chain; `fam == el` is tested explicitly now.
Nothing reported this — it is a wrong *bonus*, so it looks like the class working.

### The wrong staff is a real cost

9.0× worse on a Panzer, 12.5× worse on the other two families. **The Warden King
is a Panzer**, so the spire's climax is the one fight where bringing the wrong
staff is fatal — and with ARCHMAGE running lightning reaches ~244,000 there and
is first outright, which is the payoff for saving the bar for the fight it was
saved for.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.52) — THE PANZER BELONGS TO THE LIGHTNING STAFF

User: *"Best weapon against panzers should be the lightning staff."*

### It was the worst. Now it is the best, and every line of prose about it was inverted.

⚠️ **The mage was "deliberately the worst Panzer answer in the map" in four
places on the armory page, in `CLAUDE.md`, in the module's own define comment
and in its memory.** All of them are now the opposite of true and all of them
were corrected in this build. This is the retirement-note trap the brief warns
about, arriving in one commit: a rule that was load-bearing yesterday and is
backwards today.

The universal ×0.40 was an *implementation reading* of the v18.44 brief ("each
staff is good against what they are good against and bad against the rest"), and
it left the Panzer with **no right answer at all** — which is the same hole
`family_answerable` closed one version ago. A matchup table that punishes every
choice is not a choice. The table is symmetric at last:

| family | owner |
|---|---|
| horde **+ Panzer** | lightning |
| Rogue Protector + armored sprinter | fire |
| hellhound + Fury | ice |

### Why ×8.00 and not ×2.00 like the other two families

Both halves are arithmetic, not taste.

1. **A staff cannot crit.** Every gun figure it is measured against on the
   Verdict tab assumes head hits and therefore carries the engine's flat ×3.0
   hit-location crit. A staff hit is splash and takes none — so a third of this
   multiplier only buys that back.
2. **Lightning starts from ×1.25**, the lowest number in the matchup table,
   because its reward is rate rather than per-hit size.

`TOD_MAGE_ON_FAMILY` 2.00 × `TOD_MAGE_LIGHTNING_VS_PANZER` 4.00 = **×8.00**;
fire and ice keep ×0.40 through the renamed `TOD_MAGE_OFF_PANZER`. The arm is
still exclusive — the off-family penalty never stacks on top of it.

| | boss DPS, maxed + packed |
|---|---|
| Slasher PaP RK7 (sidearm) | 154,508 |
| **Mage lightning staff, T3** | **108,921** |
| Skirmisher PaP SPAS-12 | 90,233 |
| Assault AK-47 | 84,749 |
| Heavy Death Machine | 77,625 |
| Skirmisher MP7 | 75,293 |
| Mage **fire** staff on a Panzer | 8,478 |

**Above every primary weapon in the game, and above the assault**, which is the
map's designated boss specialist. That last row is the size of the choice: the
same mage with the same cards, pointed at the same target with the wrong staff,
does one-twentieth of the damage.

### What it does not clear, stated plainly

**The slasher's PaP RK7 at 154,508.** That is a perfect-play ceiling on a burst
pistol with every headshot landing and GUNSLINGER maxed, and the Verdict tab
already flags it as the roster's standing outlier with
`TOD_SLASHER_SEC_BOSS_MULT` named as its lever. Tuning past a number the map
wants to bring *down* would compound it.

**With ARCHMAGE running** — the obvious thing to do in a Panzer fight, and the
reason the bar exists — lightning reaches **~348,500** and is first outright. If
"best" is meant to hold on an empty bar too, the 4.00 is the only constant
involved.

### The Warden King is a Panzer

So the spire's climax fight is a mage fight now. That is deliberate rather than a
side effect, and it lands exactly where v18.51's curve was aimed: the class was
asked to be OP very late, and the King is what very late means.

**CHAIN LIGHTNING still never arcs to a Panzer**, and the reason changed rather
than the behaviour. It used to be "he is the one thing the class is built to be
weak against"; the exclusion now survives on its own merit — it is a horde ladder
worth +300% spread over six bodies, and letting it dump into a boss would turn a
trash card into the class's biggest boss card and blow past the ×8.00, which was
tuned on the direct hit alone.

## 2026-09-08 — THE 200k HEAVY: A UNIT BUG (x11), AND THE KING WALL COMES DOWN

User: "I swear he was doing 200k a shot at the warden king." He was — 225,630
on a headshot under Insta-Kill, 75,210 without it.

`TOD_DARK_OVERDRIVE_ADD` was **25**, not 0.25. It is added straight into the
additive `mult` chain in `upgrade_damage_cb`, where every other damage-side
dark add is a FRACTION (DAMAGE 0.50, HEADSHOT 0.25, GIANT SLAYER 0.20,
GUNSLINGER 0.30, RUN AND GUN 0.48, ADRENALINE 0.10). At 25 it read as +2500%,
so a full-ramp dark OVERDRIVE made `mult` 27.25 instead of 2.50 — about 11x
the intended output. The define's own comment said "+25% -> +50% at full ramp",
which requires 0.25.

It was not a rare roll. `king_max_out()` caps every domain at the Warden King
seal and `king_dark_deals()` then deals dark-only cards until nobody has one
left, so a heavy arrives at that fight maxed AND dark by construction. The bug
fired on every King fight.

Heavy, PACK III PaP'd Death Machine (460 @ 0.04s), DAMAGE Lv10, OVERDRIVE Lv5
at full ramp, per headshot:

| | shipped | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| dark, no Insta-Kill | 75,210 | 6,900 |
| dark + Insta-Kill | 225,630 | 20,700 |

Audited the rest of the additive chain: this was the only outlier. The integer
dark adds (DR 10, VITALITY_HP 18, LADDER5 13, LEECH_HP 25, TRAIL_PCT 10) all
live in integer-percent or flat-HP lanes and are correct.

**Origin.** The bug shipped with dark upgrades themselves, in the 2026-09-04
publish build (v17.14). `docs/92` row 26 specifies OVERDRIVE dark as "+25% at
full ramp -> **+50%**", so the design was right and only the constant was wrong.
The Warden King landed the NEXT day (v17.70, 2026-09-05) — meaning he has never
once been fought at honest damage, and neither has his HP ever been tuned
against it. Nothing before 09-04 was affected, and a tower-only run is
unaffected at any date: dark cards exist only in the spire.

**THE ALIGNMENT PASS (same day).** Measured at the King state — `king_max_out()`
caps every domain, `king_dark_deals()` forces the dark cards — with PACK III,
40% headshots and 65% trigger uptime:

| class | gun | gun DPS | boss mult | realistic DPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| heavy | Death Machine | 11,500 | 2.65 | 71,312 |
| assault | AK-47 | 8,828 | 3.65 | 69,548 |
| skirmisher | MP7 | 10,039 | 3.00 | 70,474 |

A **3% spread** — the three gun classes are already in line with each other and
none of them needed a class-side change. The heavy reaching the same place by a
different route (highest gun DPS, lowest boss multiplier, because GIANT SLAYER
and HEADSHOT are assault-only) is working as intended.

The only thing out of line was the wall: **`TOD_KING_HP_PER_PLAYER`
25,000,000 -> 10,000,000**. 25M was ~6 minutes of realistic shooting per player
against a 70s Warden Trial and a 191s finale road. 10M gives ~142s with PACK III,
~284s without. Per-player scaling and the 4-player cap are untouched, so party
size does not move the figure.

**DARK OVERDRIVE'S STEP IS 0.40, NOT THE DESIGN'S 0.25** (user: *"instead of 0.25
we can give it 0.4"*). Dark OVERDRIVE at full ramp is now **+65%**, not +50%; the
BASE ladder is untouched at +25%. Per headshot on a PACK III PaP'd Death Machine
that is 7,314 (182,850 DPS), up from 6,900. It also TIGHTENS the cross-class
spread from 5% to 3%, since the heavy was the low man of the three.

Every description carrying the number moved with it: the define's comment, the
use site in `unique_damage_mult`, the pause-menu DARK readout
(`tod_upgrade.lua` row 26, the only place a player reads it) and `docs/92`

## 2026-09-08 (v18.51) — THE MAGE GETS A POWER CURVE

User: *"I want the mage to be medium ranked at early mid game, late game High
ranked and Very late game OP."*

### v18.50 was measuring the wrong thing

That pass tuned against *% of a benchmark*, which cannot answer "medium / high /
OP" — a POSITION among five classes can. Ranked that way, on packed sustained
horde output with no cards, the shipped ladder had the curve **upside down**:

| | v18.50 | | v18.51 | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tier 1 | 2,153 | rank 2 of 5 — **HIGH** | 1,981 | rank 3 — **MEDIUM** |
| tier 2 | 3,365 | rank 3 of 5 — MEDIUM | 4,307 | rank 3 — **MEDIUM** |
| tier 3 | 5,257 | rank 4 of 5 — **LOW** | 8,506 | rank 2 — **HIGH** |

The field at tier 3, for scale: slasher blade 22,318 · **mage 8,506** · Death
Machine 7,965 · MP7 5,894 · AK-47 4,781. The blade is the map's standing outlier
and the Verdict tab already says so, so rank 2 here means *first among everything
that is not that*.

### The tier ladder left the gun ladder, on purpose

⚠️ **`TOD_MAGE_TIER*_MULT` WAS A DOCUMENTED LOCKSTEP PAIR WITH `TIER_DPS` AND
IS NOT ONE ANY MORE.** The divergence IS the design, and a future session that
"fixes" the drift back to 1 / 1.5625 / 2.4414 deletes the whole curve and will
see nothing fail. The claim has been corrected in three places that asserted it —
the define's own comment block, `CLAUDE.md`, and the armory's Knobs row.

Guns step ×1.5625 per rung, evenly. The mage is **0.92 / 2.00 / 3.95** — a base
cut 8% so tier 1 lands medium, then ×2.17 and ×1.98. **Its two promotions are now
the biggest power steps in the map**, and its floor-30 tier card is the most
valuable card any class can be dealt. That is what back-loading has to mean for a
class whose tiers buy no new weapon — a mage spends a promotion on the same three
staffs it already holds, so the step has to be in the multiplier or nowhere.

Nothing else moved. The matchup table, the Panzer tax, the off-family rule and
the v18.50 first-pack fix are all untouched; at tier 3 the mage is still on ×0.40
against the Panzer and the Warden King, and still the worst answer to them in the
map.

### "Very late" is not on that ladder — there is no tier 4

So it needed its own engine, and the class had exactly one candidate: **mana is
already fed by kills, and kills are what depth supplies.**

`TOD_MAGE_ARCH_MANA_KILL_LV` — each ARCHMAGE level now adds **+0.25 mana per
kill** as well as the +0.25 per second it already added. The symmetry is the
point: the per-second half pays a mage standing in an empty room exactly what it
pays one in a trial, so it *cannot* express "later is stronger"; the per-kill half
is a function of how much is in front of you.

At Lv6 a kill is worth 2.5 mana, and ARCHMAGE (×3.2 for 27 s) goes from filling
in 29 s to filling in 10 s as the kill rate climbs:

| | kills/s | bar refills | ARCHMAGE uptime | average multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| early-mid | ~0.4 | 29 s | 49% | ×2.07 |
| late | ~1.2 | 18 s | 60% | ×2.31 |
| **very late (spire)** | ~3.0 | **10 s** | **73%** | **×2.61** |

So the same maxed card is worth about a quarter more at spire depth than in the
tower, on top of a tier-3 class that already ranks second. It joins the two
depth-scaling multipliers the class already had — the per-staff card ladders
(+60% each at cap, and a won Warden Trial is the only place a build ever gets
finished) and CHAIN LIGHTNING, whose arcs land more often the denser the horde.
**No gun class has an analogue for any of the three**, which is what makes the
very-late phase a class property rather than a number.

### Which knob answers which complaint

Documented on the Mage tab, because these are not interchangeable and the
tempting one is wrong: *too strong/weak early* → `TIER1_MULT`; *the promotion
feels flat* → `TIER2/3_MULT`; *never becomes OP in the spire* →
`ARCH_MANA_KILL_LV` (the only lever that is a function of the ROUND rather than
the tier); *horde clear specifically thin* → `ON_LIGHTNING`. **Never the staff's
GDT damage** — it sits under all four, so raising it drags the off-family and
Panzer numbers up with it and quietly deletes the matchup, and it is a FULL build
where every one of those is `-GscOnly`.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.50) — THE STAFF BALANCE PASS, AND THE ARMORY LEARNED TO CHECK ITS OWN KNOBS

User: *"Please update the armory artifact with latest data. The staffs need to be
balanced."* The page was refreshed, and the refresh is what found the balance
problem — measuring the mage against the rest of the roster for the first time.

### The mage was running at 16–51% of a packed gun class. On every target.

Sustained DPS, magazine emptied and one reload folded in, because a staff never
reloads and burst is not a fair yardstick against a weapon that does:

| Class tier | Best target | Mage was | Packed gun class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | its own (horde) | 1,378 | 1,876 · **51% of one incl. the blade** |
| 3 | its own (horde) | 3,365 | 6,214 · **33%** |
| 3 | Panzer | 1,676 | 6,214 · **16%** |

**The cause was NOT the matchup table.** It was one line nobody had reason to
look at.

### THE FIRST PACK PAID THE MAGE NOTHING

A gun's first Pack-a-Punch is its `_up` ASSET, and the reward lives in that
asset's GDT — +25% damage and −20% fireTime, **×1.5625 on damage per second** —
landing the moment the player is handed the twin. That is why
`pap_tier_mult()` returns 1.0 at tier 1, and it is CORRECT to: the twin already
paid. Its own comment even says so — *"inert for the whole tower"*.

The three staffs register an **EMPTY `up_suffix`**. No twin, so their packed
form is the same asset, so that ×1.5625 was never anywhere at all. **5,000
points bought a mage a camo and the right to be offered a tier card.**

Fixed by `TOD_PAP_FIRST_MULT`, paid in `pap_tier_mult()` when the registered
`up_suffix` is empty. **Asked of the REGISTRATION, not of the mage** — any
future weapon registered the same way is covered without a class test. Paid as a
damage multiplier because damage is the only lever a shared asset has: fireTime
is baked in and cannot differ between two forms of one weapon. PACK II/III
compose on top exactly as they do for a gun.

The tier gate itself was never the hole — `pap_tier` stores every level
independently for an additive class, so a promotion does require the current
staff packed. That open question has sat on the armory's staff tab for days; it
is answered and the note now records the answer.

### A PENALTY NEEDS A CHOICE TO PUNISH

The v18.44 ask was *"each staff is good against what they are good against and
bad against the rest"* — and **"the rest" presupposes a right answer was
available and not taken.** It is not available for the whole first tier: a
tier-1 mage holds ONE staff, so from round 1 it ate a flat ×0.45 on every Rogue
Protector wave, every hellhound round and every armored sprinter **with nothing
it could have done differently.** That is not skill expression, it is a tax on
not having been promoted yet.

The penalty now asks whether this mage HOLDS the staff that answers the victim's
family (`family_answerable`). It does not at tier 1, nor for ice at tier 2, and
it always does at tier 3 — which is exactly where the full table was designed to
live. **The Panzer arm is untouched:** it is nobody's family by design, so being
weak to it is never a mistake the player made.

### Where the two fixes land

| Class tier | Target | Mage now | vs a packed gun class |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | horde | 2,153 | **115%** |
| 1 | armour / beast | 1,723 | 92% — neutral, no answer owned yet |
| 2 | armour | 8,383 | **220%** |
| 3 | horde | 5,257 | 85% |
| 3 | beast | 9,537 | **153%** |
| 3 | Panzer | 2,620 | 42% — the standing weakness, intact |

The horde column sitting a little under 100 at tiers 2–3 is deliberate slack:
lightning also carries 150/50 splash in an 80-unit radius and CHAIN LIGHTNING
arcs half the hit to six more bodies, neither of which a single-target figure can
see, and it never stops to reload. **If it still reads thin in a real run the
knob is `TOD_MAGE_ON_LIGHTNING` (1.25), not the GDT damage** — moving the GDT
would drag the off-family and Panzer numbers up with it.

### The armory: what was actually stale

Both verifiers were green and the page was still wrong in six places, because
**nothing had ever checked the KNOBS table's constant column** — only the
`tune:` strings on domains. So `verify_armory_constants.js` now evaluates that
table too, and resolves against `const NAME = value` in the twin generator as
well as `#define`. **73 constants checked → 161**, and it caught, immediately:

- `LEDGER_GUARD` **223 → 235** (the figure the map ships at, six above map 1's
  last table known to BOOT — stated as the bet it is)
- `TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_DIV` **2 → 1.25**
- `TOD_TRIAL_SECS` **90 → 70**
- `TOD_TRIAL_WIN_PTS_TIER` **1000 → 1500**
- `TOD_SPIRE_DOOR_SEAL_SECS` — **retired whole in v18.0** and still described as
  live
- the whole spire block still reading as a 100-lap, ten-trial tower, with the
  v16.21 HP ladder that has been re-set three times since

That is the class of drift a page like this exists to catch, and it was invisible
to review because none of it is a number anyone would think to re-read.

Also updated: the three staff notes (one still described the pre-v18.44 matchup),
the mage's boss row on the Verdict tab, and a **Mage row in the class table** —
which had said "the four classes against the tower" since the fifth shipped.

## 2026-09-08 — PANZER FLAME: LEAK FIXED, ONE DAMAGE OWNER, CONE PINNED AT 25/12

User: "he will shoot his fire and then end the animation to run at you but you
are still being burned as if he has his flame out."

Root cause. The flame damage lane (`function_fa513ca0` in `mechz_spiki.gsc`) is
started by the `start_ft` animation notetrack and, until now, could ONLY be
stopped by the `stop_ft` notetrack. But the flamethrower is a BEHAVIOR TREE
action, and stock leaves that action WITHOUT the animation ever reaching
`stop_ft`: `mechzShootFlameActionUpdate` calls `mechzStopFlame` and returns
SUCCESS the moment the Panzer goes berserk or decides to MELEE
(`mechz.gsc:735-752`), and `mechzShootFlameActionEnd` calls it on any other
interruption. None of those notify our lane. So "he cuts the flame short to
charge you" left the loop running for the rest of his life — and `flameTrigger`
is `LinkTo`'d to `tag_flamethrower_fx`, so it is a burn cone that FOLLOWS him
while he sprints at you. The flame-cone FX clientfield leaked the same way.

Fix. The loop now reads `mechzStopFlame`'s own state as the authority instead of
trusting a notetrack that may never play: it exits when `isShootingFlame` is
clear (every stock stop path clears it) or when stock's `stopShootingFlameTime`
deadline (`MECHZ_FT_RUN_DURATION`, 2.5s) has passed. That field is UNDEFINED
outside the behavior-tree action, so the claw grab-burn — a scripted animation
that does run its `stop_ft` — is deliberately untouched.

Also: one writer (`acc_ft_fx_off`) for the two flame-cone clientfields, used by
every stop path, plus a death watcher — the loop's `endon("death")` dropped it
mid-flame with the cone still lit, leaving a corpse holding a lit flamethrower.

Same pass, second finding, fixed on the user's call ("I want our damage not the
stock"). Nothing set `level.mechz_flamethrower_player_callback`, so stock's own
`mechzUpdateFlame` swept the flame cone every behavior-tree tick and ran
`playerFlameDamage` at the raw stock 30/20 per tick, in PARALLEL with this map's
halved twin and on a separate latch. `SetPlayerBurning` does not stack, so the
last caller of the frame won and the flame did full or half damage more or less
at random — while every comment in the file said "halved". The callback is now
claimed by `acc_mechz_flame_player_cb`, so this map owns the number outright.
That also retires the last writer of `player.is_burning`, and with it the
missing-`lava_small` shellshock hazard at `_zm_utility.gsc:3776` that this
file's comments already claimed had been removed.

With one owner, the cone's per-tick damage is now PINNED rather than derived
(user: "do 25 and 12"): `TOD_PANZER_FLAME_DMG` 25 and `TOD_PANZER_FLAME_DMG_JUGG`
12, replacing `int(30 * 1.21 * TOD_PANZER_FIRE_MULT)` = 18 and `int(20 * ...)`
= 12 — a stock base times a map-1 heritage factor times a halving pass, three
movable parts for a number the user tunes by feel. Same lesson as
`CLASS_SEC_CAP_MULT`. Ticks are 0.5s over a 1.5s burn, so the per-ignite total
against a 100 HP player goes 54 -> 75 without Juggernog and stays 36 with it.
The GROUND-FIRE pool is a separate lane and is untouched at 15/10.

## 2026-09-08 — v18.48 KEYBOARD IS THE DEFAULT AGAIN

v18.47's structural pad test treated ANY byte outside printable ASCII as a
controller, including low control characters. The keyboard bind expansion
carries one, so the test returned "pad" on every device and every keyboard
player was shown controller art.

The byte test is now high-byte only (>126) and is OUT of the device decision in
all four control surfaces. `CoD.TodKeycap.PadDevice()` and both menus'
`UsingController()` are back to positive proof only: the d-pad latch, or an
offhand bind that literally spells a pad button (LT/RT/LB/RB/L1-R2), which a
keyboard cannot produce. The pause menu's widget-free device arm is removed
entirely.

The byte test survives as a render-time guard only: `TodKeycap.paint` and both
menus' fail-safe stubs refuse to draw a pad button picture inside the keyboard
keycap art, and the switch plate falls back to the pad glyph rect when that
refusal fires. A key name our glyph sheets can render never reaches it, so it
can no longer flip the menu.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.48) — THE MAGE'S ICON IS A WIZARD HAT

`docs/122`'s drop, complete on the first pass. A pointed cone with a bent
drooping tip, a wide curved brim, a buckled band and a scatter of small stars —
mint, no figure, and the same hat in all three renderings.

**Three surfaces, not one.** The request was "update the icon", and the icon
turned out to draw in three different places at three different sizes — which is
why the sweep was done against the CODE rather than against the previous art
doc:

| File | Where | Drawn at | Found via |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i_tod_class_mage` | the glyph on the class draft card | 64 × 56 | `tod_class_select.lua` `art.icons[5]` |
| `i_tod_class_medallion_mage` | the HUD portrait and the party list | 56 × 56 | `AetheriumCharacters.lua` → PlayerInfo + PartyPlayers |
| `i_tod_upg_class_mage` | the round badge on the upgrade panel's class banner | 280 × 60 | `tod_upgrade.lua` `art.classPlate[5]` |

The third is the one a name-based search would have missed: the banner is a NAME
PLATE, and its icon lives in a ~40 px circle at its left end. Its baked
`CLASS MAGE` text and plate are untouched — only the badge art changed.

**A hat, not a weapon, and that is the point.** Every other class's icon is its
weapon — the slasher's katana, the heavy's LMG. The mage carries THREE weapons,
so no single one can be its mark; the cards show the staffs and the icon shows
the hat. That split is what let `docs/121` and `docs/122` be two requests
instead of a compromise.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.47) — THE MAGE GETS A BODY, A PORTRAIT, AND ITS REAL CARDS

### The three class cards, in wood

`docs/121`'s drop came back in two variants and the user chose the wooden one:
*"I downloaded wood versions of the class assets. Use those instead."* Dark
timber shafts with gold banding, against the pale-metal alternative.

All three are exactly to brief. TIER 1 shows the lightning staff alone under
`SPELLCASTER` with `LIGHTNING STAFF` in the panel; TIER 2 crosses lightning and
fire in an X and reads `FIRE STAFF`; TIER 3 stands the ice staff upright through
the middle of that X and reads `ICE STAFF`, 3 of 3 pips. The `UNPACKED` banner
survives on both tier cards, and every bottom panel is ONE line — no rule, no
second line — because the mage has no sidearm.

**They replace three cards that were actively lying.** The shipped set said
`ARCANE STAFF`, `TIPPED`, `EMPOWERED` and `AIR, FIRE, ICE AND HEALING`, all
written hours before the v18.30 revamp retired AIR and made the ladder
LIGHTNING → FIRE → ICE. Same filenames, so a straight file swap.

### The mage finally has a body — and it was NOT a guess

`_tod_classes::class_body_index()` had no `"mage"` case. It returned
`undefined`, `apply_class_body()` no-opped, and a mage kept whatever body stock
handed them.

**The visible symptom was a WRONG portrait, not a missing one.** The medallion is
keyed on the character id the BODY reports, and the four shipping classes own
bodies 5..8 — so a mage landing on one of those displayed the heavy's, assault's,
skirmisher's or slasher's medallion, depending on the draw.

The user picked **Richtofen** from the four free Primis bodies. His index is
**2**, and that is DERIVED rather than guessed: the body index is the position in
`core_common.csv`'s own body list, and all four known values fit that ordering
with nothing left over —

    0 dempsey   1 nikolai   2 RICHTOFEN   3 takeo
    4 beast     5 boxer     6 detective   7 femme      8 magician

boxer 5 / detective 6 / femme 7 / magician 8 are the four already shipping, so
the mapping rests on four confirmations, not one hunch.

### FIVE ROWS FOR ONE MEDALLION, and why that is the right shape

The char id a body reports is baked per character asset and **can only be
OBSERVED** — `AetheriumCharacters.lua`'s own comment block is a record of three
separate playtests that each killed a "natural" ordering (boxer 5 → char8,
magician 8 → char7, detective 6 → char6). Richtofen's id cannot be derived the
way his body index could.

Rather than ship a blank portrait and spend a playtest closing it, the mage
claims the **whole unused low range**: `char0` through `char4` all map to
`i_tod_class_medallion_mage`. That is safe because it is exhaustive on one side
and empty on the other — the four shipping classes are pinned to bodies 5..8,
which report char5..char8, all four observed, so no other class can ever reach
these rows. Whichever id Richtofen reports, the mage gets its own medallion, and
`i_tod_class_medallion_mage.png` draws for the first time since it was made.

One cosmetic cost, accepted and documented: during the 30 s draft a player still
on a stock-assigned Primis body would show the mage medallion before choosing a
class. It corrects itself the moment `apply_class_body()` runs. If a real id is
ever observed, the five rows collapse to one.

### Not in this build

The WIZARD HAT (`docs/122`) has not come back yet — the glyph, the medallion art
and the class banner's badge are still the staff. When it lands it is another
straight file swap into the three names above, and the medallion wiring done here
is what gives it somewhere to appear.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.46) — THREE PASSES SHRANK THE WRONG EFFECT

User: *"Oh i think the projectile can be bigger. Everytime i said this i meant
the impact explosion. Thats whats too big i believe."*

**The lightning staff has two effects and only one of them was ever touched.**
`projTrailEffect` is the bolt in flight; `projExplosionEffect` is the burst where
it lands. Every "too big" report was read as the trail, so v18.36, v18.43 and
v18.45 cut the trail to a third, a sixth and a fifteenth of Treyarch's sizes
while the impact — **100 elements with sprite sizes to 750** — sat untouched
through all three.

**THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE QUESTION, NOT THE NUMBER.** "The lightning fx is too
big" names an effect the weapon has two of, and nobody asked which. A second
question at the first report would have cost one sentence; instead it cost three
builds, and the change that was actually shipped three times made the thing the
user liked *worse*.

### The trail goes back up

Restored ×5, to **1/3 of Treyarch's** — the one size the user did ask for
explicitly (*"a third of the size it currently is"*, v18.36) and never complained
about again. Largest sprite 41.67 against the stock 125. The two later reports
were the impact, so the two later cuts are simply undone.

### The impact comes down

`share/raw/fx/tod/fx_tod_elec_impact_sm.efx` — our copy of
`dlc5\zmb_weapon\fx_staff_elec_impact.efx`, sprite sizes ×0.30 across 200
fields. **Largest 225, down from 750.**

**COPIED, NOT EDITED IN PLACE:** `dlc5\zmb_weapon` is Treyarch's tree and other
weapons read that file. Zoned as `fx,tod/fx_tod_elec_impact_sm` beside the
trail, and `projExplosionEffect` on `tod_staff_lightning` repointed — then
regenerated, because `tod_staff.gdt` is zoned nowhere and only the generated
`_b` twins ship. Verified: `tod_staff_lightning_b` carries the new path. Ledger
232/232.

**CHECKED FOR CHILD EFFECTS BEFORE COPYING, and that check is not optional** —
an unzoned CHILD fx black-screens the load with no message, which this map paid
for on 2026-09-07 when `fx_staff_elec_trail_bolt` spawned an unzoned
`_c` child. Every quoted token in the impact resolves to a `gfx_*` MATERIAL or
one sound alias; `emission` is empty and `childSizeScaleGraph` is a scale, not a
reference. No child .efx, so nothing else needs zoning.

**LIGHTNING ONLY.** Fire and ice keep their stock impacts deliberately: fire is a
charge shot and ice a slow single shot, so a big bloom reads as weight on those.
Lightning fires five times a second, and at that rate a 750-unit explosion is not
an impact, it is the screen.

### The build harness learned to wait

The previous run burned all four attempts in seconds against build_map.ps1's
CONCURRENCY GUARD — a peer session had started a full build at 11:41:23 and the
guard correctly refuses while another cod2map / Radiant / linker is alive,
because build_map.ps1 syncs the source tree as its first step and would rewrite
that build's inputs mid-flight.

**That is a failure to WAIT for, not one to retry**, and conflating the two with
the linker's genuine 0xC0000005 bursts is what wasted the attempts. The harness
now polls for a clear lane before each attempt and only spends a retry on a real
build failure.

That peer build was not fought or killed: its sync at 11:41:23 came AFTER this
session's v18.44 edits at 11:39, its deployed copies were verified byte-identical

## 2026-09-08 (v18.47) — CONTROLLERS STOP WEARING KEYCAPS; THE HINT PLATES FIT

User, on two screenshots of the shipped build: *"When we show A, LT, and RT
why are they inside key caps. But the d pad controlls arent. If you are using
controller we dont use key caps asset."* and *"Spacing is not best or good
design."* Four separate faults, one screen.

**1. THE MECHANISM THIS UI WAS BUILT ON WAS WRONG.** v17.55 and v18.16 both
assumed a pad expands `[{+smoke}]` to the TEXT `LT`, and matched on that
spelling. The screenshot shows what it actually is: a trigger-shaped BUTTON
ICON with LT printed on it, drawn INSIDE the pale keycap. The proof is in the
picture — no path in either menu draws a pad image and a keycap together (every
one is an if/else), so that icon can only have come out of the expansion,
through `TodKeycap`'s LUI-text fallback. The 2026-09-03 note recording "the
engine draws letters, never a picture" read `lt < Switch > rt` off a screen;
those were the LABELS ON THE ICONS — the same class of error as the v14.58
`HoldX` transcription that memory itself warns about.

So the test is now STRUCTURAL, not lexical: `CoD.TodKeycap.IsPadGlyph` scans
for any byte outside printable ASCII. Every keyboard key display name the
engine produces (SPACE, F, MOUSE3, MIDDLE MOUSE) is plain ASCII; a button
picture cannot be. It needs to know nothing about which pad, which layout or
what the button is called. Unlike the name test it is valid on ANY token,
`+gostand` included — the A/B/X/Y ambiguity is a property of NAMES, not icons —
so the lock plate is covered too, which it never was before. Twinned in all
three surfaces (both card menus, the pause legend) with no dependency on the
widget, and each menu's keycap STUB refuses a glyph expansion as well, so a
failed `require` cannot resurrect the third control set either. Third set: the
d-pad latch was the only thing that had ever cleared it, which is why the same
session's second screenshot (after a d-pad press) looked correct.

**2. THE GLYPH DID NOT FIT THE PLATE'S GAP.** `i_tod_hold_plate` is 460x70 and
carries HOLD / TO LOCK as baked lettering with an empty gap at x169..286 —
25.65% of the plate width, centred 2.5 px LEFT of the plate's own centre.
Decoded from the PNG. The draft drew a 60 px keycap into a 45 px gap and the
deal panel a 64 px one into 56, so on both menus and BOTH DEVICES the button
overhung the baked words. Gap centre, gap width and the lettering's optical
centre are now fractions, and every glyph rect is arithmetic off them — the pad
button square, the keycap at the art's true 2:1, neither wider than the gap.

**3. EVERY HINT PLATE ON THE DRAFT WAS 27% TOO TALL.** Its plate rect was tied
to the CARD's width (`xLo+5..xHi-5`), which was 200 when a class card was 210.
The mage narrowed the card to 186 and the plate to 176 while the height stayed
34: 5.18 against the art's 6.571. The plate is now sized by its own aspect and
centred on the card, overhanging it deliberately. `tod_upgrade.lua` had written
this rule down in v16.4 and still satisfied it with a literal; that literal is
now the derivation, so it survives the next card-width change.

**4. THE SWITCH ROW SAID NOTHING.** v16.88 replaced the baked switch plate with
two glyphs and hid the plate for the whole match — and the plate was the only
thing that said SWITCH. `SwitchLine1()` still spells the copy CLAUDE.md
documents and has been unreachable on every real build since. Two bare buttons
centred with nothing to read is the map's own standing rule broken: a menu may
ACCEPT eight inputs but must ADVERTISE one, WITH ITS DIRECTION. The word is
back between the glyphs, drawn in the map's baked typeface through
`CoD.TodGlyphRow` so the row is one piece of lettering, and it now sets the
spacing — the buttons flank it instead of touching each other.

Files: `TodKeycap.lua`, `tod_class_select.lua`, `tod_upgrade.lua`,
`AetheriumStartMenu.lua`.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.44) — EVERY STAFF IS NOW BAD ON SOMEONE ELSE'S TARGET

User: *"I want this class to be more skilled so each staff is good against what
they are good against and bad against the rest."*

**THE HOLE THIS CLOSES.** The matchup table only ever had BONUSES. Fire got ×2.00
against robots, ice ×2.00 against hounds, and the off-matchup case was
**neutral** — fire did full damage to the horde. So there was never a reason to
swap *back*, and a tier-3 mage could hold whichever staff had the best card and
never touch the other two. The class read as three guns with a favourite each,
not as a kit you steer.

**Rebuilt as one family table.** Every victim belongs to exactly one family, and
a staff either owns it or is punished for it:

|            | horde | robot / armored | hound / Fury | Panzer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lightning  | ×1.25 | ×0.45 | ×0.45 | ×0.40 |
| fire       | ×0.45 | **×2.00** | ×0.45 | ×0.40 |
| ice        | ×0.45 | ×0.45 | **×2.00** | ×0.40 |

Roughly, in DPS: on the horde lightning is ~1.8× the other two; on a Rogue
Protector fire is ~5.5× the others; on a hound ice is ~4×. Holding the wrong
staff is now a real cost rather than a missed bonus.

**THE PANZER TAX REPLACES THE OFF-FAMILY PENALTY — IT DOES NOT STACK.** He is
nobody's target, so a naive implementation would multiply both and land every
staff on ×0.16 against a **Warden King with 25M HP per player**. "Weak against
Panzers" was never meant to read as "cannot participate", so the panzer arm is
exclusive and the mage is exactly as strong against him as yesterday.

**LIGHTNING'S OWN FAMILY PAYS 1.25, NOT 2.00**, and that asymmetry is deliberate
rather than an oversight: it fires roughly seven times per fire-staff shot and
CHAIN LIGHTNING arcs on top, so its reward is RATE. A ×2.00 there would have
doubled the class's bread-and-butter damage — most of this map is trash — and
bought no extra decision. 1.25 is the one invented number in the table; the
other three are the shipped values.

**Three ad-hoc branches became one classifier.** `victim_family()` is the whole
truth now, so a new enemy type is one line there rather than a branch inside
every staff. It guards `isdefined( victim )` first — `boss_kind()` checks that
itself, but the sprinter test reads a FIELD, and a `.field` on an undefined
entity throws in this dialect. A missing victim classifies as trash, which is
the neutral arm and never a free ×2.

**KNOWN BYPASS, left alone deliberately:** CHAIN LIGHTNING's arcs use the CLEAVE

It is half of one hit split across up to six bodies, and narrowing it would make

## 2026-09-08 (v18.45) — THE RARITY GATE SOFTENS: S ×0.65, A ×0.85

User: *"WHat does luck do in terms of raroity of cards. Maybe we can adjust
that"*, then *"Apply a small change and send me beofre and after numbers"*.

**`TOD_TIER_R_S` 0.50 → 0.65 and `TOD_TIER_R_A` 0.75 → 0.85.** Two defines. The
luck curve itself is untouched.

**WHAT READING THE ROLL TURNED UP, because it reframes the whole domain.** Luck
does TWO things and they are wildly unequal:

1. **The dice** (`roll_rarity`) are linear and weaker than the bar's presence on
   screen implies — `reg = 80 − 0.40·bar`, `sup = 15 + 0.30·bar`, ult the
   remainder. Filling the bar from empty to full was worth **+0.50 expected
   levels** on a B card and only **+0.25** on an S card.
2. **The guarantees** (`guarantee_rarity`) are steps at bar 50 / 100 / 150, and
   the one at 100 — a free ULTIMATE — is worth more than the entire dice curve
   underneath it.

So the bar is really a step function wearing a smooth meter: below 50 it does
almost nothing a player can feel.

**AND S WAS TAXED TWICE FOR ONE REASON.** A band does two jobs — how often a
domain is OFFERED and how good the roll can be once offered — and S was
penalised on both. The draw half was narrowed to a 1:2:3 ratio earlier the same
day (v18.44); this is the matching half. Chosen over steepening the dice
precisely because it leaves the curve players already have a feel for alone.

**BEFORE → AFTER, per card:**

| bar | band | REG | SUP | ULT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | S | 90.0 → 87.0 | 7.5 → 9.8 | 2.5 → **3.3** |
| 50 | S | 80.0 → 74.0 | 15.0 → 19.5 | 5.0 → **6.5** |
| 100 | S | 70.0 → 61.0 | 22.5 → 29.3 | 7.5 → **9.8** |
| 100 | A | 55.0 → 49.0 | 33.8 → 38.3 | 11.3 → **12.8** |
| 100 | B | 40.0 (=) | 45.0 (=) | 15.0 (=) |

Expected levels per card at a full bar: **S 1.38 → 1.49 (+8%)**, A 1.56 → 1.64
(+5%), **B unchanged** at 1.75 — B's factor was and is 1.00, so this change is
invisible to it at every bar.

**Deliberately small.** The shape is unchanged, an S ULTIMATE at a full bar is
still under 10% and REGULAR is still the majority result on an S card (61%).
Two defines to walk back if it reads wrong.

**Sites:** `_tod_upgrades.gsc` (the two defines plus the worked example in
`roll_rarity`'s header comment, which quoted "15% * 0.5 = 7.5%");
`docs/armory.html` (the `RF` constant, the Knobs rarity-gate row, The Deal's
"slices are halved"). Both verifiers green.

**Build:** `-GscOnly`. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.44) — THE BAND SPREAD NARROWS TO 1:2:3, AND THREE CARDS MOVE TO B

User, in one pass: *"We need to move riot shield to B tier for all classes and
blink to B tier for mage"*, then *"And perk slots to B tier"*, then *"Also we
need to decrease tha gap in general between S, A, B. Maybe something like 6%,
12%, 18%"*.

**THE SPREAD: 100 / 50 / 20 → 18 / 12 / 6.** Those are RELATIVE weights, so what
changed is the ratio — **1:2.5:5 → 1:2:3**. B is now offered 3× as often as S
rather than 5×, and A 2× rather than 2.5×. In practice an S card is dealt about
**44% more often** than before and a B card about **13% less**.

**THE USER'S NUMBERS ARE A RATIO, NOT A SHARE, and that distinction is worth
keeping straight for the next retune.** 6 / 12 / 18 does not mean a card gets 6%,
12% or 18% of the deal — the share depends on how many cards share the pool.
Measured against the live pools, a ~13-card deck now lands near **4% / 8% / 12%**
per card. The weights were set to the user's literal figures anyway, because
6/12/18 IS exactly 1:2:3 and keeping their numbers keeps the intent legible in
the define block.

**ONLY THE DRAW HALF MOVED.** A band does two jobs: draw weight (how often a
card is OFFERED) and the rarity gate (`TOD_TIER_R_*` — how good the roll can be
once offered; S still halves its SUPER/ULTIMATE slice, A still ×0.75). The user's
figures are draw odds, so the gate was left alone and the define block now says
so explicitly — if S still feels too rare after play, that is the second lever
and it changes a different thing.

**THREE DOMAINS MOVED A → B** in the same pass: **RIOT SHIELD** (45, universal —
it was already all-classes, so "for all classes" confirms the existing scope
rather than changing it), **PERK SLOTS** (40, universal) and **BLINK** (55,
mage). Each gets 2× the draw weight and its SUPER/ULTIMATE slice widens ×0.75 →
×1.00.

**PERK SLOTS is the one with history.** Its v16.80 retirement was argued
precisely from being too RARE to be worth a card — "at 50 of ~650-780 per-class
weight it surfaced about once in seven deals, so the cap read as a hard 4".
v17.3a restored it; this move answers that original complaint directly.

**Band is NEVER drawn.** It reaches no client field, no Lua row and no card
pixel — it is server-side draw math only. So all three moves plus the spread
change are **GSC + the armory page**, with no art re-bake, no pause-menu edit and
no Lua work of any kind.

**A STALE CLAIM THE RE-MEASURE CAUGHT.** The slasher class note opened with "the
slasher has exactly one B-band domain at tier 1 — LEECH". That was already false
before today: **GUNSLINGER has been B and slasher-only since v16.51**. With RIOT
SHIELD and PERK SLOTS joining, the class now has **four** B cards at tier 1 and
LEECH sits at 12.5%, level with the rest — down from a 23.3% peak. The note now
says so, and says that it was wrong before the change as well as after. Every
share figure on the page was re-measured from the DOMAINS array rather than
adjusted by hand.

**Sites moved:** `_tod_upgrades.gsc` (the three `add_domain` band args,
`TOD_TIER_W_B/_A/_S`, and the tier block comment's "5x" and its new
ratio-vs-share warning); `docs/armory.html` (the three `band:` fields, the `W`
constant, the Knobs draw-weight row, The Deal's "five times as often" and its
"about ten" S→B claim — now about six — plus the slasher and mage class notes).
Both armory verifiers green, page renders clean.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.43) — THE MAGE ART LANDED, ALL 26 FILES, AND THE TWO ABILITY TILES WITH IT

docs/120's drop came back complete and correct on the first pass — every file at
the exact size asked for, RGBA, and the six re-bakes changed only the line they
were meant to. The headshot re-copy (docs/119) came back in the same window and
went in beside it.

### What installed

**26 mage files.** Nine new upgrade cards (CHAIN LIGHTNING / ARCHMAGE / BLINK at
three rarities, no dark rung — all six mage domains are `set_no_dark()`), three
pause plates, the mana panel and its two fills, two ability icons, and the three
staff HUD icons, which until today still showed one mint staff at three polish
levels — a class that stopped existing on 2026-09-07.

**Four headshot cards**, re-baked to drop the numbers and go from three pips to
five, closing docs/119.

**The two copy fixes are the ones worth naming.** FIRE BLAST read
`BURNS PANZERS AND ROBOTS` while every staff takes ×0.40 against a Panzer; it now
reads `BURNS ROBOTS AND ARMOR`. ICE SHATTER claimed `AND ARMORED`, which is
fire's line; it now reads `SHATTERS HOUNDS AND FURIES`. Both taught the opposite
of the class's central trade.

### THE TROUGH WAS MEASURED, NOT TRUSTED

The mana fill is positioned against literal coordinates — canvas x1104..1250,
y644..668 — derived from a trough the brief specified at x416..1008, y152..264 of
a 1024×296 panel. A trough eight pixels out would draw a bar floating beside its
own well, and nothing in the pipeline would say so.

So the delivered panel was sampled rather than eyeballed: the mint keyline's
bounding box came back **x 416..1007, y 152..263**, and the interior sampled
near-black. It is exactly on spec. The mask, track and rule that built a trough
out of a panel with none now draw at alpha 0 — kept, not deleted, because they
are the fallback if the panel art ever has to be pulled.

### THE TWO ABILITY TILES

The mage carries no grenades — the server calls `DisableOffhandWeapons` on it —
so the lethal and tactical slots in the HUD corner sat empty for the one class
with the most to put in them. They now draw **HEALING AURA** and **BLINK**, which
is exactly what those two buttons do for a mage.

The slots' own idiom carries the state: HEALING AURA uses "lit with a count,
dimmed at zero" for its charges, and BLINK borrows the same two states with the
count hidden — lit when ready, dimmed while it cools. **`everHad` is set before
`setCount`**, and that order is the whole point: the slot hides itself at zero
unless it has ever been non-zero, so a mage spending their last charge would
otherwise watch the tile vanish rather than dim. In the engine's eyes this class
never "had" a grenade at all.

**THE MAGE HUD DROPPED FROM THREE TEXT ROWS TO TWO.** The HEAL count and the
BLINK state now live on the tiles, where every other class reads its offhands, so
a text row saying the same thing beside them is exactly the duplication the user
has called out before — *"more confusing and less simplified by adding so much to
look at"*. What is left is the two things no tile can say: that a full mana bar
has armed ARCHMAGE, and that you are standing in an aura.

### THE TUNING PASS IN THE SAME BUILD

User, mid-build: *"lightning staff and fire staff need to shoot about 30% slower
each. Lightning fx is still too big."*

**Fire rates, 30% more time between shots.** Lightning `fireTime` 0.15 -> 0.195,
fire 1.10 -> 1.43. Ice is untouched at 0.80 — it was not named, and it is the one
staff the user said felt right.

**Read these out of `source_data/tod_staff.gdt` and REGENERATE.** That file is
zoned nowhere; the game loads the generated `_b` twins, so an edit that skips
`gen_tod_twins.js` changes nothing in game. Verified after the regen:
`tod_staff_lightning_b` 0.195, `tod_staff_fire_b` 1.43, `tod_staff_ice_b` 0.80.
Ledger held at 232/232.

⚠️ **THE FIRE STAFF WILL FEEL LESS THAN 30% SLOWER, and that is arithmetic, not a
mistake.** Its cycle is a charge hold plus the recovery, and only the recovery
moved: 0.90 + 1.10 = 2.00 s becomes 0.90 + 1.43 = 2.33 s, which is ~16% on the
whole cycle. The charge window is deliberately unchanged — that feel is already
approved. If the whole cycle should slow 30%, `fireTime` goes to 1.70 and the
charge constants stay put.

**The bolt is now a sixth of Treyarch's original.** v18.36 took every sprite size
in `fx_tod_elec_trail_sm.efx` to a third; this halves that again. **Sprite sizes
only** (`sizeGraph0`/`sizeGraph1`, 32 fields): scaling four field types at once —
sizes, light radius, spawn offset, cull radius — was rejected by the linker when
this FX was first authored, and sizes alone links.

The armory's gun table states both fire times, and **`verify_armory_constants.js`
does not cover that column** — it reported 72/72 matching both before and after
the change. Updated by hand. That table is a second source of truth nothing
regenerates, which is the exact shape this project has been bitten by before.

### THE NEW ZAP, AND WHY IT IS 170 ms

User, same batch: *"i just downloaded a new zap wav that we can use for the
lightning staff shots. The old one is horrible. We will need to trim this one
cause its 7 seconds like but we just want the beginning."*

The source is 7.248 s at 24 kHz. Its envelope, measured in 10 ms windows rather
than guessed at: silence to 38 ms, the zap body from 40 to about 210 ms peaking
at −4.6 dBFS, then a long quiet ramble for the remaining seven seconds.

The cut is **35 ms → 205 ms**, resampled to the bank's 48 kHz, with a 40 ms
fade-out so it ends rather than being clipped mid-decay.

**170 ms IS DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN.** The lightning staff now fires every 195 ms.
A shot sound longer than the fire interval overlaps the next shot — which is
exactly the complaint that retired the previous sample (*"even when it already
hits a zombie, it can still hear it ringing"*). **Any future retune of this
staff's fireTime owes this sample a re-cut**, in the same direction: the sound
must stay under the interval.

Peak-normalised to 0.0 dBFS, landing at mean −11.3 dB against the replaced
file's −12.1, so the alias volume did not have to move. Chunk layout verified
`fmt ` + `data` only — ffmpeg's `LIST` metadata chunk, which stock CoD wavs do
not carry, is kept out by `-fflags +bitexact -map_metadata -1`.

Credited in CREDITS.md: "Laser Zap 2", Freesound Community via Pixabay.

### Wiring

`CARD_SLUG` 53/54/55, seventeen GDT blocks and seventeen zone lines, and
`PAUSE_PLATE_MAX` 52 → 55. That last one is a **contiguous `<=` test**, so
r53/r54/r55 could only be claimed together — which is why the three plates were
requested as a set rather than one at a time.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.43) — BLINK FOLLOWS STAIRS

Blink's fixed knee-height forward trace hit ascending stairs after roughly
100 units, cutting the teleport short. `_tod_mage_elements::blink_landing`
now samples the floor every 16 horizontal units and checks each segment at
that floor's height. Individual rises are limited to 18 units; wall checks
retain the 28-unit clearance, and each landing gets a headroom check.
Characters remain excluded from the traces so Blink still passes through
the horde. Missing ground cancels the cast, and a fully blocked cast no
longer consumes its cooldown. Unobstructed casts use their full stated range.

## 2026-09-08 (v18.42) — ARCHMAGE ACTUALLY DOES SOMETHING NOW, AND THE MANA BAR IS A BAR

Two things, one build. The first is a real bug in the class's headline ability;
the second is the readout the user asked for when the ability was designed.

### THE ARCHMAGE BUG — an assignment where a multiply belonged

`_tod_mage_elements::staff_mult` opened with

```
m = attacker demigod_mult();   // x2 while the form runs
t = tod_classes::tier( attacker );
if ( t >= 3 )      m = TOD_MAGE_TIER3_MULT;
else if ( t == 2 ) m = TOD_MAGE_TIER2_MULT;
```

The two branches ASSIGN. They threw away the demigod multiplier the line above
had just computed, so **ARCHMAGE did nothing at all above tier 1** — you spent a
full mana bar and the numbers did not move. Now `*=`.

**IT HID BEHIND THE DEV HARNESS.** Tier 1 is the one tier that takes neither
branch, so the ability worked exactly where a new class first gets tried. But
`tod_dev_maxed` — on since v18.32, at the user's own request — spawns the mage
at TIER 3 with every domain maxed, which is the one place the ability was dead.
Every ARCHMAGE the user has pressed since it shipped was a no-op.

At tier 3 the form is now ×2.4414 × ×2.0 = **×4.88** before matchups, which is
what "double damage for 15 seconds" was always supposed to mean.

### THE MANA BAR — in the ammo bay, where the user put it

*"a mana bar that is used in place of the ammo section"*, 2026-09-08. Until now
that was a line of engine HUD text saying `MANA 47 / 100`.

The MAGE has no ammunition — three staffs, none of which run out — so its clip
and reserve cells were dead space. They are now one horizontal bar in
`AetheriumLoadout.lua`: **mint while mana fills** (a point a second, a point a
kill, to a hundred) and **gold and draining** while the ARCHMAGE form that bar
paid for is running. The form's own timer is the bar, which is why spending the
mana does not leave an empty trough.

**IT RIDES `LuiNotifyEvent`, NOT A CLIENTFIELD, AND THAT IS NOT A PREFERENCE.**
The clientuimodel pool is at its proven 61-bit ceiling with ONE bit spare and is
append-only; a 0..100 value needs seven. Overflowing it is not a degraded
readout, it is `Com_ERROR "clientuimodel is out of space"` and a load that aborts
to the lobby. So the value goes out as two ints — value and state — on the lane
the green health bar, the tower gauge and the owned-upgrade sync already share.
The push is CHANGE-GATED at 4 Hz, and the gate is dropped every five seconds
because the ammo bay's whole widget lifecycle re-runs on a death and would
otherwise sit blank for the rest of the life against a server that believes it
already sent that value.

The two ammo glyph rows stand down while the bar is up (`manaOn`, checked inside
both subscriptions), and `stopPulse()` goes with them so a low-ammo flash cannot
strobe a hidden row. A class switch sends state 2 and the numbers come straight
back — without that, the next class would carry the mage's bar over its own
ammunition.

**THE ART IS NOT IN THIS BUILD AND ITS NAMES ARE NOT IN THE CODE.** GATE A of
`lint_tod_assets.js` is comment-stripped and flag-blind and it caught the first
attempt, correctly: naming `i_tod_hud_mage_panel` / `_mana_fill` / `_mana_arch`
behind a `false` flag still fails the build, because `RegisterImage` on an
unzoned name draws a WHITE SQUARE rather than failing. So the bar is built out of
the flat slab every other placeholder in that file uses — mask, track, wipe-clipped
fill, coloured rule — and it is a real working bar today. The names live in a
comment until the drop can be zoned in the same build. `docs/120` is the brief.

The right-hand HUD row that used to repeat the number now carries only the one
thing a bar cannot say — that the aim button is live.

### THE DEAD DARK CARD

`i_tod_card_mage_heal_dark` was baked and zoned on 2026-09-07, but `mage_heal` is
`set_no_dark()` like every other mage domain, so it could never be dealt: **3.4 MB
of load RAM** (cards are `uncompressed` 768×1152) for an image nothing could draw.
The zone line is gone and `DARK_NONE[52]` went in the SAME edit — that row is what
stops the register loop naming an image the `.ff` no longer carries, and it is the
only order that works.

### THE ART REQUEST

`docs/120_mage_full_art_prompt.md` → `tod_mage_full_art_pack.zip`. 26 files: the
three new upgrade cards (CHAIN LIGHTNING / ARCHMAGE / BLINK) at three rarities,
three pause plates, the mage weapon panel and its two fills, the healing-aura and
blink ability icons, and the three staff HUD icons — the shipped trio still shows
one mint staff at three polish levels, which stopped being the class on 2026-09-07.
It also re-bakes six shipped cards for copy: FIRE BLAST reads `BURNS PANZERS AND
ROBOTS` while every staff takes ×0.40 against a Panzer, and ICE SHATTER claims
`AND ARMORED`, which is fire's line. Both teach the player the opposite of the
class's central trade.

Out of scope by request: the class card and the tier cards. Held back with them,
deliberately: the mage glyph, medallion and upgrade-panel plate, which all still
work and which should be re-requested in one pass IF the class card lands on a

## 2026-09-08 (v18.41) — HEADSHOT IS 12% PER LEVEL OVER FIVE LEVELS, AND ITS LAST HAND-COPIED LITERAL IS GONE

User: *"We will change headshot upgrade to 12% per tier and only 5 tiers"*, then
*"Make sure to update the pause menu where needed"*.

**5%/Lv × 10 levels → 12%/Lv × 5.** The rate and the cap moved together, which
is the whole point and the thing to quote: the CEILING barely moves (+50% →
**+60%**), but a single card is worth **2.4×** what it was and the domain
finishes in **five picks instead of ten**. This is a pacing change wearing a
buff's clothes.

**WHAT IT IS ACTUALLY WORTH, because the headline lies.** Every damage domain
adds into ONE unclamped sum that DAMAGE alone contributes +1.00 to, so a maxed
assault headshotting a boss goes ×3.10 → ×3.20 = **+3.2% real damage**, and on
the horde ×2.50 → ×2.60 = **+4.0%**. "5% → 12%" reads like +140% and is not —
the same trap the 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-30 passes both fell into, and the
define's comment block now carries the corrected arithmetic rather than the
headline.

**THE HAND-COPIED LITERAL IS GONE, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT ALREADY BIT.**
`_tod_bosses::rp_damage_feed` carried its own `* 0.05` copy of
`TOD_UPG_HS_PER_LVL` — a GSC #define is file-local, so that lane could not see
the symbol. The 2026-08-22 nerf missed the copy and a headshot on the Rogue
Protector paid **2.5× for a day**; the block comment above it has warned about
exactly this ever since. It now calls a new PUBLIC `tod_upgrades::headshot_bonus()`
which owns the rate AND the dark step — the same shape `boss_damage_bonus` has
had from the start, and the fix that comment itself recommended. DAMAGE is now
the only literal left in that lane, and the comment says so and says to do the
same thing to it next time it is touched.

**A SIDE EFFECT WORTH KNOWING:** the DARK headshot step (+25%) now applies on
the Rogue Protector lane too. It never did while the bonus was an inline
multiply there, so a dark-HEADSHOT assault was quietly paid less against a Rogue
Protector than against every other enemy in the map. That was a bug nobody had
reported; folding the dark step into the accessor fixed it as a by-product.

1. **The number.** The three light `i_tod_card_headshot_*` PNGs bake `+5 / +10 /
   +15%  HEADSHOT DMG` as pixels and the game now pays 12 / 24 / 36. Per the
   generic-card-text rule the re-bake comes back **numberless**, reusing the
   wording the DARK card has carried all along — `HEADSHOTS / HIT HARDER` — so
   the next retune of this domain owes no art at all.
2. **THE PIP ROW, which is the half that would have been missed.** All four
   cards carry **3 pips**, and 3 is the *max-10* convention; the rule is one pip
   per level for max ≤ 6, so at max 5 they need **5**. This applies to the DARK
   card too, whose wording was already correct and which would otherwise not
   have been touched. **A CAP CHANGE IS AN ART CHANGE EVEN WHEN NO VALUE MOVES**
   — nothing greps a pip count and no lint sees it. Recorded at the top of
   docs/33, which until now only tracked stale numbers.

The pause plate `i_tod_pause_r06` is name-only and needs no re-bake.

**THE STALE-DOC SWEEP THIS TURNED UP, all corrected the same session.**
`tod_upgrade.lua`'s comment on row 40 read "PERK SLOTS: DOMAIN REMOVED
2026-09-03" — v16.80 retired it and **v17.3a restored it AND the perk cap**, so
the row, `CARD_SLUG[40]` and the card zone lines have all been live for five
days. **CLAUDE.md carried the same claim**, and worse: it said
`level.perk_purchase_limit` is "a constant ABOVE the roster" and that "a tenth
machine needs NO lockstep edit anywhere". Both false — the limit is 4 again and
4 + PERK SLOTS' max 5 must equal the roster or the last perk is unbuyable. Fixed
in place, with the correction itself recorded so the next reader knows the block
has lied once.

Two more in the same file while there: **CLAUDE.md still said "4 CLASSES"** (the
MAGE is live — `TOD_MAGE_ENABLED` is 1) and quoted **"34 live domains, ids run
to 40"** against a live 43 and 55. The class bullet now carries the mage
properly — additive, three staffs held together, no sidearm or grenades, the
matchup table, speed 1.00 — and the domain line now says to run
`verify_armory_domains.js` instead of quoting a number that has gone stale here
repeatedly. A stale `0.85` mage speed in a `_tod_upgrades.gsc` block comment
went with it.

**The pattern worth naming: A RETIREMENT NOTE OUTLIVES THE RETIREMENT.** Three
separate files were still announcing a domain's removal days after it came back,
and nothing mechanical can see it — the verifiers check structure, not prose.
Read the `add_domain` call before believing any claim that something is gone.

**Build:** `-GscOnly` (GSC + Lua only). All four gating lints green: arity, Lua,
hints (95 distinct strings of 190 budgeted), assets. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.26) — THE MAGE'S ELEMENTS ARE PROJECTILES NOW, ALL THREE ON ONE WEAPON

User, first play of v18.24: *"Fire Blast seems like it just attacks the closest
zombies, Ice Shatter and Airburst seem like they shoot at my feet. My request

**ONE WEAPON, NO GDT.** The answer to the question is the design: a bolt is a
`tag_origin` script_model carrying the element's TRAIL FX, `MoveTo`'d down the
player's aim line at the element's speed, bursting on the first zombie inside
its 64u radius or where the aim line ends (`BulletTrace` with characters, so a
bolt aimed at a zombie bursts on that zombie and one aimed at a wall bursts on
the wall). The payload -- damage, burn, slow, the toss -- is applied in script
at the burst point, so the per-element difference is a switch on the KEY. The
no-twin law holds, the ledger stays 232/232 (zero headroom -- three real
projectileweapon defs would not fit), `tod_staff.gdt` is untouched, and the
staff's own trigger shot is unchanged. `_tod_mage_elements.gsc`: `launch_bolt`,
`bolt_fly`, `bolt_touching`, `bolt_impact`; `cast_target` deleted (nothing
auto-targets any more).

| element | trail (in flight) | burst | speed / range | payload at the burst |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIR BURST | Thundergun trail (`zombie/fx_trail_thundergun`) | Origins air impact | 2400 / 1200 | THE THUNDERGUN BOOM: every trash zombie in the radius (160..288 by level) dies through `mage_hit` (the mage is credited) and is TOSSED away from the burst -- _tod_bosses' proven `StartRagdoll` + `LaunchRagdoll` triple at scale 90; elites take the tenth and stay standing |
| FIRE BLAST | Origins fire bolt trail | fire impact (ug) | 1600 / 1800 | 10..35% of max HP to everything within 160, ×2 on Panzer/Protector, burn tell (value 2) |
| ICE SHATTER | Origins ice bolt trail | ice explosion | 1400 / 1400 | 8..28% within 220, ×2 on hound/Fury/armored, the 1.0..3.0 s slow (slow() keeps its own boss refusal) |

Before: AIR and ICE were 220u novas at the caster's feet and FIRE picked the
nearest zombie in a 53° cone. Cooldowns, levels, the tier floor, ATTUNEMENT and
the HUD are all unchanged.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.25) — THE KING'S CO-OP CURVE: TRIED, MEASURED, REVERTED. AND AN ALTAR FLAG OFF THE BUNDLE

Two items, one of which leaves no code behind on purpose.

### 1 · The Warden King keeps his linear health (v18.24 written and reverted, never built)

Workshop, CZ: *"i think the warden king should be a little stronger he died easy
with teir 3 heavy"*. User: *"let's treat the factor that we use for his health
the same as we do for panzer ... Lets do 30M for solo and then use our factor
math that the panzer uses"* — then, once the table was in front of him,
*"Lets revert this"*.

`TOD_KING_HP_PER_PLAYER` 25,000,000 x party (cap 4) STANDS. The 30M-base +
`coop_hp_mult` version existed for one edit and is gone; nothing shipped, and
the file is byte-identical to before apart from a warning comment.

**KEEP THE MEASUREMENT, because it is the argument against proposing this
again.** `coop_hp_mult` is 1.0 / 1.7 / 2.3 / 2.8 — deliberately SUB-LINEAR, so
a duo is not fighting two bosses' worth. The king's rule is strictly linear.
Fitting the curve to him therefore *lowers the top end no matter what base you
pick*:

| party | linear (n x 25M) | curve (30M x coop) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| solo | 25,000,000 | 30,000,000 | **+20%** |
| 2 | 50,000,000 | 51,000,000 | +2% |
| 3 | 75,000,000 | 69,000,000 | −8% |
| 4 | 100,000,000 | 84,000,000 | **−16%** |

The request was "a little stronger" and the change made him weaker for every
party above two. **IF THE KING NEEDS RETUNING, MOVE THE PER-PLAYER NUMBER.**
The curve is the wrong instrument for a boss whose value was hand-set per head
(v17.83: *"I gave you the 4 player health"*). That warning now lives in the
define block so the next reader meets it before the idea, not after.

### 2 · What the fight actually costs — the part worth keeping

Measured while pricing the retune, from the tree rather than from memory
(`gen_tod_twins.js`'s emitted GDT for damage/fireTime, the additive sum in
`upgrade_damage_cb`, `TOD_PANZER_HEAD_SCALE` 0.9). Every player arrives maxed by
construction — `king_max_out` + `king_dark_deals` run before he moves — so these
are the standard case, not a ceiling:

* Skirmisher x3.50, Assault x4.05, Heavy x3.00; with PACK III and perfect
  headshots all three land **within 4% of each other**. The tier normalization
  works.
* Head x2.70 vs body x0.35 — a **7.7x** gap. Aim, not class, is the variable.
* **A SCRIPT-ONLY DPS TABLE UNDERSTATES THIS FIGHT BY ABOUT HALF.** Double Tap
  2.0 is in the roster and `perma_perks_give` hands it to everyone at ascension,
  but its stock module is registration and FX only — the double bullet is
  ENGINE-side and no amount of reading this tree reveals it. Wisp Tea adds ~22%
  through a percent-of-max lane (`WISP_TEA_KING_SEGMENTS` 1600) that ignores the
  health wall entirely. Both folded in, a maxed player goes from ~2.2 min to
  **~1 min**. Any future King tuning should be judged against that number.
* The slasher's best King weapon is **their sidearm, not the Stormbreaker** —
  GUNSLINGER (+150%, +180% dark) x `slasher_sidearm_boss_mult` 2.25 puts the
  packed RK7 at about 1.9x the axe. Nothing tells the player that.
* Verified exclusions, from code and not from comments: DRAW CUT is Wakizashi-
  bound and gone at T3, FIRE RATE is MAC-10-bound, SECOND WIND and SUPPRESSING
  FIRE are T2 guns, and THOR'S THUNDER skips bosses at its own target filter
  (`if ( IS_TRUE( z.is_boss ) || ... ) continue;`).

### 4 · `Engine.GetPlayerCount()` DOES NOT REPORT SOLO — and why nobody noticed

User, after playing the co-op restart gate: *"I didnt see it in solo"*. The gate
hid RESTART LEVEL in a one-player game, which is the opposite of what it says.

**The call is wrong, and the reason it looked right is the whole lesson.** The
kit's Leave Game lane reads it, which is what both this gate and the 2026-08-23
solo Quick Revive price cited as proof it works. Look at that call site:

```lua
if playerCount and playerCount <= 1 then
    Engine.SetDvar("cl_paused", 0); Engine.Exec(controller, "disconnect")
else
    Engine.SetDvar("cl_paused", 0); Engine.Exec(controller, "disconnect")
end
```

**Both arms are identical.** The return value has never changed a behaviour
there, so a wrong value could not be observed — and two separate changes read
its mere presence as evidence and shipped bugs on it. `PromptPerks.lua` has been
quoting **1500 in solo since 2026-08-23**, which is the exact bug that comment
was written to fix; the menu gate was simply the first code to make the wrongness
visible. **A call nobody has watched DECIDE something is not a proven call, no
matter how many files use it.** Sibling of the v14.58 dead image guard and of
[[check-passes-wrong-question]].

**And it means v18.18's Quick Revive price fix was aimed at the wrong surface.**
That pass added a 20 s hint re-assert in GSC on a race theory. The screenshot the
user sent is the PromptPerks CARD, which never read that string.

**The fix.** `_tod_main::party_dvar_watch` publishes `GetPlayers().size` as the
`tod_party` dvar — authoritative, server-side — on the channel `_tod_gameover`
has used for `tod_go_active` since v9.24, which IS proven because it is the only
thing that makes the game-over menu appear. Both readers now use it, twinned
rather than shared (the `TodPadWord` precedent: a widget that requires another
file dies silently if the require fails).

**Both read POSITIVELY**, and the two defaults differ on purpose: the menu treats
an unreadable dvar as SOLO (keeps the button — the pre-gate behaviour, so a
failed read can never delete a feature again), while the price treats it as
CO-OP (shows the stock table value). Each falls back to what it did before its
respective change. A co-op PEER reads `""` because SetDvar is host-side and keeps
the button; pressing it drops only that peer, where the HOST pressing it drops
the party — the host is the seat this covers. The dead branch above now carries a
warning naming both bugs, so it cannot be cited a third time.

### 5 · Build note: the linker crash eats the playable build

Five consecutive `0xC0000005` linker crashes tonight — two `-GscOnly`, one full,
and twice invoking `linker_modtools.exe` directly with no script around it —
before a second full build linked cleanly (`.ff` 20:05:54, `.led` 45,041,490, the
known-good bake fingerprint). Ruled out with evidence, not guesswork: content
(the peer's 19:18 build succeeded on the same tree, no GDT newer than 19:15),
memory (7.7 GB free), and stale intermediates (five `.partial` files cleared, it
crashed again identically).

**`gdtdb /update` really does fail — and it is NOT this.** It aborts on duplicate
assets between `model_export\_blackops_coldwar_ehancepack\...\p9_fxanim_zm_gp_pap_xmodel.gdt`
and `source_data\acc_alxs_pap.gdt`, a byte-identical copy (same md5, same line
numbers) sitting in the shared tools root under MAP 1's prefix — the
[[shared-gdt-crosses-maps]] trap. It was one confident paragraph away from being
reported as the root cause; **both files are dated 2025-04-30**, so that warning
predates every build that has ever worked here. Worth cleaning up, unrelated to
tonight.

⚠️ **`build_map.ps1` TURNS A TRANSIENT CRASH INTO A BROKEN DEPLOYMENT.** Its
retry loop deletes `sound\zone` whenever the bank is missing after a link, and
the linker is the only thing that regenerates it — the repo carries no `.sz`. So
