## 2026-09-07 (v18.21) — RESTART LEVEL KICKS THE CO-OP PEER, AND WE MADE IT FINDABLE

Workshop, Ticksy: *"Fix restart level button please, it kicks the other player
out in coop!"* User: *"Do you see anything about this or made recent changes? I
never experienced that."*

**Not our button, but our discoverability.** RESTART LEVEL is the Aetherium
kit's own pause-menu entry, `Engine.Exec(controller, "map_restart")`, and it is
byte-identical in this map's first commit, in the v14.16 commit and in the
working tree — map 1 carries the same lane. Nothing we shipped ever touched it.

What we did ship is **v17.26** (2026-09-04, live in the v17.58 publish at
21:07): the pass that linked the pause menu's icon row to its button column.
Before it, `LUI.UIList` refused to leave itself at a grid edge and the button
column was **unreachable on a gamepad** — that was the user's own report
(*"it only will remain on the top 4 icons"*). Mouse hover reached it; nothing
else did. So an always-broken button became a findable one, and three days later
the reports arrive. **A fix that improves navigation is a fix that exposes
whatever the navigation could not previously reach** — the v17.26 entry should
have carried an audit of what it had just made reachable, and did not.

**Why it kicks.** `Engine.Exec` runs the console command on the PRESSING
machine. On the host that reloads the level; the connected peer does not come
with it and lands back at the main menu. "The OTHER player" places the presser
at the host, which is the only seat where `map_restart` is a legal command —
and is also why the user never saw it: they host, and on KBM they would have to
deliberately mouse onto the entry mid-co-op.

**Both restart lanes are now solo-only** (`TodCoop()` in
`AetheriumStartMenu.lua`): the pause menu's RESTART LEVEL, and the game-over
menu's RESTART MAP, which is the same call with the same defect and was gated on
the same evidence rather than on a second report. Co-op gets End Game / Leave
Game, which work.

Three deliberate choices in the guard:

* **It reads POSITIVELY** — hide only on a proven `Engine.GetPlayerCount() > 1`.
  A failed or absent read leaves the solo button exactly as it is today, so a
  flaky engine call can never delete a working solo feature. The failure mode of
  the guard is the status quo, not a regression.
* **No new engine surface.** `Engine.GetPlayerCount()` is the same call the
  Leave Game lane in this very file already makes, and the same one
  `PromptPerks.lua` makes for the solo Quick Revive price.
* **Each action re-checks at press time** and returns after `GoBack` instead of
  exec'ing. The build-time hide is the fix; this is for the case where a cached
  button list outlives a join. Closing the menu is always safer than booting a
  teammate.

`node tools/lint_tod_lua.js` → 46 files, 0 findings.

⚠️ UNPLAYED, and **NOT IN ANY BUILD** — see below. File:
`ui/uieditor/menus/StartMenu/AetheriumStartMenu.lua`.

**TWO SELF-INFLICTED BUILD FAILURES, both worth recording.**

1. **THE HINT LINT COUNTED A HUDELEM AS A HINT.** Its catch-all treats any
   literal carrying a button token as a cursor hint, so the four new labels
   hard-failed the build and moved the reported budget 95 -> 99. They are
   `SetText` on a hudelem and mint NO slot — the 250 cap is `SetHintString`'s
   alone. The catch-all now runs only in a file that actually calls
   `SetHintString` (its whole purpose is catching a hint assembled into a
   variable, which requires such a call). Count back to the true 95; the selftest
   still catches all 9 planted breaks. New blind spot stated in the code: a file
   that builds a hint and hands it to another module now escapes the catch-all.
2. **A DOUBLE QUOTE IN A CSV COMMENT KILLED THE LINKER.** The explanatory block
   added above the new alias rows carried a quote that OPENED on one line and
   CLOSED on the next. In a CSV an opening quote starts a quoted field and the
   parser swallows the line break, fusing records. Result: "sound bank missing"
   three times and `exit -1073741819` (0xC0000005). Replaced with one
   comma-padded, quote-free line on the only proven mid-file pattern in this repo
   (`zm_ai_zod_companion.csv:2`). **A data file is not a place for an essay.**
   Also on the way: a bash heredoc turned `\fire` into a literal FORM FEED (0x0C)

## 2026-09-07 17:38 (v18.21) — THE COMBAT STANCE NEVER ARMED: A CLASS TEST TAKEN AT SPAWN

User: *"the combat stance doesnt work"* — and it never could have. It was fully
implemented, correctly wired, and compiled into the build. It just never started.

`_tod_mage_elements::on_player_spawned` read the player's class at SPAWN and
returned unless it was mage. **The draft lands on an ALREADY-SPAWNED player**, so
at that moment nobody has a class yet: the test failed, the function returned,
and `stance_watch()` was never threaded. Nothing re-ran it, so ADS did nothing
for the entire match.

**The warning was already written down, in this repo, in the function that
assigns the class.** `_tod_classes::assign_class` says verbatim: *"The draft lands
on an ALREADY-SPAWNED player, so the spawn-side re-assert has long since run —
apply the body here too, or the first life of the match wears whatever stock
rolled."* That is why the player BODY is applied there. This module then read the
class the exact way that comment says not to. **A hazard noted in one file is not
a hazard handled in another** — the note has to travel to every consumer, or be
made structural.

**Also unfalsifiable from a static read**, which is why it survived a wiring
audit: `init()` is called, `on_spawned` is registered, the module is zoned, the
class key is `"mage"`, `AdsButtonPressed()` is a raw poll unaffected by
`AllowAds(false)` (proof: stock polls it in the player-ZOMBIE lane, on a player
who cannot ADS). Every link in the chain checks out individually. The defect is
purely in WHEN one link runs.

- **Fix**: arm on the SIGNAL. `class_arm_watch()` re-tests on every
  `tod_class_assigned` — the notify `assign_class` fires, and `assign_class` is
  the one site all three paths go through (the draft pick, the 30 s timeout roll,
  the station switch). Singleton via the map's own idiom
  (`notify` + `endon` on one key, `_tod_classes:947`), so respawns and re-draws
  cannot stack two loops.
- **Switching AWAY from mage now disarms**: `tod_mage_disarm` kills the watcher,
  the stance exits, and ADS is handed back — but ONLY to a player we took it
  from (`tod_mage_armed`). Calling `AllowAds( true )` on a class that never lost
  it is exactly the cross-class regression this feature is flag-gated to avoid.
- Still entirely behind `TOD_MAGE_ENABLED`; no non-mage code path changed.
- `-GscOnly`, fresh `.ff` 17:38:47. Arity lint clean, Lua lint clean, repo ==
  deployed, nothing synced after. **UNPLAYED.**

**TEST MAP AND DOCS ONLY. `zm_tower_of_doom` IS NOT TOUCHED** — the tower's staff
still names `vm_freezegun_*` in `tod_staff.gdt` and does not zone
`tod_staff_anims.gdt` at all. Nothing here can reach the production build.

User played the round-2 harness: *"yes A looks good and the rest look horrible.
They always block my face like im looking inside of something."*

**A good, B C D E all bad — and that is a clean result, not a wasted run.** Both
hypotheses died at once: the bind rig is not the cause (richtofen and synth both
failed, in both directions), and `looping` is not the cause (B and C carried
`looping "0"` and still failed). The harness itself was proven sound — A, the
known-good reference, looked right, and E, the known-bad control, looked wrong.

**Four arms failing IDENTICALLY means the cause is a CONSTANT across all four.**
No amount of varying rig or looping could have found it. That is the transferable
lesson: when every arm of an experiment fails the same way, stop varying and go
looking for what they share.

What they shared was `useBones "1"`. `xanim.gdf` names that field **"Use Bones
(Not viewmodel)"**, tooltip *"Not needed for viewmodels, but is needed for
practically everything else."* Across the entire mod tools install only four GDTs
define `vm_*` animations:

| GDT | `useBones 0` | `useBones 1` |
|---|---|---|
| `wpn_t7_zmb_bow.gdt` — Treyarch, DE bow | **40** | 0 |
| `wpn_t8_zmb_freezegun.gdt` — Treyarch | **28** | 0 |
| `tod_staff_anims.gdt` — ours | 0 | **64** |
| `sla_staff_animtest.gdt` — the harness, clones ours | 0 | **24** |

**Treyarch 68 of 68 are 0; ours 88 of 88 are 1.** No exception either side. Nor is
it "Treyarch always writes 0" — the five `ai_zm_dlc5_zombie_freeze_death_*` WORLD
anims in that same freezegun GDT are all `useBones 1`. The field tracks
viewmodel-vs-world exactly as documented. Driving the full skeleton from a
viewmodel clip transforms bones the view rig has no place for, and the mesh ends
up wrapped around the camera — the user's *"looking inside of something"* is
literally that.

**The linker's earlier `delta` complaint was the same bug wearing a different
hat**, not a second problem: the five root bones it named (`tag_camera`,
`j_shoulder_le`, `j_shoulder_ri`, `tag_weapon_left`, `tag_weapon_right`) are
exactly the bones a viewmodel set should not be driving.

**BEWARE THE AGGREGATE.** Scanning all 227 GDTs at once gives "vm_*: 68 zero vs
88 one" — which reads as no pattern at all, until you notice all 88 of the ones
are our own two files. Aggregating the wrong population turns a perfect signal
into noise. Break it down per file before concluding there is no rule.

- **Fixed at source**: 64 blocks in `tod_staff_anims.gdt` → `useBones "0"`, applied
  per-block so only `vm_*` names are touched, in all three copies (both repos and

## 2026-09-07 (v18.19) — TEST SESSION: god + unlimited money, WITHOUT the rest of dev

User: *"turn on god and dev mode as well"*, then immediately narrowed it —
*"dont give me all my upgrade. I just want the inlimited money and god mode."*

**`level.tod_dev` IS A BUNDLE, NOT A SWITCH**, and that is why it stays OFF.
Arming it also gives an upgrade event EVERY round, a Panzer from round 3 on a /3
interval, Reaver /2, a TIER card on EVERY deal and unlimited station uses. The
user asked for two of those and none of the rest — and the upgrade spam in
particular would drown the very thing being tested.

So the money loop moved onto its own flag. `level.tod_dev_money` tops every
player to 100,000 every 2s and does nothing else; `tod_dev` still implies it, so
no armed session loses anything.

**ARMED NOW: `tod_god` + `tod_dev_money`. `tod_dev` OFF.**

### The gate could not see the new flag

`build_map.ps1` scans the entry GSC for `level.tod_(dev|god)\s*=\s*true` — and
`tod_dev_money` does NOT match it, because `tod_dev` is followed by `_money`
rather than by `=`. A brand-new dev flag was therefore invisible to the publish
gate on the same build that introduced it. **A dev flag the gate cannot see is a
dev flag that ships.** Pattern is `tod_(dev\w*|god)` now, so any future
`tod_dev<anything>` is caught. Verified: the build prints both.

### Also worth knowing for the test

`tod_dev` off means TIER cards are 20% of deals and upgrade events are every 4th
round — so reaching MAGE tier 2 (FIRE BLAST, floor 10) and tier 3 (ICE SHATTER,
floor 30) is a real climb. The floor gate is deliberately NOT waived by dev.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.18) — THE THIRD CONTROL SET, THIRD ASK; AND THE SOLO QUICK REVIVE SIGN LOSES A RACE IT COULD NOT BE SEEN TO LOSE

(Written as v18.17 and lost to a concurrent write of this file by another
session at 13:25:58; re-filed as v18.18. The BUILD was unaffected — it was
already linked at 13:25:52 and its tree still matches the repo.)

Two reports, both repeats, both because a previous fix was aimed one level too
shallow.

### 1 · "I don't know how many times I have to ask for this"

User 2026-09-07: *"all I want is a KBM set and then a D pad and A set ... there's
a third one that comes up for left trigger, right trigger, and the a button. I
want that completely removed."* And the clarification that settles the design:
*"It's not that I don't want right trigger left trigger to be able to use for
controller. I just don't want the UI to say that."* **LT/RT keep working. They
may never be drawn.**

**v17.55 diagnosed this correctly and still missed it.** That pass established
the real mechanism — `Engine.Localize` expands a `[{+bind}]` token into the name
bound on the device the client is USING, so a pad player's offhand pair resolves
to "LT"/"RT", and a keycap layout then renders those pad words in keyboard art.
It put the read in `CoD.TodKeycap.PadDevice()` and had all three surfaces call
it. Sound.

**But every call site reaches it as `CoD.TodKeycap ~= nil and
CoD.TodKeycap.PadDevice() == true`** — and both card menus deliberately
`pcall`-require that widget, because a bare require that throws takes the whole
menu down silently. So if the require ever fails, the device test returns FALSE,
the pad player gets the keyboard layout, and the engine fills those caps with
LT / RT. *The guard against the third set lived inside the thing whose absence
causes the third set.* Same shape as the v13.5 Quick Revive gate two days ago: a
mechanism believed to be doing the work, never watched doing it.

**Now it is checked on the string, not on a belief.** `TodPadWord( tok )` is
twinned into both menus with no dependency on the widget (the same argument the
`TodKeycapMake` stub is built on, and stated there), and it is consulted twice:

* `UsingController()` gains a third arm, so a failed require can no longer
  resurrect the third set. Offhand pair only — A/B/X/Y are keyboard keys too, so
  `+gostand` can never decide the device.
* **`Paint()` asks it about the very token it is about to draw.** `pad` is a
  decision made once, further up; `TodPadWord( tok )` asks the only question that
  matters at the moment of drawing — *is this about to render as LT/RT?* — and if
  so paints the d-pad glyph instead. A stale latch, a failed require or a device
  switched mid-menu can no longer put a pad word on a keycap, **because the test
  is on the text**. The d-pad is a live input lane in both menus, so the glyph is
  always true.

**And the lines that ADVERTISED the extra lanes are cut.** The draft's pad line
read `SWITCH: D-PAD / STICK / LB / RB   LOCK: HOLD [ A ]` and the card panel's
read `SWITCH: D-PAD / LB / RB` — four and three inputs named for a one-button
decision, two of them the very words the user asked to stop seeing. Both now read
`SWITCH: D-PAD   LOCK: HOLD [ A ]`. Stick, bumpers, triggers, melee, reload and
WASD all still switch cards; the map's own standing rule is that a menu may
ACCEPT eight inputs and must ADVERTISE one.

### 2 · The Quick Revive sign still read 1500 — photographed on the build that fixed it

v18.15 wrote the price and re-stamped the hint **once**, and the user sent a
screenshot of the machine reading `1500` on the very next build. The charge was
already correct at 500; the sign was not, which is the half a player reads.

**It is a race, and one we cannot observe from inside.** Stock's stamp is the
LAST line of a long preamble in `vending_trigger_think`: after the Quick Revive
block waits for `start_zombie_round_logic`, after `SetHintString(
&"ZOMBIE_NEED_POWER" )`, and after a choke loop that waits **one network frame
per vending trigger** (`level._perkmachinenetworkchoke`). Our write is gated on
stock stamping `t.power_on` from a *different* thread. Which lands last depends
on machine count and frame timing — so a single write was a coin flip, and it
came up tails in play.

**So it is re-asserted rather than stamped.** Forty passes at 0.5 s = 20 s, far
past anything stock does at round-one init, then it stops. This costs **nothing**
against the 250-triggerstring cap: that cap counts DISTINCT STRINGS, and forty
writes of the same `(hint_string, 500)` pair are one slot — the same slot the
first write already took. `t.cost` is re-written each pass for the same reason;
it is the field the CHARGE reads.

`reset_vending_hint_string()` was checked as a possible later overwriter and has
**zero callers** in stock — it is dead, so the single stamp really is the only
competitor.

### 3 · The player notes were rewritten SHORT

User 2026-09-07: *"Can you simplify, SO much jargon and words for patch notes"*.
Fair — the Sep 7 section had grown to multi-sentence bullets explaining
mechanism. Rewritten to one plain line per change, keeping only numbers a player
feels. 26 bullets. docs/67 keeps the detail; docs/68 is for players.

⚠️ UNPLAYED. Files: `tod_class_select.lua`, `tod_upgrade.lua`,
`_tod_perk_lights.gsc`.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.17) — MAGE: five flags down to TWO, and the regression audit

User, on being told the mage was "behind one flag": *"Please make sure that all
the changes you're making are behind a singular flag that is false right now.
We're also working on fixing bugs for the production version to publish while
you're making changes, and we don't want those to intersect at all."* Then, on
being shown the audit: *"We can keep the code in as long as the scripts and
everything are behind a singular flag. And we arent causeing regressions for
other classes."*

**THE PREVIOUS ENTRIES OVERSTATED THE GATE.** v18.13–v18.16 reported "one flag".
There were FIVE literals in four files, and about a dozen edits behind NO flag at
all — inert by ARGUMENT, not by construction. The flag stopped the FEATURE; it
never stopped the CODE from shipping. Those are different claims and they got
merged into one.

### Now two literals, one per language, and two is the FLOOR

| literal | governs |
|---|---|
| `TOD_MAGE_ENABLED` (`_tod_mage.gsh`) | all GSC |
| `MAGE_ENABLED` (`tod_class_select.lua`) | all Lua |

`TOD_CLS_COUNT` is DERIVED now — `( 4 + TOD_MAGE_ENABLED )` — so it cannot
drift. The old comment called that form unprecedented; that was caution, not a
finding. Stock carries `#define FILTER_INDEX_VISION_PULSE FILTER_INDEX_GADGET`.
Confirmed by a real build: `_tod_class_select.gsc` compiled and packed with zero
entries in the linker errorlog.

Lua keeps its own literal ONLY because the draft geometry is computed at
file-parse time and the zone loads `tod_class_select.lua` (line 375) before
`TodKeycap.lua` (380) — a shared `CoD.*` flag would read nil there.

**`MAGE_ART` and `TOD_MAGE_ART` were DELETED, not asserted.** Each gated art
registration that cannot be switched on until the images are baked and zoned, so
both bought nothing today and cost two more literals. `build_map.ps1` now Dies
if a third Lua `MAGE_*` local reappears — that guard's first pattern matched
`IMAGE` ("I-MAGE") and failed the build on `CARD_ONE_IMAGE`; tightened.

### The regression audit — checked, not asserted

- **Five extra domains do NOT shift card RNG.** Every pool filters first and then
  picks; there is no `RandomInt` over the raw domain array anywhere.
- **`random_class_key()` is equivalent.** `register_class` is the only
  construction site and defaults `draftable` true, so all four classes stay
  draftable and key order is preserved.
- **The draft geometry is pixel-identical**, diffed against HEAD: `xLo + 73,`
  `xLo + 137` both ways, `CCARD_Y0/Y1 = 210, 525` both ways.
- The three damage-path arms guard on fields nothing writes while gated off.

### A process failure worth recording

The derived define was edited into shared source **while the user's own full
build was running**, so their build consumed it untested. It compiled — but that
was luck, not method. Worse, the comment shipped beside it claimed "it was tried,
it compiles, and the map builds" when nothing had been built yet. **A claim that
is lucky is indistinguishable from a claim that is checked, until the day it is
not.** Check for a running build stage before editing shared files.

### HEALING AURA — domain 52, `mage_heal`, six levels, band A, mage-only

The fourth combat-stance cast and the only one that is not an element. Ten pulses
over five seconds from an aura LINKED TO THE CASTER, healing every living teammate
inside it; radius 256→416, total heal 40→120% of each target's OWN max health,

with DAMAGE REDUCTION capped at 3 — both the user's calls — so its counterweight
has to be draftable from the first card, not the second staff.

Reuses `tod_upgrades::trickle_heal()` rather than writing health itself; that

### The art sweep — five families, not the one that was asked for

Enumerating every image name in `ui/` and `zone_source/` carrying a class key found
**three per-class families nobody had counted**: the small class glyph, the HUD
medallion (which every teammate also wears), and the class name plate on the upgrade
panel. Plus `i_tod_hud_gun_*`, keyed on the WEAPON — three staffs, three icons —
which is only reachable through a runtime-constructed name and so could never have
been reported missing by any lint.

Request: **docs/116**, out as `~/Downloads/tod_mage_class_art_pack.zip`, 13 files.

### Two real wiring bugs the sweep caught, both fixed

- **`if ci >= 1 and ci <= 4`** on the upgrade panel's class badge would have hidden
  the mage's plate silently. The table is the authority now; the clamp is gone.
- **`for c = 1, 4` over a hardcoded `TCLS`** would have left a live mage with no tier
  cards. Both now follow the table.

### A fourth Lua flag, deliberately NOT a fourth gate literal

`MAGE_ART` in `tod_upgrade.lua` guards the tier cards' CONSTRUCTED name, which
`lint_tod_assets` cannot see. It asks "is the art zoned", not "is the class on" —
different questions, and art may legitimately lag the class. `build_map.ps1` asserts
only the combination that is always wrong: **art on with the class off**, i.e. 3.4 MB
of load RAM per card for a class nobody can draft.

**GATE A IS FLAG-BLIND, and it cost a build to learn.** The class badge plate was
first written as a literal inside `if MAGE_ART then`; the lint failed it anyway,
because it strips comments, ignores flags, and only asks whether a literal `i_tod_*`
string has a zone line. **A literal image name cannot be in the file at all until its
zone line is** — the tier cards escape only because their name is built at runtime,
which is the other half of the same trap.

All lints green: arity across 75 files, Lua 46 files 0 findings, assets **43 live

**Still unplayed**, like everything else in the mage tree.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.15) — MY OWN REGRESSION, ONE BUILD OLD: v18.14 made solo Quick Revive unbuyable before power

User 2026-09-07, having played v18.14: *"You should be able to buy a quick revive
before turning on power on the solo. It should still be five hundred, and it
should still work ... now when I play, I cannot buy a quick revive before the
power is on. So that's a new regression just introduced."*

Correct on every count. v18.14 fixed the right bug and shipped a behaviour change
nobody asked for, in the same diff.

**WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE REASONING, because the code fix is trivial and the
mistake is not.** v18.14 correctly established that `t.power_on = false` never
refused a sale — it armed stock's post-purchase `perk_pause`, so the perk was
sold and revoked a second later. The fix for THAT is a single non-write: stop
writing the field. Instead v18.14 asked "what was the gate *trying* to do?",
found this file's own header asserting the map rule *"every perk dark and
unbuyable until the switch"*, and built a real gate to satisfy it —
`TriggerEnable( false )` until power.

**That header was a stale design note, and I treated it as the requirement.**
The user's actual rule is stock's: solo Quick Revive is self-powered from spawn,
buyable at 500, and classic-zombies tradition. Nobody had asked for it to be
gated in over a year of the map's life; v13.5 inferred it from a general
statement about perk machines, and v18.14 inherited the inference without ever
checking it against a person. **A bug that has been live for ten days does not
license a behaviour change smuggled in beside its fix** — the fix and the
redesign should have been separate, and only the fix was wanted.

**Now:** no gate of any kind. The lane is a PRICE FIX, renamed
`solo_qr_price_fix()` so the name cannot mislead the next reader the way the old
one misled me. It does exactly three things, all of which have to wait for
stock's one-shot stamps:

* **the charge** — `t.cost = 500`, because `revive_cost_override()` runs while
  `GetPlayers().size` is still 0, reads as "not solo", and LATCHES 1500 onto the
  trigger (`_zm_perks.gsc` ~:496-500). Stock's repricer only runs from the
  hot-join check, a no-op in solo.
* **the sign** — the buy hint is stamped ONCE (~:528-531) from that same 1500
  local and never re-stamped, so v13.6 corrected the charge and left the sign
  lying. Re-stamped with the same `hint_string` and 500.
* **the mesh** — a machine you can use should not look switched off.
  `coherence_pass` already lights it from the true `.power_on`; the explicit
  `SetModel` just makes it immediate.

`.power_on` is left TRUE where stock stamps it
(`_zm_perk_quick_revive.gsc:202`), and there is now a comment saying never to
write it false here again. That single non-write is the entire fix for the
original report.

**AND THE v18.14 LATCH IS RETIRED WHOLE.** `level.tod_qr_gated_dark` existed
only so the machine would read dark while that version held it unbuyable.
`coherence_pass` is back to plain
`powered = ( lvl_powered || IS_TRUE( t.power_on ) )`. Half a retirement leaves a
dead field that still looks load-bearing — this map's own standing rule.

**Net effect for a solo player, versus the SHIPPED Workshop build:** Quick Revive
is buyable at the base from round 1 exactly as it always was, it costs 500, the
sign finally says 500, and — the actual fix — it is not taken back off you a
second later, so you get your self-revive and your last stand.

⚠️ **UNPLAYED at the time of writing.** The regression it reverts was caught in
play within an hour of v18.14 being built, which is the only reason it did not
ship. Files: `_tod_perk_lights.gsc` only.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.14) — SOLO QUICK REVIVE WAS SOLD AND THEN SILENTLY TAKEN BACK: the pre-power gate never blocked a sale, it poisoned one

Workshop, fckspencer 2026-09-07: *"quick revive not working on solo. panzer comes
and eats my ass and i just die, no effect from quick revive"*. It was ours, it
had been live since v13.6 (2026-08-28), and it is the worst shape a bug can
take — the player pays, the icon lights, and the thing does nothing.

**ONE FIELD, TWO MEANINGS.** v13.5 wanted this map's rule ("every perk dark and
unbuyable until the switch") to cover solo Quick Revive, which stock
deliberately exempts — `_zm_perk_quick_revive.gsc:165-168` skips the power wait
in solo and stamps the triggers powered at `:202`. The gate expressed that by
writing `t.power_on = false` on the vending trigger, on the belief that the field
"drives stock's native refusal AND the kit's Power Required card". **It drives
neither.**

* The buy loop (`_zm_perks.gsc:537-609`) tests HasPerk, `custom_perk_validation`,
  points and the perk limit. It **never reads `.power_on`**. The sale completes.
* `.power_on` is read in one place that matters — the last lines of
  `vending_trigger_post_think` (`:659-665`): *"Check If Perk Machine Was Powered
  Down While Drinking, If So Pause The Perks"* → `wait 1; perk_pause(...)` →
  `UnsetPerk` on every player.
* The real gate is somewhere else entirely: `vending_trigger_think` parks on
  `level waittill( perk + "_power_on" )` (`:502-505`) before it ever enters the
  buy loop. That park is the thing stock skips for solo QR, and nothing here
  ever put it back.

So the sequence for every solo player who bought Quick Revive before flipping
the power switch — which is the standard opening, because QR is the cheapest buy
on the map at 500 and the power door is 750:

1. 500 points charged.
2. `give_quick_revive_perk` runs: `self.lives = 1`, `level.solo_lives_given++`.
3. One second later `perk_pause` UnsetPerks it. `.lives` stays 1 —
   `take_quick_revive_perk` has an **empty body**, so nothing clears it.
4. The player now has a life they cannot spend. `player_laststand`
   (`_zm.gsc:2521-2527`) needs `lives > 0` **AND** `HasPerk(PERK_QUICK_REVIVE)`;
   the second is false, so the 10-second self-revive never threads.
5. `_zm.gsc:5425`'s `solo_death` takes its `!HasPerk` arm → `:5449-5459` →
   `level notify( "end_game" )`. **No last stand at all. Instant game over.**
6. Re-buying is refused too (`has_perk_paused`, `:545`) — deny sound, no perk,
   500 points already gone — and one of solo's **three lifetime** revives is
   spent for nothing.

And the HUD icon stays lit throughout: `AetheriumPerksContainer.lua:44` draws on
`perkStatus > 0`, and PERK_STATE_PAUSED is 2. That is why the report says "no
effect" rather than "it disappeared".

**THIS MAP HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THIS BUG UP AND STILL WALKED INTO IT.**
`_tod_perk_phd.gsc`'s `install_machine_kvps` block describes
`vending_trigger_post_think:661` UnsetPerk-ing PhD one second after you drink it,
for exactly this reason — three days before the gate was written. It was
recorded as a **PhD symptom**, never as a rule about the field, so the field was
then used as a gate. *A postmortem that names only the symptom does not stop the
next use of the cause.*

**THE FIX IS THE ONE STOCK USES ON THIS EXACT ENTITY.**
`_zm_perk_quick_revive::disable_quickrevive` shuts the QR trigger off with
`TriggerEnable( false )`, so that is what the gate does now — taken off the air
as its first act, restored at the switch. No prompt, no sale, no charge, nothing
to revoke, and `.power_on` is left TRUE where stock put it so the post-purchase
pause can never arm.

Two consequences had to be handled, and finding them is why this is not a
one-line diff:

* **The mesh was riding on the same field.** `coherence_pass` decides dark-vs-lit
  with `powered = ( lvl_powered || IS_TRUE( t.power_on ) )` — so the poison was
  also the only thing keeping the machine wearing its unpowered model. Dropped
  naively, solo QR would sit **lit and humming with no prompt**, which reads as
  broken where dark reads as locked. The gate now raises its own
  `level.tod_qr_gated_dark` and `coherence_pass` honours it. One field, one
  meaning.
* **The sign has been lying since v13.6.** Stock stamps the buy hint **once**
  (`_zm_perks.gsc:528-531`) with the cost local it captured before its power
  park, and for solo QR that local is **1500** — `revive_cost_override()` ran
  while `GetPlayers().size` was still 0 and read as "not solo". v13.6 corrected
  the CHARGE (`t.cost = 500`) and never the SIGN, which is the half the player
  reads. The gate re-stamps the same `hint_string` with 500 at the switch. One
  extra distinct triggerstring for the match (lint: 95 of 190 budgeted).

**AND A FREE QUICK REVIVE NO LONGER SPENDS A LIFETIME LIFE.** The perk bottle
(`_tod_powerups::tod_give_random_map_perk`) pools every sellable machine, so in
solo it can roll Quick Revive — and every grant, bought or not, runs
`level.solo_lives_given++` and at 3 sets the `solo_revive` flag that flies the
base machine away **for the rest of the match**. Three lucky bottles retired the
machine for a player who had never bought it once. Stock ships the opt-out for
precisely this (*"Sometimes we want to give the quick revive and not take a use
away"*) and the hook consumes it, so it cannot leak into the next purchase.
Solo only; in co-op the whole ledger is inert.
*(The spire's `perma_perks_give` was checked for the same defect and deliberately
left alone: it only runs after the tower is torn down, so the counter it moves
governs a machine that no longer exists.)*

**A CHANGE THAT WAS MADE, PROVEN WRONG AND REVERTED IN THE SAME PASS — recorded
because the reasoning was persuasive and will recur.** `boss_player_damage`
opens with `is_player_valid( self )`, whose omitted third argument makes it
return false for a crawler; so the whole callback — the Panzer halving, the
hound cut, the Rogue Protector damage cap, the through-wall and through-floor
shields, DR, SPRINT ARMOR, BACK ARMOR — is skipped for a downed player. That
was read as "a downed solo player takes raw uncapped boss damage and dies inside
the ten-second revive", it fit the report exactly, and it was wrong: **stock
zeroes it.** `_zm.gsc:5136-5140`, *"Sledgehammer fix for Issue 43492. This should
stop the player from taking any damage while in laststand"*, a bare
`if ( self laststand::player_is_in_laststand() ) return 0;` twenty-six lines
below the callback chain. Nothing below that guard could ever reach a crawler.
The search that produced the error was itself sound — `Callback_PlayerDamage`
(`:1415-1567`) genuinely contains no last-stand early-out — and the mistake was
reading one function's silence as the system's. Worse, the "fix" was a small
regression: the first statement past the guard is the `tod_dealt_ms` stamp, so
a Panzer swinging at a body would have counted as engaged and stopped being
eligible for the stuck-watch to move it along — leaving it parked on the player
for the getup. Reverted; the site now carries the finding and a pointer to
`_zm.gsc:5136`.

**Also, in dead code:** the Mage's FIRE burn tell set `arch_actor_fire_fx` to 1.
v18.12 established twelve hours earlier that state 1 builds its FX key with a
`_loop` postfix that stock defines no entries for, and renders **nothing** on a
zombie; state 2 is the one with real sources. Corrected now while the class is
still flagged off and the line has never executed.

Files: `_tod_perk_lights.gsc` (the gate, the dark latch, the hint re-stamp,
`coherence_pass`), `_tod_powerups.gsc` (the bottle's free-grant opt-out),
`_tod_bosses.gsc` (revert + the finding), `_tod_mage_elements.gsc` (1 -> 2).
GSC-only in content, but this ships as a FULL publish build.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.13) — THE MAGE: a fifth class, built whole and shipped OFF

User 2026-09-07: *"build out the class, prepare it, get it ready ... even if you
can wire up all the implementation as well and everything, we're not gonna
enable it yet at all."* So this is the entire class — registry, draft card,
domains, ladder, runtime module — behind one flag, and the flag is 0.

**THE GATE IS THREE LITERALS IN TWO LANGUAGES, and the build script refuses to
let them disagree.** `TOD_MAGE_ENABLED` and `TOD_CLS_COUNT` live in the new
`scripts/zm/zm_tower_of_doom/_tod_mage.gsh`; `MAGE_ENABLED` lives in
`tod_class_select.lua`, because Lua cannot read a GSC define. Every disagreement
is SILENT — GSC on / Lua off draws four cards over a five-class draft and the
mage is unpickable with no error anywhere — so `build_map.ps1` hard-Dies on any
mismatch and refuses `-Publish` while the flag is 1.

**Proven inert, not assumed inert.** With the flag off: `register_class` never
runs, so `level.tod_class_count` is still 4 and no shipped class id moves; the
three staff rungs are `enabled: MAGE_ON` so the generator emits no GDT block, no
zone line, no CSV row and **zero registrations** — it still prints
`201 generated + 28 fixed = 229 (guard 229)`, and a second run is byte-identical;
the four domains are registered but carry `class_keys array( "mage" )`, and no
player can hold `"mage"`, so `domain_available` returns false before anything
else is read. The one measurable delta is four zero entries in each player's
`tod_levels` from the zero-fill. Nothing reads them.

**What the class is** (docs/114): three staff tiers that are Treyarch's own
Origins kit getting richer — shaft / shaft + tip / shaft + upgraded tip, 6
registrations at `axes: []`. A base attack from the draft. **AIR, FIRE and ICE
earned as upgrade cards, six levels each**, unlocked by staff tier through a new
`set_tier_min()` — a FLOOR, not `set_guns`, because `gun_keys` binds to the
current stem and would REVOKE air on promotion. Each element doubles against the
family it answers: fire vs Panzers and Rogue Protectors, ice vs hellhounds and
armored sprinters, air vs the horde. **ATTUNEMENT** (max 5, the shared
`ladder5()`) is the class's only throughput knob and the one card that scales all
three at once. Damage reduction caps at **3** for the mage and damage at 10, both
as the user asked. Move speed 0.85.

**Ids 48–51, and 52/53 are reserved** for LEVITATION and CONDUIT. All four sit
above `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX 47`, so they draw as text rows and owe no plate; none has
a `CARD_SLUG`, so none owes a card until the art lands (`docs/115`, pack already
sent). All four are `set_no_dark` — a dark card whose lane does not read
`has_dark()` is a card that does nothing, silently.

**The runtime module `_tod_mage_elements.gsc` has never executed** and every
number in it is unplayed. It honours four contracts that each have a wrong
obvious version: the damage lane is an ARM on `upgrade_damage_cb` (not a second
callback, which would only run where the first returns -1); `DoDamage`'s 7th
parameter is `dflags`, not a bone index; the armored sprinter is `tod_is_sprinter`
and is deliberately NOT in the `is_boss` triad, so `is_boss_or_elite()` would
skip it; and `tod_zombie_speed::slow()` owns its own boss refusal, which must not
be relaxed. **The Panzer arm is not optional** — stock's `mechzDamageCallback`
falls off the end of its hitloc/MOD ladder and literally returns 0 for a
`MOD_UNKNOWN` script `DoDamage`, so without it FIRE does nothing to the one enemy
it exists for.

Three edits touch live hot paths (`upgrade_damage_cb`, the Panzer wrap,
`grant_elite_reward`). Each is one `isdefined` on a field nothing writes while
the class is off.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.12) — TRAILBLAZER stops borrowing the Nuke: the burn tell moves to the corpse-burn lane

User 2026-09-07: *"for trail blazer we give them the nuke effect. Can we give
them something else."* Then, given the catalogue: *"Lets do 3 Corpse burn"*.

The tell was v16.87's explicit ask — *"reusing what nuke has sfx and fx would be
great"* — and it worked too well: it incremented `zm_nuked`, the nuke's own actor
clientfield, and played `evt_nuked`, the nuke's own per-zombie sound, so a trail
kill read as somebody having pulled a Nuke.

Now `arch_actor_fire_fx` = **2** (BURN_CORPSE), slot 3 of test+map's zombie
effect catalogue (`docs/02_zombie_effect_catalog.md`).

### Four things were verified before a line was written, and each was a real question

* **Registered?** Yes, in both VMs, and nothing is owed for it: an autoexec
  register in `shared/ai/archetype_damage_effects`, pulled in by
  `archetype_shared` from `_load` in both entry scripts, resident in the
  `core_patch` base zone. **Do not register it ourselves** (a duplicate register
  is the load-abort hazard) and **do not zone its FX** — zoning stock effects is
  how this map once inherited a 5,092-byte stub over a working stock one.
  Clinching proof it works here: `mechz_spiki.gsc:927` already sets this exact
  field for the Panzer's napalm zombies, and that ships.
* **Value 2 and not 1.** Value 1 (BURN_BODY) builds its FX key with a `_loop`
  postfix and stock defines no `fire_zombie_*_loop` entries at all — it renders
  **nothing** on a zombie. Value 2 takes `_os`, and those ten keys exist,
  aliasing the human fire set (torso, arms, hips, knees, head) with real .efx
  sources rather than placeholders.
* **⚠️ It is an "int", not a "counter" — which is why the tell is now ONE-SHOT.**
  An int clientfield is delta-driven: setting 2 on a zombie already holding 2
  sends nothing. A drop-in swap of the old 3 s cadence would have fired **once
  per zombie and been silently inert forever after** — a bug only visible in
  play. Re-firing would need `set(0)`, a snapshot's wait, then `set(2)`, which
  fights BURN_CORPSE's own 20 s cleanup and re-runs the char ramp each time. The
  cadence was never needed for persistence anyway: one set lights a 10 s burn
  loop and holds its FX for 20 s, far longer than a body survives standing in
  fire. So each zombie lights **once**, and the stock lane runs.
  `TOD_TRAIL_BURN_TELL_MS` is retired with it; the per-tick ignition cap stays,
  so a train through the fire is still a few bodies going up, not a wall.
* **The sound.** BURN_CORPSE starts `chr_burn_npc_loop1` on the victim itself
  and stops it on a 10 s timer, so the sustained burn needs nothing from us and a
  server loop would only double it. The ignition cue is `tod_trail_sizzle` — a
  3D non-looping alias that has sat in this map's own `tod_ui.csv` since v16.79
  with **nothing playing it**. The trail now sounds like the trail.

### The dissent, recorded because it may be right in play

One of the four verifications came back **against** this change. Its argument:
the corpse-burn look is the sparser one-shot ember set plus an instant permanent
char, where the nuke lane is a fuller sustained fire — so the *visual* may be a
downgrade — and the "someone got a nuke" read was carried mostly by the **sound**,
which the one-line `evt_nuked` → `tod_trail_sizzle` swap fixes on its own.

That is a fair reading and it is a play question, not a source question. The
user's instruction was explicit, and the revert is small and isolated: put
`clientfield::increment( "zm_nuked" )` back in place of the `set`, keep the new
sound, and restore the cadence guard. **Judge it in game.**

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` green across 74 files. The stale cross-reference in
`zm_tower_of_doom.csc` (which still explained TRAILBLAZER as riding the nuke
field) was updated with it. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-07 (v18.11) — CONCURRENCY GOES PARTY-AWARE, AND RAMPAGE BECOMES THE HARD MODE

User 2026-09-07: *"People are seriously complaining about the difficulty. Is
there a limit of zombies on map by players?"* — then, given the answer:
*"I want rampage to be the difficult mode. People are actually pretty bad ...
Can we change the zombie speed as well? Can we have rampage vs regular values?"*

### The answer to the question was NO, and that was the problem

`level.zombie_ai_limit` was a **flat 45 for one player or four**. Stock's
default is 24 solo. So a solo player held **~1.9x stock concurrency** and **four
times the per-player pressure of a quad** (45 each against 11.25 each), on an
open staircase 160 units wide with a drop on one side.

**And elites do not count toward it** — every elite sets
`ignore_enemy_count`, so 45 was trash zombies ONLY, with the Panzer,
Protectors, Reavers, hounds and sprinters all standing on top of it.

`ai_limit_for_party()` in `_tod_corpse_cleanup.gsc` (the file that owns the
field) now returns **30 / 35 / 40 / 45**, kept in step by a 2 s watcher that
writes only on a change. The quad number is untouched on purpose: 45 is the
figure the user asked for by name on 2026-08-25 and the only party size with
play evidence behind it.

**v18.1's own audit recorded this row as "24 solo / 9.3 trio"** — figures
computed from `coop_ai_limit()`, which had been dead since v10.26. The number
that most defines solo pressure was mis-recorded in the pass written to relieve
solo.

### RAMPAGE keeps every pre-relief value

The ask was for rampage to be the hard mode. **No new rampage buff was invented**
— rampage simply keeps the numbers the map already shipped with, so the gap
widens by itself and hard mode is tuning that has actually been played:

| Lever | Base | Rampage |
|---|---|---|
| Zombies at once | 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 by party | **45 flat** |
| Speed climb past full sprint | 0.21%/round (v18.2) | **0.28%/round** (pre-v18.2) |

At solo that is 30 against 45 the moment the breaker is thrown — the single
biggest difficulty step in the map, and the player chooses it. The speed gap
widens with depth: round 50 is 1.067x full sprint against 1.090x; round 80 is
1.130x against 1.174x.

`zspeed_step()` resolves the tail the same way `full_round()` already resolved
the ramp — through a function, so the two branches cannot drift.

### What was deliberately NOT touched

* **`TOD_ZSPEED_FULL_ROUND` (18).** Its own block says 18 is the END of that
  lever — pushing it further makes the per-round increment so small the early
  game stops escalating at all — and names `TOD_ZSPEED_STEP` and
  `TOD_ZSPEED_START_RATE` as the next levers instead. That advice was followed,
  not overridden.
* **`TOD_ZSPEED_START_RATE` (0.8).** It is the remaining base lever if solo
  still reads hard after a play test. Stacking a third speed nerf blind risks
  over-correcting.
* **Horde health.** v18.1 already removed the solo surcharge.

⚠️ **THIS IS THE THIRD SOLO NERF IN THREE VERSIONS** and none has been played:
v18.1 cut the elite roof 12 -> 5 and dropped the solo health surcharge, v18.9
fixed the hound director that was quietly defeating that roof, and now
concurrency. If solo reads too easy, **this ladder is the first thing to walk
back** — concurrency is the lever a player feels most directly and it moved last.

### Retired whole

`coop_ai_limit()` and its three defines are **deleted**, not left inert. Party-
aware concurrency is back in the owning file, and a dormant second implementation
with different numbers is exactly the drift the surrounding comments spent forty
lines warning about — it is a LOOP, so if anyone ever re-threaded it, it would
win. One clause was deliberately not ported: its finale clamp to 27, whose
premise (stock's 31-actor gate) retired when `TOD_ACTOR_LIMIT` went to 60 with
corpse deletion behind it.

Three comments in other files that quoted the flat 45 as a live fact were
refreshed to name the function instead.

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` green across 74 files, which also proves nothing still calls
the deleted function. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-07 (v18.10) — THE FINAL-PASS ART LANDED: UNPACKED on all eight tier cards, and the luck bar finally says what it is for

The docs/113 pack came back (`files - 2026-09-07T020147`). Nine images installed,
two of them chosen from variants the generator supplied rather than the ones
first specified — both times because the generator was right and the brief was
wrong about the geometry.

### The eight TIER cards

`i_tod_card_tier_{skirmisher,assault,heavy,slasher}_{2,3}.png`, same names, so no
wiring. Each now carries a single caution word, **UNPACKED**, in the card's own
outlined display face on a dark amber-red plate.

**THE BRIEF SPECIFIED A GAP THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and the generator measured it
rather than guessing.** It asked for a 620x76 strip between the weapon-name plate
and the pip row; on the reference cards that gap is **16 px tall** (name-plate
border ends y 988, pip row starts y 1004). Every pixel of pip padding yields
about 26 px — a 17 px cap, ~5 px on screen, i.e. illegible, which fails the
brief's own top rule.

**Shipped: the strip inside the weapon screen's lower edge** (500x76 at y 606,
54 px cap). That contradicts the brief's "never take space from the weapon
screen", and it is the right call — checked at the real 234x351 display size the
word is unmistakable, and the weapon art still reads fully above it.
`_alt_in_panel/` (the strip in the requested place, pip row nudged 10 px) was
rejected on legibility. Verified by the generator across all 16 files: zero
pixels differ from the originals outside the strip's own zone.

### The luck legend — NEW image, fully wired

`i_tod_luck_legend.png`, 420x90 drawn 280x60, reading **BETTER CARDS**. It sits
directly under the luck badge on the deal panel and captions it.

**THE NEUTRAL (steel) VARIANT SHIPPED, not the amber one**, and this is the part
worth recording: the brief told the generator to match "the badge's amber
palette", and the generator's notes point out that **amber is the badge's
FULL-VALUE STATE, not its chassis** — at 100% the border, clover and number are
gold; at 50% they are green. The fixed chassis is the pill, the black keyline,
the navy plate and the white type. A gold caption would therefore have looked
correct at exactly one luck value. The steel border sits right at every value.
(The generator also dropped the optional chevron glyph: it crowded the words at
280x60. Correct call, same rule.)

Wiring, all three lanes:
* GDT block cloned from `i_tod_badge_luck_100` (same 420x90 uncompressed chassis)
* `image,i_tod_luck_legend` in the zone — **without this the linker is silent
  and the game draws a white square**; the asset lint's Gate A exists for exactly
  this and now counts 574 zoned images, up from 573
* `tod_upgrade.lua`: `USE_LUCK_LEGEND_ART`, registered in the CARD_SET block,
  placed at x 950..1230 / y 214..274 — the badge's own box width and height, so
  the pair stacks as one unit and the art keeps its aspect exactly. Clear of
  everything: the cards start at CARD_Y0 226 but are centred (cx +/- 117), the
  LuckLine band ends at 212, the CLASS badge is the far-left mirror.

It shows and hides **with the badge** — it is a caption, and a caption under
nothing is noise.

### Why this needed a FULL build

A `.gdt` edit and a new image: `-GscOnly` skips cod2map and the LED bake, and
per-asset conversion coverage under it is unproven. Proof of landing is a fresh
content-hash `.iwi` beside an untouched control, never a raw `.ff` grep.

`lint_tod_lua.js` green (46 files, pause-row widths included), `lint_tod_assets.js`
green with the new zone line counted. Every delivered PNG was opened and read at
full size AND at its real on-screen size before installing; the baked text is
exactly `UNPACKED` and `BETTER CARDS` with nothing else added. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-07 (v18.9) — THE FINAL PASS: nine fixes where a shipped feature did nothing, plus the Workshop description that never parsed

The 106-agent pre-publish audit (player-report triage over the 130-comment
Workshop thread + eight code lenses, every finding adversarially refuted: 80
verdicts, 57 upheld, 23 killed). User 2026-09-07: *"lets fix all of this ... if
the risk is low and we can easily fix with no gameplay changes or regressions
lets do it"*, and on Widow's Wine: *"Dogs dont trigger widows wine ...
protectors have the same gap as dogs. Go ahead and implement that."*

Every item below is a case where **a shipped feature currently does nothing, or
a surface tells the player something untrue**. Nothing here is a redesign, and
the one real fix with regression risk (the boss-behind-an-unbought-door zone
overlap) was deliberately LEFT OUT at the user's instruction.

### 1 · WIDOW'S WINE: an elite that cannot be webbed no longer spends a grenade

Workshop, CZ 2026-09-06: *"dogs are taking all widows nades before i can even
kill them"*. Traced end to end, and it is **not a hound bug**: stock's contact
web is delivered through the zombie-damage callback lane, which is threaded from
`zm_spawner::enemy_death_detection` — and that only runs for actors registered
through a stock SPAWNER. This map `SpawnActor`s its elites directly, so the
**Panzer, the Rogue Protector and the hellhound have never been webbable by
anything**. The Reaver is the sole exception (its vendored pack threads the lane
itself) and is deliberately untouched; the Armored Sprinter is a promoted horde
zombie and keeps the lane too.

`ww_attacker_unwebbable()` in `_tod_perk_widows.gsc`, tested in
`ww_contact_web_wrapper` **before** the proc roll so these three neither spend a
charge nor consume the coin flip.

**THE COST, stated because it is a trade and not a free win:** the delegated call
also burst-webbed the ordinary zombies *around* the player, so being hit by one
of these three used to buy a panic cocoon of the surrounding horde at the price
of a grenade. That panic button is gone for them. Corrected from the audit's
first write-up: it was **75% of melee hits, not every bite** (the map's own coin
flip sits in front of it).

### 2 · Dark BULLET FEED was worth 0.05%

`_tod_upgrades.gsc`. The dark step only lowered the clamp *floor* and never
scaled the interval. At the cap `iv = 1.0 − 0.0889×9 = 0.1999`, already above
the dark floor 0.142857, so the clamp never fired: **5.003 rounds/s against the
plain card's 5.000**, while the pause row advertised twice the rate. The comment
three lines above names this exact trap ("the same trap as THOR'S THUNDER's
cooldown") and then falls into it. Now scales the value AND lowers the floor,
matching `thor_cooldown_ms`, which does it right.

Safe at every level because `dark_pool` only offers a MAXED domain and
`tier_up` clears the dark bit in lockstep with the level.

### 3 · Dark RUN AND GUN paid half the card

The domain has two halves in two files. The free-shot half took its dark step on
2026-09-05; the damage half never did, so `TOD_DARK_RNG_ADD` sat with **zero
readers** while the pause row advertised +100% against a delivered 52%. Added
**inside** the `if ( moving )` branch — outside it, dark RUN AND GUN would have
paid bonus damage standing still, which is the one thing this domain must never
do. *(This was item 3 of the `changelog-is-not-the-code` memory, open two days.)*

### 4 · The co-op card panel's one advertised control threw your grenade

The panel draws `[{+smoke}] < SWITCH > [{+frag}]` unconditionally, and the focus
lane's comment asserted that `menu_freeze` held `DisableOffhandWeapons()` so a
press could never throw one — true in the FROZEN lane, false in the co-op
station arm, which was `AllowJump( false )` and nothing else. Switching cards in
co-op lobbed a lethal and a tactical. Live from any Max Ammo onward, and
immediately with Widow's Wine or DISTRACTION's monkey.

Now takes the offhands alongside jump, and **guards the give-back twice**: not
while `tod_menu_frozen` (a round event can take the UI over and freeze the
player before this lane's 0.05 s poll wakes) and not to a player in last stand
(`solo_present_interruptible` returns from inside it; the 2026-08-26 audit fixed
this identical shape in `menu_freeze` — *"left them hopping around while
crawling"* — and the altars sit on open balconies and the crown terrace).

A small, deliberate softening of the co-op risk model: you still fight while you
choose, you just keep your grenades.

### 5 · A scheduled Panzer could drop into a sealed trial hall

`level.tod_king_active` was **written and never read anywhere in the tree** — the
comment claiming this director read it was fiction. So a Panzer debt banked
before a trial seal was spent on the next 3 s tick, inside the sealed hall: not
stamped `tod_spire_guard`, so it paid the 1000-point boss jackpot and a
guaranteed Max Ammo mid-holdout, and `trial_wardens` counts by
`level.tod_panzer_alive`, so it was read AS the Warden and suppressed the
redrop.

Gated **only the Panzer branch** on `!tod_trial_active` — never the whole loop,
because the protector branch below it *delivers the trials' adds* (trial I is
prot 2 / reaver 0 / hound 0; a `continue` would have run it with no adds at
all). Plus `level.tod_panzer_debt = 0` at `trial_run`'s seal (`king_run`
already did this) and in `king_win` — without the latter, a boss round passing
during the King fight dropped an ordinary Panzer onto the summit deck the moment
he died, under his own victory banner.

### 6 · Killing the Warden King stranded the spire gauge at EMPTY

`king_hp_bar` and `king_run` watch the same boss on different periods with no
ordering: the bar polls at 0.2 s and ends by writing 0, `king_run` polls at
0.25 s and calls `king_win`, which clears the field to `undefined`. Waits
quantize to the 50 ms frame, so 0.2/0.25 are 4 and 5 frames — `king_run` won
outright in 6 cases of 20 with 4 more same-frame ties, i.e. **roughly a third to
a half of King kills** left the field at 0. `_tod_gauge` shadows on
`isdefined`, not on a value, so the bar stayed empty for the rest of the run and
took the boss pip and all four teammate-down cells with it.

`level endon( "tod_king_end" )` — `king_win` notifies it six lines before it
clears the field. An endon is right *here* because this thread needs no cleanup;
contrast item 7.

### 7 · The ASCEND trigger stayed live for 6 seconds after the party EXTRACTED

`_tod_finale.gsc` states the contract — *"each retires the other by notify"* —
and only one direction was ever wired. A second player's hold landing inside
`depart()`'s 6-second send-off fired `tod_ascend`, teleported the party to the
spire and tore down the tower, and then the departure timer ended the match with
YOU ESCAPED THE TOWER over a world they had been dropped into two seconds
earlier — costing them the entire post-victory mode. Co-op only.

`choice_extract_retire()`, a small thread spawned beside the trigger, and
**not** an `endon` on `choice_watch`: a thread killed by endon runs no cleanup
(this repo's own rule), which would have stranded the "ASCEND — one way, no
return" prompt on screen for the whole send-off. The retirer clears the string
and disables the trigger; a disabled trigger cannot notify, which is what
actually closes the race.

### 8 · The hound director bypassed v18.1's elite roof

`hound_elite_roof()` returned `8 + players` (9/10/11/12), tuned against the
retired flat 12, while every other director calls
`tod_bosses::elite_roof_all()`. v18.1 lowered the shared roof to 5/7/9/11 as a
**solo relief** pass and this function quietly kept solo at 9 — about **80% of
that pass eroded at solo** and 9% at quad, the exact inversion of the intent.
Hounds also never read `level.tod_trial_reserve`, so the Wardens' first claim
did not hold in THE KENNEL, the one trial where it matters most.

Now returns the shared roof. `elite_roof_all()` and **not**
`!elites_over_roof()`, which carries a finale exemption that would have removed
the hounds' only combined ceiling on the crown road. `TOD_HOUND_ELITE_ROOF`
retired with it.

### 9 · Every hellhound healed to full 2 seconds after it spawned

`hound_tune` unconditionally re-wrote `health` and `maxhealth` after its wait
— by then a **full heal of everything the player did in the hound's first ~1.3 s
of visible life**. It also cleared stock's damage-driven run flag
(`self.health < self.maxhealth`), so a hound you had hurt stopped being flagged
"needs to run". It defended `dog_run_think`'s reveal clamp, which **cannot run
on this map** (no dog spawners — the file says so itself), and v17.92's
spawn-frame stamp had already made it a belt on a belt.

The parameter stays, with a warning: the TRAP 1 / TRAP 3 headers above it are
written as if `dog_init` runs, and a future reader following them will re-add
exactly these two lines.

### 10 · zone/workshop.json has not parsed since v17.69, so the store page is two updates stale

`JSON.parse` dies with **"Bad control character in string literal at position
6117"**: four raw CR/LF bytes inside the Description string where every other
paragraph break is an escaped `\r\n`. They sit exactly at the seam where the
WARDEN KING paragraph was appended.

**Verified against the live store page rather than assumed** — it still says
"100 floors", has no "Warden King" anywhere, and still sells the gold camo. The
repo copy was already correct on all three; it simply never reached Steam.

Repaired, plus four claims that were wrong in the repo copy too:
* **"28 abilities have one" → 27.** Measured: 37 live `add_domain` calls minus
  the **10 real `set_no_dark` CALLS**. (A bare grep hits the function definition
  and two comments and gives 24 — the wrong answer, and worth recording.)
* **"it wears a gold camo to prove it" → "a new camo"** — v17.90-91 replaced all
  three camos; gold, red hex and Element 115 are retired.
* **"twice the reach on his zaps" — DELETED.** The audit went looking for the
  King's 2× zap range and found **no reader anywhere in the tree**. The flame
  half is real (the trigger box really is doubled, and that box is the burn's
  reach) and stays. Advertising something the code does not do is the one kind of
  description error that reads as a lie rather than as staleness.
* **Nikolai restored to the Testers list.** He is credited on the LIVE page and
  was missing from this file, so publishing this copy would have deleted a real
  person's credit. Confirmed by fetching the store page.
* The file's one non-ASCII character (an em dash the store renders as `?`) is
  gone; it is pure ASCII now.

The script gates on `JSON.parse`, on every key surviving, on ASCII, and on the
1 MB cap.

### 11 · Pause-menu copy that no longer matched the code

The DETAIL row is the only place a player ever reads a value, so a stale row is a
lie to the player.

* **LUCK** — the act line now says what the bar is FOR ("a fuller bar deals rarer
  cards"). Every in-game surface that named luck was circular: this row explained
  how to raise it, the HUD art says "LUCK", the deal badge says "LUCK 60%
  BOOSTED" and stops one noun short. A player asked outright in the comments on
  2026-09-06 and the author had to answer on Steam. The 100–150 overcharge band
  stays secret.
* **CLASS TIER** — the act line stated the requirement and never the cost. Now
  "tier 3: PaP + floor 30; new gun unpacked", and the domain description says
  UNPACKED. Three separate Workshop reports describe this surprise. ("PaP" and
  not "Pack-a-Punch" because the act budget is 46 characters; the floor numbers
  are LOCKSTEP with `tier_floor_ok` and were not touched.)
* **A promotion now says so out loud** — one `IPrintLnBold` beside the sting in
  `tier_up`, naming both weapons, since `"tod_tier_up_done"` has no listener
  and the card art carries no warning. On the spire it is also the only notice
  that the PACK II / PACK III stack just reset — up to 80,000 points.
* **BOUNTY** — "banked, paid out every 10s" read as a ten-second timer next to
  seven rows where `s` means seconds. It pays on the kill in whole tens of
  points: "banked, paid in 10-point steps".
* **LEECH** — still read "per blade kill" after 2026-09-05 made it one heal per
  swing however many bodies it killed.
* **THOR'S THUNDER** — never said bosses and elites are immune, and the strike
  still visibly fires on them (it is centred on the melee victim's origin), so a
  slasher reading "64% of enemy max hp" reasonably concluded it was their boss
  answer. Same omission already fixed on TRAILBLAZER's row.

### Deliberately NOT done

* **The boss-behind-an-unbought-door fix.** Real and verified against the shipped

* **Threading `enemy_death_detection` on hounds** (the "proper" Widow's Wine
  fix). It opens per-hit scoring, Instakill one-shots and every other registrant

* **The King's BT range twins.** Fix the record, not the boss — see item 10.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.8) — Wisp Tea gets a Warden King tier: the other half of the same hole

Found while fixing v18.7, confirmed by the user the same minute. **Wisp Tea had
the identical defect the Gift of Death had**, and it was the more certain of the
two to fire.

`wisp_hit_damage` returns `maxhealth / WISP_TEA_BOSS_SEGMENTS` for anything
boss-flagged — **80 ticks to kill a Panzer whatever its health**. The King
carries `is_boss` like every Panzer, so he died in the same 80 ticks. And
unlike the Gift, which needs a powerup drop, **every spire player holds Wisp Tea**
— ascension grants the whole roster — so a pair could take him in roughly 30 s of
uptime with nobody firing a shot.

`WISP_TEA_KING_SEGMENTS` **1600**, the Panzer tier x20, matching the factor the
user chose for the Gift the same night (20 shots -> 400). In the units the .gsh
block already uses: one wisp lands at most 40 hits per 30 s life, a pair 80, so a
solo pair needs 20 full lifetimes at 100% uptime and a quad party's eight wisps
need five. Wisps contribute; they cannot decide it. Looser still in practice —
wisps seek ELITES before the Panzer and the King summons elites every 18 s, so
they will spend the fight on his adds.

Tested BEFORE the tier lookup rather than inside the boss branch, so a future
change to `wisp_target_tier` cannot re-order it away. Reading a `tod_` field
from the vendored module is established practice in this file —
`wisp_target_tier` already reads `tod_is_sprinter` for the same reason: the
pack cannot know this map's enemies.

### The pattern, worth naming once

Three effects in this map deal a FRACTION OF MAX HEALTH and are therefore blind
to any health wall: the Gift of Death, Wisp Tea, and THOR'S THUNDER. Two of them
reached the King. Thunder never could — it skips anything boss-flagged, verified,
not assumed. TRAILBLAZER's burn is a fraction of the ROUND's zombie health rather
than the victim's and skips bosses besides. **Any new percentage-damage lane owes
a King answer on the day it ships.**

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` green. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-07 (v18.7) — the Gift of Death no longer deletes the Warden King: 1/400th per hit

User 2026-09-07: *"The final warden boss should not be impacted by gift of death
either. Gift of death should do 1/400th of his health per hit. We were accidently
able to finish him in like 1 minute because someone had the death machine"*.

### Why a 100 million HP boss died in about sixteen shots

The Gift of Death (`xmas_gun`, the Death Machine powerup redirected through
`level.zombie_powerup_weapon`) does not deal DAMAGE against an elite. Its lane
in `tod_mechz_damage_wrap` returns **a fraction of the victim's max health** —
`maxhealth / TOD_XMAS_PANZER_SHOTS x TOD_XMAS_ELITE_BUFF`, i.e. 20 shots
buffed 30% = about 16 — precisely so it stays lethal at any round.

That is the right design for every other Panzer and it is fatal for this one:
**a percent-of-max-health weapon cannot see a health wall.** The King's whole
identity is a 25,000,000-per-player wall, and the Gift went through it in the
same sixteen shots it uses on a round-5 Panzer.

### The fix

`TOD_XMAS_KING_SHOTS` **400**, and one `IS_TRUE( self.tod_king )` test in
the branch that was already there. `king_setup` stamps that field, and the
King is a Panzer in every other respect, so he reaches this lane the same way
every Panzer does and the test is the entire separation.

| Party | King HP | Gift per hit, before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | 25,000,000 | 1,625,000 (~16 shots) | 62,500 (400 shots) |
| Four | 100,000,000 | 6,500,000 (~16 shots) | 250,000 (400 shots) |

**`TOD_XMAS_ELITE_BUFF` is deliberately NOT applied here.** "1/400th of his
health per hit" is an exact instruction and the +30% would quietly make it
1/307th.

No other Gift lane can reach him: `_tod_powerups.gsc` owns the Reaver and
hellhound lanes, the RP has its own at `TOD_XMAS_RP_SHOTS`, and this wrap is
`self.actor_damage_func` — it runs last and returns authoritatively, so the
level chain cannot re-scale it.

Checked and NOT affected: the HEAVY's tier-3 primary is `t6_death_machine`, a
generated twin. The branch tests for `xmas_gun`, so the class gun is untouched.

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` green. **UNPLAYED** — but the lane itself is play-proven
(it is how the Gift has killed Panzers since 2026-08-21); only the divisor is
new.

## 2026-09-07 (v18.6) — TRAILBLAZER's slow comes down 25%, base ladder and dark card together

User 2026-09-07: *"trail blazer needs a nerf on slowing down enemies"* — first
20%, corrected the same minute to **25%** — then *"We will need to update code
and pause menu description so its accurate"*.

### The ladder

`trail_slow_mult()` was `1 - (0.04 + 0.06*L)`; it is now
`1 - (0.03 + 0.045*L)` — the slow AMOUNT x0.75 at every level:

| Level | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 10% | 16% | 22% | 28% | **34%** |
| After | 7.5% | 12% | 16.5% | 21% | **25.5%** |

That lands the domain between its two previous states: v16.94 shipped 5%..17%
and the user called it "not much"; v17.84 doubled it to 10%..34%.

**The DARK card moved with it** — `TOD_DARK_TRAIL_SLOW_MULT` 0.50 -> 0.625, a
50% slow becoming 37.5%. That is not scope creep: v17.84's own note records that
the dark HAD to move when the base did, or a dark card becomes a downgrade. The
same argument in reverse says it cannot be left at double the new Lv5. If the
intent was base-only, that constant is a one-line revert.

Nothing else about the domain moved: the burn stays 2..6%/s, the life stays
2.0..4.0 s, elites are still slowed and still not burned by the base version.

### The pause row, which is the only place a player reads any of this

The baked card carries no figures (the generic-card-text rule), so
`DETAIL[46]` in `tod_upgrade.lua` is the whole readout, and its comment block
says in so many words that a retune skipping it "ships a lie". Both rows
updated — the base row's composed string and the dark row's literal — plus the
formula comment that mirrors the GSC.

The ladder now carries half-percent steps at odd levels, so the row got a small
`pctStr()` helper: whole numbers print as integers, halves print one decimal.
Rounding the READOUT is fine; rounding the ladder to keep the text tidy is not.

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` and `lint_tod_lua.js` green. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-06 (v18.3) — the melee boss buff is SLASHER-ONLY: `melee_boss_mult` splits by attacker class

User 2026-09-06, immediately after the v18.2 build: *"WHen i said melee i
specifically meant slasher"*. v18.2 raised the SHARED melee-vs-boss tax, which
handed the +75% to every class's bare knife as well.

### The split

```
TOD_MELEE_BOSS_MULT          0.33     every other class's melee  (RESTORED)
TOD_MELEE_BOSS_MULT_SLASHER  0.5775   the SLASHER only            (the +75%)
```

`melee_boss_mult()` takes the ATTACKER as its first argument now and picks
between them. **All four call sites pass it** — `upgrade_damage_cb`, the
silent-chain guard beneath it, `cleave_splash`, and `_tod_bosses::
rp_damage_feed` — and each one already had `attacker` in scope one or two
lines away (the arity lint proves the shape; the liveness was checked by hand,
because that lint does not model it).

**Keyed on the CLASS, not the weapon**, the same way `slasher_sidearm_vs_boss`
is: a slasher's melee is its class primary at every tier, and a bare-knife swing
with the sidearm out is still that class's swing.

### Where each class now lands vs a boss

| Attacker | Panzer | Every other elite |
|---|---|---|
| Slasher | 1.155 (x0.5775 x the v15 Panzer x2) | 0.5775 |
| Skirmisher / Assault / Heavy | 0.66 | 0.33 |

The non-slasher column is exactly where it sat before v18.2 — this restores it,
it is not a new nerf.

**`TOD_MELEE_PANZER_BUFF` 2.0 stays CLASS-BLIND**, and the contrast is worth
holding: it is scoped to the PANZER's damage lane, so it doubles a heavy's knife
as readily as a blade, while the v18.3 split is scoped to the SLASHER at every
victim. Both comment blocks in `_tod_bosses.gsc` that state the product now
say so.

### Bookkeeping

`docs/armory.html`: the knob row, the DPS-grid constant and the boss table's
blade label now name the slasher rate. The grid arithmetic did not change — its
melee flag is true only on the three slasher rows, so it was already computing
the class-correct number.

## 2026-09-06 (v18.2) — FIVE TUNING KNOBS: elites -10% HP, hound bite -20%, melee +75% on bosses, the trial ramp flattened, the zombie speed tail cut a quarter

User 2026-09-06, one pass: *"we need to reduce the health of elites by ten
percent, and ... the hellhound or dog is an elite. We actually need to reduce
the damage of the dog by twenty percent. Next, the melee weapons ... are weak
against the elites and bosses slash panzers ... we need to improve its damage
by seventy five percent. Also, many people are complaining about how hard the
trials get as you continue to go up ... Let's make it a bit easier as you
continue."* Then: *"there's a zombie speed multiplier ... we do need to lower
that by twenty five percent."*

Every one of these is a constant. No new systems, no art, no geometry — a
`-GscOnly` build.

### 1 · ELITE HEALTH -10% — `TOD_ELITE_HP_MULT` 0.90, a NEW shared knob

`_tod_bosses.gsc` gains the constant and a public `elite_hp_mult()`. Four
elites read it:

| Elite | Where | Before -> after (SOLO at round 30, past every anchor) |
|---|---|---|
| Rogue Protector | `spawn_rp` | 14,933 -> 13,439 per unit |
| Reaver | `_tod_reaver.gsc` | 32,383 -> 29,144 |
| Hellhound | `_tod_hellhounds.gsc` | 11,200 -> 10,080 (its anchor IS 30) |
| Armored Sprinter | `_tod_sprinter.gsc` | x10 trash HP -> x9 |

Co-op multiplies all four by `coop_hp_mult()` as before (x1.7 / 2.3 / 2.8).

**THE PANZER IS OUT OF IT, DELIBERATELY**, and that is the one call to
validate. This map's own vocabulary splits the sets — `grant_elite_reward`
pays "every ELITE (Protector/Reaver/Hound/Sprinter)" a flat 500 while the
PANZER alone keeps the boss jackpot — and the same message asked for melee to
improve "against those elites **and bosses**", naming them as two things. If
the intended reading was "everything with a health bar", adding the Panzer is
one line at `spawn_panzer`'s `boss_hp` call.

**APPLIED AT THE CALL SITES, NOT INSIDE `boss_hp`** — the opposite placement
from `rampage_hp_mult`, and the reason is the Panzer: `boss_hp` is shared
with it, and it is also the one caller that must keep `level.mechz_health`
equal to its spawn HP. The three elite call sites each set `maxhealth` and
`health` from the same local, so scaling there cannot desync anything. The
sprinter never crosses `boss_hp` at all (it converts a horde zombie), so it
re-reads the shared knob exactly as it already re-reads the rampage one.

The trial ladder multiplies ON TOP of this, so a trial add is now 10% lighter
at every tier as well as flatter (see 4).

### 2 · HELLHOUND BITE -20% — `TOD_HOUND_DMG_MULT` 0.80

The dog's bite is stock `behavior_zombie_dog` melee: the archetype exposes no
per-attack damage number to author, so the shared player-damage callback is the
only chokepoint the hit crosses. A lane in `boss_player_damage` keyed on
`tod_boss_kind == "hellhound"`, which `spawn_hound` stamps on the spawn frame
before any wait (its own TRAP 3), so no dog can land a hit the lane cannot see.

Placed BEFORE the defensive domains, so DR / SPRINT ARMOR / BACK ARMOR multiply
the already-reduced number instead of the raw one. No second hound damage lane
exists to keep in step — unlike the Rogue Protector, the dog has no scripted
attack of its own.

### 3 · MELEE vs BOSSES AND ELITES +75% — `TOD_MELEE_BOSS_MULT` 0.33 -> 0.5775

0.33 x 1.75 exactly: the ask is a percentage ON the existing tax, not a new
absolute. The blade now lands at 57.75% against the boss/elite triad instead of
one third. Nothing moves against ordinary zombies — the 2026-08-30 -20% weapon
pass is untouched.

**READ THE PANZER NUMBER BEFORE VALIDATING**: `TOD_MELEE_PANZER_BUFF` 2.0 is a
SECOND multiplier on the Panzer's own damage lane (v15), so melee on a Panzer
is now 0.5775 x 2.0 = **1.155** — slightly MORE than the raw swing. That is the
arithmetic of the ask landing on top of an existing buff, not an oversight, but
it is the first thing to look at if the blade reads too strong on Panzers. On
the round-30 solo Panzer the armory measures, a maxed slasher goes from 8 swings
to 5. Both comment blocks in `_tod_bosses.gsc` that quoted "0.33 x 2.0 = 0.66"
were corrected — they were a second source of truth for a constant that moved.

### 4 · THE TRIAL RAMP FLATTENED — `TOD_TRIAL_STEP` 1.1225 -> 1.09

One number drives both axes of the ladder (elite HP and the adds' cadence), so
this eases the back half on both at once. Trial I does not move at all; the top
comes down:

| Trial | I | II | III | IV | V | VI | VII |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (1.1225) | 0.956 | 1.073 | 1.204 | 1.352 | 1.517 | 1.703 | 1.911 |
| After (1.09) | 0.956 | 1.042 | 1.136 | 1.238 | 1.349 | 1.471 | 1.603 |

With §1's -10% on every elite on top, an add in the last trial is x1.44 of a
plain spire elite where it was x1.91 — a 24% cut at the top, nothing at the
bottom, which is exactly the shape of "it gets too hard as you continue". The
Wardens are Panzers and take only the ladder change (x1.911 -> x1.603).

The purse is untouched: trial VII still pays 14,000.

### 5 · ZOMBIE SPEED TAIL -25% — `TOD_ZSPEED_STEP` 0.0028 -> 0.0021

The uncapped LINEAR climb after `TOD_ZSPEED_FULL_ROUND` (18): +0.21%/round
instead of +0.28%. Round 30 lands at 1.025x full sprint (was 1.034x), round 50
at 1.067x (was 1.090x), round 80 at 1.130x (was 1.174x). The 0.8 floor and the
ramp to round 18 are untouched — this only flattens what happens after.

### Bookkeeping

* `docs/armory.html` carried THREE computed copies of the melee tax that
  `verify_armory_constants.js` does not cover (it only harvests
  `tune:"NAME value"` strings): the DPS-grid constant, the knob-reference row,
  and the boss table's blade row — whose `bossDps` sentinel was
  `r[4]===0.33`, i.e. it would have silently handed the blade a x3 head crit
  the moment the constant moved. All three updated; the sentinel now keys on
  the WEAPON. The page's dated NARRATIVE paragraphs still quote x0.33 as the
  finding of an earlier review — left as written history.
* `CLAUDE.md`'s zombie-speed bullet said "full sprint at round 15" and
  "+0.28%/round"; the define has been 18 since 2026-08-29. Rewritten to name
  the defines rather than restate them.
* `_tod_spire.gsc`'s `trial_tick` comment still said "x1.07 per trial = 7%
  faster each" — two retunes stale. Fixed.

### Verification

`lint_tod_arity.js` green (74 files), `verify_armory_constants.js` green
(52/52). **UNPLAYED** — every number above is arithmetic, but the hellhound
damage lane is a NEW branch in `boss_player_damage` that has never executed.
