## 2026-09-06 (v18.1) — SOLO RELIEF: the combined elite roof goes party-aware (5/7/9/11) and the horde health surcharge on solo is gone

User 2026-09-06: *"What is the solo vs 3 player multipliers. I think we need to
make solo a bit easier"*, then, given the audit: *"elites at once we can drop so
5 solo, 7 duo, 9 trio, 11 quads. Health drop to 1x, drop duo trio quad by 0.1"*.

### The audit that produced the numbers (read out of the code, not from prose)

Per-player load, solo vs trio, before this change:

| Lever | Solo | Trio | Solo penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Combined elite roof | 12 | 12 (FLAT) | **3.0x** |
| Zombie health per gun | 1.15 | 0.483 | **2.4x** |
| Zombies alive (ai_limit) | 24 | 9.3 | 2.6x |
| Hound pack | 3 | 1.33 | 2.3x |
| Protectors standing | 5 | 2.33 | 2.1x |
| Boss HP per gun | 1.0 | 0.77 | 1.3x |
| Round budget @ r20 | 60 | 56 | ~1.0x |
| Reavers / sprinters per wave | 1 | 1 | 1.0x |
| Door price | x1.0 | x1.8 | income-matched |
| Warden King | 25M / gun | 25M / gun | 1.0x |
| Trial Wardens | 1 @ x1.0 | 1 @ x2.3 | co-op HARDER |

Round budget, doors, luck and the King were already fair. The roof and horde
health were not, and they compounded.

### 1. The combined elite roof is party-aware

`TOD_ELITE_ROOF_ALL 12` (flat) becomes `TOD_ELITE_ROOF_SOLO 5` +
`TOD_ELITE_ROOF_PER 2` = **5 / 7 / 9 / 11**. `elite_roof_all()` is now the ONE
owner and `elites_over_roof()` calls it instead of reading the define, so the
two can never disagree.

The v14.20 note that shipped the flat 12 said *"FLAT, not per-player,
deliberately: the per-type roofs already scale with party size, so the combined
figure is the one thing that must not."* That reasoning was protecting the
ACTOR POOL, which is a quad-sized worry — and in solving it, it made this the
map's single worst solo penalty. The pool argument still holds at the top, which
is why quad only drops 12 -> 11: the case that motivated 12 was 18 live elites
at quad (~63 actors against `TOD_ACTOR_LIMIT` 60), and 11 is under 12.

**THE BIGGEST FEEL CHANGE IN THIS EDIT IS NOT THE HORDE.** Three spire lanes
share this ceiling and none is a director: `door_guard_panzers`,
`king_summons`, `trial_adds`. A SOLO Warden Trial reserves its Wardens first
(`level.tod_trial_reserve`), so ~3 adds stand where ~10 used to; a SOLO Warden
King keeps 4 add slots where he had 11. Intended direction, big swing, and the
first solo run should be read with it in mind. The FINALE is exempt as ever
(`elites_over_roof` returns false under `tod_finale_aggro` /
`tod_finale_holdout`), so the road ambush is unchanged at every party size.

### 2. Horde health is a TABLE now: 1.00 / 1.20 / 1.35 / 1.50

Was `TOD_ZHEALTH_MULT 1.15 + (n-1) * TOD_ZHEALTH_PER_PLAYER 0.15` =
1.15/1.30/1.45/1.60. The asked-for set drops solo by 0.15 and everyone else by
0.10, giving steps of +0.20, +0.15, +0.15 — **no base-plus-step reproduces it**,
so a formula would have meant quietly changing a number the user named.
`coop_hp_mult()` in `_tod_bosses.gsc` is the in-tree precedent for a per-size
table. Solo now pays NO surcharge over stock health; co-op still rises, which is
the 2026-08-23 *"Should get harder more players"* intent, intact.

The retired comment quoted *"solo 1.25 / duo 1.40 / trio 1.55 / quad 1.70"* —
two base changes stale by the time it was read today. A comment that quotes a
computed set is a second source of truth that nothing regenerates; the four
defines are the truth now.

### Not changed, deliberately

`coop_ai_limit` (24 solo / +2 per player), hound pack size, protector wave
size, boss `coop_hp_mult`, door pricing, luck normalisation. The user named two
levers; the rest of the audit is recorded above so the next pass starts from
measurements rather than from this file.

Script only, and the `.map` is untouched — but it ships on a FULL `-Publish`
rebuild (user: *"lets do a full rebuild and prepare release"*). **UNPLAYED, and
explicitly so** (user: *"I wont even test this cause im sure its fine"*).

## 2026-09-06 (v18.0) — THE SPIRE'S DOOR CLOCK IS RETIRED AND THE DOORS ARE 25% CHEAPER; the trial seal is the only gate left

User 2026-09-06: *"lets remove the timer on the doors for the endless spire. We
should still restrict the trial floor door so they have to defeat the trial. But
thats it. The timer slows down the game too much"*, then *"lets lower the price
of the doors by 25%"*.

### The clock seal, retired whole

`TOD_SPIRE_DOOR_SEAL_SECS` and `seal_window()` are GONE, along with the
`"^1SEALED^7 - hold this floor"` literal — retire it whole, or the string is
dead weight and the next reader has to work out which of two seals is live.
`door_manager` now threads `trial_seal_window` for a hub door and nothing at
all for an ordinary one. `seal_active()` survives as the TRIAL's refusal gate
(the audible echo of a hint that already says SEALED) and is down to one line:
`IS_TRUE( level.tod_spire_trial_seal )`. History: v14.31 wrote it at 30 s
(*"you need to stay and fight for a bit and cant just run through each door if
you have lots of money"*), v16.4 cut it to 12.

**Triggerstring budget goes DOWN**: the mode is now two constants (the price in
`spire_door_hint`, the trial literal in `trial_sealed_hint`), neither
interpolating, so re-stamping across all 70 doors still mints nothing.

**The honour guard was sized to fit inside that seal and now does not** — four
Panzers at `TOD_SPIRE_GUARD_STAGGER` 3.5 land at 0 / 3.5 / 7 / 10.5 s, i.e. the
last one used to arrive just before the door opened. They still drop on the
floor just bought, but a party with points can buy the next door before the
procession lands and climb away from it. That is the change, not a side effect:
the pacing levers are the guard and the price now, not a wait. Recorded here
because the next person to read `TOD_SPIRE_GUARD_STAGGER` will otherwise
wonder what it was tuned against.

### Price −25%

`SP_DOOR_COST` 6300 → **4725** in the generator, emitted into
`_tod_spire_data::door_cost()` (and `info.cost`). The ladder, whole: 3000
originally, 4500 v16.30, 9000 v17.10 (*"double the price"*), 6300 v17.70
(*"cut the spire doors cost by 30%"*), 4725 here. Regenerated and the `.map` is
**byte-identical** (md5 checked before/after), which is what makes this a
`-GscOnly` build — the `.map`'s own `zombie_cost` is the dead 1000 placeholder.

Net against the LIVE Workshop build (v17.58, which still asks 9000): spire
doors are now **47.5% cheaper**, so the staged Sep 6 notes read old → final
rather than quoting the intermediate 6300.

Script + generated data only; `-GscOnly`. **UNPLAYED** — both changes are feel,
and the pair pushes the same way (cheaper doors and no wait both speed the
climb), so the first run should be read as one change, not two.

## 2026-09-06 (v17.99) — EVERY CUSTOM POWERUP PICKUP AND EVERY DEATH PERCEPTION BUY THREW IN STOCK'S STAT LANE — the Workshop "weird error messages when i pick up power ups"

Workshop, Troy Terry (2026-09-05 9:25 pm PDT, on the live v17.58): *"weird error
messages when i pick up power ups, other than that hella fun map"*. Chased from
code + the 2026-09-05 console_mp.log rather than a screenshot (none offered).

### What the map draws on a pickup — nothing that can say "error"

Every text lane that fires on a powerup grab was read: the kit's
`AetheriumPowerupNotification` (only stock Max Ammo sends `zombie_notification`,
and the widget only draws a name it matched), the kill feed (`score_event`, the
label lookup always returns a real localized key — cross-checked every
`&"ZM_AETHERIUM_*"` ref in scripts/ and ui/ against the .str: none missing),
and our three grab functions + the two vendored ones (no prints, no notifies).
So the text is not ours.

### What actually throws on a pickup

Stock `_zm_powerups.gsc:1104`: `player zm_stats::increment_client_stat(
self.powerup_name + "_pickedup" )` → `add_client_stat` →
`globallogic_score::incPersStat` → `self.pers[ stat ] += 1`. Stock
`_zm_stats::player_stats_init` initPersStat's ONLY stock names
(nuke/insta_kill/full_ammo/double_points/carpenter/fire_sale/minigun/…). For
`tod_pap`, `tod_free_pap`, `tod_zombie_blood`, `infiniteammo` and `timewarp`
the slot is undefined and the add throws `pair 'undefined' and '1' has
unmatching types 'undefined' and 'int'` — the exact stack the log carried 11
times: `_globallogic_score ← _zm_stats ← _zm_stats ← _zm_powerups ←
_zm_powerups ← _zm_spawner`. Our effect already ran (the `_custom_powerups`
grab callback sits earlier in that function), but everything after the throw
in stock's grab thread is skipped: the grab FX, the intro VO,
`powerup_delete_delayed` and the `"powerup_grabbed"` notify (UNVERIFIED in
game whether the orb visibly lingers until its own timeout).

Whether a Workshop player SEES a script exception is not proven here — our
launcher runs `developer 1`, Troy's presumably does not — but this is the only
error the pickup lane raises, it fires on exactly the powerups he would call
"weird", and the fix costs nothing.

**Fix:** `zm_powerups::powerup_set_statless_powerup()` for all five names in
`_tod_powerups::__init__` — stock's own lane (`should_award_stat` reads
`level.zombie_statless_powerups`): the whole stats block is skipped, so no pers
slot and no engine `IncrementPlayerStat` with a name the stats DDL does not
know. Keyed by name; registration order against the vendored modules is
irrelevant.

### The same throw on every Death Perception buy

`_zm_perks::give_perk` (:762) runs `increment_client_stat( perk + "_drank" )`
the same way, and stock initialises `_drank` for its own eight perks only.
`specialty_combat_efficiency` (Death Perception) is not among them, so every
buy threw and `give_perk` never reached its tail: `perk_history`,
`perks_active`, the `"perk_acquired"` notify and `perk_think( perk )`. PhD is
safe (it rides `specialty_electriccherry`, initialised); Wisp Tea's vendored
module already registers its own slot on connect (`registerStats`). The second
stack variant in the log (`_zm_perks ← _tod_spire`, the ascension perma-perk
grant) is this one. **Fix:** `_tod_perk_electric_cherry` now does exactly what
Wisp Tea does — `callback::on_connect( &dp_register_stats )` →
`globallogic_score::initPersStat( EC_PERK + "_drank", false )`; idempotent,
so ordering against stock's init does not matter.

Script only, but it goes out on the v17.99 PUBLISH full build (v17.98 was
never uploaded; this supersedes it in the ledger). Proof is the next log:
zero `pair 'undefined' and '1'`.

## 2026-09-05 20:5x (v17.96) — DEAD PROTECTORS AND REAVERS NEVER LEFT THE ACTOR POOL: the Warden King's "connection interrupted", measured and closed

User, after the first post-v17.92 spire run: *"im seeing a lot of spawn failed
which is causes network connection issues?"* Read the run's `console_mp.log`
(21,927 lines). First, the v17.92 proof landed: zero `pair '100'` hound throws,
zero `_zm_zonemgr` dumps, and `island_sweep` killed the stranded tower bodies
in its first seconds (2/4/4/3 on passes 2-5). The climb was clean.

### The stall, this time with the engine's own numbers

Every one of the ten `[hound] spawn FAILED (no actor)` lines follows the
engine's `G_SpawnStaticEntity: no free actor entities` — 30 of those, ALL
between 515 s and 699 s, which is the Warden King fight (his seal registered
at 453 s). Each warning is followed by the engine printing its entity table,
~540 lines, and the timestamps show it takes ~1.3 s; the hound module's own
"spawn FAILED" print lands 12 ms after the last row, in the same script call.
So the whole server froze inside SpawnActor for 1.3 s, 23 times in one fight
(~30 s total) — with a local client, that is the "connection interrupted"
banner. Whether that print is developer-only is UNVERIFIED (the launcher runs
`+set developer 1`); the failed spawns are real for everyone either way, so a
Workshop player's King would silently stop summoning instead.

### Why the pool was full — a leak no counter could see

The entity table at every exhaustion held exactly **64 actors** (the engine's
pool; our `TOD_ACTOR_LIMIT` 60 is a script gate on top of it): 42-47 trash,
**12-16 Protectors**, 2-3 Reavers, 1-4 hounds, the King. At the same instants
`elites_all_alive()` read **5-8** and `get_current_actor_count()` read 52-58.
The difference is DEAD elite bodies: a dead Protector or Reaver stays an
`Actor` entity but is no longer in the AI array and never becomes a corpse, so
stock's clear-corpses-at-the-cap gate, our elite roof and the probe were all
blind to it. The King's summons (a Protector debt of 2 every 18 s) piled them
up faster than anywhere else in the map. docs/61 (2026-09-01) had already
recorded that only the Panzer deletes itself; v17.92 gave the hound the lane;
the Protector and the Reaver were the two still leaking.

### The fix

`_tod_bosses::death_watch` (Protector) and `_tod_reaver::death_watch` now
thread `tod_corpse_cleanup::corpse_remove( linger )` after the reward — the
same lane trash and hounds use: NotSolid, a linger (or an immediate Ghost when
the board is within `TOD_CORPSE_PANIC` of the cap), then Delete, re-checking
existence at every step. `corpse_remove` grew an optional `linger` argument
(default unchanged, `TOD_CORPSE_LINGER` 2.0); elites pass
`TOD_ELITE_CORPSE_LINGER` 5.0 (one define in `_tod_bosses.gsc`, read by the
Reaver through `elite_corpse_linger()`) so a Protector's fall and a Reaver's
death swap still read before the body goes. `_tod_corpse_cleanup` has
stock-only usings, so both new `#using` lines are cycle-free. Both watchers'
sibling threads (`boss_pause_watch`, `tod_boss_stuck_watch`) `endon( "death" )`;
the vendored fury death is a model swap + NotSolid with an empty
`apothiconDeathTerminate`, and `zm_zod_robot.gsc` has no death hook — nothing
touches either body after the Delete.

Seen, not fixed, unchanged from v17.92: the ascension throws one
`_zm_stats` `pair 'undefined' and '1'` from the perma-perk grant (11 in the
match, via `_zm_perks`), and the client logs 43 `Too many weapon costs` (the
229/229 ledger). Neither is a stall.

Script only; `-GscOnly` on the v17.95 publish build. **UNPLAYED.** Proof is the
next King-fight log: zero `no free actor entities`, and the probe's `act=`
within ~8 of `cur=` + `el=` instead of 12+ over.

## 2026-09-05 18:3x (v17.94) — THE WORLD PAUSE IS A REAL FREEZE: Furys park at idle, every elite re-frozen per tick, players invulnerable under any pause; the king's seal zeroes the family debts

User, off the FIRST REAL WARDEN KING RUN: *"the apothican furys didnt freeze
during the dark upgrades. Meaning a player could just die. During these
upgrades we should make players invincible as well just in case. But furys not
freezing is for sure an issue."* Two defects and one net, all GSC (`-GscOnly`).
**UNPLAYED as built.**

### Why a Fury kept moving (two causes, both fixed)
- **The freeze was an EDGE STAMP and the Fury has its own rate writers.**
  `boss_pause_watch` wrote ignoreall + anim rate 0.05 ONCE, on the pause's
  rising edge. The Apothicon Fury archetype writes `ASMSetAnimationRate( 1 )`
  itself at the end of every teleport/bamf/traversal
  (`mocompApothiconFuryTeleportTerminate`, `apothiconBamfIn`), so one bamf in
  flight when the pause landed put it back to full speed for the rest of the
  freeze with nothing ever writing again. Now the watcher RE-ASSERTS both every
  0.25 s tick while the pause holds (all elites — Panzer, Protector, hound,
  Fury; the restore stays on the falling edge).
- **Rate 0.05 slows a behaviour; it does not stop the tree CHOOSING one.** The
  Fury's bamf is a `ForceTeleport` that needs no animation time, its melee
  and bamf conditions run every frame, and `ignoreall` only stops
  `zombieTargetService` from picking a NEW enemy — the one already in
  `.enemy` is all those conditions read. So a Fury is now PARKED at its tree's
  own spawn gate: `zombie_think_done = false` puts the root's
  `idlespawnbehavior` (a looping idle, above every combat branch —
  `zm_genesis_apothicon_fury.ai_bt`, `_zm_behavior.gsc::zombieIsThinkDone`)
  in charge for the whole pause; the un-park writes it back to 1. This is the
  mechanism that made a parked riser a statue (memory
  parked-riser-idle-behavior) — a bug there, the lever here. Opt-in per elite
  (`tod_bt_idle_on_pause`, set in `_tod_reaver::spawn_reaver`); the other
  three trees have frozen correctly in every played pause since August and are
  not parked. `reaver_tune`'s one-second-late `zombie_think_done = 1` defers
  to the park (a meteor in flight at the pause would otherwise un-park itself).
- **Where the Furys came from at all:** `king_run`'s seal zeroed the Panzer
  debt only. Trial VII's adds had SET the four family debts and nothing zeroed
  them at the win, so the ten-second countdown drained them into fresh elites
  on the summit deck — `king_summons` only starts AFTER the deals. The seal
  now zeroes protector/reaver/hound/sprinter debts too.

### The net: players are invulnerable under any world pause
- `set_world_pause( true )` now `EnableInvulnerability`s every upright
  living player (`tod_pause_invuln`); `set_world_pause( false )` releases
  only the players it armed and only when no other lane still holds the flag
  (`pause_invuln_held_elsewhere`: zombie blood, the finale's depart, the
  summit win — stock's only in-play use is its out-of-bounds kill). Covers
  every round event, the trial reward, the solo station and the king's
  max-out + dark deals — the same call the zombie-blood window already leans
  on. Downed players are not armed (they were never frozen; bleeding is not
  being hit). A player who spawns INTO a pause is covered by the next
  `set_world_pause( true )` (run_upgrade_event and trial_win both re-call it,
  idempotently). Symmetric with `upgrade_damage_cb`'s return 0 under the
  pause: nobody hits anybody.

### Notes
- First real king run otherwise: the fight ran to the deals (the summit,
  the seal, the landing and the max-out all fired); nothing else reported yet.
- `lint_tod_arity` OK across 74 files.

User, with the console screenshot: *"Is this you?"* Yes. `dbg()` is a per-module
helper (`_tod_hellhounds`, `_tod_bosses` each carry their own); `_tod_spire.gsc`
never had one and the new sweep called it. The linker caught it — *Unresolved
external "dbg" with 1 parameters* — and **`lint_tod_arity.js` did not**: a bare
call whose name has no definition in the calling namespace is SKIPPED as a
presumed engine builtin (`lint_tod_arity.js:88`, `!local[name] -> continue`) —
it cannot tell `dbg` from `IPrintLn`. The fix is a builtin allowlist so an
unknown bare name becomes a finding. Replaced with the file's own idiom (`IPrintLn` under

`function dbg` finds none left. Lint gap noted; not fixed tonight.

## 2026-09-05 18:0x (v17.92) — THE SPIRE'S "CONNECTION INTERRUPTED": five fixes off one console log, none of them where v17.83 looked

User: *"I keep getting connection interrupted when I go up the spire? What's
going on"*, then *"go ahead and fix what can be fixed"*. Read
`console_mp.log` from the match (47,615 lines; the launcher already runs with
`+set logfile 2`, and the file lives in the RETAIL game root, not the
mod-tools tree — an hour was spent searching the wrong one). The v17.43
record already names the mechanism: a local "connection interrupted" is the
in-process server stalling, and a script-exception storm is what stalls it.
**49 exceptions before ascension, 379 after.** Nothing from the TRAILBLAZER or
ADRENALINE lanes appears anywhere in the log.

### 1. The 306 hound throws, pinned by arithmetic — and it was never a yaw

`pair '100' and 'undefined' has unmatching types 'int' and 'undefined'`, three
frames deep in stock `behavior_zombie_dog.gsc`, 306 times. v17.83 read the
`100` as the dog's yaw and moved the target guard to `ignoreme`; the count in
tonight's log is 306 again, exactly.

The throws come in **runs of 27 frames**, one run per hound spawn, starting
~1.1 s after `[hound] spawned`. Stock `need_to_run()` opens with
`self.health < self.maxhealth`, every frame the tree runs; the tree starts at
the reveal (`TOD_HOUND_SPAWN_FX_SECS` = 1.2 s) and `hound_tune` wrote
`maxhealth` at +2.5 s. For 1.3 s the compare was `100 < undefined` — `100` is
the dog's stock default health — and 1.3 s ÷ 50 ms = 26–27 frames. Fixed by
stamping `dog.health` and `dog.maxhealth` on the spawn frame in `spawn_hound`
(the +2.5 s re-stamp stays; `level.dog_health` is already `hp`, so stock's
reveal clamp is a no-op by construction).

**The lesson is the proof, not the fix:** v17.83 read the stock tree
correctly and still guarded the wrong window, because it reasoned from the
tree instead of counting. The count — 27 frames, every spawn — was the whole
diagnosis.

### 2. Bodies on the tower after ascension pinned the actor pool from minute one

Ents 24–35 were failing to path from the tower base (z≈0, x≈±460) toward a
player at x≈10,600 **from 89 s** — 6.5 s after ascension and 160 s before the
first hound. The dev probe read `cur=7` with the nearest zombie 10,156 units
away at +3.5 s, `cur=29` at +10 s. `wipe_all_zombies()` is one `Kill()` pass;
bodies still emerging when it ran, plus the spawns stock's round loop landed
at tower points before the spawn filter took hold, survived it with no path
to anyone and no way to die. Eight of them held actor slots for the whole
match. Neither net reached them: stock's failsafe waits 30 s a pass, and
`_tod_stray` is boot-only verified.

New `island_sweep()` thread from the ascension: once `tod_spire_active`, any
live actor whose origin is not `in_spire()` is `Kill()`ed — every 1 s for the
first 15 passes (the spawn tail), every 5 s for the rest of the match (the
belt). The rule underneath is simple: after ascension the tower is a place no
player can ever stand, so anything there is dead weight by definition. Kill,
not Delete — trash goes through stock's death and the corpse lane, elites
through their death watches (attacker undefined = no reward, same as the
wipe), hounds through their new delete lane. A boss mid-`drop_in` is skipped;
its landing point is on-island by the filter below.

### 3. Hounds never deleted — the August ticket, now measured

The dev probe: `act=` 43 → 46 → 50 → 54 → **60** and `el=` 1 → 10 in five
minutes; from 306 s, `WARNING: G_SpawnStaticEntity: no free actor entities`
every 1–4 s for the remaining eight (67 times). `_tod_corpse_cleanup` skips
the is_boss triad on purpose and nothing in `_tod_hellhounds` ever Deleted a
hound. `hound_death_watch` now threads `tod_corpse_cleanup::corpse_remove()`
— the same lane trash uses: NotSolid, a short linger (or an immediate Ghost
near the cap), then Delete, re-checking existence at every step.

### 4. Nothing spawns off the island

`pick_spawn_point` rejects any candidate not `in_spire()` while the spire is
active (beside the trial-box filter); `spawn_hound` falls back to the target
if the picker still hands back an off-island point, and `hound_spawn_in`
teleports back to its entrance spot at the reveal if anything moved it off.
Belt over braces — a stranded elite is the whole-match slot leak.

### 5. The spire zone chain was still the 100-lap one — and the summit zone could never enable

`zm_tower_of_doom.gsc` chained `spire_c1..c20` and `spire_c20_zone →
spire_summit_zone` on `enter_spire100`. The spire has been 70 laps = 14
chunks since v17.69. Every match since registered six zones that do not exist:
twelve `undefined is not a field object` throws in `_zm_zonemgr` at init, each
followed by a 70-line `info_volume` dump (4,690 lines of this one log). And
the summit was chained only from the phantom c20, so `spire_summit_zone` was
never enabled — a player on the summit deck stood in a DISABLED zone, the
Samantha-laugh instakill the adjacent comment warns about. The chain now walks
`tod_spire_data::spire_zone_names()` (base, chunks, summit) with each chunk
admitted by the door on its first floor and the summit by the last door — the
rule the 100-lap version encoded as literals, derived instead of counted.

### 6. Death Perception pinged spawn-frame actors

`Cannot call IncrementClientField on a 'counter' type clientfield on the
frame it is spawned … 'tod_dp_ping'` ×15, from `_tod_perk_electric_cherry`.
The ping now skips any zombie without `completed_emerging_into_playable_area`.

### Seen, not fixed

`Too many weapon costs added to weapon cost list` ×86, client-side

## 2026-09-05 16:0x (v17.86) — THE PAUSE MENU THREW ON ANY PERCENT SIGN IN A VALUE LINE (user: "I got a UI error when I paused")

One character, one line, and it has been a live landmine since v16.23.

### What happened

`CoD.TodDomainDesc` built a row's effect line with

```lua
eff = string.gsub( eff, "{V}", v )
```

**When gsub's third argument is a STRING, `%` is an escape character.** It must
be followed by a digit (a capture reference) or another `%`; a `%` followed by
anything else — a space, a slash, a comma, or the end of the string — raises
`invalid use of '%' in replacement string`.

Our value lines are made of percent signs:

```
"+15% speed and damage, heals 30%"      ADRENALINE
"burns 6%/s, slows 34%, lasts 4.0s"     TRAILBLAZER
"+10% slide speed, +25% jump height"    ATHLETE
```

Every one of those throws. **The pcall above does not cover it** — that wraps
the `val` CALL, while the substitution happens outside — and neither caller
guards: `AetheriumStartMenu.lua:623` and `AetheriumScoreboard.lua:172` both
call `TodDomainDesc` bare. So the throw takes the whole panel, and the symptom
is "the pause menu errored" with nothing naming a domain.

Fixed by switching to the **function** form, which does no escape processing at
all and inserts whatever it returns verbatim:

```lua
eff = string.gsub( eff, "{V}", function() return v end )
```

`CoD.TodRoundText` in the same file already used the function form, which is
exactly why it never hit this — line 723 was the file's last
string-replacement gsub.

### The bug is older than the row that exposed it

Only rows whose `eff` is literally `"{V}"` — i.e. the whole line comes back
from `val` as a string — can hit it. That is **ADRENALINE (25)**, **ATHLETE
(43)** and **TRAILBLAZER (46)**, live and dark.

Rows like GIANT SLAYER (35, `"+{V}% damage to bosses and elites"`) and RECOVERY
(39) are SAFE and it is worth knowing why: their percent sign lives in `eff` —
the SUBJECT of the gsub — and only the REPLACEMENT is escape-processed. Their
`val` returns a number.

So ATHLETE has carried this since v16.23 and TRAILBLAZER since v16.94.
**v17.85 put ADRENALINE on the same lane, and ADRENALINE is owned far more
often than either** — which is why a two-build-old bug surfaced tonight.

⚠️ **Diagnosed from the code and Lua's documented gsub semantics, not
reproduced in a debugger.** It is a definite defect at that line regardless of
whether it is the whole of what the user saw, and the fix cannot make anything
worse. If a pause error survives this build, the next suspect is the unguarded
call at `AetheriumStartMenu.lua:623` — wrapping it would degrade one row to
blank instead of killing the panel.

### Do not "fix" this by rewording a row

Any value line may legitimately contain a percent sign; this domain is about
percentages. The comment at the call site says so, because rewording is the
tempting wrong repair and it would leave the landmine armed for the next row.

  LENS the stars, nebula and milky way behind them (Einstein radius `lens` in

- `SKY_GAIN` 0.025 → 0.024. The sky is the world's ambient light, so the file's

## 2026-09-05 15:4x (v17.85) — ADRENALINE heals on trigger, at DOUBLE the speed/damage percentage; the four cards are re-copied and installed

User, 2026-09-05: *"for adrenaline we need to add healing on trigger. It will
match the percentage"* — then, in the same session: *"the health gain you get
on trigger should be double the percentage. So 50% health gain one time on
adrenaline trigger"*, and on being shown the ladder, *"thats for dark but of
course its dynamic depending on % for that tier"*.

### A third lane, at twice the rate

The proc now HEALS **of max health**, once, at the moment it fires — alongside
the 3 s speed and damage burst it already granted.

| | Lv1 | Lv2 | Lv3 | Lv4 | Lv5 | DARK |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| speed and damage | 3% | 6% | 9% | 12% | 15% | 25% |
| **heal on trigger** | **6%** | **12%** | **18%** | **24%** | **30%** | **50%** |

`adren_bonus()` is still the single owner and the heal is `2.0 x` it through
**`TOD_ADREN_HEAL_MULT`** — a named define rather than a `2` in the expression,
because this file already carried the rule before the ask arrived: one function
feeds all three lanes so they cannot drift, and the moment one lane needs its
own number it gets its own NAME, never a second copy of the ladder. Retune the
percent and all three still move together; retune the multiplier and only the
heal does.

Nothing else changed: 3 kills in 1.5 s, 3 s burst, 20/18/16/14/12 s cooldown.

**It is one-shot, not a heal-tank**, and the two numbers have to be read
together: 30% sounds enormous beside LEECH's flat 25 HP, but LEECH pays on
EVERY blade kill while this pays once per proc behind a 3-kill trigger AND a
12-20 s cooldown — at best once every 12 seconds.

**The heal is a PERCENTAGE where the other two are POINTS**, and that is
deliberate rather than sloppy: move speed is points of additive scale, damage
is a multiplier addend, and the heal reads against `self.maxhealth` — so it
follows Juggernog and VITALITY without anything in this domain knowing they
exist.

Three implementation notes worth keeping:

- **Ordering is load-bearing.** The heal reads `adren_bonus()`, which returns 0
  outside a live burst by design — so it has to run *after* `tod_adren_until`
  is stamped. One line earlier and it would be a silent zero, with no error and
  nothing on screen to notice.
- **`trickle_heal` is the map's one heal lane** (LEECH uses it too): clamps to
  maxhealth, never lowers, only ever raises. That last part is what keeps
  RECOVERY's health-drop poll from reading our heal as damage.
- **The last-stand guard is LEECH's, and it is not optional.** A downed player
  can still kill with a pistol and so can still fire this proc; `self.health`
  in last stand belongs to the down system, and writing it from here would be a
  partial self-revive nobody designed. The speed and damage halves stay ungated
  exactly as they always were — they write no health.

### The cards were re-copied, delivered and installed the same hour

`DETAIL[25]` and the domain descriptions were updated in the same build (the
row moved from the `+{V}%` template to the composed form, because the heal is
instant while the other two last 3 s and no single template sentence says
both). The **baked card cannot be fixed from code**: all four ADRENALINE cards
read `MULTI-KILLS GRANT / SPEED + DAMAGE`, which is now a two-item list
describing three effects.

Requested as docs/111 → `tod_adrenaline_recopy_art_pack.zip`, delivered as
`files - 2026-09-05T154021.035.zip`, **installed**. Line 2 is now
**`A POWER SURGE`**; line 1 untouched. Same filenames, so no GDT block, no zone
line and no slug — the four `image,` lines were already there.

**Generic on purpose, and it paid for itself within the hour:** the copy was
written to name the SHAPE of the effect rather than list its parts, and the
heal doubled from 25% to 50% dark *after* the art was commissioned. A list card
would have needed a second re-bake; `A POWER SURGE` is still correct.

**The install was PROVEN, not eyeballed.** The drop carried two encodings of
`regular` and `dark` (different md5s) plus a contact sheet; ffmpeg PSNR says the
duplicate pairs are pixel-identical (`inf` on every channel), so the choice
between them was arbitrary and the complete nested set of four went in. Then,
per card, against the SHIPPED file: rows 0-820 (frame, title, illustration,
ribbon, medal) `PSNR inf`, rows 1000-1152 (the pip row) `PSNR inf`, and only the
820-1000 text band differs — mechanical proof that nothing but the sentence
moved, on all four.

### ⚠️ NOT BUILT — a concurrent session is mid-geometry-change

`-GscOnly` **refused**, correctly: *"deployed map_source .map does NOT match
repo after sync"*. A second session in this repo edited `tools/gen_tower_map.js`
and regenerated the `.map` plus all four `_tod_*_data.gsc` files at ~15:25,
while this build was in flight (+99,313 / −95,503 lines). The guard stopped a
build that would have linked GSC against a `.map` neither session had settled.

The source edits here are complete and lint-clean (lua, arity, hints, assets all
pass). **The deployed `.ff` is 15:19 and does NOT contain this heal.** It needs
a build once the geometry change lands — and that will be a FULL build, not
`-GscOnly`, because the geometry moved.

UNPLAYED, UNBUILT.

## 2026-09-05 16:0x (v17.84) — TRAILBLAZER: the slow is doubled, and the base version now SLOWS elites instead of ignoring them

User, 2026-09-05: *"Double the slow rate and make the base slow elites but not
burn"*, and *"we should upgrade the description so people know exactly what it
does"*.

### The slow, doubled — base and dark

`trail_slow_mult()` was `1 - (0.02 + 0.03L)`, a 5%..17% ladder shipped in
v16.94 against *"not much"*. It is now `1 - (0.04 + 0.06L)`:

| | Lv1 | Lv2 | Lv3 | Lv4 | Lv5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| was | −5% | −8% | −11% | −14% | −17% |
| now | −10% | −16% | −22% | −28% | −34% |

`TOD_DARK_TRAIL_SLOW_MULT` went 0.75 → 0.50 **because it had to**: base Lv5
moved to 34%, so a dark card left at 25% would have been a downgrade on the one
axis the domain is now built around. Nothing else moved — the burn is still
2..6 %/s of round health, life still 2..4 s, radius still 56..88 (dark 10%/s,
100 u).

### Elites are slowed, not burned

The old tick skipped the whole boss/elite triad on the first line, so a Panzer,
Protector, Reaver or hellhound walked through a Lv5 trail with nothing
happening at all. It now classifies instead of returning: **trash takes the
burn and the slow, an elite takes only the slow** — no damage, no nuke burn
tell, no kill points. Dark TRAILBLAZER still burns the triad too.

**Why this needed a new lane rather than deleting an early-out.**
`tod_zombie_speed::slow()` refuses anything boss-flagged, and that refusal is
correct: it owns the horde's gait override, the 1.5 s keep-alive sweep and
`slow_mult()`, none of which an elite's custom locomotion ASM can survive.
So elites go through a new `tod_zombie_speed::slow_elite()` — a timed
playback-rate write and a restore, no gait, no sweep.

**It is safe on all four elites, and that is evidence rather than a guess:**
the upgrade pause has always written `ASMSetAnimationRate( 0.05 )` on every
axis AI, elites included, and every one of them threads
`tod_bosses::boss_pause_watch`, which restores its own base rate on the unpause
edge. Every card event this map has ever run has slowed the Panzer, the
Protector, the Reaver and the hounds to 5% and put them back. A 34% slow for
1.2 s is the same lever, gentler.

Three details that make it hold:

- **One stamp for the base rate.** `boss_pause_watch` already receives each
  elite's true rate (1.0 hound/Reaver, `TOD_PANZER_ANIM_RATE`,
  `TOD_RP_ANIM_RATE`) and now records it as `.tod_elite_base_rate`, so the new
  restore can never disagree with the pause watcher's restore. Deliberately
  **not** `.tod_base_rate` — that field is also the gate that picks a sky-drop
  relocation over a ground tell in `tod_boss_stuck_watch`, and stamping it on a
  hound or a Reaver would have silently handed them an entrance they are not
  built for.
- **It never fights an owner.** The drop-in entrance (`tod_dropping`), the
  upgrade pause and a menu freeze each own an elite's rate outright;
  `slow_elite` declines to write in all three, on the way in *and* on the way
  out (restoring during a card event would un-freeze a boss mid-pause). Losing
  costs one lapsed slow — the trail re-applies every 500 ms tick.
- **The emerge gate is a trash gate.**
  `completed_emerging_into_playable_area` is stock's field, set by the *zombie*
  behaviour tree when a riser clears a barricade. Every elite here is a direct
  `SpawnActor` on its own tree, so nothing was ever going to set it on a
  Panzer — left unscoped, that one condition would have made the entire elite
  lane dead on arrival while every lint stayed green.

**Dark TRAILBLAZER slows a boss for the first time in this build.** v17.10
passed the triad to `slow()`, which had already returned on its boss guard
before it read the multiplier — the dark card's advertised boss slow has never
once fired.

### The pause row says what it does

`DETAIL[46]`'s activation line read `"while sprinting; bosses immune"`: true of
the damage, and now false of the effect as a whole — precisely the wording that
leaves a player believing the trail does nothing to a Panzer. It now reads
`"while sprinting; elites slowed, not burned"`, with the dark row overriding it
to `"elites burned too"`. The value line carries all three live numbers
(`burns N%/s, slows N%, lasts N.Ns`) and the row's comment now spells out the
formula behind each against its GSC owner, since this row is the only place a
player ever reads any of them. Both fit the measured column budget
(eff ≤ 40, act ≤ 46) and `lint_tod_lua.js` passes. The domain description in
`add_domain` was rewritten to match.

**No art is owed, and the comment that said otherwise was wrong.** The
`add_domain` line carried a note that the baked card "still shows the old line
and owes a re-bake" — written before the art shipped, and left standing after
it did. The card that actually shipped (v16.65, docs/83) bakes the flavour line
`FIRE FOLLOWS YOUR SPRINT` and no figures at all, per the generic-card-text
rule, so it is as true today as it was yesterday. Note retired.

UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-05 15:3x (v17.83) — HELLHOUNDS ARRIVE ON A LIGHTNING BOLT AND TARGET FROM FRAME ONE; the Warden King is per-player; three crates were floating over the summit

Three user reports from the same session: *"they should target right away.
Also they dont have a spawn animation. They just appear ... typically the game
has an animation of them spawning in"* and *"1/4 health on solo. Should scale
linearly. I gave you the 4 player health so he basically cant die when IM
playing."*

### The hound hold is gone, and the guard it was standing in for is one field

v17.43 withheld a hound's TARGET for `TOD_HOUND_SPAWN_HOLD_MS` (2500) to kill
306 throws of `pair '100' and 'undefined'` out of `behavior_zombie_dog`'s
`GetYaw`. It worked, and it cost the enemy the thing it is for — a pack that
stood still for up to three seconds after landing (a 0.5 s watch tick on top of
the 2.5 s hold). **The right guard was in stock the whole time.** Read
`behavior_zombie_dog.gsc:378-412` in order:

```
:378  if ( ignoreall || pacifist || target invalid )   -> CLEARS favoriteenemy
:397  if ( IS_TRUE( ignoreme ) )                       -> plain return
:412  if ( isdefined( favoriteenemy ) && need_to_run() )    <- THE THROW SITE
```

`ignoreme` returns out of the target service **above** `need_to_run()` — the
exact call that threw — and, unlike `ignoreall`, it does not wipe the target on
the way past. So the hound now carries `favoriteenemy` from the `SpawnActor`
frame and still never runs the yaw math while it is materialising.
`hound_target_watch` goes back to being RE-acquisition only; the
`tod_hound_spawn_ms` / `tod_hound_first_target` pair is retired.

**And line :378 is a finding in its own right:** `set_world_pause` writes
`ignoreall = true` on every axis AI, and the dog tree answers by clearing
`favoriteenemy`. Every world pause therefore costs every hound its target. The
watch re-picks within 0.5 s of the unpause, so it recovers — but nothing else
in the map does, and that is worth knowing before adding another `ignoreall`
writer.

### The arrival — `hound_spawn_in`

Stock's `dog_spawn_fx`, rebuilt for a map that cannot call it (it asserts a
magic bullet shield and runs the tail of `dog_init`, which this map never
runs — the Ghosted/shielded/ignoreme trap this file has documented since v14).
Ours: `Hide()` + `ignoreme` on the spawn frame, the lightning buildup at the
spawn point, `zmb_hellhound_prespawn`, **1.2 s**
(`TOD_HOUND_SPAWN_FX_SECS`; stock waits 1.5), then the bolt + spawn sounds, an
`Earthquake`, a yaw-only `ForceTeleport` to face the target, `Show()`,
`ignoreme` cleared, `notify( "visible" )`.

- **The fx rides a `tag_origin` host + `PlayFxOnTag`,** not the bare `Playfx`
  stock uses on that line: a server-side ONE-SHOT does not draw here.
  `derez_burst_run` / `zap_burst_run` are the proven lane.
- **The zone line is ours now.** `zombie/fx_dog_lightning_buildup_zmb` is a
  real 53 KB effect (not one of the 298 stub `.efx`) and stock precaches it —
  but the map's `.ff` ledger has **no `fx_dog_*` row at all**; those ride in
  `zm_levelcommon`, a fastfile this zone cannot see. A `#precache` with nothing
  behind it resolves to nothing and PlayFX no-ops in silence, so an `fx,` line
  and a `#precache` of our own are both in.
- **The three `zmb_hellhound_*` aliases are unverified from disk.** The game
  ships a `hellhound` sound loadspec but the mod tools' raw alias CSVs do not
  carry them. If the bolt lands in silence, the aliases are what to look at —
  not the fx.
- No `level endon( "end_game" )` on that thread: a hound left hidden and
  untargetable forever is worse than a stray reveal at the end of a match.

### THE WARDEN KING: 25M a head, not 100M flat

`TOD_KING_HP` was a flat 100,000,000 at every party size — v17.70 read the
user's number as universal when it was the **four-player** figure, so a solo
player fought the four-player king. Now `TOD_KING_HP_PER_PLAYER` 25,000,000 x
the connected party, clamped at `TOD_KING_HP_MAX_PLAYERS` 4: **solo 25M, duo
50M, trio 75M, quad 100M.**

Deliberately **linear**, and deliberately NOT `tod_bosses::coop_hp_mult`
(1.0 / 1.7 / 2.3 / 2.8): that table is sub-linear so a duo is not fighting two
bosses' worth, but the user set the king's four-player value by hand and asked
for linear, and a curve here would quietly contradict the number he chose.
Resolved ONCE at `king_setup`, like every other boss in the map, so a join or a
leave mid-fight never moves a health bar that is already draining. Counts
CONNECTED players — a teammate bleeding out is still in the fight. Still
round-independent and not rampage-scaled.

Gauge unaffected: `tod_king_hp_frac` is `health / maxhealth`.

### THREE CRATES WERE HANGING IN THE SKY OVER THE BOSS FIGHT

User: *"i believe we have lingering ammo crates about the spire on floor 70. I
was looking up during boss fight and I swear i saw some leftover crate
models."* Confirmed, and it is the same class of defect as the sun volume
(docs/107): **a derived per-floor value that did not follow v17.69's 100 → 70
lap cut.**

`_tod_spire_data::shelf_crate_org( n )` is a FORMULA, not a table, and it had
no ceiling — it rejected floors below 5, hub floors and post-hub floors, then
returned coordinates for anything else, forever. `crate_window` materialises
every floor within `TOD_SPIRE_CRATE_WINDOW` (3) of a player and trusts an
`isdefined` on that return. On the summit deck a player reads as floor
**71** (`1 + int( 26880 / 384 )`), so the window asked for 72, 73 and 74 —
and got three valid-looking origins at z 27,456 / 27,840 / 28,224, above the
top of the tower. Three crate models in mid-air, exactly where the user was
looking.

Invisible before v17.69 because at 100 laps those floors had real shelves.

Fixed in the GENERATOR (`n > SP_LAPS` in the emitted guard) with the reasoning
written into the emitted comment, so the next lap-count change reads it. The
`.map` regenerates **byte-identical** — this is a `-GscOnly`.

Audited the siblings while here: `get_spire_door_info` is bounded 1..70
already, and `guard_spawn_org` is only ever called with a door number, which
the door set bounds. `shelf_crate_org` was the one unbounded formula reachable
from an unbounded caller.

executed — first boot is the test.

User: *"the trial banners are too big. We need like 25% smaller"* and *"I feel

### Banner size — shipped (`-GscOnly`)

`_tod_spire::trial_banner` drew every TRIAL I..VII plate and the WON plate at
`SetShader( mat, 600, 150 )`. Now **448 × 112**: 25.3% off each axis, and
EXACTLY 4:1, which is the source art's own ratio (2048 × 512), so nothing
squishes. One line, both plates — they are the same series and must match.

### The gauge — diagnosed, art pack built, NOTHING CHANGED IN GAME YET

The v17.69 re-grid (50 cells at pitch 21 → **35 at pitch 30**, for 70 floors)
was right. What went with it was the PROPORTION between a floor lamp and a
trial plate. Measured off both lit masters at luminance > 140:

| | floor lamp | trial plate | width ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| old (50 @ 21) | 119 px wide, slim body in a 21-px band | 139 px | 1.17× |
| shipped (35 @ 30) | 109 px wide, body fattened to ~22 of its 30-px band | 136 px | 1.25× |

**On paper the shipped hub plate is MORE distinct; on screen it is less** —
which is the whole lesson here. Two changes cancelled: the floor lamps grew
into fat blocks while the trial plate flattened. The gauge is drawn at
**52 × 416**, so a cell is **8.7 px tall at 720p** and only width and
brightness survive; the gold stopped being *a different kind of object* and
became *a divider line between red blocks*. The unlit master has the same
problem from the other side — an unlit trial plate is only **1.28×** the
brightness of an unlit floor plate, so the seven trials cannot be counted
ahead of time, which is the instrument's whole job.

**Evidence, not opinion:** `docs/108_spire_gauge_ref/COMPARE_onscreen.png`
(both eras, unlit + lit, rendered at the REAL 52 × 416 and magnified) and
`ZOOM_cells_1to1.png` (1:1 crops around a trial plate). Both ride in the pack.

- **`docs/108_spire_gauge_trials_art_prompt.md`** — the brief. Asks for three
  measurable things at the CURRENT grid: floor lamp slimmed to ~104 × 16 in
  its 30-px cell (7 px dark margin), trial plate widened to ~152 × 24 with its
  wings touching the rails, and unlit trial plates ≥ 2× the brightness of an
  unlit floor plate. Ratios ≥ 1.45× width AND ≥ 1.5× height — both, not one.
- The 7-px margin is deliberate: the v17.70 delivery needed
  `slice_gauge.js --band-tol 140` because it drew plates edge-to-edge. This
  brief is written so the DEFAULT band-line check passes.
- Pack: `~/Downloads/tod_spire_gauge_trials_art_pack.zip` (4 masters + a
  review sheet). No code, zone or GDT change is waiting on it — the grid is
  already 35 × 30 and `slice_gauge.js --spire` cuts whatever comes back.

- **"you will be frozen but enemies will still attack you" (spire).**
  `set_world_pause` enumerates `GetAITeamArray` ONCE and stamps
  `tod_frozen` / `ignoreall` / rate 0.05 on what is alive at that instant.
  Every boss family (Panzer, Protector, Reaver, hound) threads
  `boss_pause_watch`, the symmetric watcher that also APPLIES the freeze to
  anything that finishes spawning mid-pause — **trash zombies and armored
  sprinters have no equivalent.** Stock's `round_spawning` does honour
  `world_is_paused` (`_zm.gsc:3747`), so the ordinary riser lane is covered;
  what is not is anything already dispatched inside that loop iteration, or on
  a lane of ours. `_tod_endless_rounds.gsc` reads the pause flag zero times.
- **"dogs may be broken … many times they are frozen".** v17.43's
  `TOD_HOUND_SPAWN_HOLD_MS` (2500) deliberately leaves a hound with **no
  enemy at all** for 2.5 s after `SpawnActor`, to kill a 306-throw exception

  0.5 s. So a fresh pack legitimately stands still for up to **3 seconds** —
  by construction, in the live build. That is almost certainly the report.
  The fix is a trade against the throws that hold bought, so it wants the
  user's call rather than a guess.

## 2026-09-05 14:1x (v17.80) — THE YELLOW WAS THE SUN VOLUME: v17.69's spire cut shrank it 10,272 units, and the whole tower lit on default light parameters

Root cause of the yellow-olive cast that every build since the 09-04 crash
night carried (docs/107). CONFIRMED by a two-build bisect, both looked at by
the user at the same spot (beside the crate, round 1, pre-power):

- v17.79 (`SKY_TOP` floored at the published 39,168 + a from-nothing `.led`):
  **"Yep its good"** — dark panels, the published look.
- v17.80 bisect (floor OFF, from-nothing `.led` again): **"Yep yellow is
  back."** And the bake wrote a `.led` of 44,592,078 B — byte-identical in
  size to every yellow bake — while the good bake wrote 45,041,494 B. The
  file follows the volume height, not the deletion.

WHAT IT WAS. `SKY_TOP` sizes both the sky enclosure and the `volume_sun`
brush (the map-wide sun / light-grid volume, `grid_density 32`), as
`max(MAST_TOP, CROWN_TOP, spire term) + 300`. The spire term with 100 laps
was 39,168; v17.69's cut to 70 laps made it 27,648, `CROWN_TOP` (28,896)
took over, and the volume dropped from 39,500 to 29,228. From that build on
the engine lit every surface, the viewmodel and the zombies with a warm
light that honoured the base lights' positions but not their colour or
their lighting state (authored OFF pre-power) — default light parameters.
The published v17.58 build had the tall volume by accident of its geometry.
The mechanism inside Radiant / the engine is NOT known; the rule is
empirical and now holds by construction.

THE FIX. `SUN_VOLUME_TOP_MIN = 39168` in the generator, an extra `max()`
term under `SKY_TOP`, with the whole proof in its comment. If the geometry
ever grows past it, `max()` wins. Ship build = a STANDARD full build (no
`.led` deletion — the normal pipeline must reproduce the good result),
`-CleanPak`. The good 13:54 `.led` is parked in the session scratchpad.

WHAT IT WAS NOT (six builds, all reverted and all recorded above): the
cybercity sky, its exposure, the fsi, the spawn light, the dev flags, the
vision file, the LUT, the ssi (the `.led` embeds its direction), memory
starvation (pagefile fine), the asset DB, Radiant's caches, lighting
states, a stale `.led`. The control map (`Repositories/test+map`, the Mod
Tools template) baked clean on this host the whole time.

CREDIT: the lead came from the peer session (tower-of-doom-cybercity-9f),
which diffed the generator's derived heights against the published build
after every direct lever was exhausted.

SHIP BUILD 14:1x (`-CleanPak`, standard pipeline, nothing deleted first):
`.led` 14:15:05 at 45,041,494 B (the good size, reproduced by the normal
build), banks 14:15:31 (no retry), `.ff` 14:15:53, pack 1.67 GB clean,
deployed == repo, nothing synced after. `tod_dev` / `tod_god` false. The
A/B pair was played; the user looked at this exact build at the crate spot
(round 1, pre-power) and confirmed it: "Okay it looks good" (14:4x). CLOSED.

## 2026-09-05 04:05 (v17.74) — THE SKY IS A LIGHT SOURCE: the yellow world and the blown-out sky were the same number

User (v17.73 in game): *"Still see this yellow ish hue"* / *"The night sky is
too bright and all the buildings have this white white glow to them as well."*

- ROOT CAUSE, read from docs_modtools/SunSky_Light_SetUp.pdf: *"A sky light is
  a spherical light projected into the scene using the sky texture for value
  and color ... skyStops adjusts the brightness of the sky light"*, and the ssi
  *"is what will bake into the reflection probes."* THE SKY IMAGE LIGHTS THE
  WORLD. Our material is a clone of Miami's and carries `skyStops 10.0` — the
  highest in the pack (others 2–7) because Miami's file is near-black. The
  pack's rule, measured across three skies: image mean × 2^skyStops ≈ 1.3
  (Miami 1.3e-3 × 2^10, Amsterdam 0.146 × 2^3, Moscow 0.042 × 2^5). The v17.73
  file (mean 3.9e-3, bright in BOTH hemispheres) scored ~4.0 — three times the
  pack's ambient, poured into every wall, gun and zombie (the olive-yellow
  cast is the map's dark albedos under strong light). The same brightness,
  through the pack-constant display scale `skyScaleRGB 1097.5`, blew the sky
  and the buildings to white.
- FIX in the renderer (no material change): `SKY_GAIN` 0.06 → 0.025, the
  lower hemisphere ×0.45 (stock skies are BLACK below for exactly this
  reason), bloom 0.45 → 0.30, reflections 0.34 → 0.20. File mean 7.4e-4 →
  score 0.76 (Miami 1.35): the world lights ~0.6× the old Miami ambient,
  the sky displays ~0.56× Miami's mean with neon peaks 2.6× its horizon.
- THE KNOBS, from now on: file brightness = display; `skyStops` in
  source_data/tod_skybox.gdt = how much it lights the world (a GDT edit +
  FULL build; the bake reads it). Never touch `skyScaleRGB`.
- FULL build (04:0x). UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.63) — "SPOTS WHERE YOU CAN'T GET TARGETED": the navmesh was 18 islands, and now it is read on every build

User: *"We have been having this issue on the map where random spot on the map
zombies wont attack you ... Now around floor 42-44 they wont attack but above
and below they will. This is on main tower ... i need you to permantely solve
this so it stops happening"* and *"There are spots where you just cant get
targetted."*

### Why "can't get targeted" is a navmesh sentence

Zombies do not chase the player. They chase `player.last_valid_position` —
stock `player_shared::last_valid_position`, the player's cached NAVMESH point,
which only moves while `IsPointOnNavMesh( origin )` is true or mesh is within
100 units — and `zombieUpdateGoal` needs a PATH to it. Usermaps run the
SCRIPT enemy-selection path (`zm_usermap_ai` sets
`scr_zm_use_code_enemy_selection 0`), so `tod_closest_player` is live and it
is a straight-line pick: targeting itself was never position-dependent. Both
halves of the symptom are the mesh.

### What the shipped mesh actually was

Nothing in the repo could read a `.hkt`, so every previous pass argued from the
`.map`, the seed count and the file's BYTE SIZE. **`tools/lint_tod_navmesh.js`
decodes it** (Havok 2014.2 binary tagfile: faces, edges, vertices — format in
its header, every claim cross-checked against the decoded mesh) and the
shipped v17.61 mesh came back as **1263 faces in 18 connected components**:

- the tower was cut into horizontal slabs — z 0..6170, 6228..6938, 7045..12314,
  12342..14618, 14785..16154, 16321+ — and the spire, 10,000 units away in x,
  was cut at the SAME heights;
- every seam sat inside the **E flight of odd laps 17, 19, 33, 39 and 43** on
  both towers, plus one-to-three-face islands mid-flight on 39 and 43.
  Floor 43 (z 16128-16512) is the user's 42-44; lap 17 is the v17.7 "no
  navmesh above floor 17" ceiling, which was this seam PLUS pruning of the
  unseeded upper part;
- a vertex census was green on every floor, the seeds were uniform (8 per
  floor), `cod2map_last.log` was clean and the `.hkt` size was healthy.
  **Only the faces' `oppositeFace = -1` at the seams showed it.**

A player standing on a seam island cannot be reached from either side; a
zombie chasing across a seam stops dead and waits for `_tod_stray` to move it.
Floors 42-44 are geometrically identical to 45-46 (per-lap brush inventory
diffed: zero differences), so the cause had to be arithmetic, not layout.

### The cause, proven by compile-and-re-read

The stair ramp wedge (`clip`, the AI walking surface since v16.61a) had its top
plane passing EXACTLY through every tread's front-top nosing edge — fifteen
coplanar contact LINES per flight. Havok's overlapping-triangle fixup slivers
that, and on laps whose plane arithmetic rounds badly the ramp's faces come out
unstitched. The plane depends only on y and z, which is why the spire failed on
the identical laps. Two experiments, each a cod2map run plus a re-read (~45 s):

- a per-map `share/raw/maps/zm/zm_tower_of_doom_navmesh_settings.json`
  override (that IS the lookup path — copies in `bin/` and `map_source/` are
  ignored) with `simplification.useHeightPartitioning: false` changed the face
  count (1263 → 1202) and left EVERY seam. Not a partitioner artifact.
- **`RAMP_LIFT = 2`** in `gen_tower_map.js` (rampWedgeY/X shift the whole
  wedge up 2: no tread edge touches the plane; underside still inside the tread
  slabs; the two ends become 2-unit steps, under Havok's maxStepHeight 18) —
  the regen touched exactly 311 wedges × 6 planes and nothing else (generated
  data GSCs byte-identical), and the mesh re-read as **2 components**: the
  tower with its crown road, and the spire. All 50 tower floors and all 100
  spire floors in their tower's base component.

Players never touched the treads except at the nosings (they walk the invisible
ramp), so the visible change is feet 2 units higher on every step.

### The gate

`build_map.ps1` runs `lint_tod_navmesh.js` on the `.hkt` right after cod2map
on every full build and **dies** if any tower floor is outside its tower's base
component. A seam is a shipped bug no play-test below it can see; from now on
it cannot pass a build. `--no-gate` reports only, `--verbose` prints every
floor.

### Recorded so it is not re-learned

- cod2map by hand: PowerShell only, cwd = bin, REAL output path
  (`share/raw/maps/zm/<map>.d3dbsp`) — Git Bash and a scratch output dir both
  abort with exit 127 inside "begin navmesh generation". `-loadFrom` may point
  at the repo `.map` directly, so a regen can be compiled and read without a
  sync or a bake.
- The `.hkt` vertices are float32 IN METRES (game / 39.3701); ints are
  LEB128 with the sign in the low bit; arrays of structs are struct-of-arrays
  behind a member bitfield. Scanning the file for game-unit floats was the
  earlier "quantized verts" dead end.
- CLAUDE.md (spire/navmesh section) and the navmesh memory carry the same.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.61) — WARDEN TRIAL: the world freezes on the win, not three seconds later

User: *"We need to make sure to freeze the game during the trials reward."*

- **The gap.** The trial's card deal (`trial_upgrade_deal` →
  `run_upgrade_event`) has frozen the world since v16.36 — but only when the
  deal BEGAN, 3 s after the win, and the deal was deliberately delayed "so the
  win reads before the world freezes". Those 3 s were a live hall: standing
  Wardens hunted, adds on the floor kept swinging, the family debts
  `trial_adds` had SET kept draining into new elites (the directors only stop
  once the flag is up), and stock's trickle kept rising — under the WON
  plate, the jackpot and the Max Ammo drop. And with nobody holding a card
  (everything maxed, no dark, no tier roll) there was never a freeze at all.
- **`trial_win` now calls `tod_upgrades::set_world_pause( true )` on the last
  chord**, before any reward lands, and the freeze is held straight through
  the deal: `run_upgrade_event` re-sets the same pause (idempotent) and
  releases it with the last pick. `trial_upgrade_deal` releases it itself on
  the empty-deal path (the flag still true, no station owner) — the one path
  where nothing else would have.
- **Players are not frozen by the win** — the cards freeze each participant
  as before. The 3 s are theirs to reach the Max Ammo on a board that cannot
  touch them; damage on the frozen board is 0 as at every round event.
- **Summit extraction refuses during a freeze** (`summit_station`, the same
  gate every spire door has had since v14.31, with the deny sound). The
  hub-100 trial now ends in a frozen reward with that trigger inside the
  hall; a card-less player could otherwise have ended the run while a
  teammate was mid-pick.
- **The Max Ammo's clock starts when the freeze lifts** (`trial_ammo_drop`).
  Stock's `powerup_timeout` is real time (15 s + ~11 s blinking) and blind to
  the pause, so a drop at the win spent most of its life under the frozen
  reward — a solo player who read both cards to the end had ~8 s to reach it.
  The drop now goes out with stock's own `b_stay_forever` (no timeout thread
  at all), and the same stock `powerup_timeout` is started on it the moment
  `tod_upgrade_pause` clears. No custom clock, no level-wide override.
- `-GscOnly` build. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.56) — The spire sells no perks; dev: every spire door open

**THE SPIRE SELLS NO PERKS.** User: *"carefully remove all perks
from the spire because during the endless spire you have all perks perma"*
and *"make sure there is no residue"*. Since v16.36 every perk is
perma-granted on ascension, so the v14.0 machine migration (arena + 2 pads
per hub, reshuffle continuing) left nine props that could take 4000 points
for a perk already held. Retired whole:
- `_tod_perk_scatter::retire_all` (new) — at the ascension every machine's
  clip is ConnectPaths'd at its live pad FIRST (the module's two-phase rule),
  then trigger + model + clip + bump + FX host park at `TOD_SCATTER_PARK`
  under the spire arena, the trigger is disabled and the model hidden. The
  roster keys stay (that is what `perma_perks_give` reads). A
  `level.tod_scatter_retired` latch stops the round shuffle, the coherence
  re-align (which would have dragged the parked set back) and the QR clip

## 2026-09-04 (v17.55) — CONTROL PROMPTS: two device sets only (the "LT / RT / A" keycaps are gone)

User: *"There are 3 sets of controls on this map during the class selection
or upgrade menu. Its like dpad and A, rt lt and A, and KBM. I dont even want
rt lt as an option for the UI. The UI should only show dpad options or KBM.
Two sets only."*

**What the third set was.** Every control surface (class draft, deal panel,
pause-menu UPGRADE CARDS legend) chose pad glyphs vs keycaps off `CoD.TodPad`,
the one-way d-pad latch, which starts FALSE. A pad player who had not pressed
the d-pad yet was therefore drawn the KEYCAP layout, and the engine filled the
caps with the pad's own names for the offhand pair and jump: "LT", "RT", "A".
Keyboard art wearing controller words. Nobody designed it; it is what a
false-by-default latch draws to a pad.

**The device read was already on screen.** `Engine.Localize` expands a
`[{+bind}]` token into the name bound on the device the client is USING —
that is exactly how a pad player came to read "LT". So the expansion proves
the device: an offhand token that resolves to a pad button name means a pad.
This is the read docs/88 §"The device-detection problem" went looking for,
bounded to what it proves (a pad name proves a pad; a keyboard name proves a
keyboard). Tested on the OFFHAND PAIR only — A/B/X/Y are also keyboard keys,
so `+gostand` can never decide it.

- `TodKeycap.lua`: `CoD.TodKeycap.IsPadName()` (LB/RB/LT/RT, L1/R1/L2/R2,
  TRIGGER / BUMPER / D-PAD long forms) and `CoD.TodKeycap.PadDevice()` = the
  d-pad latch OR a pad name in the `+smoke` / `+frag` expansion. ONE reader.
- `tod_upgrade.lua` + `tod_class_select.lua` `UsingController()` and the
  pause legend's `TodPad` all route through it (nil-safe under the pcall'd
  require). By construction a keycap can no longer carry a pad button name:
  if the name is a pad name, the surface is in the pad branch.
- Inputs unchanged: LT/RT/stick still cycle where they did; only the DISPLAY
  is two sets (user: "maybe you can still cycle with rt and lt but im talking
  about displayed control sets only").
- Not fixed, not claimed: a KEYBOARD player who taps 3/4 still latches
  `CoD.TodPad` and sees pad glyphs (v16.81). The expansion could overrule the
  latch in that direction too, but that is an unverified assumption about
  which device the engine expands FOR while a pad is merely plugged in — the
  pad→pad direction is proven by the user's own "LT / RT" reading, the
  reverse is not. Left for a run with a pad plugged in on a keyboard.

Lua only, -GscOnly. lint_tod_lua: 46 files, 0 findings. UNPLAYED.

### 2. DARK UPGRADES — eligible for two means dealt two

User: *"when you have max upgrades only one Dark Upgrade shows up. There should
still be two cards ... It should be at least one dark upgrade if you have a
maxed out upgrade. But in no situation where you are eligible for two dark
upgrades should you only get one."*

The cause, in `deal_dark`: the fully-maxed player arrives with an EMPTY hand
(roll_options' `pool.size == 0` path), the first slot is forced dark, and the
second slot was a 35 % roll (`TOD_DARK_BOTH_PCT`) — so two times in three that
player looked at a ONE-CARD panel with a second dark card sitting undealt in
the pool. Two rules now, both in `deal_dark`:

1. **Structural:** an empty right slot is filled with a second dark card
   whenever one exists, regardless of the knob. The one-card panel can only
   happen when exactly one dark card is left and nothing else is eligible.
2. **The user's rule:** `TOD_DARK_BOTH_PCT` 35 → **100**, so a REGULAR card in
   the right slot is displaced by the second dark card too. The tier card keeps
   the right slot when it is dealt (a promotion is a choice the design wants;
   the user's rule is about dark eligibility, not the tier card). docs/92's
   table row updated.

it's different from what's in pause menu for dark run and gun."* Audited the

## 2026-09-04 (v17.45) — THE CAMO HAS NEVER BEEN LOOKED AT: every test since v17.36 died on its own dev print

User, after v17.39: *"Yeah still no pap camo"* — no dev print on either lane, PACK II
inert, no re-draw after the pack, *"my gun did seem upgraded tho"*. I first read that
as a wrong artifact (the subscribed Workshop copy); the user rejected it — *"We did a
build right before I played … every other change from other agents were there"* —
and was right. `console_mp.log` of that 18:02 match has the real answer, which
v17.43 had already found from the same log:

```
Error: pair 'CAMO stamp t6_mp7_up_h3  idx 1  opts ' and 'uint64' has unmatching types
  _tod_classes.gsc line 620  <- 599 (give_camo_weapon)              [class-gun swap]
  _tod_classes.gsc line 620  <- 651 (camo_regive) <- zm_cwpap 512   [secondary pack]
```

`CalcWeaponOptions` returns a **uint64**, and string-concatenating one throws. The
throw sits AFTER the `GiveWeapon` and BEFORE everything that follows it, so on every
lane the packed form was given with the right options and then the thread died:
`swap_primary` never switched to it and never took the old form (the upkeep loop
that owns reconcile died with it — v17.43's finding), `giveWeaponUpgraded` never
raised the re-dressed secondary, `giveWeaponRepacked` never raised the tier gun.
**The player kept the BASE form in hand every time.** A base gun wears no camo by
design, so "no camo" was the correct rendering of the gun being looked at; the
`_up` twin with the camo options sat unraised in the inventory. Three builds of
art and give-lane work were tested against a gun the camo was never on.

v17.43 replaced the concat with `opts != 0`. A uint64 compared against an int is
the same untyped pair as far as anyone has proven, and its failure is the same
silent death, so this build does not touch the value at all: the print says
`CAMO stamp <weapon>  idx N` and nothing else. The only thing that may ever hold
that number is GiveWeapon's second argument.

What one match should now show, in order: the yellow `CAMO stamp … idx 1` line at
the first pack, the gun RE-DRAWN into the hand (that is the swap completing, which
no camo test has seen yet), and then whatever the camo looks like. If the line
prints, the swap completes, and the gun is STILL bare, the give lane is proven and
the fault is finally isolated to the material — the slot-4 control on a dev-build
secondary answers that in the same match.

-GscOnly. Lints: arity OK across 73 files. UNPLAYED.

  `_tod_atmosphere::apply_fog` re-asserted `SetVolFog` every 0.1 s ungated
  (its comment said so, deliberately) and the engine logs `setVolFog: Old
  syntax used` on each — 1,957 lines, on a tower that has NO fog. `set_fog()`
  is now change-gated map 1's way: one key from all 8 args, early return on a
  match, key written only AFTER the builtin so the first call of every new
  state goes through (the v14.42 gate compared against a value it had just
  written and could never fire twice). Tower: one call at start. Spire: one
  call per state change.

  and 'undefined' has unmatching types`, three frames in
  `behavior_zombie_dog.gsc`, values 100/−42/−12 = the dog's own yaw). The
  tree's `GetYaw()` is `VectorToAngles( enemy.origin − self.origin )[1]`;
  our spawn set `favoriteenemy` on the spawn frame, so `need_to_run()` ran
  against the target while the dog was still materialising — and a fallback
  spawn AT the target's origin is the zero-vector case. Two guards in
  `_tod_hellhounds.gsc`: (1) never spawn within 8u of the target
  (48u random push), (2) `TOD_HOUND_SPAWN_HOLD_MS` 2500 — no target until the

  spawn, n=306), not watched in a debugger — if the throw survives, the next

## 2026-09-04 (v17.39) — PACK-A-PUNCH CAMO: THE WIRING REVIEW, THREE DEFECTS, ONE UNPROVEN ASSUMPTION

User: *"Can you look into pap camos? Ive had an agent look into but seems they
had issues. They did just apply a fix but I want you to review and see if
everything is wired correctly"*, then *"If we neeed these then yes complete
your task"*.

### What the review confirmed (v17.36 IS deployed correctly)

All nine textures are RGBA in the repo AND the tools root, the GDT is
byte-identical in both, and the 17:03 `.ff` was built from this exact tree
(deployed diff clean, nothing synced after it). The ledger carries real records
end to end: 3 materials at 1146 B, 9 images with streamed bytes, 22 per-gun
weaponcamo tables at 2.6-3.2 KB each pulled by its `_up` weapon, the techset
present. Slot semantics are right: the install's stock SHIP tables carry
`baseIndex 1` with row 42 = `mtl_wpn_t7_camo_etching`, so index N selects row
N; ours are `baseIndex 1` with the tiers on rows 1-3. Every give site the map
owns routes through `give_camo_weapon`, and the watcher is threaded per spawn.

### Defect 1 — the middle scroll layer was somebody else's camo

`gen_tod_camo.js` rewrote `colorMap`, `colorMap00` and `colorMap02` and left
`colorMap01` at the template's `i_wpn_t9_camo_madgaz1_c`. The ledger proved it
rather than a diff: that 5.6 MB orange texture's parent was `mc/tod_camo_pap3`.
The template points 00/01/02 at ONE image; now so do we. **The tints are now
identity too** — the template's `colorTint`/`colorTint1..3` are MadGaz's cyan
grades for HIS orange emissive, and a multiply by white is the only setting that
cannot recolour CIRCUIT's magenta or OVERLOAD's gold.

### Defect 2 — the normal maps were declared as colour

The proven `_n` image is `coreSemantic Normal` + `compressionMethod compressed`.
Ours stamped all nine as `sRGB3chAlpha` / `compressed high color` and only
flipped the `semantic` word — an sRGB-curved, BC7-packed height field. Lights the
etching wrong rather than hiding it, but it is not the recipe.

### Defect 3 — the machine paths rested on an unproven engine behaviour

Neither the stock-lane 5,000 buy (`giveWeaponUpgraded`, secondaries) nor the
PACK II/III buy passed through the camo give. The buy used stock's
`weapon_give` with index 42 — off the end of our four-row table — and the tier
lane re-gave NOTHING (v17.33 left the gun in hand on the reasoning "the asset
does not change"). Both were "repaired" by `camo_watch` calling `GiveWeapon` on
a weapon the player already HELD. Stock never does that: `weapon_give` branches
on `HasWeapon` and only refills ammo. Whether a second give re-applies weapon
options is unproven, and it was the only thing between a tier buy and its camo.
(Class-gun packs were already fine: the class lane latches `tod_pap_owned` and
`swap_primary` gives the `_up` form fresh, camo riding in that give.)

Now the proven shape, at the proven place: `tod_classes::camo_regive( w, raise )`
= TAKE -> GIVE with options, ammo restored by hand, then a bounded frame-paced
re-assert (ensure_equipped's 30×0.05 s) against the eaten-switch strand.
Called from `giveWeaponUpgraded` right after stock's give, and from the new
`giveWeaponRepacked` for the tier buy — the 5,000 stock lane's own take-at-the-
lever / give-after-the-show, same frame, no empty-handed window (the knuckle
wait is compile-time off). `camo_watch` is a BACKSTOP now and only re-dresses a
HOLSTERED gun: a take/give of the weapon in hand is exactly the state the
swap_primary block comment warns about, and a backstop must never be the thing
that causes the map's worst-known bug. The dev print (`camo_stamp`) now fires on
every lane, since `camo_regive` stamps.

Gates: arity OK across 73 files, hints 94/190, assets no-regression, Lua 0
findings. FULL build (GDT). **UNPLAYED.** What to look at in one match: PaP a
SECONDARY (the stock lane) and PaP the class gun; both should wear GRID, and the
dev print says the index and options for each. In the spire, PACK II should turn
the same gun CIRCUIT without a pistol flash — that flash, if it happens, is the
eaten-switch strand and the re-assert is the thing to lengthen.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.38) — THE AMMO CRATE, MASTERED: one facing, one box, one trigger, every crate in the map

User: *"check the trigger on all ammo crates. Some of them are off and you cant
get ammo unless at a certain angle. Also check the crates at the endless spire
and check if they have properly clips, facing the correct direction, and proper
trigger points to buy. Lets do this one run and master ammo crates so we dont
ever have to touch them again."*

### What "a certain angle" was

Every crate spawned its `trigger_radius_use` ON the model origin, radius 72.
The crate's own collision holds a player's origin at least 38 (the face) + ~16
(the capsule) = **54u from that origin — an 18-unit usable band**, and only on
the face's centre line, because the radius shrinks off-axis. Stand naturally,
or a step to the side, and there is no prompt. The spire arena crate was worse:
its script-clip row ran **front-to-back** through the crate (`AnglesToRight` is
the FRONT at a crate's yaw) and planted an invisible lip beyond the face.

### The contract — `gen_tower_map.js`, one block, everything derives from origin + yaw

* **Facing** `CRATE_YAW_N/W/S/E` (front = yaw + 90; v17.37's finding, now all
  four cardinals). `crateFront()` is the unit vector.
* **Occupancy** `crateBox()` — the measured yaw-270 box (13u off-axis) rotated
  to the crate's real yaw. Base, 4 breathers, crown, **spire arena, all 77
  spire shelves, 10 spire hubs**: 94 `... ammo crate body` brushes, every one
  the mesh's real footprint, every one visible to the geometry lint.
  **No script clips exist any more** — `crate_clips()` is gone, `spawn_crate`
  lost both clip arguments, `delete_crate` has nothing to `ConnectPaths`.
* **Trigger** `CRATE_TRIG_OUT 56` in front of the origin, `CRATE_TRIG_R 72` —
  the stations' and PaP machines' own grammar (`BR_FURN.pap/station.trig` = org
  + 56). Band: the face to ~128u out, ±72 across. The two numbers are EMITTED
  into `_tod_breather_data.gsc` (`crate_trig_out()` / `crate_trig_r()`) and
  `_tod_ammo_crate::spawn_trigger( org, yaw )` reads them back, so the script
  and the generator's pairwise-trigger asserts cannot drift. `trig_org_for()`
  is the one placement function; `place()` and the spire's `spawn_crate` both
  go through it.
* `BR_FURN.crate.trig` / `SP_FURN.crate.trig` are now `crateTrig(org, yaw)` —
  derived, not typed.

### What the asserts moved

The hub crate went **(376,60) → (396,120)**: the moved trigger fell inside
THE CROSS's east arm and THE INNER RING's east walls (the layout-vs-vendor
assert, `r + 8`), so it backs the drum's east wall at 3u and sits above both.
The arena crate went **y −505 → −500**: its yaw-0 box cut 2u into wall S; a new
assert refuses that. Shelf boxes are asserted INSIDE the shelf floor at either
parity (`shelfCrateBox`).

**Shelf boxes are resident** while the crate MODELS still ride the ±3-floor
window. The old "script clips so an empty shelf is clean" reasoning is
inverted: a player on a shelf is inside the window by definition, so the only
thing the script clips ever bought was a collider that matched neither mesh nor
yaw on a 128-deep ledge.

### Comments corrected

`_tod_ammo_crate.gsc` carried *"Vending yaw convention: 0 = front toward -y,
90 = +x, 270 = -x"* — the backwards belief every tower crate was placed under.
The v14.23 "flip is the experiment" notes in the spire-data emitter are
replaced by the record.

Gates: regen clean (13568 world brushes = +78 crate boxes / 2798 entities),
geometry lint GREEN 0/0/0 no-regression, hints 94/190, assets no-regression,
Lua 0 findings, arity OK across 73 files. FULL build (geometry). **UNPLAYED.**
Verify order: base crate prompt from a natural standing distance and a step
off-axis → a breather crate → the crown → spire arena → a shelf → a hub.
