`_prefabs/ALXS/alxs_cwpap_prefab.map` holds the machine at an INTERNAL yaw of
270 and its `pap_trigger_struct` at `(-25, 0, 0)` — the side a player stands on
is prefab-local **-x**. A `misc_prefab`'s angles compose with that, so the
machine's world facing is `180 + instance yaw`:

| instance yaw | machine faces |
|---|---|
| `cyaw(0)` | **WEST — into the hall, across the dais at the altar** |
| `cyaw(180)` | east |
| `cyaw(270)` | north — *what shipped: along the east wall* |

Now `cyaw(0)`. The old S-wall placement was facing EAST along the south wall for
the month it was "verified", which is why the rotation carried the error forward
intact. Cross-check that needs no prefab file: `pap_place_clips` spreads the
machine's colliders along `AnglesToForward` — "the mesh's local +X, its WIDE
axis" — so the cabinet's face is perpendicular to its entity yaw, and the four
breather machines (`BR_FURN.pap`, W wall, yaw 90, facing east, played for weeks)
fix that perpendicular at `yaw - 90`. Two riders come free: the buy trigger moves
from the machine's south flank to its front, and the collider row now runs along
the wall instead of through it.

### 2. Every ammo crate in the map: ONE convention, and the clip follows it

`west_ammo_crate_model`'s front is `yaw + 90`, not the `yaw - 90` every tower
crate was authored against. **v14.23 already ran this experiment** — the user's
answer to "which crates face wrong" was *"All of them"*, so all four spire yaws
were flipped 180 and that entry closed with *"verify by eye next run and record
the winning convention at BR_FURN"*. Nobody did. This report is that
verification: the crown crate is a tower-convention crate backing an EAST wall
at yaw 270, and it faces away from the room.

`CRATE_YAW_W` / `CRATE_YAW_E` + `crateBox()` are now the one source for both
halves, read by base, the four breathers, the crown and the spire hub:

* base, breathers, crown crates **270 -> 90** (front = west, out of the wall).
* **the clip box comes from the yaw.** The mesh is 13u off its own origin, so a
  180 flip moves it 26u — and the v14.23 flip turned four spire crates while
  leaving every box at the yaw-270 occupancy. That mismatch shipped for five
  days and is fixed here too. `crateBox()` throws on any yaw it has no measured
  occupancy for, so the pair cannot come apart again.

### 3. The crown altar is capped at 3 (was unlimited)

`TOD_STATION_USES_CROWN 3`, through the new `station_use_cap( id )`; every other
terminal keeps `TOD_STATION_USES_PER` 5. It went unlimited on 2026-08-29 *"The
heavenly alter in the crown room shouldnt have a limit"* — but that call was made
while the **price ladder** still bound it, and the ladder went flat 3000 with the
triggerstring-250 crash fix, leaving the last vendor of the run uncapped AND
flat-priced. A use cap touches no hint string, so the crash fix is untouched.
Two stale "crown 5 exempt" comments elsewhere corrected.

### 4. The count-in pillars go out at the seal

`pillar_countin` ends on `tod_finale_sealed` — an `endon` **stops a thread, it
does not clean up after it** — so the count-in's last frame stayed lit: a green
aura burning over a crossing pier for the entire hold-out. `pillar_countin_clear()`
is now step 5 of the seal block: glow off, hosts deleted (the ~1024-gentity
budget). `heartbeat_run` polls its own state instead of endon-ing, which is the
other half of the same lesson.

### 5. THE LAST MILE — the ambush was starving on the AI cap

The user's own diagnosis, and it is right. `finale_spawn_selection` picks the
riser ahead of a random living player and `tod_spawn_delay` drops the trickle to
0.1s, but **both are RATE controls**. `level.zombie_ai_limit` (45) caps how many
trash zombies stand at once, and under the endless-rounds twist a deep run sits
at that cap permanently — 45 zombies spread over 19,200 units of tower nobody is
in. Every one holds a slot, none can reach the causeway in 90 seconds, and the
spawner has nothing left to put in front of the party. "Max aggressiveness on
spawns" against a full cap buys exactly nothing, which is why the bridge was a
walk.

* **`wipe_the_map()` at the buy.** The same call the seal already makes, now at
  both ends of the road, so the first wave spawns into an empty cap.
* **`road_cull_run()` keeps it empty.** One wipe only buys the first few seconds
  — the party outruns what spawns behind them and the cap silently refills over
  a 90-second road. Every 2s, any trash zombie further than
  `TOD_FINALE_CULL_DIST` (2500) from EVERY living player is killed. Distance
  only, never geometry, so it can never touch the wave in front of them; 2500 is
  past the fog and past the longest sightline on the road. **Elites are exempt**
  (`ignore_enemy_count`) — a Panzer despawning behind you is a robbery. Downed
  players count as focus points: culling around a crawler would make going down
  safer than staying up. Dies at the seal, where the hall filter already
  guarantees every zombie is in the room.

**No cap is raised anywhere.** This is the same doctrine `finale_pressure_loop`
holds to — the ambush gets the slots the abandoned tower was sitting on, not
extra ones.

lint GREEN 0/0/0 no-regression, hints 94/190, assets no-regression, Lua 0
