## 2026-09-04 (v17.36) — THE CAMO HAD NO ALPHA CHANNEL

v17.35 shipped, linked cleanly, and rendered NOTHING. User: *"Nthing. Pap looked
the same as base. Pap I specifically."*

### The difference between our textures and every working one

```
mg_orange_base1.png / _em1 / _norm   (MadGaz, proven in this install)  colour type 6 = RGBA
i_tod_camo_pap1_c.png / _e / _n      (v17.35, renders nothing)         colour type 2 = RGB
```

The image asset declares `coreSemantic "sRGB3chAlpha"` — three colour channels
**plus alpha** — and the material's techset is
`lit_emissive_scroll_3layer_TRANSPARENT_plus_camo`. Hand that an image with no
alpha channel and the alpha it ends up with is not something anyone promised; on
a transparent techset a zero there is an **invisible camo that links perfectly,
ships real bytes, and draws nothing**. Which is exactly what the asset ledger
showed: three real materials at 1146 B, nine textures at 1024² BC7 in the pack,
and a bare gun in game.

Textures are now RGBA by construction: opaque on the diffuse and the normal, and
the glow's own luminance as alpha on the emissive layer, so the traces light and
the panel between them does not.

Two other suspects were ruled out first, without a build: the camo table's
`base_material_*` / `camo_mask_*` targets all exist in the build (checked by
name against the asset ledger), and the ports' `_up` forms use the same models as
their base forms, so the port's own ship-table rows are the right ones to copy.

### One session now separates every remaining outcome

Three causes were live at once and a single-lane test cannot tell them apart, so
this build instruments the lane. **Both are DEV-ONLY and go with the dev
harness** (`level.tod_dev`, false in every published build):

- the packed **secondary** wears slot 4 — `mtl_origins_camo_alt`, someone else's
  material, already linking with real bytes;
- `camo_stamp()` prints the weapon, the camo index and the options int
  `CalcWeaponOptions` returned (IPrintLnBold — a free lane, no triggerstring).

Reading one match:

| primary | secondary | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| camo | camo | fixed — the alpha was it |
| bare | camo | the lane works, **our material** is wrong |
| bare | bare, `opts` nonzero | the lane runs but never paints — table or techset |
| bare | bare, `opts` 0 | `CalcWeaponOptions` is the fault, not the art |

## 2026-09-04 (v17.35) — PACK-A-PUNCH CAMOS, AND WHY THERE HAVE NEVER BEEN ANY

User 2026-09-04: *"How hard is it to add pap camos to the game for different
tiers?"* — then, on being told what the lane looked like: *"I will say currently
I dont think we have any Pap camos at all."* Correct, on both towers, since the
first build. The reason is not the index.

### The defect

Stock's PaP lane has always passed `level.pack_a_punch_camo_index` (42, the Der
Riese etching) through `_zm_weapons::give_build_kit_weapon`, and every `_up`
variant this repo generates already carried its port's camo table. The break sat
one layer below both. The ledger shows it, but only if you read RECORD SIZES —
the names are all present, which is what makes this easy to get wrong (I did,
first pass: a grep for the material names came back "linked" and a grep missing
the ledger's `mc/` prefix came back "zero", and neither number was the answer):

```
assetinfo/zm_tower_of_doom.csv
  mc/mtl_glass               14 B   the KNOWN "not in gdtDB, substituted" case
  mc/mtl_wpn_t7_camo_*    20-29 B   all 124 stock camo materials — same shape
  mc/mtl_origins_camo_alt  2207 B   a real material, with its images
  mc/tod_camo_pap1         1146 B   ours
i_t7_camo_* / i_wpn_t7_camo_* images shipped: 0   (.ff and xpak alike)
```

A camo table names its materials as STRINGS inside a configstring, and the mod
tools ship no GDT for the stock ones, so what reaches the fastfile is a NAME-ONLY
STUB — no techset, no textures, and unlike `mtl_glass` not even an errorlog line.
Every stock camo index on this map has therefore resolved to nothing paintable,
and the gun has always rendered with its base materials. Map 1 is the same
picture: the same 124 stubs, the same zero textures.

Worth stating plainly, because it makes this more than cosmetic: `t9_mac10_up_*`
shares `worldModel wm_t9_mac10` with the base form. With no camo, **a packed gun
was pixel-identical to an unpacked one** — the camo is the only visual tell that
a gun is packed at all, and there wasn't one.

### The fix — own the materials

`tools/gen_tod_camo.js` (new) bakes three camos in the map's own colour language
and writes `source_data/tod_camo.gdt`:

| slot | camo | look | worn by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GRID | cyan lattice on navy | tier I — the ordinary 5,000 pack |
| 2 | CIRCUIT | magenta board traces | tier II — the spire's 25,000 |
| 3 | OVERLOAD | crown gold over spire red | tier III — the spire's 50,000 |
| 4 | (control) | `mtl_origins_camo_alt` | nothing — diagnostic, see below |

Textures are procedural (a dependency-free PNG encoder over `zlib`), 1024²,
tiling by construction, deterministic so a rebuild does not churn the `.ff`.
Generator art can replace them later at the same nine filenames with no other
change. The material block is COPIED from `mtl_origins_camo_alt` and only the
map fields move: fifteen materials in the whole install carry `useAsCamo 1` and
every one that is a real weapon camo uses
`lit_emissive_scroll_3layer_transparent_plus_camo`, so that is the proven recipe
rather than an invented one. Credit to MadGaz's custom camo pack for the shader
wiring (CREDITS.md); the artwork is ours.

`gen_tod_twins.js` now emits one `tod_camo_<stem>` weaponcamo per gun — 21 of
them — keeping each port's own `base_material_*` / `camo_mask_*` rows (those
name the materials on THAT gun's model) and swapping only `_material`. Every
`_up` variant's camo field is repointed at it. No zone lines: a weaponcamo is
pulled by the weapon that names it, and its material by the weaponcamo — proven
by the Leviathan, which is why `mtl_origins_camo_alt` is in the build today.

### The give lane — where the camo was being dropped anyway

Weapon options are a PER-GIVE value; nothing re-reads them. Every one-argument
`GiveWeapon` in this map was therefore stripping whatever camo stock had just
stamped:

- `_tod_upgrades::swap_primary` — the twin swap, i.e. **every gun-scoped
  level-up after the pack**;
- the class loadout gives on respawn and on a tier promotion;
- the no-classgun repair tick.

All now route through `tod_classes::give_camo_weapon()`. Two paths we do not own
(the PaP machine's buy and the spire's tier re-give, both stock `weapon_give`)
are covered by `camo_watch()` — a 0.5 s per-player watcher that re-gives, ammo
preserved by hand, only when a weapon's stamp disagrees with its tier. It skips
`tod_swap_busy` and last stand, and in a normal round it does nothing: only a
pack or a tier buy makes a stamp stale.

### Slot 4 is a diagnostic, kept on purpose

`mtl_origins_camo_alt` already links and renders in this build. If the tiers come
back blank in game, point `TOD_PAP_CAMO_T1` at 4 and rebuild: a camo on 4 and
nothing on 1-3 means our materials are wrong; nothing on either means the give
lane never applied options. One build separates two failure modes that would
otherwise look identical, and the slot costs nothing.

UNPLAYED. Lints green (arity, hints 94/190, assets, Lua). Guns whose camo table
could not be resolved keep what they had — no camo, never a white square.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.34) — THE TYPEFACE TAKES THE LEFT COLUMN AND THE CENTRE OF THE SCREEN

User 2026-09-04: *"Can you look into changing all the text on screen to use our
alphabet? Mainly looking at the text on Left that shows players name and HP and
the our damage numbers and points gain that show up and displayed at center of
screen. Can we change all of that to use the alphabet we created and numbers.
Our typography."*

Nine readouts moved off orbitron/ltromatic onto the baked glyph sheets:

- **Left column** — the local panel's NAME, HP and POINTS; each teammate row's
  NAME and POINTS.
- **Centre** — the crosshair DAMAGE NUMBERS (`CoD.TodDmgNum`, tod_upgrade.lua),
  the kill feed's per-entry NAME and +SCORE, and its running TOTAL.
- **Bottom left** — the floating +points / -points popups.

### One new element, not nine hand-placed rows

`TodGlyphText.lua` (zoned in `aetherium_hud.zpkg`) wraps `TodGlyphRow` in
something UIText-shaped: `setText` / `getText` / `setRGB` / `setAlpha` /
`setBox`. That surface is the point — every converted readout keeps its existing
call sites verbatim. The kill feed is the extreme case: it shifts entries down
the list by reading each row's text back out with `getText()` and picks a row's
colour by pattern-matching that string, and **not one line of it changed**,
because `getText()` returns the RAW string that was set rather than the cleaned
one that was drawn.

**IT TAKES THE BOX AND DERIVES THE REST.** Cap height is a fraction of the box
(0.80), the baseline another (0.94), alignment is a keyword, and a string too
wide for its box SHRINKS to fit — one multiply, because every term in
`row.measure` is linear in cap. That is what makes the party rows work
untouched: they compute their y from a row index, and the type follows the box
instead of carrying a second set of coordinates. Hand-placing nine caps and nine
baselines was the alternative.

**A PLAYER NAME IS NOT OUR TEXT.** The sheets are caps-only and carry 42 glyphs
(A-Z, 0-9, `- ' . / +`), and `+` and `/` exist ONLY on the digit sheet while `'`
and `.` exist only on the letter sheet — so the cleaner is set-aware, and asking
for `+` through the name set would have routed it to the letter sheet, found
nothing, and blanked the whole string. Steam names get uppercased, unrenderable
characters dropped, `_` mapped to `-`; a name with nothing left (all-Cyrillic,
all-emoji) falls back to a real TTF element with the original string, which the
three NAME readouts carry and no number readout does.

### Two boxes moved, both because the fit rule made an old overlap visible

- The local panel's name box was 90..200 and the HP readout is 168..220. They
  overlapped by 32px and only stayed apart because a left-aligned UIText with a
  short name never reached that far; a fitted row would have grown into the HP
  text instead of shrinking. Name now ends at 164.
- The kill feed's score column was 26 wide with the name starting at 29. A
  five-character "+1000" would have fitted itself to two thirds the size of the
  "+50" above it. Score is 36 wide, name starts at 40, total width unchanged.

### The damage numbers are the one file that fail-safes its require

`tod_upgrade.lua` is the highest-blast-radius file in the tree (its own header
says so), so the require is `pcall`ed exactly like `TodKeycap`'s and the pool
degrades to the UIText it was — `CoD.TodGlyphText == nil` is the one test, read
where the pool is built and again where a number is drawn. Size is a CAP now,
not a `setScale`: 14 canvas px, 17.5 on a headshot, which is the same +25% the
old 0.4/0.5 scales expressed (and 0.4 never meant anything in canvas pixels —
see the lui-text-size-is-scale-not-box note).

`TodGlyphRow` gained one function: `row.close()`. LUI does not cascade `close()`
to children, and the +points popup is created and closed per score event.

**BUILT AND VERIFIED FRESH (`-GscOnly`).** Sizes were the honest guess this pass
could make — the caps come from the boxes the UIText occupied — and
`TG_CAP_FRAC` plus each readout's own `cap`/`capFrac` is the one number to move
if anything reads wrong in game.

### v17.36 — the two sizes play judged wrong

User 2026-09-04, after playing it: *"The names in the left for players needs to
be like 20% bigger if possible. And also the on screen damage numbers need to be
about 20% smaller."* Both are exactly that, and nothing else moved:

- **NAMES +20%** — `capFrac` 0.80 -> **0.96** on the local panel's name AND each
  teammate row's, which are one family and were judged in one glance. LOCKSTEP
  pair; a comment in each points at the other.
- **DAMAGE NUMBERS -20%** — `DMG_CAP` 14 -> **11.2**, `DMG_CAP_HS` 17.5 -> **14**.
  Both x0.8, so the headshot's +25% is untouched.
- `DMG_BASEF` is now **DERIVED** (`0.5 + DMG_CAP / 68`) instead of the typed 0.71
  it shipped with. That constant centres the number in its 34px box and is a
  function of the cap — the first cap change of its life would have left every
  number sitting low, which is the exact drift this map keeps paying for.

**NAME LENGTH +6, AND WHY THE SCREENSHOT CHANGED THE FIX.** User: *"is it
possible to increase the possible limit of characters in a name? It gets cut
off ... increase by like 6 chars"*. `pool` IS the limit (a longer string is cut
where `measure` and `set` both see it), so 14 -> **20** on all three name
readouts. But the screenshot showed "GLIDE GLADIATO" filling its box edge to
edge, which means that name was **WIDTH-limited, not cap-limited** — the fit had
already pulled it to cap ~7.0 and the +20% `capFrac` would have done nothing for
it. So the box grew too: name 90..176 (74 -> 86px), and the HP readout moved to
180..226, which is 6px WIDER than it was — 226 is the shield icon's left edge and
the hard stop for this row. Net: a short name gets the full +20%, a long one
+16%, and a 20-character name is still smaller than a 14-character one. Making
long names big as well means moving HP out of row 1 entirely and handing the name
all of 90..220; that is the next step, not this one.

### v17.37 — elites and bosses finally show up in the money feed

User 2026-09-04: *"I dont think elites and bosses show up in the money gained
section. I would expect something like +500 ELITE or +1000 BOSS."* They did not.
The kill feed is fed entirely from `_zm_aetherium_hud::zombie_death_callback`,
whose arms all end in `archetype == "zombie"` or a weapon test — the Panzer is
`mechz`, and the elite bonus is paid from a completely different lane
(`_tod_bosses::grant_elite_reward`) that has been **silent since 2026-08-20**.

**The `name` parameter both reward functions already take was the missing
half.** It has been dead for a fortnight — `grant_elite_reward( "REAVER", … )`
threw the string away. It now maps through `kill_feed_name()` to an istring and
rides the same `score_event` lane the kit's fifteen KF_* rows use:

- **`+500 ELITE`, killer only** — Rogue Protector, Reaver, Hellhound, Sprinter
  and a spire trial's Warden Panzers all say the same word. Matches who the
  money went to.
- **`+1000 BOSS`, team-wide** — the round Panzer, one row per player because
  every player was paid. `quiet` (the other parameter orphaned in 2026-08-20)
  gates it. Note the payout itself is unchanged and always was team-wide: the
  `foreach` in `grant_boss_reward` is byte-identical in the initial import
  commit. Only the *visibility* is new.
- **`+5000 TRIAL WIN`, team-wide** — a spire trial pays through the same
  function but is not a kill, so it says so (user: *"Trial win should read
  +5000 TRIAL WIN"*). It is the one reason `name` is still read.
- **THE VALUE SENT IS THE FINAL ONE**, after double points and BOUNTY, rather
  than a recomputed nominal — that recompute is what caused the +100/+110
  under-report the kit had in 2026-08-23.
- **TWO WORDS, NOT SIX** (user, same day: *"It should be generic ELITE AND BOSS
  thats all no reaver or sprinter"*). The first cut named each family; those five
  strings were **retired whole** from the `.str` rather than left unreferenced,
  and `kill_feed_name()` went with them — the label is now a literal at each of
  the two sites. Elite rows draw **amber**, boss rows **orange**, so a 500 does
  not read as white text in a list of 50s.

**A trash row can appear beside an elite row for the same corpse** (a sprinter is
`archetype "zombie"`; a hellhound matches the kit's dog arm). That is not a
duplicate — they are two separate payouts, stock's kill money and this 500, and
the feed's running total is what the player actually banked.

**ARMED FOR TESTING — dev + god + the Lua mock party** (user: *"please enable dev
and god mode so i can test the mock players HUD as well"*, *"Make sure doors are
all opened as well in dev mode"*). No door code was written: HARNESS #9 already
sits behind `tod_dev` in `_tod_main::init()` and opens all 53 through
`tod_doors::dev_open_all_doors()`. The third mock name is exactly 20 characters
so the preview shows the new boundary. *** `level.tod_dev`, `level.tod_god` and
`TOD_MOCK_PARTY` ALL GO BACK TO false BEFORE PUBLISHING. ***

## 2026-09-04 (v17.33) — PACK II AND PACK III: a triple pack with no twin, and a badge that says which one you have

User 2026-09-04: *"Would it be possible to add triple pack but give the same
weapon back to the gun and under the hood we increase the damage rather then
having a twin?"* → *"itll be 25k for pap tier II and 50k for tier III. You can
do it to any gun. ONly avaibale in the endless spire PaP. And i still want the
animation of it taking the gun away and giving it back. Itll just give back the
same gun. +50% damage at each level. Also we need to update the HUD to add some
section that tells your pap level. So this include pap I."*

### It could not have been a twin, and that is not a close call

`tools/gen_tod_twins.js` prints `REGISTRATION LEDGER: 201 generated + 28 fixed =
229 (guard 229)`. **Zero headroom.** A re-packed form of every ladder rung is not
expensive, it is impossible — the generator throws and writes nothing. So the
tier is script state and the damage is arithmetic, which is the NO-TWIN doctrine
this map already runs for damage, fire rate and mag size.

- **The store** — `_tod_classes.gsc`. `pap_tier` / `pap_tier_set` /
  `pap_tier_mult`, keyed by `pap_stem()`. **Tier 1 is DERIVED, never stored**:
  the existing packed test already answers "is it packed", and a second store
  for a fact that has an authority is how the two drift apart. Only 2 and 3 are
  written.
  **Keyed by STEM, not by weapon name** — the class primary's asset name walks
  the twin ladder on every gun-scoped level (`t9_ak47_up_r1m2` → `_r1m3`) and
  gains `_up` at the pack, so a name key would silently drop a tier the player
  paid 50,000 for. A TIER PROMOTION changes the stem by design: new gun, tier 0.
  `pap_strip_tail` uses `GetSubStr` + `.size`, **not `StrTok`** — StrTok splits
  on a CHARACTER SET, so `StrTok(n, "_upgraded")` would break the name at every
  `_`, `u`, `p`, `g`, `r`, `a`, `d` and `e` in it.
- **The damage** — one line in `upgrade_damage_cb`, beside `gun_balance_mult` and
  deliberately **not** in the additive `mult` sum. In the sum a +50% would be
  worth progressively less the more DAMAGE levels a player owns (against a maxed
  +100% it lands as +25% real). Multiplying the raw damage scales the base hit
  and every damage domain together, exactly as the stock pack's +25% does.
  Additive across levels by the user's call: **II = ×1.5, III = ×2.0**.
- **The buy** — `zm_cwpap.gsc`, first arm inside the already-packed branch, gated
  on the machine's own `tod_cwpap_tiers`. `register_pap_machine` and
  `breather_pap_place` take a new defaulted-false `b_tiers`, so the tower's five
  machines are byte-identical to what shipped; `_tod_spire.gsc`'s hub vendors are
  the only caller passing true. Charge order is the class-gun lane's (afford
  before take, record before show), not `hasEnoughMoney`'s.
  **The weapon is not touched at all** — see below.
- **The copy** — three new constant hint strings (94 of 190 budgeted). Says
  **PACK II**, never PACK-A-PUNCH II: `isPAPHint` routes anything containing both
  "pack" and the other keyword to a static card that never reads the text. The
  two nouns are in `TOD_NOUNS` as belt and braces. On a spire machine the
  already-maxed line no longer points at the Heavenly Altar — **there are no
  altars on the spire at all**, which the shipped copy has been wrong about since
  the spire existed.

### The buy is the ordinary Pack-a-Punch, and only the words change

User, after the first cut shipped: *"I want it the same as other pap with
differnt text since price is different and it spap II ... Other than that it
should be same animation."*

The first version read *"the animation of it taking the gun away and giving it
back"* literally and put a **2.2 s empty-handed window** across the lever anim.
That was wrong twice over. **No Pack-a-Punch in this map has one** — the
class-gun lane never touches the weapon, and stock's `giveWeaponUpgraded` takes
and gives in the SAME FRAME, which is invisible; the machine's anim IS the
visible event. And it charged the player 2.2 weaponless seconds in a spire hub
where a trial can seal them in.

It also pointed the map's worst-known weapon bug straight at itself.
`SwitchToWeaponImmediate` is silently EATEN in several player states
(mid-sprint, mid-raise, mid-reload, ADS transition), after which `TakeWeapon`
strands the player on the pistol — the entire reason `swap_primary` exists. And
`reconcile_twin` could not have repaired it here, because **the form it wants is
the form already owned**: the weapon does not change, so there is nothing for
the self-healing lane to notice.

So `pap_regive` is gone and `pap_refill` replaces it: the weapon is left alone
and gets a `GiveStartAmmo` top-up, already this tree's idiom for the
same-asset case (`_tod_upgrades.gsc:5120`, *"same asset ... still a refill"*).
Every other Pack-a-Punch hands back a full gun; at 25,000 and 50,000 this must
not be worse than the 5,000 buy.

Also fixed in the same pass: `tod_pap_next_tier` tested a **literal 3** with a
comment naming `TOD_PAP_TIER_MAX`, because a GSC `#define` does not cross files.
`tod_classes::pap_tier_max()` is now the one authority and the ceiling is asked
for rather than copied.

### The HUD badge

A fourth 46×32 plate at canvas x1000, on the equipment row, **directly above the
gun picture** — a property of the gun, sat over the gun, and 114 units clear of
the two inventory tiles so three identical plates in a row cannot read as a
count. Hidden entirely at tier 0.

Fed by a new `tod_pap_tier` event on `_tod_gauge.gsc`'s 0.35 s heartbeat, **not a
clientfield**: the clientuimodel pool is at 60 of its proven 61 bits and a 0..3
value wants two — the only dead field is one bit, so a clientfield would have to
take bits out of a shipped feature to buy a badge. It reads the weapon **in
hand**, so it follows a weapon switch, which makes it the one lane here whose
value moves with no game state changing. Re-armed per life in `player_lui_life`.

Art: `i_tod_hud_pap_tile` + a 3-cell `i_tod_hud_pap_sheet`, wired, zoned and
packed **today** on placeholder art from `tools/gen_pap_badge_placeholder.js`
(flat navy plate, cyan keyline, numerals as thick steel bars — correct sizes and
palette, plain on purpose). `docs/96` is the commission; the drop replaces the
same four names, so installing it is a file copy plus a re-slice.

### Two tool bugs found on the way

- **`slice_hud_sheets.js` would have deleted the shipped typeface.** The
  delivered sheets are not kept in the repo, so a run that slices ONE new sheet
  finds the digit and letter sheets missing, measures no glyphs — and wrote
  `TodGlyphMetrics.lua` out anyway. That silently drops the advance table for
  every number and every weapon name in the gun HUD. The metrics file is
  all-or-nothing, so its write is now too. The MANIFEST write moved OUT of that
  block: it is derived from the SHEETS table alone, and the run that adds a sheet
  is exactly the run that must register the new name for GATE A.
- **A COMMENT nearly hijacked every Pack-a-Punch prompt in the map.**
  `lint_tod_hints.js` reads `TOD_NOUNS` by scanning the block for quoted strings,
  as any reader would. The first draft of the note explaining the new nouns
  *quoted the keyword it was discussing*, and the lint took that word as a noun —
  one that matches stock's own `&ZOMBIE_PERK_PACKAPUNCH`. Every PaP prompt in the
  map would have been dragged onto the wrong card by a comment. Caught by the
  lint; nothing else would have found it until someone walked up to a machine.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.32) — THE BASE FLOOR LINES: one width, one blue, and the power lane finally reaches the power

User 2026-09-04, two asks in one pass: *"Tiny bit brighter an dyour color
change"*, then *"the floor has these strip designs. Can we make that blue
instead of teal. Its alos not complleted I dont think. Lets redesign this strip
so it looks cleaner and consistent."*

### A correction to what this session told the user

The earlier note offered two brightness knobs — the base lights, "then `blue`
instead of `dark_blue` for the floor". **The second one is not a brightness
knob.** `blue` and `dark_blue` are the SAME plain texture at the SAME
`scaleRGB` 15, and that texture is ~96% black: the tint recolours the thin GRID
LINE and nothing else. It lifts the lines from deep blue to pale sky blue; it
does not make a single tile less black. Both changes shipped — the tint because
it was asked for and it does look lighter, the actual room brightness from
`BASE_LIGHT_BAKE` — but they are not alternatives and it was wrong to list them
as though they were.

`BASE_LIGHT_BAKE` is 1.35 on the four corner lights and the spawn light —
`bake_intensity_scale`, deliberately not radius, which would move WHERE the
pools fall and re-shape the room. Small on purpose ("tiny bit"), and one number
to move again after a look.

The core column's plinth no longer shares the floor's material: `MAT.baseColumn`
keeps it on `dark_blue` because the four core SPINES are plain `blue` for
district 1, and a plinth in the same plain `blue` would have swallowed them for
the first two bands.

### What was actually inconsistent about the strips

Three different line weights doing one job:

| line | width |
|---|---|
| perimeter ring | **64** |
| core foot ring | **40** |
| wayfinding lane | **20** |

…and the lane ran 16u INSIDE the ring's inner edge for its whole length,
parallel to it, never touching it. Two lines at different weights that never
meet is what reads as unfinished.

**And it genuinely was incomplete.** The power lane — the whole reason these
exist (Workshop 2026-08-26: *"having a difficult time finding the power. Where
is it?"*) — stopped at **x=580**. That is twenty units past the doorway, into a
hallway that runs to x=1640. It pointed at the power room and quit before the
switch.

Now every line in the arena is `TRACE_W` (40) and the same blue, and one
continuous lane runs spawn → south → through the power door → down the hall to
the switch. The perimeter ring is a properly mitred closed rectangle; the foot
ring's open EAST side is open **by construction** — the lap-1 under-stair fill
is solid across x[256,416] y[-224,256], so an east run would be buried inside
it, and the N/S runs over-run to `CORE+TRACE_W` so the ring turns its corners
and terminates against the stair instead of stopping in open floor.

Two rules decided every coordinate, both learned by nearly breaking them:

1. **Coplanar decals must ABUT, never overlap.** These are all 1u at z[0,1];
   two sharing floor is a z-fight, not a brighter line. So the lane STOPS at the
   ring's inner edge and RESUMES at its outer edge (the ring carries the
   crossing), and the door spur stops at y=-266 — where the lap-1 door gate's
   own 1u SILL begins, in that exact spot.
2. **Nothing may run under a wall.** The power room's north wall is x[280,540]
   y[-420,-400]; the lane rides y[-460,-420] so its north edge is that wall's
   south face. The old 20-wide lane cleared it by luck, not construction.

The door spur comes off the foot ring rather than the lane, because the lane is
inside the power room for all x in [280,540] and the only clear channel north
out of it is x[256,280] — 24 wide, against the core's east face — so a spur
there would be off-width and half-buried.

The TELEPORT BAY's ring is deliberately NOT widened: its E/W runs sit at x
204..220 and the up-pad squares reach x=198, so 40 wide would collide. It takes
the new blue and keeps its 16u width. A constraint, not an oversight.

### The lint needed a new kind of entry, and it was watched firing

The arena floor taking plain `blue` broke the one assumption
`lint_tod_geometry.js` rests on. It classes DECK vs BLOCK **by material name**,
and plain `blue` is also every base wall, parapet, rail and under-stair fill in
the map. One name, two genuinely different roles, and **no choice is right for
both**: BLOCK deletes the arena floor from the walkability flood, DECK gives
every parapet in the map standing room.

So `DECK_LABELS` — three labels (`ground slab`, `power hall floor`, `tp bay
floor`), the whole ground-level floor and nothing else — are deck regardless of
material. Same shape as the existing `MODEL_CLIP_COLUMNS`: an explicit
enumerated exception, not an inference from shape, and the thickness gate still
ANDs it so it can only ever promote a genuine slab. `dark_blue` is reclassified
BLOCK, which is now honest — it is only the 384-tall plinth.

**The override was watched firing rather than assumed.** A patched copy with
`DECK_LABELS` neutered, run on the same `.map`:

| | with | without |
|---|---|---|
| floor surfaces | 178461 | 173931 |
| unguarded edges | **0** | **943** |
| base → terrace | YES | **ANCHOR MISSING** |

World brushes 13488 → 13490 (+2: the ring spur and the hall lane). Geometry lint
green, no regression against baseline. `lint_tod_geometry_selftest.js` passes all
seven cases, so its zero is still a real zero. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.31) — TELEPORTER FX: the ride and the effect happened in the same server frame

User 2026-09-04: *"occasionally the teleporter fx wont trigger. The sfx always
does but sometimes you will use it and not see any teleporter lightning fx."*

### The report kills the obvious suspect, and that is the useful half

`fx_burst` opens with `h = Spawn( "script_model", origin ); if ( !isdefined( h ) )
return;` — it drops the effect **silently** when the gentity pool is full. An
exhausted pool is intermittent, load-dependent and invisible, which is exactly
the reported shape, and this map already treats ~1024 gentities as a binding
constraint. It looks like the answer.

It is not. `_tod_perk_scatter::play_sound_at_origin` (:929) spawns a
`script_origin` and carries the **same** guard — `// entity pool full — drop the
sound, never throw`. If the pool were exhausted the sound would go with it. The
sound **always** plays. One observation, one suspect eliminated — and eliminated
by the user's own detail, not by a build.

### What is left is an asymmetry the two lanes have at the moment of a ride

The riders are `SetOrigin`'d thousands of units away in the loop above, and the
arrival effects ran **in the same server frame**. The two lanes then behave
differently:

- a **sound** is emitted by an entity that lives another 3-4 s, so a client has a
  long window to resolve it;
- `PlayFxOnTag` is a **one-shot event on a host spawned that same frame**, with
  no replay. A client whose snapshot has not yet caught up with where its player
  now *is* misses it outright and never gets a second chance.

Intermittent, FX-only, and only on the lane that moves the viewer. Two
`WAIT_SERVER_FRAME`s now sit between the ride and the arrival effects.

**Honest status: the elimination is sound, the replacement mechanism is
INFERRED.** Nothing in GSC can observe a client's snapshot. What is certain is
that a same-frame teleport-then-effect is the one thing this lane does that the
sound lane does not care about, and two frames is the cheapest way to stop doing
it. **If the report survives this build the next move is to spawn the FX host
BEFORE the ride** so it is already replicating and only then `PlayFxOnTag` — and
*do not re-open the entity-pool theory*, it is dead on the evidence above.

The DEPARTURE flash is deliberately not delayed. The rider is meant to miss that
one — the sound comment on the same sequence already says why (*"the cut IS the
translocation"*) — and the bystanders who do see it never moved, so their
snapshot was never stale.

Cost: ~0.1 s of extra `tod_tp_busy` on a pad whose cooldown was armed before
`do_teleport` was even called, so nothing a player can reach is gated on it.

`shared.gsh` was already `#insert`ed in this file, so the macro needed no new
include. Arity lint green across 73 files. **UNPLAYED — and this one only
reproduces occasionally, so a single clean ride does not confirm it.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.30) — THE KEYCAP WIDGET GETS A FAIL-SAFE: an unguarded `require` was betting three menus on one rawfile

User, on v17.27: *"But we have a fail safe right? No crash if this happens"* —
about the failure this session had itself flagged: *"if the class draft or the
upgrade panel doesn't draw at all, that's the require chain."*

**THE HONEST ANSWER WAS: ONE OF THE TWO, AND NOT THE IMPORTANT ONE.** v17.27 had
a real fallback for a *glyph* failing (a character the sheets have no cell for,
or a name longer than the pool → the LUI text is drawn instead). It had **none**
for the `require` itself, and that is the failure with the blast radius.

### What an unguarded require was actually risking

A `require` that throws aborts the ENTIRE calling file, and a LUI failure is
silent — no build complaint, no crash, nothing on screen. Three files required
`TodKeycap` bare, and the cost was wildly out of proportion to a decoration:

- `tod_class_select.lua` — no class draft. Every player gets a random class on
  the 30 s timeout with no way to tell why.
- `tod_upgrade.lua` — the file its own lint header calls the highest-blast-radius
  in the tree: the upgrade panel, the crosshair damage numbers, the tower gauge,
  the luck bar, the finale banner, the rampage seal **and** the `tod_input_pad`
  receiver, all gone at once.
- `AetheriumStartMenu.lua` — **the pause menu**. A player who cannot open it
  cannot leave the match.

### The fix

`pcall( require, ... )` in all three, and every call site routed through a local
`TodKeycapMake( owner, text )` that returns the real writer when
`CoD.TodKeycap` is present and otherwise a stub with the same `hide`/`paint`
shape, degrading to the plain LUI text each menu already builds. Worst case is
now **the pre-v17.27 look — small text — not a missing menu.** `pcall` is
already in use in this tree (`tod_upgrade`'s `val`/`act` guards,
AetheriumStartMenu's dvar try-list), so this is not a new dependency on an
unproven global.

- **THE STUB IS DELIBERATELY TWINNED, NOT SHARED.** Three copies of ~18 lines,
  against a repo rule that hates exactly that. The reason it is right here: a
  fail-safe that lives inside the thing it guards against is not a fail-safe. Put
  the stub in `TodKeycap.lua` and it dies with the file it exists to survive.
- **AND THE CONTRACT IS STATED ONCE.** Each caller's guard is a single
  `if CoD.TodKeycap then` test, so the widget must never exist half-alive:
  `TodKeycap.lua` now nils its own export if `CoD.TodGlyphRow` is absent. The
  require above would normally throw first — this covers only a TodGlyphRow that
  loads cleanly and still fails to export, which is the one case a single test
  could not see by itself.

### On "no crash"

Correct, and it is worth writing down rather than assuming: a Lua fault here does
not crash the game. This tree's own record says so twice — the `.zone` comment
beside the rawfile lines (*"Lua runtime errors surface in-game as UI Error <n>"*)
and `lint_tod_lua.js`'s header (*"the menu fails to load and every one of those
disappears at once, in game, with no build-time complaint"*). **Which is exactly
why a fail-safe was needed**: a crash announces itself, and this does not.

- Lua only → `-GscOnly`. `lint_tod_lua.js` clean (45 files),
  `lint_tod_assets.js` clean against baseline.
- Version numbering: v17.28 and v17.29 were taken by a peer session while this
  was written.
- Verification note: this landed DURING a peer's full build, so whether it rode
  that `.ff` has to be checked after the fact — deployed-vs-repo diff plus the
  `-newermt` pair, per the doctrine, never assumed from the clock.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.29) — GROUND LEVEL: every floor-1 door is the tower door's blue, and the teleport bay's green landing square is gone

User 2026-09-04, after v17.28: *"We can make all the doors on first floor blue
like the tower door. Also the teleporter bay has a landing area. I dont mind
where it is but I do want to remove the green square we made to indicate it.
There will be no landing zone but they will still land in that zone. Just no
visual zone."*

### The two green doors had no material at all

`DOORS.push` for the power room and the teleport bay never set `slabMat`, so
both fell through to `MAT.door` (green) while the lap-1 door standing a few
hundred units away took the district hue from `edgeMatOf(lap - 1)`. Both now
carry `GROUND_DOOR_MAT`, which is **that same expression** — `edgeMatOf(0)`,
literally what floor 1's door resolves to — and not a hardcoded
`blue_tinted_edge`. If district 1 is ever re-hued these follow it instead of
quietly becoming the odd ones out, and under `FACELIFT = false` the tower door
is green, so "like the tower door" correctly still means green.

Verified in the regenerated `.map`: `tod_door_power`, `tod_door_tpbay` and
`tod_door_lap1` all read `blue_tinted_edge`; `tod_door_roof` still reads
`green_tinted_edge` — it is 19,200 units up and is not a floor-1 door.
`MAT.door` keeps the roof door, the causeway gate and the crown door.

**This drops the green/blue split Nikolai proposed alongside the black floor**
("only leave the green buyable doors and blue buyable door"). Deliberate, on the
user's call: the three ground doors sit in three different walls in three
different rooms, so they were never actually told apart by hue, and against the
v17.28 black floor one saturated blue is the strongest "buy me" this pack can
draw.

### The landing square was only ever a decal

`tp bay arrival mark` was a 1u green square painted on the floor over
`TPB_ARR_Y`. The landing POINT is that constant, read by `_tod_teleport.gsc`;
the brush marked it and did nothing else, so deleting it removes the marker and
moves nothing. Players arrive on exactly the same spot — which is the whole ask:
*"no landing zone but they will still land in that zone."*

Two neighbours deliberately kept:

- **the arrival LIGHT** (`tp bay light 2`) — one of the bay's three, and pulling
  it would leave the north apron dark. That is a different change from the one
  asked for.
- **the four 176-unit squares under the UP pads** — those are the FACELIFT §4
  destination colour code, they mark something you stand on and press rather
  than something that happens to you, and they answered a different Workshop
  report ("not aligned perfectly and feel quite confusing to know which is
  which").

### Proof

World brushes **13489 -> 13488**: exactly one brush removed, nothing else moved.
Doors still 53. Geometry lint green, **no regression against baseline** (0
misplaced walls, 0 unguarded edges, base→terrace / terrace→citadel /
spire→summit all walkable) — the floor under the old decal is the v17.28 base
slab and is still standable without it.

**UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.28) — FLOOR 1 GOES BLACK: the buyable door was the dimmest blue in a room full of brighter blue

Workshop, Nikolai 2026-09-04: *"for floor 1 (ground level) the walls all have
the black and blue grid color. My recommendation would be to remove the blue
only on the first floor and just make it consistently that black and blue grid
checker (only leave the green buyable doors and blue buyable door) ... right now
the blue wrapping around it makes it a little more difficult for those to see
which blue is the buyable door ... add that black and blue checker to the bottom
part of the column of the tower outside where the blue purchasable door is."*

### He is describing a measurable fact, not a preference

The whole vertigo pack is TWO textures and one brightness number. Read out of
`emox_mwiii_vertigo_assets.gdt` (30 materials, 2026-09-04):

| suffix | texture | look | `scaleRGB` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<colour>` | `i_..._e` | BLACK tiles + a thin bright grid line | 15 |
| `<colour>_tinted` | `i_..._tinted_e` | FILLED tiles glowing at the seams | 10 |
| `<colour>_tinted_edge` | `i_..._tinted_e` | **the same texture, the same tint** | 5 |

So **`_tinted_edge` is not an edge variant of anything — it is `_tinted` at half
brightness.** (`edgeMatOf`'s comment calling it "dark tiles with GLOWING SEAMS"
described the texture both share, and read as a distinction that does not exist.)

That single fact is the whole report. At ground level the arena FLOOR was
`dark_blue_tinted` (filled, 10) and the core's lap-1 band `blue_tinted`
(filled, 10), while the buyable door slab is `blue_tinted_edge` (filled, **5**).
The door is the same texture and roughly the same hue as everything around it,
at **half the brightness of the wall it is cut beside**. It was the dimmest blue
in the room.

### The change — `BASE_GRID`, one switch

Ground level drops to the PLAIN family, so the only FILLED blue left down there
is the door slab and the 1-10 teleport pad it is colour-matched to:

- **the arena slab, the power-hall floor and the teleport-bay floor** →
  `dark_blue` (plain). The exact plain twin of `dark_blue_tinted` — same tint
  `0.067 0.198 1`, grid texture instead of filled. "Keep the colour, drop the
  fill."
- **the first `BASE_GRID_LAPS` (2) core bands' quadrants** → the same material,
  so the column visibly stands ON the floor it is lit against and the floor-1 and
  floor-2 door slabs are the only lit fill in their frames. The four plain-hue
  SPINES are untouched, so the column keeps its vertical lines all the way up.
- **the inlay ring, the three wayfinding traces and the core foot ring** →
  `cyan_tinted`. They were `blue_tinted_edge`, i.e. **byte-identical to the door
  slab** — the one thing on the floor that says "the way through" was drawn in
  the door's own material. Cyan is already the arena's accent (pilasters +
  cornice) and no district uses it, so at ground level cyan now means "this room"
  and blue means "the way up". It is also brightness 10 against the old 5, so the
  traces read BETTER on the darker floor. `cyan_tinted` deliberately: the pack
  ships **no `cyan_tinted_edge`**, and the linker substitutes an invented name
  silently.

Nothing above floor 1 changes. `MAT.ground` keeps its old value and its other
three callers — the tower shell, the crown hall floor and the spire's base slab —
which is why floor 1 needed its own `MAT.baseFloor` entry rather than a retune of
`ground`.

### The floor material is load-bearing for the geometry lint

`lint_tod_geometry.js` classes DECK vs BLOCK **by material name** and HARD-FAILS
on a name it does not know. Every plain `<colour>` in its table is BLOCK
(parapets, rails, base walls, door slabs), so handing the arena floor a plain
material the lint already knew would have deleted the floor from its walkability
model and reported the map unreachable.

`dark_blue` is used **nowhere else in this map**, so it can be added as DECK with
a one-to-one meaning — which is that lint's own rule, that a material's class is
derived from the labels that use it. Had the floor been given plain `blue`, one
name would have had to be both DECK and BLOCK, and either the arena floor
vanishes from the flood or every parapet in the map offers standing room. Keep
`dark_blue` one-to-one with "ground level floor".

Verified in the regenerated `.map`: 66 `dark_blue` face lines = the 3 floors (6
faces each) + 8 core quadrants (48); 84 `cyan_tinted` = the 14 glow decals. Lint
green, **no regression against baseline** (misplaced walls 0, unguarded edges 0,
base→terrace / terrace→citadel / spire→summit all walkable). No brush was added, removed or
moved: every edit is a material string on an addBox that already existed, so the
bake budget and `measure_lit_area` are untouched by construction.

### STILL OPEN, and it is the same defect one floor up

The door slab takes `edgeMatOf(lap - 1)` (the district's `_tinted_edge`) and the
core band it is cut beside takes `stepMatOf(lap - 1)` (the district's `_tinted`
on even band indices, **`_tinted_edge` on odd ones**). So on **25 of the 50 lap
doors the slab is byte-identical to the wall beside it**, and on the other 25 it
is the same texture and hue at half the brightness. `MAT.door`'s own comment
already recorded this failure mode for the pre-facelift red door — *"A FIXED HUE
CANNOT SOLVE THIS ... the door has to differ in KIND, not in hue"* — and v16.11's
district-hued doors reintroduced it. Nikolai's fix generalises: plain core-band
quadrants for the whole tower would make every filled door slab pop on all 50
floors. Not shipped — that is a 50-floor look change and it is the user's call.

**UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.27) — KEYCAPS IN THE MAP'S OWN TYPEFACE; and the screenshot that killed v17.24's sizing model

User, with a picture of the class draft: *"So it looks tiny. And also is it
possible to use our typography alphabet and numbers instead of LUI"* — after
*"the placeholders we have in the class menu always have text that overflows"*.

### The picture said the opposite of the word, and the picture was right

The complaint was reported as an OVERFLOW and v17.24 was built on that reading.
The screenshot shows the reverse: the right switch cap drew `G OR MIDDLE MOUSE`
— 17 characters — in roughly **61 canvas px, about 3.6 px per character**, INSIDE
its 96 px cap. Nothing was running past anything. It was **tiny**: an ~8 px
string sitting three pixels from the baked `HOLD` / `TO LOCK` lettering at more
than twice its size, which is what made it read as broken.

**AND THAT MEASUREMENT KILLS THE SIZING MODEL THE REPO HAS USED SINCE v16.32.**
A 30 px box at scale 0.72 would have to be drawing a ~22 px font, and no 22 px
font fits 17 characters in 61 px. So in this LUI **the font is a fixed base times
`setScale`; the element's box height does not size it at all.** v16.32's *"if the
line overflows the pill, shrink the box height"* said of itself that it was a
first guess, and it was wrong — so **every box-height write in v17.24 was
inert**, and the only part of that build that could ever have done anything was
the multi-bind trim. Two builds of arithmetic were written on top of an unmeasured
model before anyone took a picture. It is the map's own lesson one level up: *a
guard nobody has watched fire is not a guard.*

### The fix is the user's idea: our typeface, which can be MEASURED

Every keycap now sets its bind name in the baked glyph sheets through
`CoD.TodGlyphRow` — the same shared row the gun HUD and the v17.25 ROUND readout
use. That is not only a look. `row.measure()` returns the **exact** canvas width
of a string at a given cap height, out of metrics `tools/slice_hud_sheets.js`
derives from the art's own alpha channel. So:

- **The size is chosen, not guessed.** Cap height = 0.52 of the keycap (sized
  against `i_tod_hold_plate`'s own baked lettering, so the key and the words
  around it come out at one optical size), shrunk only if the measured string
  genuinely will not fit the face. The estimated character width v17.24 needed
  is gone, and there is nothing left to calibrate.
- **A redrawn glyph re-fits itself** on the next slice. The art and its spacing
  cannot drift apart.
- **`TOD_KEYCAP_TEXT_SCALE` (v17.4) is retired in both menus**, not left sitting
  unread — a half-retirement is how dead constants become false documentation.
- **The LUI text stays as the fallback**, exactly like `AetheriumLoadout`'s
  `weapon_name`: a key name with a character the sheets have no cell for (a
  bracket, a semicolon, an unresolved `[{+bind}]` token) degrades to readable
  text, never to a gap. A name too long for the 12-glyph pool takes the same
  road, because `row.set` TRUNCATES silently on its own.

`ui/uieditor/widgets/HUD/AetheriumWidgets/TodKeycap.lua` owns all eleven caps —
2 switch + 4 card locks in the draft, 2 + 2 in the deal panel, 3 in the pause
legend. One writer, because this map has paid twice for control copy that lives
on three surfaces and gets fixed on two (v16.83, then v16.93).

### Two things that carry over from v17.24, both still right

- **THE MULTI-BIND IS TRIMMED TO ITS FIRST KEY.** `+frag` is on BOTH `G` and
  `MOUSE3` in the user's `players/bindings_0.cfg`, and the screenshot confirms
  the engine renders that as `G OR MIDDLE MOUSE` — which is also where the
  separator is now read from rather than guessed. A keycap advertises ONE key.
  **It also proves a key display name can contain a SPACE**, so a plain space is
  never treated as a separator: cutting there would print `MIDDLE` and lie about
  the bind.
- **THE CAP'S GEOMETRY IS MEASURED.** Decoding `i_tod_key_blank_wide` (384x192),
  the bright face runs x 29..354 and y 19..148, with a dark outline at y~152 and
  a grey lip below. Face inset 7.6% each side; its centre at **43.5% of the cap
  height, not 50%**, which is where every caller used to centre — pushing glyph
  bottoms onto the lip. The glyph ink is centred on the face, not the rect.
- The glyph art is a light face with a dark outline, so the ink tint MULTIPLIES
  both down into one dark silhouette on the pale cap. `^7` is stripped from every
  token: it was fighting `setRGB`, and on a near-white keycap the loser of that
  fight is the player.

- Lua only (the `.zone` rawfile line landed in v17.24) → `-GscOnly`.
  `lint_tod_lua.js` clean (45 files), `lint_tod_assets.js` clean against
  baseline. Every glyph the sheets carry is already zoned (29 letters, 13
  digits) — no new asset.
- Version numbering: v17.25 and v17.26 were taken by a peer session while this
  was written. v17.25 is also what made this possible — it lifted the typeface
  out of `AetheriumLoadout` into the shared `TodGlyphRow`, one build before a
  third caller needed it.
- **UNPLAYED.** First checks: the two switch caps under the draft cards reading
  one big dark key each (`E` and `G`), the four HOLD-plate caps reading `SPACE`,
  and the same three in the pause legend.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.26) — THE PAUSE MENU WAS MOUSE-ONLY: nothing linked the icon row to the button column

User: *"I'm using an Xbox controller, when I'm in a match (solo atm) if I scroll
left or right with the joystick it moves along top icons. If I try to move down
to return to game, restart, etc it only will remain on the top 4 icons."*

Correct diagnosis. The pause menu is two INDEPENDENT `LUI.UIList`s — the four
settings icons across the top (`SmallButtonList`, horizontal) and Return To Game
/ Restart Level / third person / Game Settings / Leave Game below
(`ButtonList`, vertical) — and **nothing linked them**. Initial focus lands on
the icon row, so a gamepad could walk left and right forever and never reach a
single one of the menu's actual actions.

### Why a UIList cannot leave itself

`LUI.UIList.new` registers `LUI_KEY_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT` callbacks that call
`GridLayout.navigateItem*()`, and those **return `false` at the edge of the
grid** (read out of the decompiled `ui/LUI/LUIList.lua` + `LUIGridLayout.lua`,
`Dumps/PC_Ship_2025-05-31`). A one-row horizontal list therefore answers DOWN
with `false` and the press dies there. The framework's linkage is
`LUI.UIElement.navigation` — the `{up=,down=,left=,right=}` table stock menus
set, and which `LUI.UIVerticalList.UpdateNavigation` pushes onto its edge
children — and the kit sets it on nothing. **The bug is upstream's**: the
Aetherium kit source and map 1's copy of this file are both missing it.

**A MOUSE HID IT.** Mouse hover focuses either list directly, so on KBM every
button in the menu is reachable and the menu looks finished. The one input
device that has to *navigate* is the one it was never driven with.

### The fix: own the direction, don't race for it

We deliberately did NOT use the `navigation` table. A UIList hands each ITEM an
empty navigation table and its own table is reached only after the press
bubbles, so whether the list's internal move or the navigation hop wins depends
on the relative order of two different input paths — the `ButtonBits` model
subscriptions that drive `buttonFunctions`, and the `gamepad_button` event that
drives `handleGamepadButton`. Lose that race and UP jumps out of the column from
the middle instead of stepping one row.

Instead the two EDGE callbacks are replaced — a second
`AddButtonCallbackFunction` for the same element+button overwrites
`element.buttonFunctions[button]` — so **one handler owns each direction and the
order question never arises**:

- **DOWN on the icon row** tries `navigateItemDown()` first (stock behaviour,
  `false` for a single row), then hops to `ButtonList`.
- **UP in the button column** tries `navigateItemUp()` first — so stepping
  between rows is byte-for-byte the stock behaviour — and only hops back to the
  icon row from the top row.

The hop replays the two steps stock's `doNavigationForElement` performs —
`gain_focus` on the target, then `lose_focus` on the source with
`ignoreFocusCheck` — but it does **not** gate on the `gain_focus` return value
the way stock does. The decompiled `LUI.UIList.gainFocus` is lossy (dead stores,
no visible return), so what it hands back is unknown, and guessing wrong there
either strands focus on nothing or leaves both lists lit. It gates on the
observable post-condition instead: `hasListFocus`, the flag `UIList.loseFocus`
and `setListItemInFocus` both read. **If the target refuses, focus stays exactly
where it was** — the failure mode is "the press does nothing", which is today's
behaviour, not a dead panel. Both directions register the keyboard arrows too
(`"UPARROW"` / `"DOWNARROW"`), matching what `LUI.UIList` registers for itself.

**Guard.** Game-over mode calls `SmallButtonList:makeNotFocusable()` and the
Game Settings page hides it, so `TodHopLists` refuses a non-focusable target and
UP at the top of the column is inert in both rather than focusing an invisible
row. A dead panel is impossible by construction.

Initial focus is UNCHANGED — the icon row, as the kit shipped it. It is now one
DOWN press from Return To Game.

⚠️ UNPLAYED. Verified against the decompiled framework, not in a match.

`ui/uieditor/menus/StartMenu/AetheriumStartMenu.lua`.

### Build note: the wav-converter null-ref cost a build, and the retry again was not the cure

The first `-GscOnly` of this change hit the documented intermittent converter
fault (`ERROR: <skye_ports wav>` + `Object reference not set to an instance of
an object`) and **burned all three of build_map.ps1's linker attempts** without
emitting a bank — the guard Died correctly on a fresh `.ff`, `sound\zone` held
only the `.sz` stubs and the 2 KB english pair, `CachedBanks\all` absent. Second
data point for the 2026-09-02 correction: the in-script retry buys a coin flip,
not a fix. The manual ritual cleared it — `sound\zone` moved aside, rebuild,
**"sound bank recovered on linker attempt 3"**, 143.3 MB `.all.sabs`. Free RAM
was 3.7 GB of 15.6 at the failure, matching the correlation logged last time.

`.ff` OK 153,000,832 (12:30:30), freshness-verified: `scripts/` + `ui/`
byte-identical to deployed, nothing in the deployed tree newer than the `.ff`.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.25) — THE ROUND COUNTER IS OURS: stock's widget deleted, "ROUND n" set in the map's own typeface

User: *"We have the round image in the top right of screen but I am looking to
replace with the alphabet and letters we have downloaded. so I want it to be
Round X. Instead of how stock cod does it. Lets remove stock and track
ourselves."*

`AetheriumRoundCounter.lua` was a nine-line wrapper around `CoD.ZmRndContainer`,
the vanilla BO3 round widget — stock's digits, stock's animation, stock's idea
of what a round counter looks like. It is gone, `require` and all, and nothing
in the tree references it any more. In its place: **ROUND n**, right-aligned at
x1268, assembled from the same baked glyph sheets the gun HUD uses.

### The typeface moved out of the gun HUD (`TodGlyphRow.lua`, new)

The pooled glyph row, the two image mappers, the set pickers and the layout
maths lived as ~150 lines of locals inside `AetheriumLoadout.lua`. Two widgets
now set text in the baked typeface, so the block was **lifted verbatim** into
`ui/uieditor/widgets/HUD/AetheriumWidgets/TodGlyphRow.lua` (`CoD.TodGlyphRow`)
and the loadout keeps its three names as aliases. Diffed line-for-line against
the extraction: **only two comment paragraphs were retargeted, no code changed.**

Copying it instead would have been the worse kind of duplicate — the layout
maths is the **consumer** of the GENERATED `CoD.TodGlyphMetrics`, so a re-slice
of a redrawn glyph would have fixed one copy and not the other, and the failure
mode is text overlapping by two pixels, which nobody files a bug about.

New `rawfile,` line in `zone_source/aetherium_hud.zpkg`. Without it BOTH the gun
HUD and the round counter die on the require, silently, with no build-time
complaint — the same warning the `TodGlyphMetrics` line already carries.

### The number is the SERVER's, not the engine's

The free option was the engine's own `gameScore.roundsPlayed` model. **It was
not taken, and the reason is visible in `AetheriumStartMenu.lua`:** the pause
menu reads that model and prints `math.max( 1, roundsPlayed - 1 )`. Whatever it
counts, it is not "the round number" — somebody had to subtract one to make it
read right, and this map replaces stock's entire round flow
(`_tod_endless_rounds.gsc` overrides `round_wait_func`,
`zombie_round_change_custom` and `func_get_delay_between_rounds`). Reading a
stock counter through three replaced functions and an unexplained `-1` is how a
HUD ends up off by one in exactly the mode nobody tests.

So `_tod_gauge.gsc` pushes `level.round_number` — the number the boss cadence,
the spawn budget and the zombie-speed ramp all read — on a new int-only
`tod_round` LuiNotifyEvent. **Zero clientuimodel bits**, which is the whole
reason: the pool sits at 60 of its PROVEN 61 (`_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc`) and a round
number wants ten. `#precache( "eventstring", ... )` present, same trap as every
other event in that file.

It rides the gauge loop rather than a module of its own because that loop is
already the map's per-player HUD-push heartbeat, and it already owns the
per-life re-arm contract.

### The re-arm that is NOT for the menu it sits in

`_tod_upgrade_ui::player_lui_life` now clears `self.tod_round_shown` on every
spawn — and that list's own header says the kit HUD "needs none of this",
because the engine re-runs its lifecycle per spawn. **That is exactly the
problem.** The engine rebuilds the widget; a change-gated feed then says nothing
to it until the round flips, which can be minutes. A fresh counter reading
ROUND 1 in round 40 is the failure mode. `_tod_gauge` re-sends within one 0.35 s
tick of the tracker going undefined.

### Two round readouts, one source

`CoD.TodRound` is published by the widget and the pause menu now prefers it,
falling back to the stock model only for the window before the first push. Same
cross-menu global trick as `CoD.TodOwned`. Two readouts that disagree is worse
than one being a beat late.

### Layout

`TodScaleHud` **dropped** for this widget, following `AetheriumLoadout` and for
the same reason: 1.15 about (1175,75) pushes a right edge of 1268 out to 1282,
two canvas pixels past the screen. Final sizes are authored directly. The right
edge 1268 is **flush with the gauge (GA_X 1216 + GA_W 52) and with the gun HUD**,
which was pushed to that same edge in v17.22 — three right-hand elements, one
line.

#### The first cut set the word at cap 16 against the number's 40, and that was wrong

User, on the first screenshot: *"Why are they not the same size?"* The split
size was a deliberate hierarchy — number loud, word quiet — and it read as a
mistake, which is the only verdict that counts.

The fix is not "set two caps to the same value". **There are no longer two of
anything:** `ROUND n` is now ONE string through ONE row, so the cap, the
baseline, the tracking and the word space all come out of a single `set()` call
and cannot disagree. The gap between word and number is the typeface's own
`TOD_SPACE_ADV` rather than a constant invented here, and the two sheets mix on
one cap-normalized baseline exactly as the weapon-name row does for `AK-47` —
proven path, not a new one. Two rows, two caps and a hand-tuned gap was three
numbers that could drift; this is one, `RC_CAP`.

#### Then, from play: 25% smaller and further into the corner

User, on the second screenshot: *"Lets move it up a bit more towards the corner
and make it 25% smaller."* `RC_CAP` 34 → **25.5** is that 25% exactly rather
than a re-guess, and because the readout is one string it is the **only** number
that had to move — word, number, tracking and word space all scale off it.

The baseline had to follow, and this is the part that is easy to get backwards:
the row hangs glyphs UP from the baseline, so **shrinking alone moves the block
DOWN**. Cap 25.5 at the old baseline 96 tops out at y66 — nine canvas pixels
*lower* than cap 34 did. `RC_BASE` 96 → **60** puts it at y30.5..62.6 (physical
46..94 at 1080p), which also lands its top edge on the LUCK bar cluster's, the
mirror readout in the opposite corner.

`RC_R` deliberately **did not** move: 1268 is shared with the tower gauge and the
gun HUD, and the 12 remaining canvas pixels to the screen edge are not worth
breaking a three-element alignment for. Measured against the generated metrics:
188 physical px wide at one digit, 221 at two, 255 at three, 289 at four.
Worst-case pool use is 9 glyphs — the space consumes no slot — against 10.

**UNPLAYED.** Lints green (lua / arity / assets / hints). Not built by this
session: two concurrent sessions were editing the same tree, and a build packs
whoever synced last.


## 2026-09-04 (v17.24) — KBM KEYCAPS: the cap grew, the text grew faster, and a double-bound key named both of them

> ⚠️ **SUPERSEDED BY v17.27, AND HALF-WRONG — NEVER SHIPPED IN A BUILD.** The
> screenshot this entry was waiting for arrived and chose reading **(B)**: the
> font is a fixed base times `setScale` and the box height does NOT size text,
> so every box-height write below was **inert**. The symptom was not overflow at
> all, it was text far too SMALL. What survives from here is the multi-bind trim,
> the measured cap geometry, and the one-writer file. Read v17.27 for the model
> that is actually true.

User: *"KBM UI is still pretty bugg. The placeholders we have in the class menu
always have text that overflows."* (Screenshot pending — one thing below is
still unproven and the picture settles it; see the ⚠️ at the end.)

### Two causes, both real, both in the same six pixels of arithmetic

**1. v17.4's widening HELD FEWER CHARACTERS THAN THE CAP IT REPLACED.** In this
LUI the rendered font size follows the ELEMENT'S BOX HEIGHT (the repo's own
v16.32 finding: *"if the line overflows the pill, shrink the box height"*). Every
caller sized the bind text as `capTop+9 .. capBottom-9`, so the text scaled with
the cap. v17.4 grew the switch keycap from 72x36 to 96x48 to hold a longer
string — and grew the text box 18 -> 30 along with it. Width x1.33, font x1.67,
so capacity went **DOWN about 20%**. A keycap that scales uniformly can never fix
a text overflow; only the ratio of width to font size moves it.

**2. A MULTI-BOUND ACTION NAMES EVERY KEY IT IS ON.** Read out of the user's own
`players/bindings_0.cfg`: `+frag` sits on **G and MOUSE3** — the only action in
that file with two keyboard keys — so `[{+frag}]` expands to a string naming
both. That is a two-lane advertisement inside a one-key picture, against the
map's own standing rule that a menu **advertises one lane**. It is now trimmed at
the first separator and shows the first key.

**3. AND `^7` WAS FIGHTING `setRGB`.** Every call site passed `"^7[{+bind}]"`
while also setting dark ink for the pale cap. If LUI honours the inline code the
key drew WHITE ON A NEAR-WHITE KEYCAP; if it does not, the code was dead weight.
The token is stripped now, so `setRGB` is the only writer of that colour — right
under both readings.

### One writer, because this copy lives on three surfaces

`ui/uieditor/widgets/HUD/AetheriumWidgets/TodKeycap.lua` (new, `require`d by both
card menus and the pause legend, `rawfile,` line added — **a `require` of an
unzoned file takes the whole menu down silently, so the four edits move
together**). It owns the trim, the fit and the cap's geometry. Eleven keycaps go
through it: 2 switch + 4 card locks in the draft, 2 switch + 2 card locks in the
deal panel, 3 in the pause legend. The map has paid twice already for control
copy that lives on three surfaces and gets fixed on two (v16.83, then v16.93).

**THE CAP'S GEOMETRY IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** `i_tod_key_blank_wide` is
384x192; decoding it, the BRIGHT face runs x 29..354 and y 19..148, with a dark
outline at y~152 and a grey bottom lip below it. So the readable face is inset
**7.6% each side** and its centre sits at **43.5% of the cap height, not 50%** —
every caller centred on 50% and pushed the glyph bottoms onto the lip. Both
numbers are now constants in the new file with the measurement recorded beside
them.

**THE FIT CAN ONLY SHRINK.** Each call site passes its CURRENT box height as the
ceiling, so no keycap can come out bigger than it is today. That is deliberate:
it makes this safe to ship before the screenshot arrives.

- Lua only (plus one `.zone` line) → `-GscOnly`. `lint_tod_lua.js` clean (45
  files), its selftest 7/7, `lint_tod_assets.js` clean against baseline.
- Version numbering: v17.22 and v17.23 were taken by a peer session while this
  was written; this is v17.24.

⚠️ **UNPROVEN, AND THE SCREENSHOT DECIDES IT.** Two readings of how this LUI
sizes text both survive the evidence in-tree: **(A)** font = box height x scale
(believed since v16.32, but that line calls itself a first guess), under which
only the multi-bound `+frag` cap overflows and this change is the whole fix; or
**(B)** font = a fixed base x scale, under which the height write is INERT, every
cap draws the same size regardless of its rect, and **every** keycap overflows —
which is what the user's word "always" would mean. The pause panel's measured
"6.8 px/char at a 14 px box and scale 0.90" cannot separate them, because a 14 px
base and a 14 px box give the same answer. If the picture shows single-letter
caps overflowing too, it is (B) and the fit must drive `scale` instead of the box
height — one line in `Fit()`. The `CHAR_ADV` estimate (0.62) is the other knob,
and it is re-calibrated the same way: measure a known string's drawn width
against its cap's 96 px.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.23) — THE GUN ICON: the one input with evidence behind it was the one we threw away, twice

A fresh-eyes read of MAP 1 (`abandoned_cyber_city_zombies`), at the user's
suggestion — *"This exist on the aethierium HUD in abandonde cyber city ... I
would expect this to be easily found in that code."* It was, and it reverses
v17.19.

### Both arguments for retiring `viewmodelWeaponName` were wrong

1. **"map 1 subscribes it and DISCARDS the value."** This **conflates three
   different models**. The line cited across v17.13/v17.19 (`acc_hud.lua:1515`)
   is `currentWeapon.`**`weapon`** — a different model, in a different widget,
   used as a weapon-changed pulse to reset an ammo baseline. Map 1's **icon**
   rides `currentWeapon.`**`viewmodelWeaponName`** and **uses** the value.
2. **"an element can only carry one subscription."** **Refuted.** Map 1's own
   `AetheriumLoadout` hangs THREE on its root (the shield slot) and
   `AetheriumPlayerInfo` hangs SEVEN, all shipped and working. The double
   subscription v17.19 removed was never the fault. (v17.19's own entry conceded
   this was a suspicion, not a rule — it should not have been built on.)

### What that model actually carries: a lowercase ASSET CODENAME

Map 1's `GetWeaponIcon` is an EXACT key match on lowercase codenames after a
suffix-strip chain — no lowercasing, no `ingame_name` path, no display names at
all. So anything it renders proves the payload. Two live observations in map 1's
CHANGELOG:

- the **Grav drew a WHITE BOX** — an image registered but never packed. A table
  MISS draws `blacktransparent`, i.e. nothing. So the lookup HIT.
- the icon **"went blank mid-run even for mapped guns"** until strips were added
  for `_acc_*` / `_rdw` / `_fast%d` — suffixes that exist only in ASSET names.

**So this map deleted the only input anybody has evidence for.** It is back as a
SECOND feed on its own element, subscribed and painted once — the exact shape
map 1 ships — and `TOD_GUN_CAT` is live again rather than the dead second chance
v17.21's comment admitted it had become. Neither lane can clobber the other into
a *wrong* icon: an unresolvable value returns nil and keeps the last good state.
The viewmodel feed never touches the NAME — `Engine.Localize` of a codename is
the codename, which would put `T9_MAC10_ZM` on screen where `MAC-10` belongs.

The probe now reports the LIVE state and which lane won: `SMG V` (viewmodel),
`SMG N` (name), `NIL -` (neither ever resolved).

### Corrected: a comment that misattributed the kit's table to map 1

The header claimed `sat_ar_hawk` / `_condor` / `_macaw` were "MAP 1's roster".
They are the **vendored kit's** entries. Map 1 DELETED them — *"that art isn't
shipped in the Aetherium asset pack, so the entries could only ever render
blank"* — and replaced the table with its own 263-line roster. This map kept the
kit's copy untouched.

### Riot shield: both on-screen prints removed

User: *"riot shield shows diaplyed text on screen when its broken. IT already
makes a sound"*, then the same for the recharge. Both gone.

**Verified before removing, not assumed:** both aliases are registered in
`sound/aliases/tod_ui.csv` with wavs on disk — `tod_shield_break` (3d, vol 92,
125 KB) and `tod_lounge_arrive` (2d, vol 90, 384 KB) — so neither removal leaves
a silent event.

⚠️ **But `TOD_SHIELD_BACK_SND` is a SHARED alias, not a shield sound.** It is
`tod_lounge_arrive`, the breather-lounge first-arrival chime, also played by
`_tod_atmosphere` at every lounge and `_tod_spire:1692`. That was harmless while
text named the event; with the text gone the chime is the ONLY signal, and the
same arpeggio now means both "your shield is back" and "you reached a lounge".
Flagged at the call site; it wants its own wav.

### The build that failed: the wav-converter null-ref, and the RAM correlation

One `-GscOnly` burned all three linker attempts without emitting a bank and the
guard Died correctly ("do NOT test this build") on a fresh `.ff` — the exact
signature on record. No linker or game process was running, so NOT a two-linker
collision. **Free RAM was 2.6 GB of 15.6**, below the 3.2 GB noted alongside the
last occurrence; that correlation is now two-for-two and worth checking first.
The next build recovered on linker attempt 2 (`.all.sabs` 143.3 MB) without the
manual `sound\zone` delete, so the in-script retry is still a coin flip rather
than a cure.

Gates green. `-GscOnly`. **UNPLAYED — and the gun icon is still unfixed.** This
build carries the probe that is meant to end that.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.22) — GUN HUD: the dual-wield split reverted, and the panel slides flush with the tower gauge

### The "8/8" dual-wield split is out, one build after it went in

User, on being told the engine publishes only one clip: *"Is there anything we
can do to the cleint UI pool to fix this? ... If not then I want this reverted
cause there is no poimt if they are not indpeendent guns."*

**The pool was checked rather than quoted, and the answer is no.**
`_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc` counts itself from the tree (2026-08-30): **16 fields /
60 bits against the PROVEN-BOOTED ceiling of 18 / 61 — one bit spare**, and a
clip needs five to eight. The only dead field, `todMagBonus`, is 1 bit. Freeing
enough means cutting a shipped feature — `todDmgNum` is 14 bits, the damage
numbers — to buy a cosmetic, and an overflow is not a degraded readout but
`Com_ERROR "clientuimodel is out of space"` and a map load that aborts to the
lobby. Behind that sits a second unproven lane: whether the SERVER can read the
off-hand's clip at all. Back to the honest doubled figure.

Two pieces of that work are KEPT, because neither rests on dual wield:
- the `_rdw`/`_ldw` tests stay deleted — they matched asset suffixes against a
  display name and could never fire;
- the clip glyph pool stays 7 and keeps its auto-fit. `row.set()` truncates past
  its pool silently, and it truncates a RIGHT-ALIGNED layout — an overlong value
  does not look overlong, it looks like a different number — and 4 was exactly
  the documented worst case with zero margin.

### HUD_DX — the panel slides as one, and it is one number

User: *"push the gun HUD like 10 units to the right so its aligned with the
tower image on the right of screen ... Ill analyze after and we can adjust."*

Measured before moving: the tower gauge is **x1216..1268** (`tod_upgrade.lua`,
`GA_X` 1216 + `GA_W` 52) and the panel is **x1000..1256**, so its right edge sat
**12** short of the gauge's, not 10. Offered the measurement, the user took 12,
so the two right edges are now FLUSH at 1268 rather than approximately aligned.

**`HUD_DX` is one constant and every x anchor is written as its DESIGN
coordinate + `HUD_DX`** — panel, gun bay, name box, name/clip/reserve right
edges and both offhand slots. The design numbers in the comments therefore stay
TRUE, and the next adjustment is one number instead of nine edits (which is
what made the 10 -> 12 change a one-line diff). Widths (`NAME_MAXW`,
`CLIP_MAXW`) are not offsets and do not move. Ceiling: the rightmost element is
the lethal tile at 1256, so `HUD_DX` has room to 24 before the canvas edge.

**NOT applied to the widget root**, deliberately: `self` is 0..1280 and the perks
