## 2026-09-04 (v17.21) — GUN HUD: the low-ammo flash was measuring the wrong magazine; a dual-wield split built and reverted in one build

### The low-ammo flash was volume, not percentage — and the icon bug was causing it

User: *"when low ammo the clip will blink red. But i thnk the trigger is volume
and not percentage of clip left."* Correct, and the two open HUD bugs turned out
to be the same bug.

The threshold **is** written as 25% of the magazine — but the magazine is
`clipMax`, learned by observation and reset only when `curWeapon` changes, and
`curWeapon` was written **only on the icon resolver's success path**. While the
icon was broken, `clipMax` never reset: it climbed to the largest magazine held
all run and stayed there. Hold an HK21 once and every pistol, shotgun and blade
after it sits permanently under the threshold and flashes red on a full
magazine. The weapon's identity is now recorded unconditionally, before and
independently of whether its category resolves.

### Dual wield: built, then reverted the same build, by the user

Asked for `8/8` instead of `16`. Built it — then reverted on the user's call:
*"there is no poimt if they are not indpeendent guns."* They are right. The
engine publishes ONE clip (the hand the player fires), so the split drew the
same number twice: one reading in a disguise, and worse than the honest 16
because it would keep reading 8/8 if the hands ever diverged.

**The costing, so this is not re-opened without new information.**
`_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc`'s own count from the tree (2026-08-30): **16 fields / 60
bits against the PROVEN-BOOTED ceiling of 18 / 61 — one bit left**, and a clip
needs five to eight. The only dead field (`todMagBonus`) is 1 bit. The bits
would have to come out of a shipped feature (`todDmgNum` is 14 — the damage
numbers) to buy a cosmetic, and an overflow is not a degraded readout, it is
`Com_ERROR "clientuimodel is out of space"` and a map load that aborts to the
lobby. Behind that sits a second unknown: whether the SERVER can read the
off-hand's clip at all is itself unproven.

Kept from that work, because both stand on their own: the **`_rdw`/`_ldw` tests
are gone** (they matched asset suffixes against a display name and could never
fire — an off switch, not a fallback), and the **clip glyph pool is 7, not 4**
(`row.set()` silently truncates past its pool, drawing a right-aligned layout's
leftmost cells — an overlong value does not look overlong, it looks like a
different number, and 4 was exactly the documented worst case with zero margin),
plus an **auto-fit** on the clip cell, which is 85 canvas px and was already one
pixel short of a four-digit count.

### The gun icon: a probe instead of a fourth guess

v17.19 did not fix it (user: *"still broken. Showing the pistol image for all
guns. I tried with skirmisher"*). Every link has now been ruled out with
evidence — the subscription (the icon shares the weapon-name callback and the
name swaps), the image write (the pistol on screen is drawn by the same line),
the art (14 zone lines, 14 converted `.iwi`), and the table (a script checked all
44 `displayName` values in the twins GDT; every one resolves). Two things ship
instead of a fourth guess:

- **A normalising resolver.** Keys are mirrored with every separator stripped, so
  a display string differing by punctuation, spacing or a non-ASCII dash still
  resolves. This is insurance against the one link never checked: that
  `Engine.Localize` returns the GDT's `displayName` character for character.
- **`TOD_HUD_DEBUG`, a gated probe.** Armed, the name band reads
  `MAC-10 SMG` / `MAC-10 NIL`, separating the three states that look identical
  today: resolver works (fault is the image write) / lookup fails on a string
  that looks right / **no suffix at all, meaning this `.ff` is not the one
  running**. Gated in `build_map.ps1` like `TOD_MOCK_PARTY`: warns every build,
  dies on `-Publish`. Verified firing: `WARN: TOD_HUD_DEBUG ARMED`.

### The account is SUBSCRIBED to its own published Workshop copy

`steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_311210.acf` carries `"subscribedby"` for item
3788921059, whose `.ff` is the **03:13 v17.14 upload** — before any of these
fixes. A subscribed published copy loading instead of the `usermaps` build is a
hazard already recorded in this project. If that is what happened, v17.19 was
never tested rather than disproven. Unsubscribe before the next test; the probe's
"no suffix" state settles it either way.

dual-wield revert lands in the next one). **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.20) — ENDLESS SPIRE: 60% of the v16.9 round speed-up given back

User, after playing v16.9's halved budget: *"The rounds progress too fast in the
endless spire. I know we made a change for this. I dont want to revert but I do
want to half it. Maybe even 60% less faster."*

`TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_DIV` **2 → 1.25**, taken as the far end of that range.

### Why the counter was racing, and why this is the lever

v16.9 halved every spire round's spawn budget to kill the 15-minute round. Round
length is proportional to budget in the budget-bound regime the spire runs in
(spawning stalls on the 45 `ai_limit`, so the trickle floor cannot move the
clock) — so halving it did not just shorten rounds, it made the round NUMBER
climb twice as fast, and every per-round ramp climbed with it: the +0.28%/round
zombie speed, the boss cadence, the HP curve, all against a physical climb whose
length did not change.

Reasoned in round LENGTH, which is what a player feels:

| DIV | budget | round length | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stock | L | pre-v16.9, "15 minutes" |
| 2 | 50% | 0.50 L | what was played |
| **1.25** | **80%** | **0.80 L** | **here — 60% longer than DIV 2, still 20% shorter than pre-v16.9** |
| 1.333 | 75% | 0.75 L | the milder "half it", if 1.25 overshoots |

### One constant, no lockstep

The single use site is `int( n / TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_DIV )` in
`_tod_endless_rounds::tod_max_zombies`; the division is float and `int()`
truncates, so a non-integer divisor is fine. **Checked for a second copy and
there is none** — `_tod_spire::ascend` clamps the round already in progress at
ascension by RE-RESOLVING through `zm::get_zombie_count_for_round`, which comes
back through this same hook, so it follows the change by construction. The
`TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_MIN` 12 floor is untouched and bites less at the larger budget.

The define's LEDGER comment now records that **2 was played** — it previously
said "nothing has been measured at either yet", which was true of 3 and 2 both
and is no longer true of 2.

**Renumbered v17.16 -> v17.20** on 2026-09-04: three sessions were writing
this CHANGELOG the same day and v17.16 was claimed twice. The number is
allocation order, not build order — this entry's own `.ff` time is below.

Gates green (arity / hints / lua / assets). `-GscOnly`. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.19) — THE GUN ICON, AGAIN: v17.13 fixed the right thing and never ran

User, after playing v17.14: *"we have these little gun HUD icons that show up
depending on which gun is out ... our solution isnt working and I only see the
MR6 even when I have different guns out."*

### The symptom did not move, and that is the whole diagnosis

v17.13 replaced the category lookup wholesale — off `viewmodelWeaponName` +
asset stems, onto `weaponName` + a 49-entry display-name table. The player saw
**exactly** what they saw before it. **A change that resolves the answer from a
completely different table and produces a byte-identical symptom did not execute
at all**; it did not "miss a lookup". That reading was available before the build
and was not taken, which is how this became the third report of one bug.

### What was ruled out, from the repo, with no play session

- **`RegisterImage` / the art.** The pistol the player is looking at is
  registered by the *same line* in `refreshGunIcon()` that would register
  `i_tod_hud_gun_smg`. If that line works once it works for all 14 — and all 14
  have a zone line and a converted content-hash `.iwi`.
- **The table.** "MAC-10" and "BULLDOG" are both in `TOD_NAME_CAT`.
- **The build.** `.ff` 03:04:37, `diff -rq` clean on scripts/ zone_source/ ui/,
  nothing in the deployed tree newer than the `.ff`, and the Workshop copy
  uploaded 03:13 is byte-size-identical to it. Both copies had the fix.
- **The model.** *Asked the user*: the weapon NAME text swaps correctly. So
  `currentWeapon.weaponName` fires and its payload is real. One question settled
  what two builds of guessing had not.

That leaves DELIVERY — and `self.gun_icon` was **the only element on this panel
carrying two `subscribeToModel` calls**. Every single-subscription readout here
(name, clip, reserve, both offhand counts) works.

### The fix

- **The icon rides the weapon-name handler.** Same callback, same element, same
  model, ONE subscription — the exact shape of every readout on this panel that
  works. The icon can no longer be more broken than the name *by construction*.
- **`viewmodelWeaponName` is retired WHOLE** — subscription, `todFeed` helper,
  and the claims made for it. It never produced a match here across v17.9→v17.14.
- **Painted once at construction**, which the v17.9 rewrite had dropped for the
  name lane too. Map 1 paid for that line: the model is often set BEFORE this menu
  exists, and the HUD is rebuilt on every death→spectate transition.
- **THE MR6 AND "DEATH & TAXES" WERE NOT IN `TOD_NAME_CAT`.** `pistol_standard`
  is stock, so the GDT-generated block never had it, and the exception list missed
  it. The one weapon every player spawns with, every HEAVY carries as a T1 sidearm
  and every downed player crawls with could not be resolved at all — invisible
  only because `pistol` is also the cold-start default. (Note the literal `&`:
  `todApplyWeapon` does not do `setWeaponName`'s `&`→` AND ` expansion, so the
  key is spelled as the value arrives.)
- **`TOD_NO_MAG` was missing `katana`.** v17.12 split the wakizashi out of the
  blade cell so the SLASHER's tier-2 promotion would show on the HUD, and split it
  out of this set at the same time without meaning to — so the exact defect item 3
  of the v17.9 rebuild was written to kill, a melee weapon reading a literal
  `0 / 0` as the biggest element on the panel, was live again for the wakizashi
  and the Yamikirimaru. **A category added to one table owes an answer in every
  table keyed on categories.**
- **Precautionary, not proven:** the two perk watches on `self.lethal.icon` moved
  onto the slot TILES, which carry none, leaving no element on the panel with more
  than one subscription. `refreshLethalIcon()` is idempotent and reads perk state
  fresh, so this is a no-op if a multi-subscription element is fine and a fix if it
  is not. The kit itself hangs five subscriptions off one element in
  `AetheriumPlayerInfo`, so this is a suspicion earned from THIS panel's evidence,
  not a proven engine rule — the comment says to come back and confirm.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.18) — ENEMIES THAT STAND STILL AND NEVER TARGET YOU: the parked riser, and nothing in the map could see it

User, after playing v17.14/15: *"We are still seeing an issue occasionally on the
map especially random spots on the endless spire where enemies just cant target
you so they just stand still."* **Still** — v17.14 had already seeded the spire
per riser (22 → 278), so this is what is left after the navmesh fix, and it is a
different bug wearing the same face.

### THE MECHANISM, read end to end in the stock reference

A riser whose CLIMB-OUT never finishes is a **statue**, and every part of that is
stock's own machinery:

- `_zm_spawner::do_zombie_rise` sets `in_the_ground`, threads `hide_pop` — which
  `Show()`s the zombie **0.5 s in, unconditionally** — runs
  `AnimScripted( "rise_anim" )`, then blocks in `zombie_shared::DoNoteTracks`, a
  bare `for(;;) waittill(flagName)` with **no timeout** (`shared.gsc:387-405`).
  Only *after* it returns does the function clear `in_the_ground` and fire
  `"risen"`.
- `zombie_think` is parked on that same waittill (`_zm_spawner.gsc:581`), so
  `self.zombie_think_done` is never set.
- And the **root** of the behaviour tree runs `idlespawnbehavior` — a parallel of
  `condition_script_negate zombieisthinkdone` + a **looping** `idle@zombie`
  (`behavior/zm_zombie.ai_bt:117-137`) — which sits **above** the playable-area
  branch that carries `findfleshservice` (`:552`).

So the zombie is visible, alive, holding an `ai_limit` slot, and has **no enemy,
no goal and no FindFlesh tick, forever**. That is the report verbatim, and it is
per-zombie and position-independent, which is what makes it read as "random
spots".

**AND NOTHING IN THE MAP COULD RESCUE IT.** `_tod_stray::eligible` refuses
`in_the_ground` by design, `_tod_zombie_speed::apply_speed_for_round` refuses it
by design, and `tod_boss_stuck_watch` is elite-only. Three correct guards with no
one behind them.

### The fixes

- **A BOUNDED ESCAPE FROM THE CLIMB-OUT** (`_tod_stray::rise_watch` /
  `force_risen`). Any climb-out still running after 14 s is completed by hand, in
  `do_zombie_rise`'s own order — `Unlink` + delete the anchor if one is still
  live, `StopAnimScripted`, `Show`, clear `in_the_ground`,
  `notify( "risen", "find_flesh" )`, re-assert the gait. Every one of those calls
  is one stock already makes on this exact path, which is why none of them needed
  an engine experiment. **We deliberately do not diagnose WHY it stalled** — a
  stomped anim rate, a nullified rise-death `StopAnimScripted`, a missing end
  notetrack and a failed anchor spawn all land in the identical state, and only a
  bounded escape makes the whole class self-healing. Its own sweep, not a lane in
  `stray_sweep`, because that function stands down for exactly the states a rise
  is most likely to stall in.
- **ONE PROVEN PRODUCER, CLOSED AT SOURCE.** `_tod_upgrades::set_world_pause`
  stamps `ASMSetAnimationRate( 0.05 )` on every axis AI, and the unpause branch
  delegated the restore to `_tod_zombie_speed`'s keep-alive sweep — which
  early-returns on `in_the_ground` (correctly: it must not fight a scripted
  animation). So nothing restored the rate for a zombie that was mid-rise when a
  card pick began. The freeze half was symmetric and stays; the missing restore
  is now explicit.
- **THE STRAY WATCHDOG COULD NOT SEE A ZOMBIE STANDING NEXT TO YOU.** Its only
  admission test was `stray_cost > 6000`, and cost is `Distance2D + 4·|dz|` on a
  tower whose cross-section never reaches 1700 — a pure "four laps of vertical
  separation" rule. A zombie 300 units from a player scored ~300 and was actively
  re-marked **healthy** every sweep. New **IDLE LANE**: has not moved 48 units in
  6 s, is 96+ units from the nearest player (in melee range a still origin is an
  attack cycle, not a strand), is within cost 4000, and `HasPath()` is false.
  Remedy is cheapest-first — re-goal through the loosening navmesh ladder, then
  clamp the zombie itself onto the mesh, and only after two free passes the
  module's existing relocation with its climb-out arrival. The motion stamp gets
  its **own unbudgeted pre-pass**: inside the budgeted loop, a busy sweep would
  leave the tail of the array stale and read it as motionless.
- **THE ELITE WATCHDOG WAS SWITCHED OFF BY ARCHITECTURE.**
  `tod_boss_stuck_watch` reset its stall accumulator unconditionally within
  `TOD_BOSS_NEAR_PLAYER` 1500. A spire hub hall's trial box is ~1,220 units corner
  to corner, so **no elite sealed into a Warden trial could ever accrue a single
  second of stall time** — at the exact place the user reports enemies standing
  still. Now the near-reset requires a sign of life: displacement over 256 across
  the whole window (≈14 u/s, far under any elite's speed) **or** damage inside 8 s
  (`tod_actor_cb_ms`, already stamped on every damaged actor). An elite the party
  is fighting is engaging even if it never moves, and must never be teleported
  out of that fight.
- **AN ABANDONED WARDEN DROP LEFT A LITERAL STATUE.** `trial_wardens` carries
  `level endon( "tod_trial_end" )` and called `spawn_panzer()` **synchronously**,
  and that call blocks for the whole of `drop_in`. A win landing inside the drop
  killed the stack mid-fall: `drop_in`'s teardown is all on the far side of its
  waits, so the `script_model` proxy wearing the boss's model **stood there for
  the rest of the match** looping `fly_civil_protector_loop`, while the real boss
  stayed `Ghost()`ed, `SetCanDamage(false)`, `ignoreall`, and held a
  `level.tod_panzer_alive` slot that suppresses every later Warden. The drop moved
  to its own thread; `drop_janitor` now backstops **every** caller so no future
  one can reintroduce it.
- **Two smaller holes on the same trail.** `_tod_stray::pick_destination` had no
  `level.tod_trial_box` filter — the other two spawn selectors both have one — so
  a relocation during a sealed hold-out could drop a zombie *outside* the gate,
  manufacturing the very strand the module exists to prevent. And
  `spawn_panzer`'s early returns sit **above** its `level.tod_boss_force_org`
  consume site, so a refusal armed that anchor for the next Panzer anywhere in the
  run; both spire callers now clear it.

### SEED EVERY WALKABLE SURFACE — the rule, stated a third time and finally about surfaces

Seeds were emitted **one per riser**, and §6f states in its own words that risers
live only on **landings**. So every stair FLIGHT, every spire crate shelf, every
hub porch fan and the summit apron carried **no seed at all** — and cod2map is
Havok **region pruning**, not a flood: a region connected to a seeded one can
still be dropped. The evidence was already in the repo and unread as evidence:
v17.14 took the spire 22 → 278 seeds with **byte-identical geometry** and the
`.hkt` went 110,468 → 114,624. Entities that add no surface cannot grow a mesh
unless previously-pruned regions are now kept.

- **The ramp seeds ride inside `rampWedgeY` / `rampWedgeX` themselves**, computed
  from the very arguments the wedge is built from, so a new flight anywhere in
  this map is seeded by construction and cannot be forgotten again. That covers
  all **311** wedges — 100 tower flights, 200 spire flights, the crown stair, the
  summit stair and the 9 causeway road stairs.
- **The tower's four BREATHER laps had no landing seed either**, and that is a
  clean example of why a spawn table must never be a coverage table: v10.12/v13.2
  moved laps 10/20/30/40's risers into the lounge and onto the teleporter spur, so
  the spiral's own two landings on those floors were left unseeded — while the
  seed block's comment went on asserting "the tower's two risers per lap sit on
  the mid and end landings". Parsed out of the emitted `.map` before fixing: the
  tower's 149 seeds had z gaps of exactly 384 at 3650, 7490, 11330 and 15170, and
  nowhere else. Seeded from the geometry now.
- `node_pathnode` **427 → 1478**; `.map` entities 1748 → 2799; **world brush
  planes unchanged at 84,624** — this change adds zero surface, which is what
  makes the next `.hkt` reading a clean signal rather than a guess.

### What the pre-build review caught, and why it is recorded here

Every one of these was a defect in the FIX, found before the build. They are
written down because each is a shape that will recur.

- **`force_risen` replayed only two of stock's four exit lines.** It omitted
  `notify( "rise_anim_finished" )`, which is what disarms
  `zombie_utility::zombie_rise_death` — a watcher threaded on `level` that waits
  for the zombie's health to reach 1 and then stamps the *sink-back-into-the-
  ground* death animation and calls `StopAnimScripted`. Left armed, every rescued
  zombie carried it for the rest of its life and would have died wrong, minutes
  later, somewhere else entirely. **A function whose stated rule is "replay
  stock's own exit" has to replay ALL of it.**
- **20 of the 30 new hub-porch seeds were inside the solid core column.** The
  porch fan's westmost slabs are emitted below the core's top (`mid - SLAB`) and
  inside its footprint, so they are buried; seeds keyed to those slabs were
  buried with them. Caught by testing every emitted seed for containment in the
  axis-aligned world brushes before building — **20/1478 before the clamp, 0
  after.** cod2map's `Could not drop node` would have said the same thing, one
  full build later.
- **The idle lane read "is it busy fighting?" against the wrong player.** The
  melee exemption measured to `nearest_upright()`, which drops crawlers on
  purpose — correct for choosing where to SEND a zombie, wrong for asking whether
  one is BUSY. Zombies target downed players by stock design, so a mob on a
  downed teammate scored as a field of statues and would have been relocated off
  him mid-bleedout. Now measured against `nearest_any()`.
- **A band of 2,000 units belonged to neither lane.** The idle lane carried its
  own 4,000 cost cap while the distance lane starts at 6,000, so a zombie stuck
  at cost 5,000 was cleared as "near" by one and refused as "far" by the other.
  The redundant cap is deleted: the caller's single `<= TOD_STRAY_COST` split is
  now the only divider, so a gap and a double bid are both impossible by
  construction.
- **Three timing holes of my own making**: a world pause counted as idling until
  the sweep learned to re-baseline; the motion stamp sat inside the budgeted
  loop, so a busy sweep left the tail of the array stale and would have read it
  as motionless; and `rise_watch` restarted its clock on every paused sweep
  instead of holding it, which a run with frequent card picks could have deferred
  forever.
- **Two slow effects nearly got stomped.** `rise_watch` would have force-completed
  a climb-out that a Widow's Wine cocoon legitimately owns, and the new pause
  restore was the only anim-rate writer in the tree not checking
  `under_anim_slow()`.
- **`fought` could only ever see damage TAKEN.** `tod_actor_cb_ms` is stamped on
  the *damaged* actor, so an elite cornering a player it was beating on — hitting
  someone, taking nothing — read as pinned. `boss_player_damage` now stamps
  `tod_dealt_ms` and either direction counts.
- **A relocation during a Warden trial would have worked against itself.** With
  `pick_destination` newly filtered to the trial box, the idle lane's rescue of
  the zombies stranded *outside* the shut gate would have teleported them *into*
  the sealed hold-out, quietly stacking the whole outside horde onto a fight
  sized by `trial_recipe`. A running trial is now the module's fourth
  stand-down — the exact analogue of `tod_crown_sealed`.
- **Checked and NOT changed:** the three sites that write `level.tod_upgrade_pause`
  directly (`_tod_finale`, `_tod_spire`, `_tod_upgrades::init`) were flagged as
  missing the new restore. They are fine — none of them ever froze AI, because
  the finale `wipe_the_map()`s instead. **A guard is only missing if the thing it
  guards can happen.**

### Verification — and the navmesh number came back POSITIVE

FULL build, `.ff` 06:12:03, 145.75 MB. Lints green with no baseline edit:
geometry (0 misplaced walls, 0 unguarded edges, 0 detached, base→terrace /
terrace→citadel / spire arena→summit all walkable), arity, weapons, hints (91
distinct of 190 budgeted), lua, assets. Freshness proven both ways per doctrine:
`diff -rq` clean on `scripts/`, `zone_source/` and `ui/`, **and** nothing in the
deployed tree newer than the `.ff` — so no peer sync is standing in for my build.
Generated `_tod_door_data` / `_tod_crown_data` / `_tod_breather_data` /
`_tod_spire_data` carry no seed-related change.

**THE NAVMESH GREW 114,624 → 128,042 BYTES (+13,418, +11.7%) ON BYTE-IDENTICAL
GEOMETRY.** World brush planes are 84,624 before and after — a `node_pathnode`
adds no surface — so every one of those bytes is **mesh that cod2map was
previously PRUNING and now keeps.** That is direct compile-time proof that
walkable regions on these towers had no navmesh under them, which is exactly the
"stand still, cannot target" symptom, and it is a much larger recovery than the
per-riser pass bought (v17.14's spire seeding gained 3.8% on the same measure).

`tools/cod2map_last.log` is clean of every Havok marker — no `Could not drop
node`, no `below the area threshold`, no `too far from a seed`, no `Keeping the
largest region`. **All 1,051 new seeds anchored**, which is the direct validator
for seed placement. The only warning is the documented-benign
`NavVolume generation is skipped` (no `nav_volume` brush; nav volumes are for
flying AI).

Seeds were also checked for solid containment BEFORE the build by parsing the
emitted `.map`: **0 of 1,478 inside a world brush** (20 were, before the porch
clamp).

**STILL UNPLAYED.** The compile-time numbers prove mesh now EXISTS where it did
not; only a run proves zombies path on it, and only a run exercises the four GSC
watchdogs. A dev-gated `dev_mesh_probe` ships silent beside `dev_target_probe`:
on ascension it samples 600 points up the 200 spire flight ramps — deliberately
OFFSET from the seed coordinates, so it measures the flight rather than the
seed — and prints `spire mesh: N/600 flight samples OFF-MESH` with the first bad
coordinate. That is the measurement to run if this report comes back.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.17) — THE OWNED-UPGRADES LIST: dark rows never synced, and the panel was two rows too small

User: *"We have an issue where dark upgrades dont show in the pause menu? I have
both dark luck and dark riot shield and neither of them are in the pause menu
showing the dark version. Also I dont even see riot shield in the pause menu. Is
there too many upgrades to fit inthe menu for heavy class?"* — then, mid-fix:
*"Also check the scoreboard menu as well. Also not wired up correctly."*

Three separate defects behind one screen. The last question was the diagnosis.

### 1. A DARK PICK NEVER REACHED THE CLIENT

- `apply_upgrade`'s dark branch (`_tod_upgrades.gsc`) returns EARLY, above every
  levels test, because a dark card is dealt on a domain with zero headroom. It
  paid the bit, poked both inventory reconcilers — and skipped the
  `refresh_upgrade_list()` that every other payout path ends with. The dark bit
  reaches the client ONLY as `sync_max()`'s +200 on a `tod_upg_sync` row, so a
  dark pick was invisible until some OTHER domain gained a level and re-sent the
  whole table.
- In the spire that is close to never: a won trial is the only deal, and a dark
  card is by definition dealt on a domain with nothing left to level.
- **AN EARLY RETURN PAST THE TAIL OF A FUNCTION INHERITS NONE OF ITS
  OBLIGATIONS.** Every payout lane owes the same three — the level write (here,
  the bit), the inventory reconcile, and the client sync. Two of the three were
  copied down into the new branch; the one that was invisible from inside the
  function was not.

### 2. THE PAUSE PANEL DREW 14 ROWS AND EVERY CLASS COULD HOLD MORE

- Counted off the live `add_domain` scopes: **SKIRMISHER 16, ASSAULT 15,
  HEAVY 16, SLASHER 15** (15 domains plus the CLASS TIER row for the two 16s)
  against `2 columns x ROWS_MAX 7 = 14`. Rows render in ASCENDING DOMAIN ID, so
  overflow always eats the NEWEST domains: **45 RIOT SHIELD fell off for all
  four classes**, 42 FULL STEAM for the heavy too, 47 DEADSHOT for the assault.
- The code was honest about it — it printed `+2 MORE` — and nobody read it.
  **A truthful count of what you dropped is a last resort, not a fallback**: the
  row it drops is always the newest domain, i.e. the one the player is most
  curious about.
- Fixed with a **COMPACT PRESET** in `AetheriumStartMenu.lua`: a 15+ row list
  scales every row metric by 50/59 (row pitch 59 -> 50, plate 210x31 -> 177x26,
  pips 13/15 -> 11/13, text 0.90/0.79 -> 0.76/0.67), buying a 9th row per column
  for a capacity of **18**. Under 15 rows the panel is byte-identical to what
  shipped. The three bounds are re-checked at the worst real case (16 rows, 8 per
  column): right 314 <= COL_W 369, last act line ends 584, legend 586..617 < the
  637 the signature images paint over. The legend Y is clamped as well.
- **THE COMMENT HAD NOW BEEN STALE TWICE.** The single-column version claimed "at
  most 8 domains"; the two-column version that replaced it claimed "the true
  ceiling is 14 rows ... 2 columns x 7 covers it exactly" and was already wrong
  the day RIOT SHIELD landed. A ROW BUDGET IS NOT A COMMENT — it moves every time
  `add_domain` is called.

### 3. THE SCOREBOARD DREW THE SAME LIST AND KNEW NONE OF IT

- `AetheriumScoreboard.lua` renders the same `CoD.TodOwned`. v17.10 passed
  `o.dark` into `CoD.TodDomainDesc` there, so the panel has printed the DARK
  VALUE since the day the feature landed — and then drew the ordinary blue plate
  over it. The number moved with nothing on screen saying why.
  **HALF-WIRING IS WORSE THAN NOT WIRING**: a plain row showing a number the
  plain row cannot explain reads as a bug in the number.
- Its capacity was already fine (3 x 6 = 18 slots, and it drops row 24), which is
  why only the pause menu lost RIOT SHIELD.
- The rule now has **ONE OWNER**: `CoD.TodDarkPlate( id, plateMax )` in
  `tod_upgrade.lua` — the menu both screens already depend on for
  `CoD.TodDomainDesc` — holding `USE_DARK_PLATE_ART` and the `DARK_PLATE_NONE`
  not-yet-baked list. Both screens call it; neither builds an
  `i_tod_pause_rNN_dark` name itself.

### THE GATE (tools/lint_tod_assets.js, runs on every build incl. -GscOnly)

- **GATE C, hard fail.** Parses the reachable domain set per class off
  `add_domain`'s own `class_keys` argument and each panel's capacity off its own
  constants (`ROWS_MAX` for the pause menu, `TOD_UPG_COLS x TOD_UPG_ROWS_COL` for
  the scoreboard, which excludes the tier row), and fails naming the exact rows
  that would be dropped. Reverting `ROWS_MAX` to 7 reproduces the user's report
  verbatim, class by class.
- Same gate refuses a second Lua file that builds an `i_tod_pause_rNN_dark` name
  itself — the shape of defect 3.
- `DARK_PLATE_NONE` is now searched across `ui/` rather than read from one
  hardcoded path, so moving it again cannot silently empty the set.
- `lint_tod_assets_selftest.js` grew four cases (15 total, all must fire): the
  pause panel losing a row, the scoreboard losing a column, a NEW UNIVERSAL
  DOMAIN pushing a class past capacity (the case that will actually fire in
  anger — nobody edits `ROWS_MAX` by accident), and a second file inlining the
  dark-plate name.

**UNPLAYED.** Built `-GscOnly`; the fix is three Lua/GSC lanes and no geometry.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.16) — RIOT SHIELD: elite kills cut the recharge, and the dead-shield trap

Two things, one file. User: *"riot shield needs an ability where every elite you
kill takes off 2 seconds from the recharge time. Also is it wired correctly for
dark riot shield? I never got it back after the upgrade and it broke."* — then,
mid-build: *"this only applies to the dark shield max upgrade."*

### ELITE KILLS SHORTEN THE RECHARGE — A DARK-RUNG TERM

- **2 seconds per elite, KILLER ONLY, DARK HOLDERS ONLY**
  (`TOD_SHIELD_ELITE_CUT_SECS`, `elite_kill()` behind
  `level.tod_shield_elite_kill`). The user's second message the same day —
  *"this only applies to the dark shield max upgrade"* — so it is a THIRD term
  on the dark upgrade beside the 700 HP and the 1:30, reading the same
  `has_dark()` bit `shield_hp` and `recharge_secs` already read. One source; a
  Lv5 holder without the dark card is refused here exactly as they are refused
  the 700 HP.
- It shortens a recharge that is actually RUNNING and does nothing otherwise —
  there is nothing to bank against a shield you are still carrying. Cutting past
  the deadline is the point: the loop polls twice a second and hands the shield
  straight back. Four elites inside one Warden Trial take 8 s off 90.
- **HUNG ON `grant_elite_reward`**, the one function every elite death already
  resolves to a single killer — Rogue Protector, Reaver, Hellhound, Sprinter and
  the spire's Warden Panzers all land there. **Plus ONE second site**: a
  scheduled boss-round Panzer takes the `grant_boss_reward` fork instead (the
  v14.31 economy split), and a player counts the Panzer as an elite even though
  the money does not. The call sits inside that `else`, so a guard Panzer is cut
  once and a boss Panzer is cut once — never both.
- Advertised on the pause menu's **DARK** row for 45 (`DARK[45].act`, "hold or
  wear it; elite kills -2s recharge"), not on the base row — the base row and
  the `add_domain` desc are unchanged, because at Lv1-5 nothing happens.

### THE DEAD SHIELD (the "never got it back" report)

Not reproduced, and the dark wiring itself checks out: `has_dark` is keyed on
the same `"riotshield"` domain string the domain registers, `apply_upgrade`'s
dark branch pokes `level.tod_shield_reconcile` by hand (a dark bit is not a
level write), and both `shield_hp` and `recharge_secs` read it — 700 HP, 1:30.
Nothing there refuses to give the shield back.

What the report DOES pin down is that `reconcile()` had a state it could not
escape from, and the dark card is the one that would expose it: **a dark card is
only ever dealt on a MAXED domain, so every dark riot shield holder is at Lv5 —
the level that carries the second weapon.**

- **THE TRAP.** Stock's `player_take_riotshield` clears `hasRiotShield` FIRST,
  then calls `zm_equipment::take( self.weaponRiotshield )` — a field stock
  recomputes inside `UpdateRiotShieldModel`, which opens with a
  `WAIT_SERVER_FRAME`. If that take does not land, the weapon stays in the
  inventory with stock's flags down: a shield that blocks nothing and draws an
  empty bar. `held_shield()` reads the inventory, saw it, and reported the slot
  FULL — so the recharge return did nothing, and the 2 s maintain did nothing,
  forever.
- **THE SWEEP.** `shield_is_dead()` now cross-checks the two sources — inventory
  says carried, stock says not a shield — and `clear_shield()` reaps it
  (front-door `zm_equipment::take`, raw `TakeWeapon` + slot clear behind it for
  the case take() early-outs, which is the failure being survived). A grace
  window after our own give keeps it from reaping a shield handed out a frame
  ago.
- **THE RETURN VERIFIES ITSELF.** `recharge_loop` no longer fires one reconcile
  and trusts it: give, look, retry up to four times. Every give path downstream
  has early-outs that return SILENTLY, and this is the one call the player has
  been waiting up to four minutes on.

UNPLAYED. If the shield still goes missing after this, the dev print in
`recharge_loop` ("recharge return did not land") says whether the give is being
refused or whether the break was never seen at all.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.15) — RIOT SHIELD: a card refills the shield you are carrying

User: *"when you receive a Riot Shield card upgrade and you already have one it
should refill the health on your existing one with the health it just got
improved to."* It did not — `reconcile()` saw the right shield already in the
slot and left it alone, so a Lv2 shield one hit from breaking stayed one hit
from breaking after the Lv3 card; the card only made the *next* shield better.

- **THE REFILL.** `reconcile()` now tops the held shield back up to the new
  maximum when the card improves it. There is no engine setter for the shield
  pool — `DamageRiotShield()` only burns it, and stock's
  `player_shield_reset_health` repaints the HUD bar to 1.0 **without touching
  the pool**, so calling that alone would have drawn a full bar over a shield
  about to break. The one real refill is the re-give (take + buy), which is
  exactly what the Lv5 model promotion already does — so the refill reuses
  `swap_shield( held, held )`, latch and all, and a Lv4 -> Lv5 card was already
  refilling by construction.
- **TRACKED AS THE HP NUMBER, NOT THE LEVEL** (`tod_shield_hp_seen`, replacing
  `tod_shield_lvl_seen`). The DARK rung raises HP to 700 without moving the
  level and lands through this same reconcile; one number covers both, and it
  can never read a downgrade as an improvement. Fires exactly once per
  improvement — the 2 s maintain re-stamps the number on its first pass.
- **A CARD TAKEN MID-RECHARGE STILL ONLY SHORTENS THE WAIT**, and now the dark
  rung shortens it too: the deadline is re-derived from the break time at the
  current rate and taken **only when it lands earlier**, instead of being
  re-derived on a `lvl > seen` test that the dark rung could not trip.

UNPLAYED. The mechanism is the shipped Lv5 promotion path, which is itself
unplayed — the assumption both rest on is that `TakeWeapon` + `GiveWeapon`
resets the engine's shield pool (stock's own crafted-shield rebuild is the
evidence). If the bar comes back full but the shield still breaks in one hit,
that assumption is the thing that is wrong.

## 2026-09-04 (v17.13) — THE GUN ICON NEVER SWAPPED: it rode the one model nobody had proven

User, after playing v17.12: *"my gun icon in gun HUD on bottom right doesnt swap.
I swapped to mac and bulldog and it only showed a pistol the whole time. Gun ammo
swapper correctly. But gun icons didnt."*

### The cause, and it was written down before it shipped

The icon lane subscribed to `currentWeapon.viewmodelWeaponName` and nothing else,
matching its value against weapon STEMS. It never produced a match, so `curCat`
stayed nil and the cold-start default — the pistol — was all anyone ever saw.

**That model was the single fact an adversarial pass flagged as UNPROVEN before
v17.9 shipped**, in as many words: nobody can settle what it returns from source,
`share/raw` ships no Lua, and map 1's HUD subscribes `currentWeapon.weapon` and
then DISCARDS the value, using it purely as a "something changed" pulse. That is
the strongest available tell that its payload is not to be trusted. It was in the
notes and the code shipped on it regardless.

### The fix does not try to find out what that model contains

It drives the icon from the lane this map demonstrably HAS. The weapon NAME swaps
correctly in game — the name text sits beside the icon doing it — so that model
fires and its payload is real.

- **`TOD_NAME_CAT`**: 49 display names, base and PaP, keyed to the same 14
  categories. **Generated out of `source_data/tod_weapon_twins.gdt`** rather than
  typed, so a name cannot be misspelled here, plus the four weapons that GDT does
  not generate (the AMP63 pair, the Gift of Death pair, the riot shield). Matched
  exact-first then longest-substring, so "MP117 REDACTOR" cannot be claimed by a
  shorter key and "SPAS-12" cannot be claimed by "12".
- **One resolver, two inputs.** Both `weaponName` and `viewmodelWeaponName` feed
  it; display name is tried first, the asset stem second. Whichever carries
  something usable wins. An unresolvable value keeps the LAST GOOD icon rather
  than falling back to a wrong one.
- **Painted once at construction, per model.** Map 1 paid for this line already:
  *"the model is often set BEFORE this menu exists (the STARTING weapon), and the
  subscription alone never re-fires for a pre-existing value."* The HUD menu is
  rebuilt on every death->spectate transition, so "before this menu exists" is
  every single life, not just the first.
- **The dual-wield doubling was riding the same dead value.** It now also fires on
  `curCat == "akimbo"`, which is reached from the display names "Tokyo & Rose"
  and "Voice of Justice & Raging Judge". Both are PaP forms carrying
  `"dualWield" "1"`, and the PaP Executioner's name was corrected from pistol to
  akimbo in the same pass.

Checked before building: all **14** categories the two tables can produce have a
zone line — `akimbo axe blade gift katana launcher lmg minigun nailgun pistol
rifle shield shotgun smg`, 0 missing.

**Gates green, `-GscOnly` BUILD OK, `.ff` 02:51:19. UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-04 (v17.10) — GUN HUD: two offhand glyphs never drew, a melee weapon drew a handgun, and the v2 art pack

The v17.9 art is in and working. This is the follow-up pass: one real bug found
by an adversarial sweep over the mapping, two weapon keys that were missing, and
the v2 art brief (docs/96) built and sent.

### THE BUG: a guess that cannot match is not a fallback, it is an off switch

v17.9 picked each offhand glyph by substring-matching the value the engine
publishes on the `CurrentPrimaryOffhand` / `CurrentSecondaryOffhand` models,
guessing at `frag`, `grenade`, `cymbal`, `monkey`, `widow`, `web`. **The
engine's actual vocabulary is four names**, and they are sitting in the base ZM
asset list the whole time — `<modtools>/zone_source/all/assetlist/
zm_levelcommon.csv:6088-6091`:

    uie_t7_zm_hud_inv_icnlthl / icntact / icntactlilarnie / widowswine

Only `widow` could ever match. So the bespoke frag and cymbal monkey were set
once at construction and then **permanently overwritten** by the first model
callback — two commissioned images dead on arrival, and what the player actually
saw was the kit's own icon. The art was fine; the selection was dead.

**Now selected from STATE, not from string matching.** The tactical slot is
always the monkey (this map has exactly one tactical since the octobomb left
DISTRACTION in v16.49). The lethal slot reads PERK STATE, which is authoritative:
`hudItems.perks.widows_wine` and `hudItems.perks.electric_cherry` (PhD is hung
on the electric-cherry specialty slot here — the specialty is not the perk).
That also solves a problem the weapon alone cannot: PhD makes a Widow's grenade
split WITHOUT changing the held weapon (`_tod_perk_phd.gsc` watches
`grenade_fire`), so weapon-based selection could never have told the two apart.
The engine value survives as a last-resort fallback, and it is safe — those four
names are in `zm_levelcommon`, not the DLC `specialty_*` family that
white-squares on a published usermap.

### TWO WEAPON KEYS

- **The Widow's Wine knife drew a PISTOL.** Buying Widow's Wine swaps the melee
  for a widow variant, and nothing in `scripts/` ever calls
  `set_player_melee_weapon` — so the base melee stays `knife` and stock's
  generic branch gives `knife_widows_wine`. No key, so it fell to the pistol
  cold-start default: a melee weapon drawing a handgun. Three keys added.
  (Related correction: `_tod_classes.gsc`'s "the slasher's bowie replaces the
  base knife everywhere" is about INVENTORY, not the melee slot —
  `self.current_melee_weapon` stays `knife`.)
- **Bare fists** — two stock paths reach `zombie_fists` (the shield destroyed
  while held; going down holding it with no other primary). Both are closed by
  inventory here because a player always carries a primary plus a sidearm, so
  this is unreachable TODAY rather than absent. Keyed as insurance.

### THE v2 ART PACK (docs/96)

Out for generation. Three files: the gun sheet redrawn with real interior

## 2026-09-03 (v17.9) — THE GUN HUD REBUILT: the weapon icon was blank for every gun in the map, and a melee class read "0 / 0"

User: *"We have updated the left side player HUD but want to move over to the
Gun HUD at bottom right. We would need a component for clip, reserve, gun, name,
lethal and tacticals, which would be monkeys and grenades only on this map but
you can verify."* Then: *"I wonder if we should get creative with digits and
letters as well so we can have custom text and numbers as well."*

Design, measurements and the art pack: `docs/95_gun_hud_art_prompt.md`.
The bespoke art is OUT FOR GENERATION; this entry is the code half, which ships
and plays without it.

### Two defects nobody had reported, both found by measuring rather than looking

**THE WEAPON ICON HAS DRAWN NOTHING SINCE THE KIT WAS VENDORED.** Not dim —
absent. `AetheriumLoadout.lua`'s `GetWeaponIcon()` looks the gun up in
`CoD.AetheriumWeaponData`, whose gun entries are `sat_ar_hawk`,
`sat_ar_condor` and `sat_ar_macaw` — **map 1's roster**. Not one of this
map's 24 ladder weapons is in it, so every one falls to
`["default"] = { icon = "blacktransparent" }`. A 190 x 112 physical-pixel hole
in the middle of the panel, every gun, every run.

**A SLASHER READ "0" AND "0" FOR THE WHOLE RUN.** All 36
`t9_me_knife_american_*` / `t9_me_wakizashi_*` / `leviathan_*` variants carry
`clipSize 0` and `maxAmmo 0`, and that class holds a blade at all three tiers —
a quarter of the roster. In Lua `0` is truthy, so `if ammoInClip then` passed
and a literal zero was drawn as the largest element on the panel. The riot shield
lands in the same case. Map 1 hit this and fixed it (`acc_hud.lua:1484-1494`);
this map never had the fix. Both now show `-`.

### A claim this session got WRONG, and the correction

The first draft of docs/95 stated that **the lethal slot could never fill** — no
wall buys, no mystery box, and nothing in `scripts/zm/zm_tower_of_doom/` grants
a frag. All of that is true and the conclusion was still **wrong**. Stock
`_zm.gsc:4564 award_grenades_for_survivors()` GIVES the lethal and sets its clip
to 2/3/4, called from `round_think` at `_zm.gsc:4408` — outside all three round
pointers `_tod_endless_rounds.gsc:172-174` overrides, with `headshots_only` set
nowhere. **Every survivor gets 2-4 free frags at the start of every round.**

A grep over the MAP's own scripts cannot prove a STOCK lane does not run. The
reference image inside the art pack had already been rendered with the wrong
caption baked into it; it was regenerated before the zip went out.

### What changed in code

- **`AetheriumLoadout.lua` rebuilt.** New geometry: the whole readout is
  x1000..1256, y568..678 canvas = **384 x 165 physical px**, bottom edge level
  with the minimal player readout in the opposite corner. Every art box's aspect
  now matches its source EXACTLY (panel 256/74 = 1024/296; gun bay 96/44 =
  288/132; tile 46/32 = 276/192) — zero aspect error, which is the defect
  docs/89 was written to kill.

  guns emit both halves; if the model ever reported the left one the doubling

- **`TodScaleHud` removed from this widget.** Canvas x 1.5 = 1080p exactly, no

- **Deleted:** the orb plate, the AAT/ammo-mod icon (this map ships no alternate

- **Nine kit images retired whole**, entry and art together: the orb plate, both
  offhand swoosh tiles and their empty twins, the two empty glyph twins, and both

## 2026-09-03 (v17.8) — WISP TEA two at once and boss-seeking; WARDEN TRIALS: own track, 70s, 25% easier start; the v14.55 music cut reverted

User: *"Is it possible for us to have wisp tea spawn in two at once max and
have them prioritize bosses? Can we write the code for that and update the UI
to buy it that says Two Wisps Max"*.

### Two at once — a CAP on concurrency, not a pair

A summon still produces ONE wisp; a second lucky hit can now put a second one
out while the first is still alive. `WISP_TEA_MAX_WISPS` (2) in
`_zm_perk_wisp_tea.gsh` is the whole knob.

The pack was single-wisp by construction in **three separate places**, and all
three had to move together or the second wisp would have been a ghost:

1. **The cooldown was a per-player BOOLEAN** (`wispTeaCooldown`) — it can hold
   exactly one summon. It is now **CHARGES**: a summon spends one, and that
   charge returns `WISP_TEA_COOLDOWN_TIME` (120 s) after **its own** wisp
   expires, so the two slots run independent clocks. Per slot the perk's rate
   is untouched; there are simply two slots.
2. **`wispExpired` was notified on the PLAYER** and every follow/attack loop
   `endon`'d it there — a broadcast. The first of two wisps to expire would
   have retired the second one's loops as well and left it drifting, linked
   and inert, for the rest of its life. The notify moved onto the **wisp
   entity**; the loops `endon` the wisp's own `wispExpired` + `death`.
3. **One hardcoded idle offset** `(120,-100,0)`. Two wisps parked there are one
   wisp to the player's eye, so each live wisp claims a free slot
   (`wisp.wispSlot`, offsets `WISP_TEA_WISP_IDLE_OFF_A|B`). A lone wisp still
   parks exactly where the pack put it.

Belt and braces on the cap: the charge is the RATE limit, and a **live count
rebuilt from the entities themselves** is the CAP. The count is recomputed by
pruning `self.wispTeaWisps` rather than kept in a counter, so nothing can drift
out of step with the world — a spire teardown `Delete`, a host migration or a
re-give mid-summon all just prune. `give_wisp_tea_perk` refills charges (the
boolean was cleared there too, so this is unchanged behaviour, and it matters
under the spire's perma-perks, which re-give the roster on every respawn) but
**deliberately does not clear the live list** — clearing it would let a re-give
with two wisps in the air put four out at once. The spawn gate is re-tested
inside `spawnWisp`, not only in the damage monitor: a shotgun spread is many
damage events in one frame and `thread` does not run its body until the next
dispatch, so the monitor's own test can pass twice against one charge.

### Prioritize bosses

`wispFollowEnemy` took `ArrayGetClosest` over every axis actor and *then* asked
whether that one happened to be near the player. Two failures: a Panzer eight
feet away lost to any shambler a foot nearer, and a nearest-target that was out
of the player's range parked the wisp even when something else was well inside
it. `wispPickTarget` now walks the whole array and keeps the best by
**(tier, distance)** — tier from `wisp_target_tier()`, distance from the wisp.

`wisp_target_tier()` is the ladder `wisp_hit_damage()` was already using, lifted
into one function that both now read: 2 = Panzer-class, 1 = elite
(protector / reaver / hound / armored sprinter), 0 = trash. Panzer is claimed
first because it also carries `is_boss`. One ranking decides both what the wisp
goes for and what it does when it arrives, so a wisp can never seek a target it
has no damage tier for.

**THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: the zombie-count gate now binds TRASH ONLY.** Every
boss and elite on this map sets `ignore_enemy_count`
(`_tod_bosses.gsc:1704`/`:2202`, `_tod_hellhounds.gsc:361`,
`_tod_reaver.gsc:267`) and stock's `get_current_zombie_count()` skips exactly
those — so the number it returns is the **trash population and nothing else**.
The pack's `> 1` was a "never take the round's last zombie" rule; applied to the
whole array, it also parked the wisp for the back half of every thinned-out boss
fight, which is precisely when a boss-seeking wisp is supposed to be working.
Boss priority would have been silently dead in the one situation it exists for.

One incidental fix falls out of the rewrite: the old loop's out-of-range branch
re-linked the wisp to the player but left `wisp.attackTarget` set, so a wisp
that had flown home kept landing 0.75 s ticks on whatever it was last touching,
from anywhere. `attackTarget` is now cleared on every path that parks the wisp.

### ⚠️ The v14.20 Panzer invariant no longer covers a full pair

`WISP_TEA_BOSS_SEGMENTS` is unchanged at 60 and the .gsh block now says why that
matters. The 40-hit ceiling behind *"a wisp ALONE can never kill a Panzer"* is
**per wisp**. Two wisps land 2.67 hits/s, and boss-seeking means they pile onto
the Panzer instead of splitting over trash — so 60 segments is ~22.5 s of
unbroken two-wisp focus. **That is inside one 30 s duration**: a full pair can
now finish a Panzer. It is the deliberate shape of what was asked for; to
restore the old guarantee against the pair as well, that ONE number goes to 120
(past the 80 hits two wisps can ever land) and nothing else moves.

### UI

`AetheriumPerks.lua`'s WISP TEA row: *"Hits may summon a boss-hunting wisp; two
wisps max"*. That row's `description` is what the buy card draws (the in-world
hint string is never displayed for a perk — the cursor-hint kit routes it to
`PromptPerks`, which reads the table, so rewording the hint would have spent
nothing and shown nothing). LOCKSTEP: "two wisps max" is the word-form of
`WISP_TEA_MAX_WISPS`, and that line is the only place a player is ever told the
cap.

**Fifty characters on purpose.** `PromptPerks`' `perkDesc` box is x 620..766 =
**146 px**, LEFT-aligned with no wrap, no auto-scale and no scroll — a long line
runs off the right of the card rather than clipping or shrinking. The old text
was 49 characters and filled it; this says strictly more in one more character.
A first draft ran to 78 and was cut before building. ⚠️ **The PhD FLOPPER row is
82 characters and is very likely overflowing right now** — untouched here
because nobody has judged it on screen. And the pause-panel width gate added to
`tools/lint_tod_lua.js` earlier today does **not** cover this table; it reads
only `tod_upgrade.lua`'s DETAIL rows, so perk-card copy has no gate at all.

### Later the same evening: seek order, −25% damage, 3000

User: *"They should target Elites, Panzers, then zombies. In that order. Also
make their damage 75% since we have two now and price will be 3000 now"*.

**THE SEEK ORDER AND THE DAMAGE TIER ARE NOW DIFFERENT NUMBERS, and this is the
one dangerous edit in the batch.** Hours earlier this file gained a single
`wisp_target_tier()` with a comment reading *"ONE ladder, read twice — one
ranking decides both what the wisp goes for and what it does when it arrives"*.
Renumbering it to put elites on top would have handed the **Panzer the ELITE
damage tier** and made wisps kill him five times faster — a buff, inside a
change asked to be a nerf, with nothing to catch it. So:

- `wisp_target_tier()` keeps its meaning: an **identity** (2 Panzer, 1 elite,
  0 trash). `wisp_hit_damage()` still prices off it, unchanged.
- `wisp_seek_rank( n_id )` is new and owns the **order**: elite 2, Panzer 1,
  trash 0. A pure function of the identity int, so it cannot drift from what
  the same victim will be charged.
- The seek loop reads the identity for the trash gate and the rank for the
  ordering; `n_best_tier` became `n_best_rank`.

**Elites over the Panzer inverts the health order deliberately.** A wisp dents
a Panzer and can barely finish one; the protector/reaver/hound/sprinter that
would actually have reached the player dies in seconds. Sending a pair at what
they can finish beats sending them at the biggest health bar.

**DAMAGE TO 75% MEANS SEGMENTS ×4/3, NOT ×0.75.** Damage here is
`maxhealth / SEGMENTS`, so multiplying the segments by 0.75 would have *raised*
per-hit damage by a third. 3/12/60 → **4/16/80**, verified as exactly 75.0% of
the old per-hit value at all three tiers.

**80 at the Panzer tier is exactly the 80 hits a full pair can land** in the
30 s of both their lives, so two wisps finish a Panzer only at 100% uptime, on
the buzzer — never in practice, since they have to fly to him and he moves. The
v14.20 invariant "wisps alone cannot kill a Panzer" is back, narrowly, and it
matters less now that wisps go for elites first anyway.

New times to kill (a hit every 0.75 s): trash 3.0 s solo / 1.5 s paired, elite
12.0 / 6.0, Panzer 60.0 / 30.0.

**Price 2000 → 3000**, `WISP_TEA_PERK_COST`, with the `AetheriumPerks.lua` card
row in lockstep (both read back and compared, not eyeballed). The in-world hint
takes the price by `&&1` substitution, so it needed no edit and spends no new
triggerstring.

### Two wisps, two sides, two targets

User: *"How about their positioning? Can one be on left side and one on right
side. I believe the one is always on right side currently. This could allow
their area to be different and they can target different enemies most of the
time."*

**The flanking half already shipped earlier in this entry** — the pack's single
hardcoded `(120,-100,0)` became a pair of mirrored slots claimed per wisp, so a
pair does sit on opposite sides rather than stacking into one silhouette. The
user's read of the current build is right: a lone wisp rides the pack's
original spot, and they report that as their right.

**WHICH SLOT IS PHYSICALLY LEFT IS NOT PROVEN AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT
MATTER.** The evidence conflicts: stock `_siegebot.gsc` pins
`AnglesToRight` at `+60` for its RIGHT arm and `-60` for its LEFT, which proves
the *function* points right but says nothing about a `LinkTo` tuple's y; and
`_straferun.gsc:1052` pairs its own `offset_y` with `AnglesToRight`, which reads
the opposite way to the usual Quake basis. The user's in-game observation is the
better evidence and the comment says so. **Nothing downstream depends on the
answer** — the slots are symmetric and the split is not done with a side test —
so if they turn out mirrored, swapping the two vectors fixes it and nothing else
moves.

**THE "DIFFERENT ENEMIES" HALF IS THE ACTUAL CHANGE, and it is NOT a side
test.** Both wisps ran the same picker over the same list with the same
ranking, so they converged on the same body — flanking the player and then
both flying at one zombie. `wisp_target_is_free()` now makes a candidate
another live wisp is already going for lose a tiebreak:

    rank (elite > Panzer > trash)  ->  unclaimed  ->  nearest to this wisp

**Claim sits BELOW rank on purpose**: an elite still outranks an unclaimed
shambler, so "elites first" survives intact. And because it is only a tiebreak,
two wisps still both go for the last elite in the room — which is correct, and
"most of the time" was the ask.

**A wisp's own current target always counts as free**, which is the bug this
would otherwise have: both wisps re-pick every network frame, so on the frame
after they split each would see the other's claim, both would bail, and they
would swap targets forever without landing a hit. Stickiness on your own quarry
is what makes the split settle.

**`wispTargetEnt` is written every tick including the undefined case** — a
stale claim would fence the other wisp off something nobody is going for.

Note what does the geometric work here: the wisps park on opposite sides, so
"nearest to this wisp" already resolves to "the one on my side" most of the
time. The claim rule only decides the ties that leaves — which is why no dot
product against an unproven axis was needed at all.

**UNPLAYED.** Lints green (arity, hints 91/190, assets, Lua).

### The v14.55 music cut is reverted

User: *"I think we lowered music some time back. Is that true? Im looking to
revert that since they can lower music in settings now"*. Yes — **v14.55**,
2026-08-31: *"lower music by like 5% on the map. Include all music, endless
spire, boss, floor music."* All seven `BUS_MUSIC` aliases in
`sound/aliases/tod_ui.csv` came down 5 points and are now back where they were:

| alias | v14.55 | now |
|---|---|---|
| `tod_ambient_music` | 90 | **95** |
| `tod_music_city` | 90 | **95** |
| `tod_music_relay` | 90 | **95** |
| `tod_music_eclipse` | 90 | **95** |
| `tod_music_spire` | 90 | **95** |
| `tod_boss_music` | 95 | **100** |
| `tod_music_finale` | 95 | **100** |

Cross-checked two ways before touching anything: the v14.55 entry names the
before/after values, and `git show HEAD:sound/aliases/tod_ui.csv` (a commit that
predates the cut) carries exactly those numbers. The rewrite sets `VolMin` /
`VolMax` **by column header, not by position**, asserts each row is on
`BUS_MUSIC`, and asserts it touched exactly 7 rows.

**`grp_music` in the VolumeGroup column STAYS.** That is v14.46, not v14.55, and
it is the thing that makes the settings slider work at all — a diff of these
seven rows against the pre-cut commit now shows `grp_music` as the ONLY
difference. Reverting the volume without keeping it would have handed back the
5% and taken the slider away, which is the opposite of the reason for the
revert.

⚠️ **One correction to the premise, worth knowing rather than acting on:** the
slider fix (**v14.46**) landed EARLIER on 2026-08-31 than the cut (**v14.55**) —
the in-game Music slider already worked when the 5% was taken off. So this is a
pure taste reversal, not a fix for something that has since become redundant.
Nothing about the decision changes; the 5% is off.

The two perk-machine jingles `mus_perk_wisptea_jingle` / `_stinger` are NOT
music-band aliases (they sit on `BUS_FX` / `grp_ambience` at 81.5) and were never
part of the −5%; untouched. Alias-only changes need no full build — the linker
rebuilds the sound banks on `-GscOnly`.

### The Warden Trials: own track, 70 seconds, and a 25% easier first rung

User: *"in the trials i believe we play boss music but I want to change it.
It'll still fall under boss volume but its the most recent wav i downloaded.
And the trials will now only last 60 seconds and the tower bar on the right
will reflect it and once over it will go back to track endless spire progress.
Also the trials are starting off way to hard. They should start off about 25%
easier. Then build up from there. I think I said 8% harder each level."*

### The track

`~/Downloads/Chaos Unleashed.wav`, 2026-09-03 22:45 — the newest wav there by
six hours, and already 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, so the bank contract needed no
resample. Suno, per the user; credited. It lands as
`sound_assets/tod/music/tod_music_trial.wav` (79.5 s, LOOPING like every music
alias) behind a new `tod_music_trial` alias, and `trial_begin`'s
`channel_play` names it instead of `tod_boss_music`. At `TOD_TRIAL_SECS` 70 a
trial hears all but the last ~9 s of it.

**"It'll still fall under boss volume" is true by construction, not by
copying numbers.** The alias row is a CLONE of `tod_boss_music`'s with exactly
two columns changed — proved mechanically after writing it: Name and FileSpec
and nothing else, 102 fields to 102. `Bus` `BUS_MUSIC`, `VolumeGroup`
`grp_music` (so the settings slider moves it), `snp_never_duck`, `VolMin` /
`VolMax` 100 all come along.

**And it is level-matched to the track it replaces, which is the half that
alias volume cannot do.** The download measured **−15.9 LUFS** against
`tod_boss_music`'s **−12.2** — 3.7 dB quieter, at the same alias volume, which
would have read as "the music drops out when the trial starts". `volume=3.7dB`
puts it exactly on −12.2 with peak at −1.7 dB (5.4 dB of headroom was
available, so the limiter never engaged). Matching the BOSS track rather than
the −8.0 band tracks is deliberate: the trial track replaces the boss track in
that exact moment at that exact alias volume, so equality there makes the swap
inaudible as a level change. Reaching −8.0 would have wanted +7.9 dB against
5.4 dB of headroom — the squash the music README warns about.

⚠️ **`alimiter` auto-levels by default and overshot the target by a dB** — the
first pass asked for +3.7 and measured +4.7 (−11.2 LUFS). Redone with
`level=disabled` and re-measured. Written into the README, because the recipe
the README already carried has this bug in it.

⚠️ **CREDITS.md carries a placeholder** — the track's source is unknown here and
publishing needs it. Marked "SOURCE UNCONFIRMED, must be filled in before
publish".

### 90 s → 70 s, and the frenzy derived from it

`TOD_TRIAL_SECS` 90 → **70**. `trial_seal_window` waits on the WIN flag rather
than a duration, so the next door's seal follows for free.

**It went to 60 first, then to 70 an hour later** — the user's *"the trials will
now only last 60 seconds"*, then *"make the trial 70 seconds instead"* once the
track's length surfaced: `tod_music_trial` is 79.5 s, so a 60 s trial never
reached the last third of it. **The length is NOT pinned to the wav** and the
comment says so, because the next reader will assume it is: the track LOOPS, so
any length is safe, and this number is free to move for feel alone. The FINALE
is the opposite case — `TOD_FINALE_SONG_SECS` genuinely is its wav's length and
moving it plays the ending over the song's second intro.

**`TOD_TRIAL_FRENZY_SECS` IS NOW DERIVED — `( TOD_TRIAL_SECS / 3.0 )`** — which
is what two length changes in one evening earned it. The frenzy has been the
LAST THIRD of the fight since it was authored (30 of 90); as a literal it
silently reshapes the fight every time the length moves (at 30 of a 60 s trial
it is HALF — a difficulty *increase* inside the change asked to be 25% easier).
~23.3 s at 70. The three recipes that set their own `frenzy_at` already derived
it from `TOD_TRIAL_SECS`, so the whole lane now follows one number.

A nested arithmetic `#define` is proven in this tree, not assumed — checked
before writing it: `_tod_finale.gsc:138` ships
`#define TOD_FINALE_HOLD_SECS ( TOD_FINALE_SONG_SECS - TOD_FINALE_ROAD_SECS )`.

**A stale lockstep note went with it.** The constants block demanded that
`TOD_TRIAL_FRENZY_SECS` and the frenzy print move together because the print
said "THIRTY SECONDS". v16.25 had already replaced that string with the
constant "THE FRENZY"; the note outlived the string it guarded by a week and
would have sent the next reader hunting for a number that is not there.

### The ladder, re-set from the second real run

Two axes, both toned — the same shape v16.21 used, because a hold-out's
difficulty is HP *and* the adds' cadence, and nerfing one would have moved half
the fight:

| knob | was | now | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TOD_TRIAL_HP_MULT` | 1.275 | **0.956** | ×0.75 |
| `TOD_TRIAL_TICK` | 4.6 | **5.75** | ×1.25 (slower = easier) |
| `TOD_TRIAL_FRENZY_TICK` | 2.3 | **2.875** | held at exactly half the tick |
| `TOD_TRIAL_STEP` | 1.07 | **1.08** | "8% harder each level" |

The ladder (`STEP^(tier-1)`) now reads **I ×0.956, II ×1.032, V ×1.301,
X ×1.911** against the old 1.275 / 1.364 / 1.672 / 2.344.

**Trial I lands just BELOW 1.0 and that is the arithmetic, not a slip** — 25%
off 1.275 is 0.956, so a first-trial elite is a hair weaker than a plain spire
elite. The ladder is back over 1.0 by trial II. `TOD_TRIAL_TICK_MIN` (1.5) is
untouched: it is a late-trial floor, not a starting-difficulty knob, and even
trial X's tick (5.75 / 1.911 = 3.0 s) never reaches it — it did not reach it
before either.

### The tower bar — already wired, no change needed

Verified rather than assumed, by reading both ends. `trial_begin` sets
`tod_finale_song_start` / `_end` to a `TOD_TRIAL_SECS` span, `_tod_gauge`'s loop
calls `finale_cell()` unconditionally, and `finale_cell` sizes itself with
`cells_for_mode()` — so in spire mode the trial fills all **50** cells over its
own clock. `trial_win` clears both fields ("the gauge goes back to being an
altimeter") and `finale_cell` returns −1, dropping the bar back to spire
altitude. The only thing the length change does here is shorten the span. The boss
pip and the down cells stay suppressed for the trial, same as the finale — the
party is sealed in one hall, so neither means anything.

**This lane has never been played** (the spire gauge shipped v16.44 UNPLAYED and
the trials have had exactly one real run, at hub 10, before v16.21 reshaped
them). The reading above is from the source, not from a screen.

## 2026-09-03 (v17.7) — PUBLISH BUILD: THE TOWER HAD NO NAVMESH ABOVE ~FLOOR 17 (149 seeds), cod2map's log stops being thrown away

User, mid-session and escalating: *"Major bug where zombies are spawning in and
not moving"* → *"Only if you get close they move"* → *"If i throw a monkey it
disapears instantly and i hear samantha"* → *"seems to happen around floor
18-20. When I teleport back down i cna throw monekys and they target"* → *"as we
keep going up still not working. Maybe we msised everytng above this"*. Then,
after the armed verification run: *"Okay it works."*

**v17.6 SHIPPED THIS BUG TO PLAYERS.** It went up at ~20:10 and the user found
this while playing the published build — which is also why it was found at all
(v17.6 is the build that disarmed god mode, and god MASKS the tell). So v17.7's
player notes are ONE BULLET: everything else in the window went out with v17.6.
⚠️ The ledger disagreed — row #27 sat `pending` because `patch_notes.js
uploaded` was never run, and I initially wrote v17.7's notes as the whole
33-bullet window on the strength of that. **The ledger records what the TOOL was
told, not what Steam holds**; when its `pending` row contradicts the user, the
user is the source of truth. Row #27 is closed as v17.6 (upload time `approx`,
Steam 429'd on two attempts) and v17.7 is row #28.

### The bug: fifty floors of tower riding on two seed points

**THE TOWER CARRIED ZERO NAVMESH SEEDS ABOVE THE BASE ARENA.** Grepping the
emitted `.map` for every class in `radiant/configs/navmesh.json`'s `"seeds"`
list (`node_*`, `mp_*spawn*`, `cp_*spawn*`, `info_player_start`, `actor_*`)
returned exactly **two**, both standing on the base deck at z≈0:
`actor_spawner_zm_factory_zombie` and `info_player_start`. All 22
`node_pathnode`s in the map were the SPIRE's (x≈10240, added v14.19). Every
other entity this generator places is on the *exclusion* list — `script_struct`,
`info_volume`, `script_brushmodel`, `light` — so not one floor of the spiral was
seeded by accident. 19,200 units of climb were vouched for by two points at the
bottom.

**THE MECHANISM IS HAVOK AI REGION PRUNING, NOT A FLOOD.** cod2map64 is Havok
AI (`hkai*`, `NavMesh\hkaiNavMeshPruningUtils.cpp`). It meshes the walkable
world, splits it into CONNECTED REGIONS, then keeps each region only if **its
area clears a threshold OR a seed point sits on it**. The exe's own fallback
string is the proof, and the conjunction is the whole story: *"All regions are
below the area threshold AND too far from a seed point. Keeping the largest
region."* `pruning.minDistanceToSeedPoints` is **14** in
`bin/default_navmesh_settings.json` — that is the tolerance for a seed counting
as sitting ON a region, not a coverage radius, so one seed vouches for its
entire connected component. There is no `minRegionArea` key and **no per-map
`<map>_navmesh_settings.json` exists**, so tuning the thresholds is not an
available lever without inventing one.

**ONE CAUSE, ALL FIVE SYMPTOMS.** An off-mesh zombie has no path and no
`find_flesh`, so it stands still until stock's direct proximity aggro fires. A
Cymbal Monkey needs mesh under it to become a `zombie_poi` and is discarded the
instant it lands without one. The Samantha laugh is this map's own documented
tell for the out-of-playable monitor (`zm_tower_of_doom.gsc:532`, `:845`). It is
a hard CEILING rather than a pocket because the pruning drops whole regions. And
the base is fine because that is where the two seeds are.

**WHY IT HID FOR SO LONG, AND WHY IT SURFACED NOW.** `:845` in that file already
recorded it: **god mode MASKS the out-of-playable instakill**, because that
monitor deals raw `DoDamage` and the Sam laugh is its only remaining tell. God
was armed across most recent test sessions; v17.6 disarmed it for publish, and
the next session up the tower heard the laugh. The ceiling also MOVED with
unrelated floor and stair work, because where the mesh fragments is a function of
the geometry — which is why it read as "we just redid the floors so maybe this
spot was missed".

### The fix

- **`tools/gen_tower_map.js`, the shared `for (const zn of ZONES)` emission
  loop:** one `node_pathnode` per RISER at riser origin **+2 z**. Per-riser and
  not §6f's per-zone on purpose — each lap's two risers sit on the mid and end
  landings, i.e. one at the top of each flight, so no lap can be orphaned by the
  one below it failing to hand the mesh upward. `node_pathnode` 22 → **171**:
  149 tower seeds spanning floor 1 to z=19650 (whole climb + causeway), the 22
  spire seeds untouched. It is on the exclusion list (carves nothing), is
  invisible, and **spawns no runtime gentity**, so it does not touch the
  ~1024-gentity budget the spire is bound by.
- **PROVEN AT COMPILE TIME, THEN IN GAME.** `zm_tower_of_doom_navmesh.hkt`
  **84,171 → 110,468 bytes (+31%)** across the fix, with byte-identical geometry
  (same world brush count, same `lint_tod_geometry` output — 178714 floor
  surfaces both sides). Entities that contribute no surface cannot grow a mesh
  unless previously-PRUNED regions are now KEPT. The armed run then confirmed it
  where it counts: zombies target above floor 17, monkeys survive the throw, no
  laugh.

### The generalisation, because the old rule was too narrow

`docs/44` and the §6f comment both said *a NEW DETACHED REGION needs its own
seed*. **That is not the rule.** The spire was detached; the tower is one
continuous staircase from the base and lost its mesh anyway. The real rule is
that **any region can be pruned**, and connectivity to a seeded region does not
save it once the mesh fragments. Seed every walkable region, not just the
obviously-islanded ones.

### cod2map's transcript was being captured and then deleted

`build_map.ps1`'s `Invoke-BuildExe` redirects cod2map's stdout/stderr to two
temporary files, reads them into `$r.Out`/`$r.Err`, and **deletes both in its
`finally` block**; the call site printed them only on a non-zero exit. So on a
SUCCESSFUL build every Havok warning was discarded and nothing reached disk —
which is why this failure left no log to read and the diagnosis had to be
rebuilt from the `.map` and the Havok config. **A build that only prints on
FAILURE cannot explain a build that SUCCEEDS and ships broken.**

- The transcript now goes to `tools/cod2map_last.log` on every build (`*.log` is
  already gitignored), and any line matching the navmesh set is surfaced as a
  `Warn`: `Keeping the largest region` / `below the area threshold` / `too far
  from a seed` / **`Could not drop node at (x,y,z)`** / `too many edges or
  faces` / `ran out of memory` / `No regions found` / `Empty nav mesh` /
  `Removed degenerate navmesh face` / `NavVolume generation is skipped`.
- **`Could not drop node` is the one that matters after any seed change:** it is
  cod2map failing to anchor a seed onto walkable mesh AND NAMING THE COORDINATE.
  All 149 seeds rest on the assumption that every riser stands on walkable
  landing floor — true by construction today, and exactly the kind of assumption
  this outage was made of. It now self-reports. Full builds only: `-GscOnly`
  never runs cod2map, so an empty log there means nothing ran, not nothing wrong.

### Two things checked and CLEARED, recorded so nobody re-opens them

- **`HKAI_MAX_NUM_FACES` is not in play.** It sits beside `HKAI_MAX_NUM_SECTIONS`
  and `_EDGES` as a reflection enum name (Havok's packed-key bit budget, in the
  millions). A real overflow is LOUD — *"Nav mesh generation created a mesh with
  too many edges or faces..."* — never silent truncation. And a mesh at its cap
  cannot grow 31% from entities that add no geometry.
- **`zm_tower_of_doom_navvolume.hkt` at 0 bytes is CORRECT**, not a failing step,
  despite `-navvolume` being passed every full build. cod2map says why: *"NavVolume
  generation is skipped ... there is no nav_volume brush in the level."* The
  tower has zero `nav_volume` brushes (map 1 has one, hence its 47 KB). Nav
  volumes are for FLYING AI; every enemy here is a ground actor on the navmesh.

### Publish hygiene

- **All four disarms confirmed, not two:** `level.tod_dev` and `level.tod_god`
  back to `false` with their ARMED block deleted in the same edit (the rule in
  that function); `TOD_MOCK_PARTY` and `TOD_HP_DEBUG` verified already `false`.
- The `.map` regeneration is entity-only — no brush moved — so the geometry lint
  is green against baseline with identical surface counts, and the LED bake had
  nothing new to light.
- Generator change → **FULL build**, `-Publish` (implies `-CleanPak`).
