## 2026-09-03 (v17.5) — PAUSE MENU AUDIT: rows that overlapped, wording a new player can read, and a gate so it stops recurring

User, with a screenshot of the panel: *"Looks how horrible it is. We need to
remember that this has to be short and concise. This has happened multiple times
where our description is super long and overlaps"*, then *"can we do an audit on
making things more clear and removing unecessary words"* and *"Players who are
new should be able to read it and exactly know whats going on ... what each
upgrade does"*.

### The overlap, and why counting characters missed it

**THE PANEL DOES NOT WRAP, IT OVERLAPS.** A long line paints on top of the row
below — visible on TRAILBLAZER and RIOT SHIELD in the screenshot. Budget,
measured off the real rows (`COL_W` 369, eff at scale 0.90, act at 0.79): about
**40 characters for eff, 46 for act**.

**THE TRAP THAT MADE IT RECUR FOUR TIMES:** a row whose `eff` is literally
`"{V}"` hides its true length inside the `val` FUNCTION. Reading the table finds
nothing — TRAILBLAZER measured **4** characters in the table and rendered **76**
on screen. Every new domain wrote its row without ever seeing the panel full.

- Shortened: 46 TRAILBLAZER (the eff BUILDER, 76 -> 33), 45 RIOT SHIELD (act 91
  -> 38), 8 SCAVENGER (56 -> 29, the `(56% of a round each)` second reading
  dropped), 24 CLASS TIER (both branches), 43 ATHLETE, 41 DISTRACTION,
  26 OVERDRIVE, 44 GUNSLINGER, 47 DEADSHOT.
- **`tools/lint_tod_lua.js` NOW GATES IT** on every build, including `-GscOnly`.
  It measures the literals AND the strings built inside `val`, from the RETURN
  expressions only with comments stripped. The first cut summed every literal in
  the row and reported DETAIL[8] at 213 chars and DETAIL[47] at 5594 — it was
  counting comment prose and, for the last row, everything to end of file. **A
  lint that cries wolf gets switched off**, so it is bounded to what reaches the
  screen and the per-value estimate was tuned from 4 chars to 3 after it flagged
  ATHLETE at 41 against a real 35.

### The wording audit

- **"ALWAYS ON" IS GONE FROM 16 OF 38 ROWS.** Five said only that; eleven used
  it as a prefix. When almost everything is always on, saying so teaches nothing
  and crowds out the qualifier that matters — `always on, MAC-10 only` is now
  `MAC-10 only`. Pure passives draw NO sub-line at all. The convention comment
  above the table says so, so the next domain does not re-add it.
- **CLEAVE WAS NOT WORDY, IT WAS WRONG.** `+{V}% extra targets per swing` on a
  domain that grants *"+33% / Lv chance to hit an extra zombie (max +1)"* — at
  Lv3 it read **+100% extra targets**, i.e. double the targets, when the truth is
  a 100% chance of ONE more. Now `{V}% chance to hit 1 extra zombie`. Found by
  reading the `add_domain` line rather than trusting the row.
- Jargon out, plain words in: `weapon kick, hip and ads` -> `recoil`;
  `no sprint-out` -> `shoot without breaking sprint`; `shots free` ->
  `of shots free`; `regen` -> `health regen`; `blade swing time` -> `time between
  swings`; `shoots through {V} cover` -> `bullets pierce {V} cover`.
- **A SUB-LINE THAT RESTATES THE MAIN LINE IS DELETED**, not shortened: 13 LEECH
  read `heal +N hp per blade kill` over `blade kills`, and 36 BACK ARMOR read
  `-N% damage taken from behind` over `hits from behind`.
- Trigger lines tightened where the detail was for us, not the player:
  `on a melee hit, 60u, caps at +1` -> `melee hits, within 60 units`;
  `permanent; controller aim assist` -> `controller only`;
  `on each kill, banked, paid out in 10s` -> `banked, paid out every 10s`.

- Lua only. `lint_tod_lua.js` clean (42 files, width gate included);
  `lint_tod_arity.js` clean (73 files).
- ⚠️ **BUILD DEFERRED:** BlackOps3 was running at edit time and the gate refuses
  while it is up. One `-GscOnly` once the game is closed.
- Both dev flags remain ARMED — not publishable.

## 2026-09-03 (v17.4) — Skirmisher sidearms: the −10% is reversed to +10%, except the SPAS-12 at −5%

User, having played v16.99: *"I think we need to revert the skirmisher
secondary nerf and instead buff by 10%. Except the spaz. That'll actually be 5%
nerf instead."*

- **MEASURED FROM THE ORIGINAL, NOT FROM THE NERF.** v16.99 took
  `CLASS_SEC_CAP_MULT.skirmisher` to 1.19025 (1.3225 × 0.90). "Revert and
  instead buff" means the new target is the PRE-NERF 1.3225 × 1.10 = **1.45475**,
  not the nerfed value × 1.10 — getting that wrong would have landed the class
  1% under where it started instead of 10% over.
- **TWO TARGETS, ONE SHARED KNOB.** The cap is per-CLASS, so it cannot give the
  SPAS-12 a different answer from the other two. `dmgMult` is applied AFTER the
  cap (the lane SLASHER_SEC_BUFF documents), so the SPAS carries a correction
  written as the RATIO between the two targets — `SKIRM_SPAS_NET /
  SKIRM_SEC_BUFF`, 0.95/1.10 — never a second absolute number. Written as the
  division on purpose: hard-coding 0.8636 would decouple it the moment either
  target moves, which is the same failure the CLASS_SEC_CAP_MULT pin exists to
  prevent one level up.
- **THE NERF DID REACH A BUILD** — the 18:48 fastfile carries it, so the values
  a player holds right now are the v16.99 ones. This is a real change to them,
  not an unwind of something nobody saw.
  Live → pending (base/PaP): Bulldog **32 → 39/49**, SG12 **49 → 60/75**,
  SPAS-12 **116 → 123/154**. Against the PRE-NERF baseline that is **+8.3% /
  +9.1% / −3.9%** where the targets were +10 / +10 / −5.
- **WHY IT MISSES BY ABOUT A POINT, stated rather than hidden:** the cap chain
  rounds TWICE — `Math.round` on the reference damage at line 1655, then again
  on the derived cap at 1798 — and at a base damage of 36 a single integer point
  is 2.8%. That is the granularity of the pipeline, not a tuning error, and
  chasing the last percent would mean over-fitting the constants to a rounding
  artefact. The relationship in the source is exact; the emitted integers are
  what they are.
- Ledger 220 of 224, unchanged — no new registrations, the same forms re-emitted.
- **ALSO: the GUNSLINGER comment block was still the pre-v16.99 design** and
  argued AGAINST the additive form that shipped — it reasoned that an additive
  term is "worth a third" against a 2.25x hit, which is arithmetically correct
  and is exactly the effect the user asked to remove. Left alone it would have
  talked the next reader into reverting the change. Rewritten to state the
  additive contract, name BOTH callers that must carry the term
  (upgrade_damage_cb and _tod_bosses::rp_damage_feed), and record why the small
  number is deliberate. Comment-only; no behaviour change.
- **ARMORY** refreshed at the same URL: the three sidearm rows and the boss
  table's PaP SPAS-12 figure (11,328 → 12,031 DPS).
- ⚠️ **NOT BUILT YET** — BlackOps3 was running and the build gate refuses while
  it is up (locked sound banks). Generator change, so this owes a **FULL build**
  when the game is closed. The tree carries the new GDT already.

## 2026-09-03 (v17.3) — No operator face before the draft, and the co-op HUD is testable solo again

Two user asks in one pass. *"Before you select a class there is a placeholder
image. Can we remove that? Its dempsey and then switch after I select, so it

- **`CoD.GetClassPortrait()` is the new one authority**: it returns the icon
  only when it resolves to an `i_tod_class_medallion_*`, and nil otherwise.
  Both call sites draw `blacktransparent` on nil, so the slot is simply EMPTY
  until the draft lands. **Image, not alpha** — `AetheriumPartyPlayers`'
  `playerScoreShown` handler owns that element's alpha and would have
  overwritten an alpha set here on the next slot update.
- What it costs, stated rather than discovered later: the operator faces stop
  being the "this mapping is broken" canary the fallback comment describes.
  Acceptable *now* and not before — all four char ids were OBSERVED and closed
  on 2026-09-03 (v16.73), so the table is complete. A future break shows as an
  ABSENT portrait instead of a wrong face, which is still visible and no longer
  costs every player a wrong face during every draft.
- **4-PLAYER HUD MOCK, ported from map 1** (`_zm_aetherium_hud.gsc::mock_party_feed`
  + `TOD_MOCK_PARTY` in `AetheriumHud.lua`). Two halves: the Lua puts fake
  name/score/medallion rows in the three party slots, the GSC feeds their
  `player_health_N` world clientfields so one bar visibly sweeps. Mock char ids
  are SKIRMISHER / ASSAULT / SLASHER, so drafting HEAVY yourself puts all four
  medallions on screen at once.
- **NO CHANGE-GUARD NEEDED, unlike map 1's copy.** Map 1's version wrote 12
  world clientfields a second forever and grew a hand-rolled `sent[]` table
  after becoming the prime suspect in a corrupted-configstring CTD. This map's
  `set_world_clientfield()` already early-outs on an unchanged value, so slots
  1 and 2 write once and only slot 3's sweep ticks. The GSC half is gated
  INSIDE the function after `initial_blackscreen_passed` — `__main__` runs
  during system init with no ordering guarantee that `tod_resolve_dev_flags()`
  has assigned `level.tod_dev` yet — and only ever writes UNOCCUPIED slots, so
  it is harmless in co-op even armed.
- **THE LUA HALF IS NOT SO POLITE, AND IT CANNOT BE DEV-GATED** (Lua has no
  `level.tod_dev`): while armed it MASKS REAL TEAMMATES. Map 1 shipped the
  identical flag with a comment saying to "manage it manually", which is
  exactly how a flag ships armed. **So it is a BUILD GATE here instead** —
  `build_map.ps1` greps the assignment, WARNs on any build and FAILs
  `-Publish`, the same shape as `level.tod_dev`. Self-tested by arming the flag
  and confirming the gate fires, then disarming.
- ⚠️ **SHIPPED ARMED ON PURPOSE** so the preview is visible without a round
  trip (`level.tod_dev` was already `true` in this tree). **`TOD_MOCK_PARTY`
  must go back to `false` before any co-op test or publish** — the gate will
  stop a publish, but it will not stop a co-op session showing three ghosts.
- `-GscOnly` BUILD OK. `lint_tod_arity` OK across 73 files; `lint_tod_lua`
  42/0; `lint_tod_assets` flat against baseline. UNPLAYED.

## 2026-09-03 (v17.2) — DMG REDUCTION gets a cap PER CLASS: 3 / 5 / 7 / 10

User, on the armory finding that three of the four classes had identical
defence: *"Yes lets do 3, 5, 7, 10 as the max / Skirm, slash, assault, heavy"*.

- **THE PROBLEM IT FIXES.** DMG REDUCTION is the only mitigation the
  skirmisher, assault and slasher have at all — BACK ARMOR went heavy-only in
  v14.11 and SPRINT ARMOR was retired in v14.59b — so capping it at 5 for
  everyone left those three on **exactly identical effective HP**. The fastest,
  highest-damage class in the map was no squishier than the slowest, which
  removes the counterweight the speed and damage were supposed to be paid for.
  **The cap is now the trade:**

  | Class | Cap | Damage taken | e-HP |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Skirmisher | 3 | 85% | 176.5 |
  | Slasher | 5 | 80% | 187.5 |
  | Assault | 7 | 76% | 197.4 |
  | Heavy | 10 | 70% | 214.3 (260.0 with VITALITY 5) |

- **NO LADDER WORK WAS NEEDED** — `dr_pct_for_level` already ran past level 5 on
  `TOD_UPG_DR_LN`, a tail whose own comment reads *"every level past 5, if the
  cap ever rises"*. It diminishes 6/5/4/3 then pays a flat +2 per level, so the
  new rungs are deliberately the cheapest: the heavy spends five more cards to
  buy roughly what its first three bought.
- **IT DID NEED A NEW MECHANISM.** The existing `bonus_class`/`bonus_max` lane
  maps ONE alternate value onto a SET of classes — it can say "6 for the
  assault" but never "3, 5, 7, 10". New `set_class_max( key, pairs )` takes a
  FLAT list and builds the keyed map itself, because GSC's `array()` builds a
  NUMERIC-INDEXED array: `array( "heavy", 10 )` is `[0]="heavy"`, `[1]=10`, and
  a lookup by class name on it returns undefined. Putting the map construction
  inside the function is what makes that unreachable at the call site.
  `domain_max` checks the table FIRST, and `sync_max` rides it, so the pause row
  shows each player their own cap for free.
- **LUA LOCKSTEP:** `drPct` clamped at level 5 (`T[math.min(l,5)]`) and now
  mirrors the GSC tail exactly. Left alone it would have frozen the pause
  readout at −20% for the two classes that go past it while the game applied
  more — a silent lie in the one place a player reads the number. `DOMAIN[2]`
  max 5 → 10 (the ceiling; per-class values arrive per-player over
  `tod_upg_sync`), and the desc drops its baked ladder because the ladder now
  ends somewhere different for every class.
- ⚠️ **CARD ART OWES A RE-BAKE, and it is specified.** The three DMG REDUCTION
  cards bake a **five-socket pip row**. The deck rule is pips = max when
  max ≤ 6, else a flat 3 — which is what DAMAGE and BOUNTY (both max 10)
  already ship, verified by opening both PNGs. One card is dealt to all four
  classes and they no longer share a cap, so no socket count can encode it;
  three is correct precisely because it stops trying. The value line reads
  `TAKE LESS DAMAGE` with no figure and is untouched, so this is a pip-row edit
  only. Prompt: **docs/95**, same filenames so no wiring changes.
- **ARMORY REFRESHED** at the same URL: the page's own `dmax` now mirrors
  `domain_max`'s precedence (classMax first), the DR row carries the four caps
  and the full ten-rung ladder, and the To Max figures moved with it —
  skirmisher 43 → 42 picks, heavy 47 → 50.
- `-GscOnly` (scripts + Lua). Lints green: arity, Lua, assets, hints. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-03 (v17.1) — LATE-ROUND LUCK: zombie kills pay +4% a round past 15

User: *"specifically on zombie kills we need a slight buff later rounds ... Like
4% extra after round 15"*, with a worked table — r16 104%, r17 108%, r18 112% —
and *"Would that be crazy?"*. It would not; their own table is the safe reading.

**FIRST, THE ANSWER TO "DID WE ALREADY DO THIS": NO — WE DID THE OPPOSITE.**
`TOD_LUCK_KILL_BUDGET` was cut 40 -> 18 on 2026-08-20 (*"way too easy, basically
maxed every time"*) and nothing has raised it since. That cut applies at every
round, so it was never a late-game measure in either direction.

**WHY THE EXISTING NORMALIZATION WAS NOT ENOUGH.** `per_round_rate()` divides
the budget by the round's zombie count, which is exactly right IF YOU CLEAR THE
ROUND — a full clear always pays the budget whatever the round number. Late game
you cannot clear: stock's count grows with the SQUARE of the round past 10
(`get_zombie_count_for_round`, `_zm.gsc:3853`) and the endless twist starts the
next round on the last SPAWN, not the last kill, so the horde outruns you and you
take a shrinking SHARE of a per-kill value that is itself shrinking
quadratically. **Two other late losses compound it and are worth naming:** door
income (`TOD_LUCK_DOOR` 10) stops ENTIRELY once the tower is bought — a source
that simply ends — and `TOD_LUCK_DOWN` 25 costs more than a whole round's fair
share of 18, so one down late outweighs a clean round.

- `TOD_LUCK_LATE_FROM` 15 / `TOD_LUCK_LATE_PER_RND` 0.04, applied in
  `per_round_rate()` after the normalization: rounds above 15 multiply the base
  rate by `1 + 0.04 * ( round - 15 )`. Verified against the user's table:
  r16 104%, r17 108%, r18 112%.
- **LINEAR, NOT COMPOUNDING — and writing down which one it is matters more than
  the number.** They are near-identical for a few rounds and diverge violently
  by spire depth:

  | round | linear | compounding |
  |---|---|---|
  | 20 | 1.20 | 1.22 |
  | 30 | 1.60 | 1.80 |
  | 50 | 2.40 | 3.95 |
  | 100 | 4.40 | **27.6** |

  The user's table is linear, so linear is what shipped. "4% a round" said aloud
  is ambiguous and would have been a 6x error at floor 100 of the spire.
- **WHERE IT SATURATES**, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug: a
  fair-share full clear pays `18 x mult`, reaching the 100 bar cap around round
  130 — deep spire territory. Deliberately NOT capped; an unrequested ceiling is
  the kind of silent divergence this repo keeps paying for, and the bar cap
  already bounds the outcome.
- **THE SPIRE STACKS CLEANLY.** Its halved round budget already doubles per-kill
  luck through the same hook and a full clear still pays the fair-share figure;
  this multiplier scales that rather than bypassing it.
- `-GscOnly`, one file. `lint_tod_arity.js` clean (73 files). Built 18:20:22,
  freshness verified. **UNPLAYED.**
- Both dev flags remain ARMED (v16.87) — not publishable.

## 2026-09-03 (v17.0) — The player HUD goes MINIMAL: the shell is gone, and a layout that was written twice stops drifting

User, after playing v16.98: *"Okay I like what we have actually. But i do want
to make it minimal and remove that whole shell part — just the icon, no square,
name, money, health, and maybe something for shield health. ALso we may have
hardcoded 150 in the asset which would be a bug."* Full record: `docs/90`.

- **THE 150 IS NOT IN THE ASSET — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED.** Scanned the plate PNG
  over the three zones live text lands in: max luminance **11.5** and ZERO
  pixels brighter than 90 in all three. Nothing is baked. The `150` the user
  saw is real but it is in the Lua as `self.maxHealth or 150`, a fallback, and
  `_tod_gauge.gsc` pushes the true `p.maxhealth` on the first tick after spawn
  (`p.tod_gauge_mh` starts undefined, so the "change-only" feed always fires
  once). It is on screen for a frame. **It is still a second source of truth
  that nothing checks** — it happens to equal `TOD_UPG_BASE_HP` today, and
  would silently go stale if base HP were ever retuned. Pinned with a comment
  naming the constant.
- **THE SHELL IS GONE.** `i_tod_hud_player_plate` — one build old — is retired
  from the `.zone`; its file and GDT block stay, so re-zoning one line brings

  square WAS the plate.** What is left is six free-floating readouts in a

  to track the constructor by hand. They did not: its "original" HP position

## 2026-09-03 (v16.99) — GUNSLINGER goes ADDITIVE; skirmisher primaries −5%, secondaries −10%

User, after reading the armory's new boss table: *"Yes make gunslinger
additive."* and *"Also nerf skirmisher primaries by 5% and secondaries by 10%.
ALl of them"*.

- **WHY GUNSLINGER WAS THE MAP'S LARGEST OUTLIER.** It returned
  `TOD_SLASHER_SEC_BOSS_MULT × (1 + 0.30·Lv)` and that whole product multiplied
  the FINAL damage — *after* DAMAGE, the head crit and everything else had been
  summed. So a maxed level was a flat **×5.625 diluted by nothing**, scaling
  every other term along with it. Measured against the shipped guns that put a
  maxed slasher's sidearm at **220,725 boss DPS** versus the ASSAULT's 82,100 —
  and the assault is the class whose entire identity is boss damage. GIANT
  SLAYER, by contrast, adds +0.60 into a sum that already holds DAMAGE's +1.00,
  so it moves the assault ×2.50 → ×3.10, a 24% gain. **An additive boss bonus
  and a multiplicative one are not the same kind of object.**
- **THE FIX:** `slasher_sidearm_boss_mult()` now returns the **2.25 class
  baseline only**, and a new `gunslinger_bonus()` returns the per-level term as
  an ADDITIVE `+0.30·Lv` that joins the same sum GIANT SLAYER lives in. Both
  share one gate helper (`slasher_sidearm_vs_boss`) so the two halves can never
  disagree about when they apply. Wired in BOTH damage lanes — the actor chain
  and `_tod_bosses::rp_damage_feed` — because that fallback has a documented
  history of drifting from the main one, and into the silent-return guard so a
  player whose only active term is GUNSLINGER still returns a real number.
  **Ceiling 220,725 → 154,508, a 30% cut.** Same rate, same gates, same max, so
  **no card, ladder or pause row changes.**
- **THE BASELINE STAYS MULTIPLICATIVE ON PURPOSE.** ×2.25 is the structural
  compensation for the blade's ×0.33 boss tax, not something a card buys. It
  alone keeps the slasher sidearm ~1.9× the assault, so the class is still first
  on bosses. If that reads wrong in play, `TOD_SLASHER_SEC_BOSS_MULT` is the
  next lever — not the GUNSLINGER rate, which is now in the same units as every
  other damage domain.
- **SKIRMISHER, TWO SEPARATE KNOBS, and that is the point.**
  `CLASS_DAMAGE_MULT.skirmisher` 1.071225 → **1.01766375** (−5%, its THIRD cut:
  two −10% passes on 2026-08-30 took it from 1.3225) and
  `CLASS_SEC_CAP_MULT.skirmisher` 1.3225 → **1.19025** (−10%). v14.32 pinned the
  secondary ceiling ABSOLUTE precisely so primary cuts stop dragging the
  shotguns with them — so "nerf both" is always two edits, and doing only the
  first would have moved nothing on the sidearms. Shipped: MAC-10 150 → 142,
  MP5 304 → 288, MP7 434 → 411; Bulldog 36 → 32, SG12 55 → 49, SPAS-12
  128 → 116. All three sidearms sit exactly ON the cap, so the −10% lands in
  full. Ledger 220 of 224 — unchanged, no new registrations.
- **ARMORY REFRESHED** at the same URL: new gun and sidearm numbers, the boss
  table recomputed, and **two page errors fixed while checking** — the sidearm
  DPS column divided damage by fire time and ignored `shotCount`, under-stating
  every pellet shotgun eightfold; and the defence table still quoted the
  pre-v16 flat DR (×0.75 / 200 e-HP) when the shipped ladder caps at −20%, so
  the real figures are ×0.80 and **187.5 e-HP** (heavy 227.6 front). The class
  tables now sort by BAND, and DEADSHOT counts as 3 levels in the To Max
  accounting because its rarity lock means it can only ever arrive as an
  ULTIMATE.
- **FULL build** (generator change → new GDT → new weapon assets). **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-03 (v16.98) — The player-panel art lands: four assets in-house, uncompressed, and the essence glyph unified across all 9 sites

The docs/89 drop came back 15 minutes after the pack went out. Installed,
verified, FULL build. UNPLAYED.

- **THE ZIP HELD TWO COPIES OF THE SET AND THEY WERE PIXEL-IDENTICAL.** Loose
  at the top level, nested inside `tod_player_hud.zip` with the generator's own
  `build_player_hud.py`; every md5 differed and the loose set was MISSING the
  health fill. Decoded both and diffed byte-for-byte after un-filtering: all
  three shared files identical, so the md5 gap was PNG encoding alone (the
  nested set saved with `optimize=True`). Took the nested set because it is the
  complete four. **A visual A/B said the loose plate was "punchier" and that was
  my rendering artifact, not the art** — the comparison drew the two at
  different sizes. The pixel diff is the answer; a side-by-side render is not.
- **ACCEPTANCE CHECKED ON PIXELS, NOT BY EYE** (`verify.js`, a zlib PNG decoder
  since there is no Python here): frame = 14 dividers → 15 cells with cell
  interiors at alpha 0 and cells even at 55–56 px; fill = every column
  identical, alpha 255 everywhere, max saturation 16/255; plate = bay interior
  exactly 227×227 at (89,151), readout region mean luminance 14.9, tail alpha 0
  on the last column; icon = 256×256 RGBA, 41.3% ink. The fill's
  column-uniformity is the one that would have shipped a bug quietly — it is
  wipe-cut at an arbitrary x every frame.
- **PROVEN UNCOMPRESSED, not merely flagged.** The `.iwi` header's byte-8
  uncompressed size is exact arithmetic: 262,240 / 396,384 / 325,216 /
  3,145,824 = `W×H×4 + 96` for all four. DXT5 would have been a quarter of
  each. Same measurement that convicted the kit's images in v16.97, run in the
  other direction.

  panel — the scoreboard, the teammate rows and six prompt cards drew the same

  models only `i_tod_*` literals, so it guards the four ADDITIONS and is blind
  to `i_mtl_*` names in a `.zpkg`. Verified four other ways instead: no literal
  in `ui/` or `scripts/`; no concatenation builds those names; every
  variable-fed `RegisterImage` reads from a mapping table under `ui/` that the

## 2026-09-03 (v16.97) — The bottom-left player panel: the portrait was an ellipse, and the "low detail" is not resolution

User: *"Our atherium player HUD on bottom left is pretty bad in terms of
detail. Looks low detail the icons and kinda squished. ... get maybe 4k images
for those icons ... Maybe its the HUD fault IDK."* It is the HUD's fault. Full
measurement, the four causes and the art brief: `docs/89`.

- **NOTHING IN THAT PANEL IS STARVED OF PIXELS, so 4K art would have changed
  nothing.** Every element already carries 2–10× the pixels it is ever shown
  at: the plate uses 54% of its source width at 1080p, the portrait 30%, the
  health frame 11%, the points glyph **9%**. Asking for bigger source art was
  the natural read and it would have produced a set of files the game throws
  away. Drawn rects out of the Lua, source sizes out of the PNG headers,
  physical pixels = canvas × 1.5.
- **SQUISH #1, FIXED: the portrait box was 51 wide × 59 tall.** LUI stretches
  an image to fill its box, so the 256×256 `i_tod_class_medallion_*` discs were
  pulled 13.6% vertically — a circle drawn as a visible ellipse, bottom-left,
  where the eye goes. **This is the same bug v16.21 fixed for the TEAMMATE rows
  the day before** (`AetheriumPartyPlayers.lua`: *"Any image put here must be
  SQUARE"*); the local player's own panel was missed in that pass. Now 51×51,
  re-centred 629..680. Width is pinned by the plate's painted bay and the name
  text at x=98, so the height comes down — same reasoning as the party fix.
- **SQUISH #2, NEEDS ART: the health frame is a ~48-segment ladder shown 194 px
  wide.** Under 4 physical pixels per segment including its gap, so it resolves
  to a grey smear; it is *also* squeezed 17% narrower than its source aspect,
  packing the segments tighter still. **More source resolution makes this
  worse** — the defect is segment COUNT against on-screen width.
- **LOW DETAIL: every Aetherium kit image is DXT5, ours are not.** Proven from
  the converted `.iwi` headers rather than inferred — the essence glyph
  decompresses to 65,632 B for 256×256 (DXT5 + 96 B header), the plate to
  307,296 B for 960×320, while `i_tod_class_medallion_assault` decompresses to
  262,240 = 256×256 RGBA8. `bo7_aetherium_hud.gdt` says `compressed` on all of
  them; all **505** entries in `tod_ui_images.gdt` say `uncompressed`. 4×4 block
  quantisation is worst on exactly what this kit is made of: smooth blue
  gradients, thin strokes, soft alpha.
- **That GDT is NOT ours to edit** — it lives in the mod-tools root under
  `model_export/_OwensAssets/`, is not in this repo, and is shared with map 1
  (its `.acc-purple-orig` backups sit beside it). So the four assets get
  re-authored as `i_tod_hud_*` in our own GDT instead, which fixes the
  compression, the segment count and the beveled-3D-at-24px problem in one
  move, version-controlled.
- **Points icon box squared** too: 16×15 → 16×16, re-centred 661..677. A 6.7%
  squeeze, small next to the portrait's 13.6%, but the same defect and free.
- **Art pack built**: `.\tools\make_art_pack.ps1 docs\89_player_hud_art_prompt.md`
  → `~/Downloads/tod_player_hud_art_pack.zip`. Four deliverables at
  256×256 / 1032×96 / 1016×80 / 1536×512 — *smaller* than 4K on purpose, with
  the reason stated in the brief so the generator does not "helpfully" upscale.
  Carries `docs/89_hud_ref/current_panel_onscreen.png`: the panel at its true
  1080p size next to a magnification, which is the brief in one picture.
- **Two follow-ons parked in docs/89, not done:** the party-member plate (so
  co-op still reads as one HUD), and the +15% `TodScaleHud` this widget was
  skipped by in v15 — at 1.15 its overlap with party row 1 goes from 16 px to

## 2026-09-03 (v16.96) — The trail's fire sound stops cutting out after two seconds (one bed per player, not one per patch)

User: *"The sound seems off and not continuous. Stops after like 2 seconds. Is
that intentional?"* Not intentional. Two compounding defects in how v16.79
wired it, both mine.

- **THE TWO SECONDS WAS LITERAL AND MEASURABLE.** The loop was a
  `PlayLoopSound` on the fire patch's host entity, and the reaper DELETES that
  host at its node's expiry — deleting an entity takes its voices with it
  (memory `loop-sound-stop-by-handle`). `trail_life_ms` is `1500 + 500*lvl`, so
  a Lv1 node and its sound died at **exactly 2000 ms**. The number in the report
  is the constant.
- **AND IT NEVER SUMMED INTO A BED EVEN WHILE SPRINTING.** Every new node
  restarted the same 4 s file FROM ITS START, roughly five times a second at
  sprint speed (spacing is one patch width, 56 u at Lv1), against an alias
  capped at 6 voices stealing the oldest. That is a phasey pile of restarts, not
  continuous fire — the "seems off" half of the report.
- **FIX: ONE VOICE PER PLAYER**, on for exactly as long as that player has live
  trail. `trail_sound_reconcile()` runs in `trail_loop` ABOVE every
  early-continue, so the bed follows the nodes down in the states that skip the
  rest of the loop (no domain, wrong class, downed, dead, world paused for a
  card). Same shape as FULL STEAM's wind, which the user named as the model:
  `PlayLoopSound` on the player, `StopLoopSound( fade )` — the SERVER signature
  takes a fade time, not a handle. LATCHED so the play call happens once per
  burst: a second `PlayLoopSound` of one alias on one entity starts a second
  generation that is no longer addressable by alias and rings forever.
- **The ignite one-shot stays on the patch host**, where it belongs — it fires
  at the world position the fire actually started.
- **THE WAV IS NOW A REAL SEAMLESS LOOP.** It never mattered before, because a
  host only ever played the first 2-4 s and never reached the end. As one
  sustained voice it loops every 4 s, so the 0.08 s fade-in I had put on the
  head would have dipped on every pass. Rebuilt by blending the body's own
  natural continuation over its head: `[3.5,7.5)` fading in, mixed with
  `[7.5,7.85)` fading out. Measured seam: **−15.7 dB into −15.6 dB**, a tenth of
  a decibel apart, so the wrap is inaudible. Alias volume 74 → 82, because one
  voice no longer has four overlapping copies summing with it.
- **AND THE TIER RAMP IS PUT BACK ON PURPOSE.** Collapsing to one voice would
  have made every level sound identical, because the old per-patch loop scaled
  with level only BY ACCIDENT — more live nodes meant more overlapping copies,
  and v16.92's spacing change had just made that roughly twice as bad at Lv1
  (about 5.7 → 10.7 live nodes; figures from the session that made the change).
  Losing it silently would have contradicted the tier-progression ask this same
  round is serving. So the ramp is re-created deliberately: `tod_trail_loop_sm`
  at vol 68 below Lv3 and `tod_trail_loop` at 82 from Lv3 — two alias rows over
  the SAME wav, split at the same boundary as the small/large flame. One knob,
  two rows, no second asset. The alias is chosen when the bed starts and held
  for that burst.
- `-GscOnly` (one script, one wav, two alias rows). Lints green. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-03 (v16.94) — TRAILBLAZER becomes attrition: damage gutted, a slow added, 30 a kill, numbers, a size ladder and the real fire sound

User: *"the burn should do pretty little damage that increase but it should also
slow down zombies and increase every level. Not much. I have an issue im
thinking that players can just spam this. We need the damage low enough where
players wouldnt dare wasting time getting kills like this. Also should only
reward 30 per kill. I also dont see damage numbers for these."* Then: *"fx needs
to be smaller on smaller tiers. You should be encouraged to go to higher tiers
visually and impact wise."* Then a supplied sound.

- **DAMAGE GUTTED, and this is the anti-farm lever.** `trail_pct` was
  12/16/20/24/28 % of the round's zombie health PER SECOND — a full-health trash
  zombie died in about four seconds of contact, inside the 2-4 s a patch lives,
  so circling a train really was a way to farm and the fire did the gun's job.
  Now **2/3/4/5/6 %/s**: at the Lv5 cap that is ~17 seconds of continuous
  contact per trash kill. The trail can now only finish something already hurt,
  or wear a train down over many passes.
- **THE SLOW replaces that damage as the reason to own it** — 5/8/11/14/17 %
  slower by level, deliberately modest. It rides
  `tod_zombie_speed::slow()`, the same public lane SUPPRESSING FIRE uses, which
  buys three behaviours free: bosses exempt, a zombie under a STRONGER foreign
  slow (Widow's cocoon, Time Warp, a trap) is never stomped upward, and the
  keep-alive sweep multiplies it back in on every re-assert instead of a
  one-shot rate write decaying. Re-applied every 500 ms tick against a 1200 ms
  duration, so it reads continuous in the fire and returns within a second out.
- **A KILL THE FIRE FINISHED PAYS A FLAT 30**, via stock's own mechanism rather
  than a refund: `_zm_spawner.gsc` sets `deathpoints_already_given` and returns
  early if it is already true, so claiming that flag before the lethal DoDamage
  makes stock skip its normal award entirely. No subtracting points back off a
  player, and no dependence on whether the death-event callback runs before or
  after the award. Lethality is exact here — the per-tick dedupe guarantees this
  is the only trail damage in flight for that zombie, and DoDamage is
  synchronous.
- **DAMAGE NUMBERS.** The burn had none because BOTH exits of its branch in
  `upgrade_damage_cb` skip the normal push site: the sprinter arm returns its own
  value and the ordinary arm returns -1 to stay silent. Now pushed from the
  branch itself (the insta-kill branch already does this for the same reason),
  with the value the victim actually takes — so a burn on an armored sprinter
  reads reduced AND red. Rides the same 0.05 s window, so a trail across a train
  sums to one number per tick, not one per zombie.
- **A VISUAL SIZE LADDER.** Levels already differed in patch COUNT (1/2/3) and
  radius but every level drew the same flame, so Lv1 read nearly as loud as Lv5.
  An `.efx` cannot be scaled from script, so the ladder is two authored effects:
  `fire/fx_fire_ground_rubble_sm_50x50` below Lv3 and the existing
  `fire/fx_fire_ground_rubble_50x50` at Lv3+. Both real stock ground fires with
  proper flame materials, neither referencing a `_pcloud`. Precached AND zoned,
  because this map has now shipped the missing-zone-line bug twice.
- **THE FIRE SOUND IS THE USER'S.** Their supplied 10 s "whooshing fire wind"
  replaces the synthetic crackle on `tod_trail_loop`. Trimmed to a 4 s window
  from its SUSTAINED BODY rather than used whole: the file ramps in and its
  first three seconds run 4-5 dB under the rest, and since a patch lives 2-4 s
  and plays from the file's start, whole-file use would have played only the
  quiet ramp and never the body. 0.08 s fade-in kills the spawn click,
  peak-normalised to −1.0 dBFS, 48 k/16-bit/stereo. The ignite whoosh is still
  synthetic.
- **LOCKSTEP:** `tod_upgrade.lua` DETAIL[46] carried a hand-copy of the old
  `8 + 4*L` damage formula and now carries `1 + L` plus the slow figure — it is
  the only place a player reads either number. Domain descriptions in both files
  now say the trail slows.
- **NO ART RE-BAKE IS OWED, checked by opening the PNG rather than reasoning
  about it.** An earlier draft of this entry claimed the baked card was "now
  under-described" and owed a re-bake. It is not and it does not. The card
  carries exactly one generic line — **`FIRE FOLLOWS YOUR SPRINT`** — with no
  number and no claim about heat, damage or duration (docs/83 specifies "No
  second line, no number", and the shipped 768×1152 confirms it). That sentence
  is exactly as true after this retune as before, which is precisely what the
  generic-card-text rule buys: a value line with no figures in it survives a
  balance change untouched. The phrase I mistook for card text — "longer, wider
  and hotter" — is the DOMAIN DESC in the GSC and Lua, the text-fallback path,
  which this entry already updates. The pause nameplate says only
  "TRAILBLAZER". Nothing to re-bake, no pack to build.
- `-GscOnly` (scripts, Lua, one zone fx line, one wav). Lints green: arity,

## 2026-09-03 (v16.93) — The pause legend gets the glyphs too; and a real device-read probe

User: *"Pause menu didnt get updated. Also i thought we aligned on the class
menu continuously switching input assets depending on what it detects and after
your first selection it stays with that input for rest of game?"*

### 1. The pause legend was left behind

v16.88 gave both card panels baked button art and **the pause menu's UPGRADE
CARDS legend was not touched** — v16.83 had fixed its WORDING and nothing since
had revisited it, so the one screen whose whole job is to tell you the controls
was still spelling out key names while the card panels drew buttons.

- The legend now draws the same glyphs: two switch buttons, the word SWITCH,
  the lock button, the word LOCK, inside the 868..1210 band the text used.
- Rects computed PER DEVICE, the same rule the card menus carry: the pad glyph
  is square (30) and the keycap is wide and short (56 x 28), so one fixed rect
  would stretch one of them.
- **THE LESSON IS NOT "WE MISSED A FILE".** A readout that disagrees with the
  thing it describes is precisely what v16.83 was fixing (the legend then named
  fire and aim, lanes v16.57 had removed). It is not enough for a readout to be
  CORRECT — it has to MATCH, and any change to how controls are PRESENTED owes
  the legend the same edit as the panels. There are three of these surfaces:
  `tod_upgrade.lua`, `tod_class_select.lua`, `AetheriumStartMenu.lua`.

### 2. "Detect, then lock in at class select" — the honest status

**The design is right, and it has never been buildable, because nothing has
ever DETECTED anything.** That is the part worth being blunt about: every
"detection" in this map so far has been a guess about which BUTTON was pressed,
never about which DEVICE pressed it.

- The lock buttons are jump and use. Both exist on both devices, so **locking
  in a class proves nothing about the hardware**.
- The action-slot latch (`tod_input_pad`) is not a device proof either — v16.81
  established a keyboard binds 1-4 to action slots, which is how a KBM player
  who taps 3 got treated as a pad for a whole match.
- So freezing the guess at lock-in would not deliver the feature; it would make
  the WRONG ANSWER PERMANENT and remove the one thing that currently saves it,
  which is that the guess is re-evaluated every render. That is why it was
  refused in v16.32 rather than shipped — but the refusal was recorded as "this
  cannot work" when the accurate version is **"this cannot work UNTIL a device
  read exists"**, and nobody went looking for one for a month.
- **`GetControllerType()` is the first real candidate.** Mod tools API docs,
  `CLIENT/SERVER: Server`, per-player, "returns the controller type of the
  player", and the only device-type API in the docs. Stock never calls it
  anywhere in `share/raw`, so it is unexercised and its return values are
  unknown — it may report the pad MODEL rather than keyboard-vs-pad.
- **This build PROBES it, deliberately without branching on it.** Two `tod_dev`
  prints in the class draft: one at draft open, one at lock-in alongside what
  the old pad-latch believed. Dev is armed, so the values land on screen in the
  next run. **Do not write a predicate against this until both readings are
  known** (keyboard-only, and pad-in-hand) — a guessed predicate is the same
  failure as the latch with extra steps.
- If the values separate the devices, the user's design ships whole next build:
  poll it during the draft so the glyphs swap live, freeze it at lock-in. If
  they do not, the fallback is a manual pause-menu override, which is what PC
  games do when detection is unreliable.

- Lua + one GSC probe. `lint_tod_lua.js` clean (42 files); `lint_tod_arity.js`
  clean (73 files); `lint_tod_assets.js` unchanged at 464 zoned, unnamed
  209/209.
- ⚠️ **BUILD DEFERRED:** BlackOps3 was running again at edit time and the gate
  refuses while it is up (locked `.sabs` = sound-bank corruption). One
  `-GscOnly` once the game is closed.
- Both dev flags remain ARMED (v16.87) — not publishable.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.92) — TRAILBLAZER: the fire trail stops lagging behind you (spacing derives from patch width)

User: *"Also the fire trail fx is delayed. Anything we can do to tighten the
latency of when I run over a spot and it gets burned based on fx"*.

**IT WAS NOT LATENCY, IT WAS GEOMETRY.** Node SPACING and node COVERAGE were
set from two unrelated numbers: a patch every `TOD_TRAIL_NODE_MS` 350 ms of
sprint (~105 u) while `trail_radius` only covers 56 u at Lv1, rising to 88 at
Lv5. So at low levels **the patches landed further apart than they were wide**
and the trail read as discrete blobs dropping in behind the player. At Lv5 the
88 radius nearly closed the gap, which is why it looked acceptable there and
nowhere else — a bug that hides at max level is a bug nobody demos.

- **SPACING NOW DERIVES FROM THE PATCH WIDTH.** New `trail_spacing( lvl )`
  returns `trail_radius( lvl )`, and the drop gate is DISTANCE from the last
  node rather than a timer, so consecutive patches just touch and the trail is
  continuous **by construction at every level** and adapts to real speed. Keyed
  to the radius deliberately: a radius retune now moves spacing with it, or the
  gaps come straight back.
- **THE OLD GATES ARE GONE.** `TOD_TRAIL_NODE_MS` (350) becomes
  `TOD_TRAIL_NODE_MIN_MS` (80), a pure spam floor; `TOD_TRAIL_NODE_MIN_DIST`
  (48) is retired outright — the new distance gate subsumes its anti-spin job,
  since standing still never travels a patch width. Verified no live reference
  to either retired name survives.
- **POLL 0.1 -> 0.05.** The poll is pure latency stacked on top of the spacing
  gate, and at sprint speed a tenth of a second is most of a patch width. The
  loop body is a few cheap tests until the domain is owned, so it costs nothing
  for anyone who does not have it.
- **LENGTH IS UNCHANGED, and the arithmetic matters.** Trail length = sprint
  speed x `trail_life_ms`, INDEPENDENT of spacing — tighter spacing buys more
  nodes over the same ground, not less ground. It only shortens if the
  per-player node CAP binds first. At Lv5 the new cadence wants ~13.6 nodes
  against a cap of 12, so `TOD_TRAIL_MAX_NODES` goes 12 -> 14 purely to stop
  the cap becoming the new limiter. Host cost at Lv5 rises 36 -> 42 of the
  map-wide 60; every other level spawns ONE host per node and stays cheap.
- **DENSITY DOES NOT CHANGE DAMAGE**, and the next person to read this code
  needs to know why: `trail_burn_tick` dedupes on `z.tod_trail_burn_ms == now`
  — one node per zombie per tick, map-wide — precisely so overlapping nodes
  read as a line instead of stacking. That is what let spacing be retuned on
  looks alone. Do not "fix" the dedupe thinking it is dropping damage.
- **A PEER CLAIM CHECKED AND REJECTED.** Session f6 flagged that "the FIRST
  patch can lag sprint start by ~450 ms regardless of spacing". It cannot:
  `last_ms` is seeded to 0 and `GetTime()` returns match time in ms, so
  `now - last_ms >= 350` is trivially true on the first poll, and the same
  holds on every sprint RESTART because `last_ms` still carries the previous
  node's stamp. The only real restart cost was the 48 u `MIN_DIST` measured
  from the last node's position, and that is exactly what this change removes.
  Their other two points (the node cap bounds LENGTH not density; the burn
  dedupe) were right and shaped the fix.
- ⚠️ **ONE THING THIS CANNOT FIX.** The ground fire is stock
  (`fire/fx_fire_ground_rubble_50x50`) and `.efx` files are binary, so if the
  effect has its own visual ramp-in, that delay is baked into the art and no
  cadence change touches it. Tightening spacing is the cheap test that tells
  the two apart: if it still reads late with patches overlapping, the remainder
  is the effect.
- `-GscOnly`. `lint_tod_arity.js` clean, 73 files. **UNPLAYED.**
- Both dev flags remain ARMED (v16.87) — not publishable.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.91) — CORRECTION: the nuke's burn was never broken; v16.90's override reverted

User, contradicting v16.90 from actual play: *"I mean on this map when i get a
nuke i can see the zombies are burned. So whats your conclusion?"* They are
right and the v16.90 entry below is wrong on its headline claim.

- **A PLACEHOLDER `.efx` IS A MISSING *SOURCE*, NOT A MISSING *ASSET*.** That
  is the fact v16.90 missed. Treyarch shipped 5,092-byte placeholder sources in
  the mod tools for effects they did not release, but the real COMPILED effects
  are in the base-game fastfiles. An effect a map **never zones** resolves from
  those at runtime and renders normally. You only inherit the empty version
  when **your own zone packs it**, because then your fastfile supplies it.
- **Which is why both observations were true at once.**
  `zombie/fx_fire_torso_zmb` is NOT in this map's zone, so the nuke burn has
  always worked. `zombie/fx_dog_fire_trail_zmb` WAS in the zone (v16.62), so
  TRAILBLAZER packed the placeholder over a good asset and drew nothing. Same
  file signature, opposite outcomes, decided entirely by the zone line.
- **Reverted:** the `character_fire_death_torso` / `_sm` override in
  `zm_tower_of_doom.csc`, its `#precache`, and the
  `fx,fire/fx_fire_ai_human_torso_loop` zone line. Keeping them would have
  swapped the nuke's own fire for a different one map-wide — the opposite of
  "give it the nuke burn effect". The comment block that replaced it explains
  why there is deliberately no override there.
- **KEPT, and still correct:** v16.79's trail fire swap (the zone line really
  was packing a placeholder), and v16.90's burn tell — `zm_nuked` increment +
  `evt_nuked` on a burning zombie. With the override gone that tell now draws
  the **actual nuke fire**, which is what was asked for.
- Still genuinely blank, both zoned AND placeholder-sourced, neither touched:
  `zombie/fx_thundergun_smoke_cloud` (THOR'S THUNDER's cloud) and
  `env/light/fx_light_god_rays_dust_motes` (the lounge motes). Fix is to drop
  the zone line or swap the source; unverified either way.
- Process note: v16.90 asserted "the nuke has never burned in this map" from
  file inspection alone, against a feature the user plays regularly. The map's
  own doctrine covers this — cheap to change is not cheap to be wrong about,
  and only looking at it in game proves an effect draws. Memory
  `stub-efx-in-mod-tools` rewritten around the corrected rule.
- `-GscOnly`. Lints green. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-03 (v16.90) — Burning zombies actually burn: the nuke's own fire and sound on TRAILBLAZER (and the nuke was broken too — WRONG, see v16.91)

User: *"When a zombie is burned can we give it the nuke burn effect? This would
look way better. And we need better sfx for when the burn is on them and they
get damaged. I think reusing what nuke has sfx and fx would be great."*

- **THE NUKE'S BURN HAS NEVER RENDERED IN THIS MAP, and that is the actual
  find.** Stock's nuke does not play an effect on its victims: it sets the
  `zm_nuked` ACTOR clientfield and the client half answers with
  `zombie_death::flame_death_fx`, which draws
  `level._effect["character_fire_death_torso"]`. `zombie_death.csc:13-14` points
  both fire handles at `zombie/fx_fire_torso_zmb` — a **5,092-byte STUB** whose
  single material is literally `gfx_debug_missing_fx`. So every nuke in every
  build of this map has gibbed heads and played `evt_nuked` over zombies that
  never caught fire. Same trap as the v16.79 dog-trail effect; memory
  `stub-efx-in-mod-tools`.
- **The fire is now real:** `zm_tower_of_doom.csc` overrides both handles with
  `fire/fx_fire_ai_human_torso_loop` (132 KB, real flame materials, base-game
  `fire/`, no `_pcloud` — the crash class that killed map 1's fungus pod). The
  override sits after `waitforclient( 0 )` ON PURPOSE: stock assigns these in
  `function autoexec init_fire_fx()` which does `WAIT_CLIENT_FRAME` first, so an
  override written any earlier is silently overwritten a frame later. **This
  fixes the nuke as a side effect** — nuked hordes now burn.
- **TRAILBLAZER's burn tell rides the same lane for one line.** A zombie taking
  a trail tick gets `clientfield::increment( "zm_nuked" )` plus
  `PlaySound( "evt_nuked" )`, the nuke's own per-victim sound. No new
  clientfield, no new `.csc`, no bits spent: the field is already registered in
  both VMs because this map `#using`s the nuke module. The synthetic
  noise-generated sizzle from v16.79 is gone from the call path.
- **Cadence:** `TOD_TRAIL_BURN_TELL_MS` 3000 per zombie, `..._PER_TICK` 3, on
  the existing 0.5 s burn tick. Re-igniting an already-burning zombie is free —
  the client keeps its own 12 s `is_on_fire` latch and returns early — so the
  cadence governs the SOUND and how many bodies light up at once, not the
  flame. The flame is a looping effect with no stop handle (stock's design, it
  assumed nuked zombies die instantly), so a burned zombie that survives stays
  alight until it dies. Acceptable here because the trail kills trash quickly;
  if a permanently-burning elite reads badly, the fix is a shorter one-shot
  effect, not a stop call.
- Unused after this: the `tod_trail_sizzle` alias row and its wav. Left in
  place for one build so a per-tick sound is one line to restore; drop them if
  the nuke sound lands well.
- `-GscOnly` (scripts + one `fx,` zone line). Lints green: arity, assets, hints,
  Lua. **UNPLAYED.**

## 2026-09-03 (v16.89) — The switch glyphs go back under the cards, centred

User: *"So you put them to the side but i wanted to keep the position under the
cards in the middle of the screen. Same spot as before"*.

v16.88 moved the two switch glyphs out to the cards' outer edges, on the
argument that direction reads better as a POSITION than as a caption. That
argument is not wrong, but it was mine and not asked for, and it traded away
the spot players have been finding the control hint in since the panel existed.
**The familiar position wins**, and nothing is actually lost: the d-pad glyph
carries its own arrow, so direction still reads without the placement trick.

  plate occupied — y 644..692 on the deal panel, 566..614 on the class draft.
  The countdown bar drops to 700..714 so it clears them.
- **THE RECT IS COMPUTED PER DEVICE, NOT FIXED AT CONSTRUCTION.** The pad glyph
  is square (48) and the keycap is wide and short (72 x 36); one
  construction-time rectangle cannot serve both without stretching one of them,
  which is how the v10.4 hint plate ended up 18% squashed for six builds. Each
  slot now stores only its SIDE (-1 / +1) and the writer derives
  `cx = 640 + side * ( halfWidth + gap / 2 )`, so the pair stays centred and
  correctly proportioned at either size.
- **A REAL BUG FELL OUT OF THE REWRITE.** The class draft's painter had the
  TACTICAL token hardcoded inside it while taking a token parameter it never
  used, so both glyphs would have shown the LEFT key — a right-hand glyph
  telling the player to press the left-hand button. It now uses the token it is
  handed, which is what the deal panel already did. Nobody would have caught
  this by reading the call sites: they passed the right values all along.

  files); `lint_tod_assets.js` unchanged at 464 zoned images, unnamed 209/209.
- ⚠️ **BUILD DEFERRED, NOT SKIPPED.** `build_map.ps1` refused while BlackOps3 was
  running (pid 10680) — building against locked `.sabs` is the sound-bank
  corruption failure, so the gate is right and was obeyed. The tree is ready;
  the build is one `-GscOnly` once the game is closed. Until then the live
  `.ff` is v16.88's, with the glyphs still at the card edges.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.88a, NO BUILD OF ITS OWN) — KEEPING THE BUILD SMALL IS A GATE NOW: `lint_tod_assets.js` on every build

User: *"Lets make sure we keep this process of minimizing the build as much as possible where there is deadcode or assets ... We dont want to cause regression but as you can see we somehow had 7GB of random stuff not even used on the map."* The size is now handled — but **the 7 GB was mostly not unused assets**, and the record should say so, because the three causes have three different fixes: **~5.3 GB was build history inside the pack** (the linker appends forever; fixed by `-CleanPak`, implied by `-Publish`), **~1.2 GB was texture resolution on assets the map DOES use** (machines/axe/shield, `downscale_pack_textures.js`, a judgement call), and **only ~130 MB was genuinely unused** (Street Sweeper, Mahem, 12 retired cards). Only the first was automated. This entry automates the third.

**`tools/lint_tod_assets.js` — runs on EVERY build including `-GscOnly`**, because both of its failure modes are pure zone/Lua edits the linker never reports. **GATE A (hard fail):** an image a live path names with no `image,` line — the game draws a WHITE SQUARE and nothing else catches it. Sources: every literal `i_tod_*` in `ui/**/*.lua`, every `CARD_SLUG` slug x 3 rarities (or x1 for a `CARD_ONE_IMAGE` domain), every live domain id <= `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX`, and the 8 TIER cards built from `TCLS`. **GATE B (regression-gated against `lint_tod_assets.baseline.json`):** a `CARD_SLUG` slug whose domain has no live `add_domain` (the exact v16.86 bug), a zoned card no slug declares, a dead pause plate, plus an advisory count. Everything is PARSED from the live sources (`domain_id`, `add_domain`, `CARD_SLUG`, `CARD_ONE_IMAGE`, `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX`, `TCLS`), so renames follow. **THE RULE IT ENFORCES: a card slug and its zone lines are ONE unit — retire both or neither.** Five domains had been retired half-way before anything checked.

Written the way this repo's other gates are: `lint_tod_assets_selftest.js` breaks the map **nine** ways and requires the right outcome on each — six that must fire, a clean control, and **two shapes that must NOT fire** (a concatenation prefix; a one-image card), both of which the lint got wrong in its first ten minutes and which the self-test now pins. The baseline's `why` block records which current numbers are ACCEPTED and why (the 10 retired-domain pause plates stay by convention, ~0.5 MB) — never raise one to go green.

**A peer session caught a real gap before the baseline set:** the 8 TIER cards are built from a table, so no literal names them — and an early `if /^i_tod_card_/ continue` had made them invisible to the lint entirely, neither gated nor advised. Deleting one would have been an uncaught white square. Now parsed from `TCLS` + the loop bounds under `USE_TIER_CARD_ART` and required by GATE A, with a self-test case that deletes `i_tod_card_tier_heavy_3` and demands the catch. Cross-checked GATE A against that session's independently-derived `card_contrast_report.js --list`: **114 live cards, 0 missing a zone line** — two models built from different directions agree. The 5 zoned cards outside their list are the 4 class-draft cards (literals, live) and `i_tod_card_base` (the known never-drawn composite lane). Another session then used the lint's GATE A logic by hand and caught two images it had zoned but never referenced (`i_tod_key_blank`, `i_tod_hold_fill`) before they shipped.

CLAUDE.md carries the standing rule (Build/run), including the two failure modes that made this necessary: **never delete on a name-grep alone** — the gift gun looked unused because nothing calls `GiveWeapon` for it (it is the Death Machine powerup, redirected through a level field), while the Mahem rocket looked used because its function existed (nothing had called it since 2026-08-20). Record: docs/86 §9.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.88) — REAL BUTTON GLYPHS: the card panel and the class draft stop printing "LT" (docs/88)

User: *"Hey i cobfused did you not uopdate the class selection screen? Where
are the dpad icons?"* — and they were right to ask twice. **The art had been
delivered at 13:38 and this session never inspected the drop**, then told them
the icons "do not exist yet". They did exist. Inspect every `files (N).zip`
that lands; a delivered drop sitting unopened is indistinguishable from a
missing one, and only one of those is the user's problem.

**THE PREMISE THAT DIED (v16.83 -> here).** A pad test showed the panel reading
`lt < Switch > rt`. **The engine renders a `[{+bind}]` token as a TEXT NAME,
never a picture.** The repo, `CLAUDE.md` and docs/69 had all said "the bound key
name **or pad glyph**" for days, on the strength of one transcription of an
`X` — a character that reads identically whichever way it was drawn. Nobody had
ever seen a picture. So there is no engine glyph to inherit, and baking our own
is the only route.

- **NINE IMAGES DELIVERED, SEVEN SHIPPED.** `i_tod_pad_dpad_left` / `_right`
  (the lit arm carries the direction), `i_tod_pad_button_a`,
  `i_tod_key_blank_wide`, `i_tod_hold_plate` (HOLD / TO LOCK baked, with an
  empty gap for the button), `i_tod_timer_track` + `_fill`. Verified before
  install: the loose and nested copies in the drop are **pixel-identical** (0
  differing px on all three duplicates), both keycaps are genuinely EMPTY, and
  both fills are **perfectly uniform left-to-right** so a stretched part-filled
  bar cannot smear.
- **TWO WERE DELIBERATELY NOT ZONED**, because a packed-but-undrawn image is
  pure load-time cost (the png-art-audit finding):
  `i_tod_key_blank` (the SQUARE keycap — the bind expansion can be `MOUSE3`
  and nothing here can measure text in advance, so the WIDE cap is used for
  every key) and `i_tod_hold_fill` (**the plate bakes its lettering ON TOP of
  the groove**, so a fill over the plate covers the words and a fill under it
  is hidden by the opaque plate — the progress bar sits below the plate on the
  timer pair instead). Both PNGs and GDT blocks are kept, with the reason
  recorded at the registration site.
- **ONE BAR PAIR SERVES BOTH JOBS.** A hold-to-lock and a countdown are the
  same object, one filling and one draining, so they share art rather than
  minting a second pair that would need visual lockstep forever.
- **THE COUNTDOWN LOST ITS DIGITS.** `AUTO IN 15s` was the last pure-LUI element
  on the control UI; it is now a draining bar. **The panel is never told the
  timeout length** and the clientuimodel pool is at its proven 61-bit ceiling,
  so the bar LEARNS the maximum by watching: the first tick of a deal is the
  largest value it will ever see. Exact for a round deal and the shorter
  station deal alike, with no server change — and it resets on hide, or the
  next deal would open part-drained against the previous clock.
- **THE HOLD BAR IS NEW ELEMENTS, NOT A RE-SKIN.** `CoD.TextWithBg` lives in the
  bytecode LUI core, so whether its `.Bg` accepts `setImage` is UNVERIFIABLE
  from this tree — and a wrong guess in LUI fails SILENTLY, taking the whole
  menu with it. The colour quads stay constructed and are held at alpha 0
  whenever the art is on; with `USE_CARD_GLYPH_ART` off they are still the bar.
- **DEVICE RULE, AND ITS KNOWN COST.** The glyph set is chosen by `CoD.TodPad`,
  the one-way action-slot latch, because there is still no proven device read
  (`GetControllerType()` is documented but stock never calls it — docs/88). That
  latch is not a device proof: a keyboard player who taps 3 or 4 will see pad
  glyphs. Accepted deliberately, and strictly better than the status quo where
  EVERY pad player read letters. **The fix is a real device read, not a
  different guess.**
- Both menus, same treatment — the draft is the first menu of the match and
  showing it text while the deal panel showed glyphs would have been the worse
  half to skip.
- FULL build (a `.gdt` edit always is). `lint_tod_lua.js` clean, 42 files.
  **UNPLAYED** — first checks: d-pad glyphs flanking the four draft cards and
  the two deal cards on a pad; a keycap carrying the real key on KBM; the A
  button sitting in the plate's gap; the hold bar filling and the countdown
  draining.
- ⚠️ Both dev flags remain ARMED (v16.87) — this `.ff` is not publishable.


## 2026-09-03 (v16.87) — DEV MODE NO LONGER CHANGES ENEMY CADENCE (dev + god stay ARMED)

User: *"I think dev mode has all these xtra elites spawning in. Can we remove
that now. They have been tested and everything"* → and, on the first attempt
disarming both flags: *"No i want both on. Im saying there are extra elites when
dev is on. I want to remove that specific thing"*.

**THE ASK WAS SURGICAL AND THE FIRST READ OF IT WAS NOT.** Disarming
`level.tod_dev` would have removed the extra elites, but it also takes away
dev money, upgrades every round, the 100% TIER card, unlimited station uses and
the diagnostics — everything the user is currently arming the build FOR. Both
flags are back to `true`; what changed is the four cadence gates.

- **THE DEV CADENCE IS GONE FROM ALL FOUR ELITE FAMILIES.** Each ran a dev
  interval about twice the shipping one, so an armed session was a measurably
  different game:

  | family | dev | ship |
  |---|---|---|
  | Panzer | round 3, then every 3 | round 5, then every 5 |
  | Reaver | every 2 | every 4 |
  | Hellhounds | every 2 | every 3 |
  | Armored Sprinter | every 2 | every 3 |

  `panzer_due`, `hound_due`, `reaver_due` and `sprint_due` now read the ship
  `#define` unconditionally, and the five `TOD_*_DEV` constants are retired in
  place (commented, with the value, so the history is readable). Verified no
  live reference to any of them survives.
- **THE REAL COST WAS NOT THE SPAWN RATE, IT WAS THE TESTING.** Every armed
  playtest since the flags existed exercised cadences the map does not ship, so
  a build could feel right armed and wrong shipped, or vice versa, with nothing
  to attribute it to. That is the same shape as the dev-only bug class this repo
  has been bitten by before: **a lane that only ever runs in one build
  configuration is untested in the other.**
- **LOCKSTEP, RECORDED:** the four sites are now a set. Re-adding a dev branch
  to one family alone reintroduces exactly the drift this removed; the note on
  `panzer_due` says so, and each of the other three points at it. To test a
  family again, drop its SHIP define for the session rather than running a
  second cadence only some builds see.
- The only `tod_dev` left in those four files is the hellhound `dbg()` print,
  which is a diagnostic and correctly gated.
- The ship-deltas block in `tod_resolve_dev_flags()` is annotated as stale on
  its Panzer/Reaver lines: dev still changes upgrade frequency, the TIER card
  rate, station uses, dev money, the diagnostics and demigod — but no longer
  how often anything spawns.
- `-GscOnly`. `node tools/lint_tod_arity.js` clean, 73 files. **UNPLAYED** —
  first check is simply that an armed run no longer sees a Panzer at round 3,
  and that Reaver/hound/sprinter arrive on their door-anchored ship intervals.
- ⚠️ **BOTH FLAGS ARE STILL ARMED, SO THIS `.ff` IS NOT PUBLISHABLE.** Flip
  them and delete the ARMED block before any publish build.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.85) — UPGRADE CARD CONTRAST PASS LANDED: 114 cards re-toned so the artwork reads (docs/87)

User: *"we need to enhance the contrast on them a bit"* → *"Yes basically i
just want the card content to be more easily seen."* Drop returned, both gates
passed, installed, FULL build 13:39:51, `.ff` 134.34 MB.

  DEADSHOT's single ULTIMATE, the 8 CLASS TIER cards) through the content-lift
  curve `0:0, 32:30, 60:88, 110:145, 170:198, 255:255` on RGB, alpha untouched.
  Everything below L32 is unmoved, so the panel field, the black outlines and
  the card body are exactly as they were; the 32→110 band lifts at ~2× slope,
  which is where every illustration lives. Measured on the shipped result: the
  share of the art panel that is DRAWING rather than background roughly tripled
  on the faint cards — RECOIL regular 7.1% → 24.6%, HANDLING regular 8.7% →
  25.4%, DRAW CUT regular 7.7% → 25.2%, SPRINT super 11.0% → 34.5% — and the
  SUPER rarity's effect text climbed 6.1:1 → 8.2:1 toward the ~11:1 the other
  two rarities already had. Within a tenth of a percent of the calibration

- **BOTH GATES RAN.** `card_contrast_report.js --compare` on all 114: no size,
  colour-type or ALPHA change, no file whose contrast went the wrong way (the
  alpha check is the load-bearing one — the transparent corners and the
  SUPER/ULTIMATE/TIER glow halo live there, and an editor that flattens them

  legibility actually moved. Proof of the build: **114 NEW content-hash `.iwi`

- **ATHLETE + ADRENALINE: NEW ART *AND* THE LIFT, a collision that would have
