## 2026-09-03 (v16.84) — SOLO freezes the world at the Heavenly Gift Altar

User: *"Also on solo when you use the alter can we freeze the game like on the
round based upgrades. I only want this applied on solo"*.

The personal upgrade station has been deliberately unfrozen since 2026-08-20,
and "the world does NOT pause; that is the risk" is written into four places in
this repo. That risk was always a **CO-OP** argument: with a teammate up,
fifteen seconds of standing still is a cost somebody else absorbs. Alone it is
nobody's, so a solo buyer paid 3000 points for a choice they could not afford to
read — and the map's one concession (`TOD_REVEAL_LIVE_SCALE`, the half-speed
reveal while the world is live) only ever shortened the exposure.

- **Solo now gets the round-event treatment, through the SAME two functions the
  round event uses** — no second implementation of a freeze:
  `set_world_pause( true )` (stock's `world_is_paused` halts `round_spawning`,
  every tod boss director and spawner reads `level.tod_upgrade_pause`, live AI
  takes `ignoreall` + a 0.05 anim rate) and `menu_freeze( true )` (weapons off,
  jump off, movement pinned). `station_freeze_wanted` is the ONLY gate, and
  `GetPlayers().size != 1` answers it first, so **co-op is byte-for-byte
  unchanged**.
- **Three things follow for free**, all already keyed on
  `level.tod_upgrade_pause`: the reveal plays at FULL speed (the half-speed cut
  existed only because the world was live); `upgrade_damage_cb` returns 0, so
  nobody farms a frozen horde through the panel; and **every input lane opens on
  the card panel** — v16.81's d-pad-only station rule was earned by the player
  being mid-fight, and a frozen solo buyer is not. Not one of those three needed
  an edit.
- **THE RAW `tod_upgrade_pause` READ STOPPED BEING A TAKEOVER TEST** the moment
  the pause became self-inflicted. `solo_present_interruptible` polls that flag
  and returns -1 = "a round event took the UI over"; read raw, a solo pick would
  hand back -1 on its first poll and re-present itself forever. New owner field
  `level.tod_station_pause_owner` + `station_owns_pause()` is the whole
  difference. The loop-top read in `solo_upgrade_flow` is left RAW on purpose
  and says why: we can never own the pause there, and a guard nobody can watch
  fire is not a guard.
- **THE ROUND EVENT CLAIMS THE PAUSE AT ITS TAKEOVER.** `run_upgrade_event`
  now clears the owner in the same synchronous block as the
  `tod_global_upg_takeover` notify. Without it, its own
  `set_world_pause( false )` at the bottom would clear a station's freeze out
  from under a player still reading cards. Claiming it makes
  `station_pause_end()` a no-op: the event owns both lanes, and its
  `player_choice_flow` re-freezes and unfreezes the player like any other
  participant. This is the long-standing "never call `menu_freeze(false)` on
  the takeover path" corollary, now ENFORCED in one function instead of
  asserted in a comment.
- **THE FINALE IS THE ONE SOLO CARVE-OUT** (`level.tod_upgrades_suppressed`),
  for exactly the reason `event_scheduler` skips its own events there: the
  closing song IS the run's clock, a freeze stops the world but not a music
  stream, and every frozen second of card-reading slides the ending out of sync
  with the track. The CROWN altar stays live-world once extraction is called.
  The spire sets the same flag and has no stations at all.
- **A watchdog, because a permanently frozen world is the worst thing this file
  can leave behind.** `solo_upgrade_flow` carries `self endon( "disconnect" )`,
  so a disconnect between begin and end kills the only thread that would have
  released the pause. In solo that disconnect ends the match anyway — which is
  precisely the kind of reasoning that stops being true the day someone adds a
  path. `station_pause_watchdog` releases at `TOD_UPG_CHOICE_TIMEOUT + 12`
  (27 s) and is keyed on a SEQUENCE, not the player: buy, release, buy again
  inside the ceiling and a player-keyed watchdog would tear down the second
  pick's pause.
- **Mid-pick now outranks the pause deny in `station_use_loop`.** A solo pick
  makes `tod_upgrade_pause` true, so a second press would have drawn the
  round-event deny SOUND: the wrong reason, and a noise in the ear of someone
  who is only holding a key while they read. The more specific state wins, and
  it is silent for the same reason the laststand branch is.
- The down-mid-pick path needs no bleedout refund (unlike the round event's):
  the pause opens BEFORE the down, and `solo_present_interruptible` aborts
  within its 0.8 s confirm grace, so at most that much of a bleedout clock is
  spent frozen.
- Copy lockstep: the station block header, `init()`'s one-liner, the
  `TOD_REVEAL_LIVE_SCALE` note and the v16.81 input-lane note all now say
  "co-op" where they used to say "the station".
- `-GscOnly`. arity, hints (91 distinct, unchanged) and Lua lints green.
  **UNPLAYED.** First checks, solo: buy at the base altar — zombies stop dead,
  you cannot move, shoot or jump, the reveal plays at full speed, WASD/R/V and
  the d-pad all move focus; the world resumes the instant a card locks. Then
  buy with a round event due and confirm the takeover still steals the panel and
  gives it back. Co-op: buy at an altar and confirm the horde keeps coming.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.83) — CARD PANEL CONTROLS: one lane per action, and its direction (docs/88)

User: *"Can we improve and simplify the control UI in the upgrade menu? I feel
like our last update made it more confusing and less simplified by adding so
much to look at."*

**MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** Read against the user's own `players/bindings_0.cfg`
(`+smoke`=E, `+frag`=G, `+melee`=V, `+gostand`=SPACE, `+activate`=F), one
15-second deal drew **three plates, four lines and seven key names** for a
two-button decision:

```
SWITCH: E / G / V / D-PAD          <- bottom plate, line 1
LOCK: HOLD SPACE / F               <- bottom plate, line 2
HOLD SPACE / F TO LOCK             <- under the focused card: the SAME
                                      instruction, said a second time
AUTO IN 15s
```

**NOTHING WAS EVER REMOVED.** Before v16.32 this was ONE baked plate with ONE
line. v16.32 split it in two to fit the live-bind tokens; v16.57 swapped in the
offhand pair and kept the `D-PAD` tail. Every step added, none subtracted. The
user's read is exactly right, and it is a process finding as much as a UI one:
three consecutive changes each defensible on its own, never re-read together.

- **A LIST HAS NO DIRECTION — that is the real defect.** `SWITCH: E / G / V`
  says which keys are live and never says *which card each one moves to*, the
  one fact the player needs. Both plates now lead with direction:
  `[E] < SWITCH > [G]` and `HOLD [SPACE] TO LOCK`.
- **ONE LANE IS NAMED: the offhand pair.** It is the only pair correct on every
  device everywhere — `_tod_upgrade_ui::wait_for_choice` reads tactical/lethal
  ABOVE the station's device gate, so it survives the pad's d-pad-only station
  rule, and by v16.57's argument it sits left/right on every pad layout by
  construction. Melee, reload, WASD, the strafe stick and the d-pad are all
  UNCHANGED and still work — they are simply no longer advertised. Stock does
  the same: "Hold [X] To Buy" never lists its alternatives.
- **LOCK IS SAID ONCE**, under the focused card, where the eye and the hold bar
  already are. The bottom plate stopped repeating it, so it is one line again
  and back to the art's true 280x43 aspect — ONE geometry for both the frame
  path and the baked path, which can no longer be different sizes.
- **NO DEVICE BRANCH IN ANY CONTROL STRING.** The `D-PAD` tail was the last
  text keyed off `CoD.TodPad`, and that latch is not a device proof (v16.81 — a
  keyboard binds 3/4 to action slots), so a falsely-latched keyboard player
  could be shown pad wording. Every token is engine-expanded per device now, so
  the v16.81 "cosmetic, noted, unchanged" caveat is closed for these plates.
- **LIVE BUG FOUND IN THE PAUSE LEGEND** (`AetheriumStartMenu.lua`). The
  UPGRADE CARDS line still named `+attack` and `+speed_throw` — fire and aim —
  which **v16.57 REMOVED as menu inputs**. `wait_for_choice` still reads them,
  but only for the dev probe; neither assigns `want`. A player following that
  legend pressed fire, watched the focus not move, and concluded the menu was
  broken. It now names the same single lane the in-world plates do, so the two
  readouts cannot drift apart again.
- Same treatment on the CLASS DRAFT (`tod_class_select.lua`), the twin: four
  cards, tactical/lethal step and wrap, same strings, same one-line geometry.
- Net: **4 lines -> 2, seven key names -> three, direction stated for the first
  time.** `SwitchLine2` and its text element are gone from both menus.

**ART REQUESTED (docs/88, `~/Downloads/tod_card_controls_art_pack.zip`).** TEN
images: four CONTROLLER glyphs (`i_tod_pad_dpad_left` / `_right`,
`i_tod_pad_button_a`, `i_tod_pad_button_x`), two blank KEYBOARD keycaps
(`i_tod_key_blank`, `i_tod_key_blank_wide` for SPACE / MOUSE3), and four
furniture pieces (`i_tod_hold_plate` with HOLD / TO LOCK baked in,
`i_tod_hold_fill`, `i_tod_timer_track`, `i_tod_timer_fill` — the countdown
becomes a draining bar, so there are no digits to draw). The only baked
lettering in the set is the `A` and `X` moulded into the two face buttons plus
HOLD / TO LOCK; both keycaps ship EMPTY, because the engine prints the live
bind into them.

**THE REQUEST WAS REWRITTEN THREE TIMES AND EACH TURN LEFT A RULE.**

1. *"why do we have fills in the images? Cant the images contain only the
   content they need?"* — four images cut to two. The chevrons had been specced
   as TABS (a navy shell around the arrow), which adds boxes to a screen whose
   problem is boxes; `i_tod_hold_fill` asked art to do a job a coloured quad
   already does (`HoldTrack` / `HoldFill` are `CoD.TextWithBg` rectangles); and
   `i_tod_hold_track` was a new plate to replace `i_tod_hint_frame`, already
   shipping. **AN IMAGE SHOULD CARRY ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE CAN DRAW.**
2. *"we dont want any LUI ... everything seen to be an asset ... way easier to
   visualize"* — back up to a full set, deliberately restoring those fills. Not
   a flip-flop: the first question was whether a shell adds anything (it does
   not), the second is whether a flat colour quad belongs on screen at all (it
   does not). The audit that followed found MORE LUI than had been counted —
   the hold bar and the countdown had never had a pixel of art.
3. **THE USER'S IN-GAME TEST KILLED THE PREMISE THE WHOLE THING RESTED ON.** On
   a pad the panel read `lt < Switch > rt`. **The engine renders a bind token as
   a TEXT NAME, never a picture.** This changelog, `CLAUDE.md` and docs/69 had
   all said "the bound key name **or pad glyph**" for days, on the strength of
   the v14.58 `HoldXAMMOCRATE` transcription — an `X`, which reads identically
   whether the engine drew a picture or the letter. Nobody had ever seen a
   picture. So there is no engine glyph to inherit and baked per-device art is
   the only route; the chevrons were dropped because a d-pad glyph carries its
   own arrow. Memory `lui-bind-tokens` corrected. **A single character is not
   evidence of a RENDERING MODE.**

**TWO FINDINGS FROM THE RESEARCH, BOTH UNRESOLVED, NEITHER BLOCKING:**

- **`GetControllerType()` EXISTS** — `docs_modtools`, `CLIENT/SERVER: Server`,
  per-player, and the only device-type API in the docs. Memory
  `bo3-menu-input-apis` fact 4 has said "there is no server-side device read"
  since 2026-08-30 on the grounds that no gamepad builtin appears in
  `share/raw` — a claim about stock USAGE, not about the API EXISTING, and the
  same memory says the API doc is the authority. **NOT SOLVED:** verified that
  stock never calls it anywhere, so it is unexercised and its return values are
  unknown (it may report the pad MODEL rather than keyboard-vs-pad). A one-line
  `tod_dev` probe rides the install build; if it is useless the fallback is a
  pause-menu override, which is standard on PC anyway. **"Stock never calls X"
  is not "X does not exist".**
- **`+activate` MAY NOT RESOLVE ON A PAD.** Read out of the user's own
  `players/bindings_0.cfg` and `bindings_1.cfg`: it is bound to keyboard `F`
  and to NO controller button in either profile (pad "use" is `+usereload` on
  `BUTTON_X`). That token is the footer of all eight cursor-hint cards — every
  door, perk, PaP, ammo crate, teleporter, power switch and the extraction buy.
  What it renders with no pad binding is UNKNOWN: CoD may alias activate to use
  and print `X`, or print nothing and leave "Hold  To Open" with a hole in it.
  If the latter, **v16.29 introduced it** when it replaced the hardcoded `"F"`,
  and it has been live for every controller player since. Ten-second test: look
  at a door with the pad active. `i_tod_pad_button_x` is in the pack either way
  — a cosmetic upgrade if the token renders, the fix if it does not.

Placement rects and the install-time Lua plan are in the doc.

- `-GscOnly` (Lua only). `node tools/lint_tod_lua.js` clean, 42 files.
  **UNPLAYED** — first checks: at a round deal, does the bottom plate read
  `E < SWITCH > G` on one line; does the focused card read `HOLD SPACE TO LOCK`;
  do E and G actually move to the card each sits beside; does the pause menu's
  UPGRADE CARDS line agree with both. On a pad the same four with the pad's own
  glyphs. If any token renders as a literal `[{+...}]`, that bind name is wrong.
  The `<` `>` glyphs are the one unproven element (ltromatic.ttf is a display
  face and no tod string has used them before) — but the line DEGRADES
  GRACEFULLY by construction: with them missing it still reads `E  SWITCH  G`,
  and each key is still sitting on the side it moves to.


## 2026-09-03 (v16.82, NO BUILD) — ALL 114 UPGRADE CARDS SENT OUT SO THE ARTWORK CAN BE SEEN (docs/87)

User: *"can we look at all the upgrade cards and send them in a zip and we need
to enhance the contrast on them a bit"* → then, decisively: *"Yes basically i
just want the card content to be more easily seen."* Pack built and waiting for
the drop — no code, no assets, no build in this entry.

- **THE FIRST BRIEF ASKED FOR THE OPPOSITE OF THE FIX, AND WAS REWRITTEN BEFORE
  THE ZIP WENT OUT.** "Enhance the contrast" as an instruction means deepen the
  darks and brighten the highlights, and that is what the first version of
  docs/87 specified. Measured per card band, the chassis is not the problem:
  the title plate reads 9.8:1, the rarity band 11.8:1, the effect text 11.1:1
  on REGULAR and ULTIMATE. What is hard to see is **the illustration inside the
  screen panel** — most icons are drawn in dark charcoal or dark navy on a dark
  navy panel, so the object's body sits inside the field's own luminance band
  and only its black outline separates it (opened and looked at: the RECOIL and
  HANDLING rifles and the SPRINT boot are near-silhouettes). A conventional
  contrast curve pushes those bodies FURTHER into the field. The shipped brief
  inverts the shadow half: **hold everything below L32 exactly where it is and
  lift the 32→110 band at about 2× slope**, which is where all the artwork
  lives. `0:0, 32:30, 60:88, 110:145, 170:198, 255:255`, RGB only, alpha
  untouched. Verified by rendering five cards and OPENING them: the faint
  illustrations read, the already-good ones do not blow out.
- **THE SET IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED.** `tools/card_contrast_report.js` (new)
  reads the live `add_domain` calls in `_tod_upgrades.gsc`, maps them through
  `_tod_upgrade_ui::domain_id()` and the Lua `CARD_SLUG` table, and emits the
  **114** live card files: 36 live domains × 3 rarities, DEADSHOT's single
  always-ULTIMATE file, plus the 8 CLASS TIER cards. `--list` prints them. The
  ten retired card sets still on disk stay OUT by construction, as do the four
  CLASS DRAFT cards and `i_tod_card_base`.
- **TWO METRICS WERE BUILT AND DISCARDED, AND BOTH PASSED HONESTLY WHILE
  MEASURING THE WRONG THING** — the standing `check-passes-wrong-question`
  trap, hit twice in one hour. An Otsu ink/field split of the art panel scored
  every illustration at 7:1 or better, because it counts the white sparkles and
  cyan speed lines as "ink"; a brightest-second-mode measure reported "panel
  L31 vs icon L42" for *every* card, the bright orange rocket included, because
  the runner-up mode is the lit corner of the panel's own vignette. The
  surviving measure is INK COVERAGE — the share of the panel more than 25
  luminance steps from its own field, i.e. how much of that panel is drawing
  rather than background — and it was only trusted after its ranking was
  checked against the images by eye. On the worst cards it roughly triples
  (RECOIL 7.1% → 24.7%, HANDLING 8.7% → 25.5%, SPRINT super 11.0% → 34.5%), and
  the SUPER rarity's effect text climbs 6.1:1 → 8.2:1 toward the 11:1 the other
  two rarities already had.
- **TWO GATES FOR THE DROP.** `--compare <dir>` is "nothing broke": it FAILS on
  a size or colour-type change, on ANY alpha difference (the transparent corners
  and the SUPER/ULTIMATE/TIER glow halo live in the alpha — an editor that
  flattens them ships a card with a black box around it), or on contrast that
  went down. `--regions --from <dir>` is "it actually worked". Note the
  discarded Otsu `art` ratio DROPS slightly under the new curve by construction;
  that is not a regression, and the doc says so where it will be read.
- Doc: `docs/87_upgrade_card_contrast_art_prompt.md` →
  `~/Downloads/tod_upgrade_card_contrast_art_pack.zip` (37 MB: 114 references +
  114 previews at the real on-screen 351×527). Zero WARN, zero FAIL from

## 2026-09-03 (v16.81) — The "frozen d-pad" on the card panel: the device latch was never a proof, and slot 3 could mask slot 4

User: *"Is there any race condition or something? Yes my dpad was frozen. And
another player reported this too"* → *"No it was before riot shield was
added"* → *"We played the steam build couple days ago and they noticed this.
We did a rework on controller and kbm controls. Im thinking something in
that"*. The Steam build in question is v16.5 (Sep 1); the rework is the
2026-08-30 d-pad-only device latch. No race: the class draft and the card
panel share `todUpgFocus`, but the draft's level loop waits on `tod_cls_done`,
which is set AFTER the flash — they never overlap; the scheduler calls
`run_upgrade_event` synchronously; the station dies on the takeover notify.
Two real defects instead:

- **THE LATCH'S PREMISE IS FALSE.** Every version of the input research since
  v10.20 said "BO3 PC binds NO keyboard key to an action slot in zombies", and
  the whole device latch (`tod_input_pad`) rests on it. The player's own
  `<game>/players/bindings_0.cfg` reads `bind 1 "+actionslot 1"`,
  `bind 2 "+actionslot 2"`, `bind 3 "+actionslot 4"`, `bind 4 "+actionslot 3"`
  (3 and 4 SWAPPED). So a KEYBOARD player who taps 3 or 4 during the draft or
  a deal — a weapon-switch habit from every other shooter — was latched as a
  controller for the rest of the match and lost WASD, R and V on the card
  panel: two cards up, nothing moves, only 3/4 (reversed) and the bumper pair
  left. That is the co-op partner's report. The v10.20 research read stock
  SCRIPTS; nobody read a bindings file.
- **THE FIX IS SCOPE, NOT DETECTION** (no input tells the devices apart — the
  memory's fact 4 still holds, and now so does its converse): at a ROUND EVENT
  the world is paused, movement pinned and weapons disabled, so nothing is
  "awkward to fight through" — **every lane is live for every device there**:
  d-pad, tactical/lethal, stick (dead under the pin anyway), WASD, melee,
  reload. A pad whose d-pad read has died still has R3 / X; a KBM player
  falsely latched still has WASD / R / V. The 2026-08-30 d-pad-only rule keeps
  its bite where it was earned: the PERSONAL STATION, where the world is live.
- **SLOT 3 COULD MASK SLOT 4.** The d-pad block was `if (slot3) … else if
  (slot4)` with ONE edge latch: a slot-3 read that stays true (stock binds
  action slot 3 to the held weapon's altMode, `_zm.gsc:1836` — the read most
  exposed to weapon state) hid slot 4 for the whole panel: no edge, no right
  card, "my d-pad is frozen" in exactly the user's words. Both slots are now
  read independently with their own latches. Which weapon states, if any,
  pin slot 3 is UNPROVEN — the dev probe below is how the next repro settles
  it.
- **The dev input probe now prints the whole picture** once a second while a
  panel is up: `d3 d4 tac let | sel two lock pad ev` next to the old reads. On
  a dev run, hold d-pad right and read it: `d4=0` = the engine is not
  delivering the slot; `d4=1` with `sel` stuck = the lane; `sel=2` while the
  HUD highlights the left card = the Lua. The single-card refusal also names
  itself under `tod_dev`.
- Lockstep copy: the latch note in `wait_for_choice`, the draft's inlined
  latch comment, `CLAUDE.md` (the "only device-proving input" sentence carries
  the correction) and memory `bo3-menu-input-apis` all say the same thing now.
  The pause-menu legend and the hint plates still key their ART off the latch
  — a KBM player who tapped 3/4 sees pad glyphs; cosmetic, noted, unchanged.
- `-GscOnly`. UNPLAYED: first checks — KBM at a round event after tapping 3
  and 4: WASD still moves focus; pad at a round event: d-pad, LT/RT (or LB/RB
  on the default layout), R3 and X all move focus; station on a pad: d-pad and
  triggers only, as before.

## 2026-09-03 (v16.78) — PhD + Widow's Wine: the cascade's REAL cause (deferred grenade_fire), stamped children, and the PURPLE tell

User: *"The never ending phd web grenades still exist. I threw one and it never
stopped spreading. Also with phd the web nades need a purple glow and
explosion. Thats the whole point its both combined and the purple small glow
tells that"*.

- **WHY v16.70/v16.72 STILL CASCADED.** `MagicGrenadeType` RETURNS the child
  entity (stock reads that return: `_zm_craftables.gsc:883`), so the v16.70
  "last tracker wins" dedupe did run — and lost anyway: the engine raises
  `grenade_fire` for a script-launched grenade on a FOLLOWING frame, after the
  call has returned. The watcher's generation-1 tracker therefore arrived
  LAST, won the notify/endon dedupe, and every child was a fresh throw again:
  nova + ring, forever. Two builds, two assumptions about notify order, both
  wrong — the correction is to stop depending on order at all.
- **THE FIX** (`_tod_perk_phd.gsc`), three independent layers:
  (1) `phd_widow_split` STAMPS `child.tod_phd_gen` on the returned entity and
  the watcher SKIPS any stamped grenade (the deferred notify finds it tagged);
  (2) the split DECLARES its children first (`tod_phd_child_pending`, a
  500 ms window, `phd_child_seen`) so a notify raised inside the call is
  consumed as a child too; (3) `phd_grenade_track` never DOWNGRADES a stamp,
  so a stray generation-1 tracker on a child is a no-op. Thrown grenades are
  stamped 1 at the throw. DEV prints name every burst and every ring.
- **THE PURPLE TELL** (`TOD_PHD_WIDOW_GLOW`, `TOD_PHD_FX_*`): every combo
  grenade — the one thrown and each of the eight — wears a small purple trail
  in flight (`zombie/fx_trail_rpg_purple_doa`, looping, on a `tag_origin`
  host `LinkTo`'d to the grenade — the derez-burst host lane, since a bare
  server `PlayFXOnTag` on a weapon model is what the perk glow found does
  not draw); the thrown grenade's nova is a purple RPG blast

  `_zm_perk_widows_wine.gsc` has no nesting of any kind (checked the shipped

  is ours alone (v16.57) and so was the bug.

  `grenade_fire` on the player — an engine assumption nobody had watched

  guards its children by giving them a DIFFERENT weapon, never by trusting
  silence). Every child was a fresh lethal to the watcher: 6 more per
  burst per second, each with its own half-round-health flop nova.
  NOW the recursion is DECLARED: every tracked grenade carries its
  GENERATION (1 thrown, 2 its ring, 3 the ring's children), splits only
  below `TOD_PHD_WIDOW_DEPTH` (3 — the user's "3 levels max"), and each
  grenade has exactly ONE tracker (notify/endon pair on the grenade; the
  split threads the child's generation-tagged tracker AFTER
  `MagicGrenadeType` returns, so it outranks any tracker the watcher may
  have started for the same entity). Correct whether or not the engine
  raises `grenade_fire` for script-launched grenades — neither case is

  webs. Knobs: `TOD_PHD_WIDOW_CHILDREN` 6 at the first split,
  `TOD_PHD_WIDOW_CHILDREN_DEEP` 3 at the deeper one — 1 + 6 + 18 = 25
  grenades / 25 webs, the last generation ~1 s after the first burst, each
  ring at its own random phase so the webs carpet rather than stack.

  reading.** Both deal paths ask `tier_card_roll`, which returns true at
  `tod_luck_bar >= 100` with FULL eligibility, and both read the bar
  before it is spent. What can withhold the card while a player believes
  they qualify, in the order the deal tests them: in last stand; already
  tier 3; class gun not Pack-a-Punched BY NAME (or the free-PaP latch);
  a powerup gun in hand; and the FLOOR — tier 3 needs floor **30** since
  2026-09-02 (was 20), a floor-blocked draw is dealt LOCKED with the
  badge. NOTE the current build has `tod_dev` ON, which makes the tier
  roll 100% on every deal — no dev session can exercise the guarantee at

  `roll_options` deal and the maxed-player pre-roll in
  `run_upgrade_event`), naming the first failing rule, the floor
  shortfall, or "eligible; luck N/100 -> GUARANTEED / rolled at 20%".
  To do it without a second copy of the rules,
  `tier_card_ready_but_for_floor` is now the boolean view of the new
  `tier_not_ready_reason()` (one string per refusal, "" when ready) —
  zero behaviour change, one owner kept.

User (five reports, one session): *"Triggers in the class and upgrade system
are swapped i think. Left bumper goes right and right goes left"* / *"Im heavy
and Im seeing slasher icon on my HUD. But upgrade menu shows correctly"* /
*"PHD Flopper Widow's Wine combo doesn't work. Typically they will expand out

  (`_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc` wait_for_choice, `_tod_class_select.gsc`). Root cause
  read straight out of the user's own `players/bindings_0.cfg`: their layout
  puts AIM on the left bumper and FIRE on the right, and both menus mapped
  FIRE -> left card, AIM -> right card — which is only correct on a MOUSE
  (fire is the LEFT button there). Every pad layout puts fire on the right
  hand and aim on the left (default RT/LT, bumper-swapped RB/LB), so the pair
  is reversed on EVERY pad and the server cannot tell the devices apart

  pair has no such split: every BO3 layout keeps TACTICAL on the left-hand
  button and LETHAL on the right (default LB/RB, swapped LT/RT — the user's
  triggers), so TACTICAL = left / LETHAL = right is physically correct on every
  pad by construction and a stable key pair on keyboard. `SecondaryOffhand-
  ButtonPressed` / `FragButtonPressed` (both stock-used server builtins),
  always live — nobody holds a grenade button while fighting, and menu_freeze
  holds `DisableOffhandWeapons()` so a press can never throw. Fire/aim reads
  stay for the dev probe only. D-pad, stick (draft), melee/reload toggles and
  hold-to-lock unchanged. Plates (`tod_upgrade.lua`, `tod_class_select.lua`)
  now lead with `[{+smoke}]` / `[{+frag}]` bind tokens (engine-expanded per
  device); the flag-off text fallbacks say TACTICAL / LETHAL.

  order, or the reverse) make the index->char map a reversal, so the reversal
  gives every class its own icon under either reading. If a class still
  wears another's icon: report which saw which, permute again.
- **PhD + WIDOW'S WINE** (`_tod_perk_phd.gsc`, `TOD_PHD_WIDOW_*`): a holder of
  both perks throws a Widow's grenade that, at impact, fires the flop nova AND

  MAG SIZE is one of the six real weapon-variant ladders, so it RESETS on
  every tier promotion. Rarer draws + a REGULAR skew + a max of 3 means
  reaching +60% before the next promotion wipes it is now genuinely

  clear a crowd at any round, the down-flop keeps its full 1.0. Kill credit is
  the thrower's, so points / luck / elite rewards flow as for any grenade
  kill. The old `phd_explode` is now `phd_nova( v_burst, n_frac )` with the
  down-flop calling it at 1.0.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.45, tooling only, no build) — ART REQUEST PACKS: one doc, one tool, one zip (`tools/make_art_pack.ps1`, docs/73)

User, after the tier-gate badge came back hard to read: *"Lets finalize this
process of zipping up reference images and instructions. This makes it easier
where I can just send the zip to my asset generator and they can easily know
the task and goal."*

- **`tools/make_art_pack.ps1 <docs/NN_thing_art_prompt.md>`** builds
  `~/Downloads/tod_<name>_art_pack.zip` from the repo brief: the doc's
  `<!-- PACK:BEGIN -->..<!-- PACK:END -->` section becomes `INSTRUCTIONS.md`
  verbatim; the `<!-- art-pack -->` header names the pack, the `refs:` (the
  CURRENT shipped files to match, one-line role each -> `reference/` +
  a generated `reference/README.md`) and `preview:` WxH (every PNG ref
  downscaled to its real on-screen size -> `preview_onscreen_WxH/`, so the
  generator judges against what the player sees). Gates: refs must exist;
  an absolute path in INSTRUCTIONS FAILS (the generator cannot open it);
  repo-internal words WARN; a ref never named in a prompt WARNs; a preview
  whose aspect is not the source's is skipped (a stretched preview teaches
  the wrong thing). PNG headers are read and reported.
- **`-Inspect 'files (N).zip'`** for the drop: extracts (nested zips too) and
  prints size / colour type / md5 / IDENTICAL-to-repo vs REPLACES vs NEW NAME
  (which needs GDT + zone + Lua wiring). Installs nothing: LOOK first.
- **docs/73 (tier-gate legibility re-bake)** is the first brief in the format
  and the worked example; the pack that went out was regenerated from it by
  the tool and matches the hand-built one file for file. Until now every
  pack was hand-zipped and the flow lived only inside individual prompt docs
  (four peer sessions had to be polled to reconstruct it today).
- CLAUDE.md gains the "ART REQUEST PACKS" section; memory
  `art-request-pack-recipe` points at the tool. The script is pure ASCII on
  purpose: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less file in the ANSI codepage,
  and an em-dash inside a string decodes to a right-quote that CLOSES the
  string - the first run died on exactly that.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.37) — THE SPIRE KEEPS YOUR BUILD: no max-upgrade grant, PERMA PERKS, trial wins deal the cards

User: *"defeating the map and going to the endless spire will give you max
upgrades lets remove that. You will keep what upgrades you have. Instead it
will give you perma perks. You will get all the perks and then also keep them
even when you die. Also that means you must be given the max perk bottle
upgrade so that one we can gift. When you beat a trial you will get an
upgrade. Thats how you will continue upgrading your class. We should have no
alters on the spire."*

- `_tod_spire.gsc` **`grant_all` rewritten.** Ascension now hands out: PERK
  SLOTS (id 40) to its cap (`grant_perk_slots` — the same `tod_levels` field
  + `tod_upg_sync` the card picker uses), EVERY PERK the map sells
  (`perma_perks_give`, the live scatter roster), full ammo, full health. GONE:
  the T3 promotion, the free-PaP latch, the sidearm PaP, every domain at its
  cap, and the luck-bar zeroing (the bar drives the trial deals' rarity now).
  The class-tier floor stamp (`mark_top_reached`) stays so a tier card won in
  a trial is never floor-refused.
- **PERMA PERKS.** Stock strips perks on a down (`perk_think`); the keeper
  `perma_perks_watch` (one per player, latched) re-gives the roster 0.5 s
  after every `player_revived`, and a new `callback::on_spawned`
  (`on_spire_spawned`, a no-op until `level.tod_spire_active`) covers the
  bleed-out → respawn and the late joiner / reconnect (perk slots + perks +
  keeper). Deliberately NOT stock's `_retain_perks`: `onPlayerSpawned` zeroes
  `num_perks` every spawn and a retained perk would sit outside the count with
  its give-thread dead; take → give through `zm_perks::give_perk` re-runs
  every perk's give hook (Jugg's max health, PhD / Cherry / Wisp Tea).
  **SOLO QUICK REVIVE IS A LIFE, NOT A PERK:** stock consumes it on the
  self-revive, so the revive/spawn lane withholds it in solo (`b_qr` false via
  `use_solo_revive`) or a down would refund the life it just spent and a solo
  spire could never end. It comes back on ascension and on every WON TRIAL
  (`trial_grant_perks`, now a thin wrapper over the perma lane) — one free
  life per trial, which is what the v16.21 grant already amounted to.
- **TRIAL WIN = AN UPGRADE.** `trial_win` threads `trial_upgrade_deal`: 3 s
  after the sting, `tod_upgrades::run_upgrade_event()` — the REAL round-event
  deal (participant filter, world pause, luck floor, tier card at its odds).
  The round clock stays suppressed on the spire (`tod_upgrades_suppressed`,
  comment corrected), so a won trial is the spire's ONLY upgrade source.
- **"No altars on the spire" — already true, verified, nothing removed:** the
  upgrade stations are base (id 0), the four breathers (1-4) and the crown
  altar (5) only (`station_spawn`); the spire's vendors are the hub
  Pack-a-Punch, the crates and the migrated perk machines (generator
  `SP_FURN` = pap / crate / perk_e / perk_w). PaP stays: a tier card needs
  the class gun PaP'd, and the party no longer arrives packed.
- `_tod_upgrades.gsc`: `perk_slot_limit`'s v14.60 spire floor stays as a belt
  under the new braces (comment says why). Docs: CLAUDE.md spire bullet,
  `docs/44` §decisions note, `spire_wip/HARNESS.md` + `WIRING.md` ladder
  lines.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.36) — RUN AND GUN REQUIRES SPRINT FIRE: domain prerequisites

User: *"you can unlock a lot of sprinting things like shoot while running
reduces ammo shot and things. But you may not have the upgrade that allows
shooting while running. Can we sequence it correct where you cant get those
specific upgrades until you have [sprint fire]"*.

The skirmisher could draw RUN AND GUN (id 23 — free shots + damage while
moving) before owning SPRINT FIRE (id 21 — the card that lets the gun fire
mid-sprint at all). The card was not dead (the "moving" test also passes on a
run-speed hip-fire) but it paid for a thing the player could not yet do.

- `_tod_upgrades.gsc`: a domain PREREQUISITE lane. `add_domain` stamps
  `d.requires = undefined`; `set_requires( key, prereq_key )` names the domain
  the player must own (≥1 level) before `key` can roll; `domain_available`
  checks it before the class test, so every lane that asks that question —
  `eligible_pool` (the deal + the luck-floor redeal), `player_has_domains_left`
  (the station's "anything to sell?"), the deferred-card revalidation, and both
  grant-all loops — agrees. `set_requires` checks at init that the prerequisite
  is registered BEFORE its dependent, because the two grant-all loops
  (`dev_grant_maxed`, `_tod_spire`'s ascension grant) walk registration order
  and would otherwise skip the dependent on the one pass they get.
- Installed: `set_requires( "runandgun", "sprintfire" )`. Both are scope
  "class" (survive a promotion together), so a tier-up can never strand a RUN
  AND GUN level behind a reset SPRINT FIRE.

User: *"Downloaded. Implement and let me know what other things we can do to

something and then they lock in ... once they lock in a class we will know

**THE ASSETS (files (96).zip, all four from the docs/69 §5 brief):**

and `i_tod_hint_switch_kbm` re-baked with `/ [F]` (the flag-off look), and

`source_data/tod_ui_images/_images`, two GDT entries cloned from their style
references, two `image,` zone lines. Full build (a `.gdt` edit is always a
full build).

**THE OVERLAY (docs/69 §6, now real): `USE_HINT_FRAME_ART = true` in
`tod_upgrade.lua` and `tod_class_select.lua`.** The switch plate is the blank
frame (drawn 320×49 / 300×46 — aspect held, room for two lines) with two LUI
text lines over it, and the plate under the focused card is the frame with one
line; every string carries the engine's `[{+bind}]` tokens and is set through
`Engine.Localize` at SHOW time (the expansion happens when the string is set).
KBM: `SWITCH: [{+attack}] / [{+speed_throw}] / [{+melee}] / D-PAD` over
`LOCK: HOLD [{+gostand}] / [{+activate}]`; card: `HOLD [{+gostand}] /
[{+activate}] TO LOCK`. Once the d-pad latch has fired (CoD.TodPad):
`SWITCH: D-PAD` / `LOCK: HOLD [{+gostand}]` / `HOLD [{+gostand}] TO LOCK`.
Every show/hide site in both menus now goes through ONE writer each
(`ShowSwitchPlate( on )`, `CardHint( card, mode, a )`) so the frame path and
the baked path cannot disagree; the LOCKED plate stays baked under both (it
names no key). Flag off = the re-baked keyed plates, unchanged behaviour.

**WHY THIS ANSWERS THE LOCK-IN QUESTION.** The server cannot tell which device
locked a class: the lock buttons are JUMP and USE, and both exist on both
devices (A/X on a pad, SPACE/F on a keyboard), so a lock-in proves nothing —
the only device-proving input the server will ever see is the d-pad
(`ActionSlotThree/Four`, which no keyboard key binds). So "detect until they
lock in, then freeze" would freeze on a guess. The overlay does better than
any lock-in: the ENGINE knows the device and the binds, it redraws the plate
for the live device at every render, and it keeps doing so for the whole
match — a player who swaps devices mid-run is right again at the next plate.
The d-pad latch survives ONLY as the hidden input gate (pad = d-pad-only
switching, the v14.20 rule) and, on the plate, to shorten the line once the
pad is proven. D-PAD is named on the pre-latch line on purpose: a pad player
who reads "SWITCH: [RT] / [LT] / [R3]" would use those, never press the
d-pad, and keep the shared lanes live at the station — the exact awkwardness
v14.20 gated. The draft's old "D-PAD / STICK" wording is gone: the stick
reads ~0 under the menu freeze on both devices (the v10.20 research), so it
never was a lane.

(`USE_TOD_CTL_HEADER_ART`, text header kept as the fallback); the live-bind
line moved down 4 px under it.

**UNVERIFIED IN GAME.** Boot is what the build proves. The four bind names

## 2026-09-02 (v16.31) — ATHLETE: the slide-jump launch was the ENGINE; jump_max_velocity and jump_height now follow the slider just-in-time

User, after playing v16.28: *"When jumping out of my slide im launching. We
need a creative way to keep the speed of the player throught the slide jump
with calculations or something ... Still feels like i slide then jump and my
jump is launching me in the direction. Like its a stutter step and randomly
gain speed"* — and, to be clear: *"this really only needs to apply to players
with athlete. I have no complains about how it works without athlete."*
Record: `docs/62` §9.9.

### The finding

`jump_max_velocity` ("The max velocity of the players jump if they enter it
from a slide") is the speed the engine LAUNCHES a slide-jump at, capped by the
dvar — not a clamp on the slider's own speed, which is how v16.1 read it when
it set 1000. The complaint pattern is the proof: default → "you slow down a
ton" (v16); 1000 with a one-frame-late script cut → "kind of speed boosts"
(v16.21); 1000 with the cut removed → "launching … stutter step … randomly
gain speed" (v16.28). Treyarch's table has no separate boost dvar (checked).

### The fix — THE JUST-IN-TIME RULE (`_tod_athlete.gsc` lane 1)

A global movement dvar becomes per-player if it is written from the one
player who is in the state that consumes it, every frame of that state, and
rested otherwise. Every SLIDING tick of an athlete now publishes
`jump_max_velocity` = that player's current horizontal speed and
`jump_height` = the engine's base height × (1 + 0.25·Lv); the first
non-sliding tick publishes zeros; the landing stumble (`jump_slowdownEnable`)
is off while any athlete is airborne. An arbiter (`jit_update`) takes the MAX
over everyone in the state and writes only on change; when nobody is, every
dvar rests at the engine's PRISTINE default (captured once per Steam session
into `tod_ath_orig_*`; a session that ran v16.1..v16.28 captures the poisoned
1000 — the dev print says POISONED; restart the game once).

- A jump straight out of a slide now has ZERO script writes: the engine
  launches at the slide speed and the level's height, client-predicted. The
  vz multiply survives for run / stand-up / hop jumps only.
- The other three classes get STOCK slide-jumps and the stock landing stumble
  back — v16.1/v16.2 had changed both for the whole map, untested by anyone
  but the slasher. User: "All these changes are for the athlete upgrade."
- Co-op exposure: a non-athlete slide-jumping inside an athlete's ~0.5 s
  slide, or landing inside an athlete's ~1 s flight, gets the athlete's
  numbers. Accepted, documented.
- Edge insurance kept for slide-jumps only (cut above +15%, restore below
  −40%), to be measured: the jump line now prints `jmv=` and `jh=`, and
  `launch=B>A` with B == A is the success signature. `TOD_ATH_JUMP_VZ_MAX`
  520 (the JIT height at Lv5 launches at ~375).

### Page, records

`docs/armory.html`: ATHLETE note prepended; the two engine Knobs rows
rewritten for the JIT lanes (`TOD_MOVE_SLIDE_JUMP_TRACK / _REST /
_HEIGHT_JIT`, `TOD_MOVE_LAND_STUMBLE_OFF`); the jump-edge row updated.
`docs/62` §9.9; the movement-levers memory carries the semantics and the rule.
`tod_dev` / `tod_god` STILL ARMED.

UNPLAYED. If the launch still stutters, the `slide` jump lines answer it in
one glance: `B >> J` means the dvar is not taking effect on this host and the
whole lane is moot; `B == J == P` with the stutter still felt means the stutter
is the engine's own stand-up.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.29) — KBM audit: every cursor-hint card said "F"; the engine now draws the bound key

User: *"probably half our player base is KBM ... make sure the button and
assets can properly reflect the input ... Assets are quite important ...
Players read and rely on them more than I would think. Whether its assets
generated as png or LUA."*

**THE BUG: EVERY PROMPT CARD HARDCODED A LITERAL "F".** The vendored Aetherium
kit draws its cursor-hint footer as three elements — `"Hold "` + `"F"` +
`"To Buy"` — and the `"F"` is a string literal in all eight `Prompts/*.lua`
(the comment beside it says "reactive to button binding"; it never was). So
every CONTROLLER player read "Hold F To Buy" at every door, perk, crate,
teleporter and finale buy, and every keyboard player who rebound USE (E is the
common one) was told the wrong key. Map 1 shipped the identical literal; the
kit repo has it too. The `[{+activate}]` token the GSC hint carries — the thing
the engine resolves into the device's bound key or pad glyph — was stripped by
PromptDefault's parser and replaced with the literal.

**THE FIX: LET THE ENGINE DRAW THE KEY.** Each card's footer is now ONE `UIText`
set to `Engine.Localize( "Hold ^3[{+activate}]^7 <verb>" )` — the stock idiom —
through a per-card `SetFooter( self, verb )`, re-called on every hint update so
a mid-match device swap or rebind is right at the next prompt. One element, not
three, because the expansion's width is not ours to know (pad glyph, "F",
"MOUSE3", "SPACE") and inline flow can never overlap the verb. Evidence that LUI
text expands the token, since no stock Lua is readable on this box: the v14.58
raw-write bug poured the untouched hint through exactly this call into a
`UIText` and the user transcribed the result as "HoldXAMMOCRATE" — an X, the
pad glyph, not the token and not an F; and every stock zombies hint reaches the
screen through the same pipeline with its key gold and device-correct. Eight
files: Default, Doors, Perks, PAP, PowerSwitch (the five `classifyHint()` can
route to) plus MysteryBox, BBG, WallBuy (unreachable here; patched so no
literal key survives in `Prompts/`).

**PAUSE MENU: UPGRADE CARDS controls legend** (`AetheriumStartMenu.lua`, under
the button list, y 576–611). The card panels' plates are baked with DEFAULT
binds; this is the one place the LIVE binds are readable:
`SWITCH: [{+attack}] [{+speed_throw}] or [{+melee}]  LOCK: HOLD [{+gostand}] or
[{+activate}]` (pad, after the latch: `SWITCH: D-PAD  LOCK: HOLD [{+gostand}]`).
It is also the first in-game proof of which bind NAMES the engine expands —
`+activate` is proven, the other four are the standard names and unproven here;
if any renders literally, that name is wrong and the frame-plate art must not
use it.

**AUDIT SIGN-OFF (docs/69):** the card-menu input lanes are KBM-complete and
edge-latched (MOUSE1/MOUSE2/V/R switch, hold SPACE/F lock, both menus); the
plates default to KEYBOARD and flip to pad on the server-proven d-pad press;
the latch receiver is provably open before the draft's first press (upgrade HUD
opens 0.05 s after the blackscreen flag, the draft panel 0.5 s after); the
pause menu takes mouse and keyboard. Three gaps remain, all in the baked
plates: default binds only, Xbox glyphs only, pad plate only after a d-pad
press. All three close with ONE new asset (`i_tod_hint_frame`, a blank plate)
plus the token-overlay path specified in docs/69 §6 — deliberately NOT written
dormant, because it cannot be tested without the art and the bind names are
unproven until the pause legend has been seen. One known one-way stays: a
player who latches the pad and then switches to keyboard keeps d-pad-only
switching (lock still works on SPACE/F); no server-side device read exists.

**Build:** packed by session 79's `-GscOnly` at 10:55:23 (its sync ran after
the last Lua edit; freshness diff on scripts/zone_source/ui empty, nothing
deployed newer than the `.ff`). Boot-verified only; the glyph rendering is

pad (expect the pad glyph), and the pause legend.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.28) — ATHLETE: fresh-eyes review, six fixes — aiming never moves you, the front hemisphere is free, the edge rule can no longer refund friction

User: *"Okay so we have all the optimizations possible on this system? Shall we
think more about what we did and if it makes sense? Maybe fresh eyes."* Then:
*"Do what ever players would find intuitive and a bit beyond that to make it
fun."* An independent reviewer read `_tod_athlete.gsc` cold; eleven findings,
six fixed, one rejected on evidence, the rest turned into trace measurements.
Record: `docs/62` §9.8.

### The six (`_tod_athlete.gsc`)

1. **The edge rule was still a boost lane.** `pre` is up to 50 ms old and
   landing friction bleeds ~20% per 50 ms, so the ±15% band refunded speed a
   hop had honestly lost, one frame after launch. The restore now fires only
   on a SLIDE-jump whose launch is >40% under the slide speed
   (`TOD_ATH_EDGE_CLAMP`) — a shortfall only the engine clamp can produce. The
   "boost cut" branch is gone (nothing live can throw a mid-air impulse).
2. **A jump edge needs a jump press** inside 100 ms (`TOD_ATH_JUMP_LATCH_MS`).
   A ramp-crest hop while sprinting up a flight, or a mantle ending airborne,
   no longer gets the height pop; such an edge is traced **"nojump"** and left
   alone — and that line is the measurement of whether crest hops exist.
3. **A bunny hop inside one server frame is seen.** Land-and-rejump between
   two ticks shows no grounded tick; a sudden vz rise (`TOD_ATH_HOP_DVZ`) is
   now an edge ("hop") with its own height and a fresh cone anchor.
4. **Forward/back never steer** (`TOD_ATH_AIR_STEER_FWD` 0). With the full
   stick, holding W and glancing at a zombie rotated your momentum toward it,
   and holding S swung the line through sideways before it pointed back — off
   the side of a flight. A horde game is hopping away while shooting behind
   you, so aiming must not move you. The strafe axis steers, relative to the
   view: push left, curve left of where you look. One flag brings "fly where
   you look" back.
5. **The free cone is the front hemisphere** (`TOD_ATH_AIR_CONE_DEG` 180, was
   120): every spiral landing is a 90° turn and the old cone taxed it 16% each.
   The cap is a pure function of the current deviation — the "only ever falls"
   ratchet is gone (trimmed speed was never refunded anyway, so it only ever
   punished a glance). A U-turn still bleeds: 120° 78% · 150° 57% · 180° 35%.
6. **A 3° deadband** (`TOD_ATH_AIR_DEADBAND`): no write when you already fly
   where you push. Fewer corrections for the client to smooth, far fewer for a
   remote client in co-op. The mantle guard also leaves `was_ground` false.

**Rejected after checking:** "a Lv2 jump clears the 56-unit parapet" — every
lap rail on the tower AND the spire carries a `RAIL_CAP_H` 112 clip cap

## 2026-09-02 (v16.24) — ATHLETE: THE MOMENTUM CONE, the air-steer rate walked back, and why there is no 10 ms poll

User, after playing v16.23: *"its for sure comical. But we know its possible.
Now its about smoothing it out and making it make sense. I would say they
should be able to keep max momentum up to 120 degrees in front of them. And we
need to poll every 10ms for smoothness. Yeah issue right now is that i can
slide and then go backwards max speed. Obviously that doesnt make sense. So we
can tweak it while keeping it fun and slight exaggeration on physics."*
Record: `docs/62` §9.7.

### The cone (`_tod_athlete.gsc` lane 4, `air_retain`)

Every air episode is ANCHORED on the heading and speed it began with (the
first airborne tick — a jump after the edge rule has run, or a ledge drop).
While the current heading is within ±60° of the anchor (`TOD_ATH_AIR_CONE_DEG`
120) the launch speed is kept in full; past it a CAP falls linearly to
`TOD_ATH_AIR_REVERSE_KEEP` 0.35 of the launch speed at a full reversal (90°
84% · 120° 68% · 150° 51% · 180° 35%). The cap only ever FALLS inside an
episode (speed shed in a turn is not refunded by turning back), never under
`TOD_ATH_AIR_CAP_FLOOR` 200 u/s (walking pace — a standing jump can still be
steered by the engine's own air control), trims the engine's own small
airborne additions too ("keep velocity" means exactly that), and RE-ANCHORS
when something external throws the speed past ×`TOD_ATH_AIR_REANCHOR` 1.25 in
one tick (a boss fling is never fought). Measured against the LAUNCH heading,
not the view — a view-relative cone would have kept the exact reported case
(look back, push forward, full speed backwards).

### The rate

`TOD_ATH_AIR_TURN_BASE` 120 + `TOD_ATH_AIR_TURN_PER_LV` 60 per level =
180/240/300/360/420 deg/s = 9..21° per server frame, scaled by the stick
magnitude (a half-pushed stick turns at half the rate; a keyboard reads 1).
v16.23's 360/Lv wrote up to 90° per frame and zigzagged.

### "Poll every 10 ms" — not available, recorded so it is not re-asked of the code

`shared.gsh:264 SERVER_FRAME .05`: every script `wait` rounds up to the 50 ms
server frame, the T7 API doc has no faster wait, and Treyarch's dvar table has
no server tick-rate dvar. The client's `cg_errorDecay` ("Decay for predicted
error") is what hides server corrections, and it is a client dvar T7 gives no
server lane to set. Smoothness is therefore the step per frame, which is what
the rate ladder now bounds.

### Text, page, records

- `tod_upgrade.lua` DETAIL[43].act → "air steer N deg/s; full momentum within
  120 deg ahead" (N = 120 + 60·Lv, LOCKSTEP with the two GSC constants).
- `docs/armory.html`: ATHLETE row (eff / lad / tune / note) and the two air
  Knobs rows rewritten; `verify_armory_constants.js` green.
- `_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc` domain_id comment; `docs/62` §9.7; the movement-levers
  memory carries the server-frame floor and the cone rule.
- Trace: the jump line ends `dev=D keep=K%` (widest deviation from the launch
  heading, momentum the cone left). `tod_dev` / `tod_god` STILL ARMED.

UNPLAYED. The two "make sense" numbers to retune from feel are
`TOD_ATH_AIR_REVERSE_KEEP` and the half-cone; the smoothness number is the rate
ladder.

## 2026-09-02 (v16.23) — ATHLETE: the boost was the script carry; momentum preserved, never added; COMICAL AIR STEERING

User, after playing v16.21 (the armed spire harness, ATHLETE Lv5): *"athlete is
not so smooth. It kind of speed boosts when you jump out of a slide which is
exactly the issue I was worried about. It also needs more aerial handling
meaning you can keep velocity but change directions in the air very very
easily. And that handling increases with each level."* Then, mid-task: *"The
air handling should be comical for now. Like you are air steering and flying
thats how crazy. We should be able to tweak after but I want us to get comical
just so i can see the actual differences. Smoothness should not be comical."*
Record: `docs/62` §9.

### Where the boost came from — no dev numbers needed

v16.1 lifted the engine's slide-jump clamp (`jump_max_velocity` 1000, KEPT) and
then ALSO kept map 1's script carry as belt-and-braces: a grounded PRE-JUMP
TOP-UP (jump button down inside a 500 ms window after the slide → scale the
player back UP to the slide's last speed) and, on the jump edge, a raise-only
RESTORE to that speed plus three raise-only airborne re-asserts. With the clamp
gone those lanes had nothing left to restore — every action left to them was a
speed INCREASE, delivered one server frame after the launch. A player who let
the slide end, lost speed on the stand-up frames and then jumped was
re-accelerated to full slide speed *at* the jump: the reported symptom,
verbatim. **Rule for the KB: a correction lane must be able to CUT as well as
RAISE, or it is a boost lane with a nicer name.** The whole carry is gone
(grace window, top-up, braked floor, re-asserts, `restore_speed`).

### `_tod_athlete.gsc` — the v16.23 lanes (one `SetVelocity` per tick at most)

- **Lane 1, ENGINE (global), unchanged:** `jump_max_velocity` 1000 and the
  landing stumble off.
- **Lane 2, SLIDE START (per player):** velocity = BASE × (1 + 0.10·Lv),
  raise-only, one-shot. **CLEAN-ENTRY RULE:** on a slide entered from a normal
  speed (previous tick ≤ `TOD_ATH_CLEAN_ENTRY` 440 u/s) BASE is the engine's own
  start speed and is remembered as the player's reference; on a fast entry (a
  slide-hop landing rolled into a slide) BASE is the reference. So the chain
  slide → hop → land → slide → hop rides at REF × (1+0.10·Lv) whether the engine
  assigns `slide_speedBase` or carries the entry speed into the slide — v16.1
  multiplied whatever the engine started at and, under the second reading,
  compounded 1.5ⁿ up to the 800 wall.
- **Lane 3, THE JUMP EDGE (per player):** the launch must be within ±15%
  (`TOD_ATH_EDGE_TOL`) of the speed on the last grounded tick, sliding or not.
  Inside the band NOTHING is written — the launch is the engine's own,
  client-predicted, smooth. Below it the engine clamped (lane 1 off or
  unreplicated) and the pre-jump speed is written back; above it something
  boosted, and it is written back too. No grace window, no floor, no
  re-assert: with nothing to add there is nothing to time.
- **Lane 4, AIR STEERING (per player, NEW):** every airborne tick the velocity
  HEADING rotates toward the movement stick (`GetNormalizedMovement` — the left
  stick / WASD; proven live input by the 2026-08-21 card-focus experiment,
  which flipped focus per tick with the player's velocity pinned to ~0) by up
  to `TOD_ATH_AIR_TURN_PER_LV` × Lv × 0.05 s, magnitude untouched: **360 deg/s
  per level = 18/36/54/72/90° per server frame; Lv5 reverses in 100 ms.**
  Comical by request; the ladder is the one knob. No stick = no rotation.
  Left/right sign rests on the class-draft stick lane, never live-verified on
  its own: `TOD_ATH_AIR_RIGHT_SIGN` exists for that doubt and the trace prints
  the stick with the largest turn step.
- **Jump height** unchanged (z × sqrt(1+0.25·Lv) on the edge, ≤50 ms late by
  nature — the one script discontinuity left in the loop).

**The client-predicted steering lane is DEAD, recorded so nobody re-researches
it:** the engine's own air accelerate rides the move-speed scale, which the
client predicts — but that scale ALSO drives ground acceleration and is still
in force on the landing frames until the server sees the landing (≤50 ms). At
the ×5..×10 an air-steer feature needs, those frames are a landing rocket
toward the stick. `doubleJump_accel` / `doubleJump_speed` exist in Treyarch's
table but belong to the `doublejump_enabled 0` system. `SetPlayerGravity`
pre-armed does NOT raise a jump (the engine derives launch vz from gravity —
same apex, slower); set after launch it stretches the rise by the full height
factor: the floaty "hang time" lever if "flying" ever needs it.

### Text, art, page

- `tod_upgrade.lua` DOMAIN[43].desc → "slide faster, jump higher, steer in the
  air"; DETAIL[43].act is now a FUNCTION of the level (the CLASS TIER row's
  idiom, `CoD.TodDomainDesc` pcalls it): "air steer N deg/s; always on,
  survives promotion". LOCKSTEP: the 360 there = `TOD_ATH_AIR_TURN_PER_LV`.
- `_tod_upgrades.gsc` add_domain desc + comment; `_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc`
  domain_id comment.
- Card art STAYS (docs/57 addendum): it was baked level-agnostic and
  numberless, and a mid-air direction change is the same idea. An optional
  re-bake prompt with a bending trail is in docs/57 for when the user wants
  the art to show the new half.
- `docs/armory.html`: ATHLETE row rewritten (eff / lad / tune / note), three
  new Knobs rows (air steer, edge band, clean entry), the launch-ceiling row
  reworded. `verify_armory_constants.js` 31/31, `verify_armory_domains.js` OK.

### Trace (tod_dev is STILL ARMED from v16.21 — this build prints)

`ATH slide eng=E set=S next=N end=Z Tms clean=C ref=R` and `ATH jump slide|run
pre=P launch=B>A vz=V minair=M air=Nt turn=T/Smax stick=F,R land=L +300ms=Q`.
`B == A` means the momentum rule wrote nothing (the engine launch was already
right); `Smax` should read ≤ 90 at Lv5; if pushing LEFT turns you RIGHT, flip
`TOD_ATH_AIR_RIGHT_SIGN`. Full reading guide in `docs/62` §9.5. Note the
harness grants ATHLETE Lv5 outright, so this build shows Lv5 vs none — the
per-level differences need a run that earns the card.

  stays mapped** in `domain_id()` and in the Lua DOMAIN/DETAIL tables

  `killreload_kills_needed()` and the three `TOD_KILLRELOAD_KILLS_LV*` defines.

## 2026-09-01 (v16.9) — Endless Spire rounds turn over ~2x faster: the spawn BUDGET is halved

User: *"Can you make sure the endless spire cycles through round a bit faster.
I played and each round was like 15 minutes. We need to triple the speed"* —
then, before the first test: *"Make it 1/2 and not 1/3"*. The divisor shipped
at 3 for one build and is **2** now; the mechanism below is unchanged.

**Why the existing knob could not do it.** The spire already ran its spawn
trickle at the 0.18 s floor (v14.0). Under the endless twist a round ends when
its budget is SPENT, and stock `round_spawning` stalls on
`level.zombie_ai_limit` (45) whenever that many zombies stand — so once the
party cannot out-kill the cap, round time = budget ÷ kill rate and the trickle
floor is irrelevant. Stock's budget past round 10 grows as round²
(`get_zombie_count_for_round`): round 40 is 168 zombies solo and 888 for four,
round 50 is 249 / 1374. A party ascends at round 30-60, and each spire round
was asking for that many kills of 40k-HP zombies. That is the 15 minutes.

**The change.** `_tod_endless_rounds::tod_max_zombies` is installed on stock's
own `level.max_zombie_func` hook (stock only defaults it when undefined, and
nothing else in the tree assigns it). It returns stock's curve verbatim
everywhere except while `tod_spire_active`, where it divides the round total
by **`TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_DIV` 2** (floor `TOD_SPIRE_BUDGET_MIN` 12, so a dev
ascension at round 2 does not roll rounds on a handful of zombies). Spawn
delay, `zombie_ai_limit`, `zombie_actor_limit`, elite roofs and the honour
guard are untouched: as many stand at once as before, the round just asks for
half as many.

**The round already running at ascension** would have kept the tower's full
budget, because stock stamps `zombie_total` once at the top of each round —
the same trap the v14.0 live test hit with the spawn delay. `_tod_spire::ascend`
now re-resolves the budget through the hook (already at spire size by then)
and clamps the unspent remainder to it, right after the 0.18 direct write.

**What follows by construction.** `_tod_luck` normalizes luck-per-kill on the
same hook, so a spire kill pays 2x the luck and a full clear still lands +40
(the fair-share invariant holds). `_tod_doors`' party-size ratio resolves
through it too and is unchanged by a uniform divisor. Upgrade events (every 4
rounds) and the +0.28%/round speed curve arrive 2x sooner in wall-clock terms,
which docs/44 §6a already names as the intended compounding.

Files: `_tod_endless_rounds.gsc` (new `#using zombie_utility`, the two defines,
`tod_max_zombies`, the init hook), `_tod_spire.gsc` (new `#using _zm`, the
ascension clamp), docs/44 §6a, CLAUDE.md spire bullet. `-GscOnly` build.
**Untested in game** — the user's next spire run is the measurement; if rounds
still drag, the divisor is the one number to move.

## 2026-09-01 (v16.2) — landing stumble OFF (forward velocity after the jump)

User, clarifying v16.1 before testing anything: *"I'm actually more concerned
about forward velocity rather than the jump velocity ... Forward velocity after
sliding and jumping. It's the forward velocity that causes clunkiness."*

Nothing in v16.1 was vertical except the pre-existing height multiply, but one
FORWARD-speed loss had been left in place on purpose: the engine's landing
stumble (`jump_slowdownEnable` — "Slow player movement after jumping"), wired
behind `TOD_MOVE_LAND_STUMBLE_OFF` and shipped OFF as a whole-map change nobody
had asked for. The steer makes it the obvious next lever — it costs forward
speed on every landing, and ATHLETE's higher jumps land harder — so it is now
ON: `SetDvar( "jump_slowdownEnable", 0 )`, probe-first like the clamp lift, the
exact write Treyarch makes in ZM's own old-school mode
(`zm/gametypes/_globallogic.gsc:191`). GLOBAL, every class. If the dev print
shows `jump_slowdownEnable = 0` with no "(was 1)", ZM never had the stumble and
the write was a harmless no-op. The trace's `land=L +300ms=P` pair measures the
result either way.

The forward-velocity chain through the loop, and which lever now owns each link:
slide start (lane 2 multiply) → slide→jump launch (lane 1 clamp lift, lane 3
carry + re-asserts) → airborne (engine: no horizontal decel) → landing (this
switch; then the engine's own friction bleeds the excess toward sprint speed,
which is the natural decel) → slide-out / re-sprint (`slide_out*`,
`sprint_rampIn` — still stock, defaults unknown until the print is read).

## 2026-09-01 (v16.1) — ATHLETE: the slide-jump rebuilt from the engine up

User, after playing v16 in the armed dev build: *"the velocity of a character is
clunky when running and sliding and jump ... that slide speed boost never
transfers momentum properly to the jump so you slow down a ton ... make the
player experience as smooth as possible with the Slasher class."* And of map 1's
version of the same mechanic: *"still very clunky ... think from a new lens and
perspective to make ours perfect."* Research record: `docs/62_slasher_movement_research.md`.

### What the engine does to a slide-jump (the part nobody had read)

Treyarch's own dvar table — recovered from the string table in
`<tools>\bin\cod2map64.exe`, descriptions verbatim — names every discontinuity
in the run → slide → jump → land loop:

| dvar | Treyarch's description |
|---|---|
| `jump_max_velocity` | "The max velocity of the players jump if they enter it from a slide" |
| `slide_outSpeedScale` / `slide_outShouldScaleSpeed` / `slide_outAllowSprint` | "Scale down your movement speed by this when exiting a slide" / "... during the slide out" / "Allow sprinting during the slide out" |
| `slide_subsequentSlideScale` / `slide_subsequentSlideTime` | spam-slide speed penalty |
| `jump_slowdownEnable` | "Slow player movement after jumping" — stock ZM turns it OFF only in `scr_oldschool` (`zm/gametypes/_globallogic.gsc:191`) |
| `slide_speedBase` | "The slide start speed if no player energy" — ZM disables player energy, so the slide's start speed is an ENGINE CONSTANT |

**THE ROOT: the engine clamps the launch of a jump entered from a slide, on the
client, at full frame rate, before any script runs.** v16 (map 1's design)
noticed one server frame later and wrote the speed back — that is the dip-then-
jerk. And on a strong ATHLETE it did not fire at all: `restore_speed()` bailed
at its own 0.5 braked-player floor whenever the clamp cut more than half the
speed, which is exactly the strong-slide case the upgrade exists to create.
"Never transfers momentum" was literally true from about Lv3.

**The defaults of that family are not readable from any file on this box** (the
retail exe hashes dvar names; no public dump carries them — `jump_max_velocity`
IS in the T7Overcharged retail hash list, so it is registered). They are now
PRINTED by every dev build; see below.

### The rebuild — three lanes, each doing the one thing only it can do

- **Lane 1, ENGINE (global):** `jump_max_velocity` → 1000 via probe-first
  absolute `SetDvar` (stock precedent `_zm.gsc:218-224`; map 1's two traps
  honoured — an unregistered name is skipped, never scaled from the live value).
  Zero correction latency because the engine simply stops clamping. ⚠️ GLOBAL:
  every class's slide-jump keeps its speed now; what stays ATHLETE-only is the
  MAGNITUDE. `jump_slowdownEnable 0` (the landing stumble) is wired the same
  way behind `TOD_MOVE_LAND_STUMBLE_OFF` and shipped OFF — a whole-map feel
  change the user has not asked for; the trace measures the post-landing
  profile so that call can be made on numbers. Co-op replication of this
  family is a strong inference from stock's own `doublejump_enabled` writes,
  not a proof — test in co-op; the tell is non-host rubber-banding.
- **Lane 2, SLIDE (per player):** on the first sliding tick, horizontal
  velocity × (1 + 0.10·Lv). One lane, one number, literally the spec, correct
  whether or not the engine derives slide speed from the move-speed scale. The
  v16 "+0.10 scale while IsSliding()" flag lane is RETIRED (`athlete_slide_bonus`
  and the `tod_athlete_sliding` flag are gone from `_tod_upgrades.gsc`): the
  engine's slide is not input-driven, so a scale term could not honestly be
  slide speed, and two lanes for one number was a double-count waiting to
  happen. The v16 slide-start kick (+50 u/s/Lv) is folded into the multiply —
  it was the part of v16 that actually moved the slide, and it over-paid the
  spec at high levels.
- **Lane 3, CARRY (per player):** the direct slide-jump (jump edge within 150 ms
  of the last sliding tick) gets the restore with NO braked floor, plus three
  airborne re-asserts (raise-only, heading-preserving). The floor survives only
  on the stand-up path, where the player genuinely had time to brake. Wall
  500 → 800 (Lv5 is now ×1.5 on the engine's own start speed and the old wall
  would have capped it). Jump edge gated to the engine's launch band
  (vz 10..400) so an external pop is never multiplied.
- **Jump height:** unchanged (z × sqrt of the height factor). The API also has a
  per-player `SetPlayerGravity()` — found today, the movement-levers memory
  said no per-player jump lever existed — deliberately NOT used: for the same
  apex, lower gravity stretches airtime by the full height factor, the velocity
  multiply by only its square root. Velocity is the snappier jump; gravity is
  the lever if a floaty jump is ever the ask.

### What to read in the next dev test (tod_dev is ARMED in the current build)

- At map start, after the sprint-dvar lines: `dvar jump_max_velocity = 1000
  (was X)` — X is the engine default nobody has ever seen, and the whole
  `slide_*` family under it. `<UNREGISTERED>` on `jump_max_velocity` means lane
  1 was skipped and lane 3 is carrying alone.
- One bold line per slide: `ATH slide eng=E set=S next=N end=Z Tms
  onslide@end=B`. `next ≈ set` proves the lane-2 write sticks; `next ≈ eng`
  means the engine re-derives slide speed and lane 2 must become a per-tick
  additive delta. `onslide@end` tells us whether `IsOnSlide()` (a second
  builtin, distinct from `IsSliding()`, never used by stock) covers the
  slide-out phase.
- One bold line per slide-jump: `ATH jump direct|standup|none carry=C
  launch=B>A vz=V minair=M air=Nt land=L +300ms=P`. `B` is what the engine
  launched at (the clamp, if lane 1 is off), `A` after the restore, `P` vs `L`
  is the landing-stumble number that decides `TOD_MOVE_LAND_STUMBLE_OFF`.

## 2026-09-01 (v16) — ATHLETE: slide-jump momentum carry

User: *"Typically when you jump i think you lose your velocity. Can we make it so
that you keep the velocity somehow... just make it so that you dont really lose
speed when you jump out of a slide and you have athlete."*

Ported from map 1's `_acc_movement.gsc`, gated on the ATHLETE domain rather than
global. Map 1 shipped this as a *boost* (its rocket shield's 2× was live during
the slide, so the recorded speed was already doubled); the mechanic itself is
pure **preservation**, which is exactly what was asked for.

### Three things about BO3 slide-jumps that make the naive version fail

**THERE IS NO "MOMENT OF THE SLIDE-JUMP" TO KEY OFF.** A BO3 slide-jump is
slide → **STAND UP** → jump, and the stand-up is GROUNDED with `IsSliding()`
already false for several frames. Anything keying on "sliding at the instant of
the jump" observes a state that never exists. So the carry records the slide's
speed and stays armed for a 500 ms grace window.

**THE FIX THAT MATTERS FIRES WHILE STILL GROUNDED.** Ground friction clamps the
player back toward walk speed during that stand-up gap, so without a pre-launch
top-up they leave the ground already slowed and a mid-air correction has to jerk
them forward. Catching `JumpButtonPressed()` *before* the engine launches means
the arc simply starts fast. A second liftoff restore is the fallback for when
the 20 Hz poll misses a tap between ticks.

**MOMENTUM IS VELOCITY, NOT A SPEED SCALE.** Map 1 tried holding the slide's
move-speed scale up after the slide (a "grace window") and decaying it (a
"release ramp"); the user rejected both on feel. `SetMoveSpeedScale` scales
INPUT-driven movement, so what you get is a player *walking* fast — it reads as
ice, and it leaks a free boost after every slide. `athlete_slide_bonus()` is
therefore unchanged and stays strictly slide-only; the carry is a separate
`SetVelocity` lane. Setting velocity works WITH the engine: airborne it does not
decelerate horizontal velocity, and on landing its own ground friction bleeds the
excess off. That natural decel IS the smooth landing the ramp was failing to fake.

`restore_speed()` **only ever raises, never lowers**, so it cannot clamp a boss
fling or a knockback back down. It preserves DIRECTION (steer out of a slide-jump
and keep the speed in the new heading) and preserves Z, so it composes with the
existing height multiply rather than fighting it.

### The peer question that found a real bug

The `-9c` session was auditing the user's *"we have to make sure the player cant
jump oob"* and asked one sharp question: **what is the ceiling — can a chain of
slide-jumps compound?** Answering it required checking the two velocity writes
*separately*, and they had different answers:

- **`restore_speed()` cannot compound.** `carry_speed` is **assigned** (not
  maxed) from actual velocity on every sliding tick, and the function bails at
  `sp >= want`. It can only put back what THIS slide had.
- **THE SLIDE KICK COULD, and that was a real bug.** It is additive —
  `GetVelocity() + forward * kick` — and fired on every slide-start edge **with
  no speed test**. Land fast → slide → +kick → the recorder captures the higher
  speed → jump carries it → land faster → slide → +kick again. Whether that runs
  away or settles depends entirely on per-cycle friction, **which nobody has
  measured**. Over the plank (120 wide, +256, above a 19,000-unit void),
  "it probably settles" is not shippable.

**FIXED:** `TOD_ATH_SPEED_MAX` (500 u/s) now bounds *both* writes — the kick is
skipped at or above it, and `carry_speed` is clamped to it. The loop is bounded
**by construction, independent of friction**, which is the property the audit
needed rather than a number that would have had to be defended.

⚠️ **500 IS A GUESS PENDING ONE MEASUREMENT.** It is deliberately generous — well
above any single legitimate slide — and its only job is to stop an unbounded
chain, not to shape feel. Two symptoms tell you it is wrong in opposite
directions: a normal slide-jump feeling **capped or notchy** means TOO LOW; a
chained slide-jump still reaching somewhere it should not means TOO HIGH. Tune
`TOD_ATH_SLIDE_KICK_LV` for feel; leave this as the wall.

**The shape of the OOB risk changed, and that is worth stating:** the height
multiply is Z-only, so it clears a taller RAIL but leaves the arc the same
length. The carry makes the arc LONGER. Height alone does not cross a gap;
height plus preserved horizontal speed does.

- `tod_upgrade.lua`'s FULL STEAM comment corrected — the three cards were re-baked
  to **"KEEP SPRINTING FOR SPEED"** (no number), so the note claiming a re-bake was
