## 2026-09-01 (tooling) — the registration-ledger guard now guards the WRITES

`tools/gen_tod_twins.js` threw its over-budget error at `:1948`, but its three
`writeFileSync` calls sat at `:1911`, `:1914` and `:1941` — **above it**. So a run
that exceeded `LEDGER_GUARD` had *already* rewritten the weapon GDT, the twins
zpkg and `zm_levelcommon_weapons.csv` before failing.

**"It throws" did not mean "it did nothing."** The guard fired, visibly, every
single time — and protected nothing. It had already fired for real: an
over-budget run at 01:36 today left all three outputs rewritten. Harmless only
because the generator is deterministic and the inputs had not changed; the next
person to edit an axis and run it would have been left holding an over-budget
tree that still looked correctly generated.

**FIX:** the ledger block (`LEDGER_FIXED` / `ledger` / print / throw) moved above
the writes. Order is now print → throw → GDT → zpkg → CSV, and the error ends
**"NOTHING WAS WRITTEN."** Safe because neither input depends on the writes, both
checked rather than assumed: `total` has no mutation anywhere after the
generation loop, and `countFixedRegistrations()` explicitly skips `OUT_ZPKG`
("our own output"). `node --check` passes.

**PROVEN BY RUNNING IT**, not by reading it:

```
md5 before:  6c08bdee9fa4 / c6c83a8cbca3 / 7b4ec9b60703
REGISTRATION LEDGER: 191 generated + 32 fixed = 223  (guard 220; ...)
Error: ledger 223 exceeds the 220 guard — NOTHING WAS WRITTEN.
md5 after:   6c08bdee9fa4 / c6c83a8cbca3 / 7b4ec9b60703
mtimes still 2026-09-01 01:36:23 on all three
```

The untouched **mtimes** are the load-bearing half — a rewrite with identical
content would still have moved them.

### Two second-order effects

**A number you cannot read without mutating the tree gets quoted from memory
instead of measured.** The ledger figure had been passed between three sessions
all night from recall. The run above is the first time it was actually
measured: **191 generated + 32 fixed = 223**.

**It makes the HANDLING question answerable.** Set `AXIS.h.levels` to 4, run,
read the real cost — and if it is over budget, nothing on disk moves. That
workflow did not exist before this change, and it is what lets item 28 be
reopened cheaply.

### HANDLING (item 28): closed-not-shipped, by the user's choice

The user asked for HANDLING at 5 tiers, then 4; it ships at **3**. HANDLING is
one of the few upgrades that *must* be weapon variants (reload / swap / ADS are
baked weapon stats with no script lever), and variant axes **multiply** — 4 tiers
costs 235 registrations, 5 costs 247, against a measured wall of ~230 (map 1
shipped a booting 229, crashed at 368). Offered four options; the user chose to
leave it at 3. **Not blocked — decided.**

⚠️ **`223 boots` is BELIEVED, NOT PROVEN.** It is the live shipped state and has
been in every `.ff` since 01:36, but no session can point at a confirmed boot of
a 223-ledger build, and silence is not a boot. Until someone reports one, the
~7 units of margin under the ~230 wall are **assumed**. That distinction is
exactly what a HANDLING revisit would depend on.

## 2026-09-01 (v16) — BALANCE: DR goes diminishing and common, SPRINT goes rare, Double Tap 3500

Three user asks in one pass. All `-GscOnly` except the card re-bake they imply.

**DMG REDUCTION: flat −5%/Lv → a diminishing ladder** (user: *"damage reduction
should go +6%, +5%, 4%, 3%, 2%"*). Those are PER-LEVEL INCREMENTS, so the
cumulative reduction is **−6 / 11 / 15 / 18 / 20%** at Lv1..Lv5.

**DMG REDUCTION: band S → A. SPRINT: band A → S** (user: *"sprint needs to be
moved to S tier … move damage reduction to A tier"*). They swapped. Draw weights
are B 100 / A 50 / S 20, and the band also scales the SUPER+ULTIMATE slice
(A ×0.75, S ×0.50), so each move hits frequency AND rarity together:

| | draw weight | SUPER/ULT slice | net |
|---|---|---|---|
| DR S → A | 20 → 50 | ×0.50 → ×0.75 | dealt ~2.5× as often, and richer |
| SPRINT A → S | 50 → 20 | ×0.75 → ×0.50 | ~60% rarer, and skewed to REGULAR |

> **The ladder and the band move pull in opposite directions, and that is the
> design.** DR's first card is now worth MORE (+6 vs +5) and its fifth worth LESS
> (+2 vs +5); the cap falls −25 → −20. Crossover is Lv3, where old and new both
> pay −15%. So DR stops being a rare game-definer you hoard and becomes a common
> early pick whose last two levels are deliberately not worth chasing. SPRINT
> goes the other way: on a max-10 domain fed +1/+2/+3 a card, reaching the +33
> cap was already the longest grind in the map and is now materially longer.
>
> At the cap, a 150-HP class's effective HP goes 200 → 187.5, about −6%.

**Double Tap 3000 → 3500.** Two sites, and the second is not optional:
`#precache("triggerstring", "ZOMBIE_PERK_DOUBLETAP", "3500")`. The triggerstring
cache key is the **string + cost PAIR**, not the string, so an unprecached pair
renders the buy prompt with a **blank cost** — this map shipped exactly that bug
on six perks at once until 2026-08-27. The old 3000 pair was REPLACED rather than
kept: a pair no machine sells is a permanent cache slot spent on a dead string,
the same reasoning that deleted the Deadshot pair. Hint budget unchanged at 83.

### The hand-copied literal is gone, and the ladder is what forced it

Both of `_tod_bosses.gsc`'s player-damage lanes carried a bare
`1.0 - 0.05 * dr_lvl`, because a GSC `#define` is FILE-LOCAL and the constant in
`_tod_upgrades.gsc` could not reach them. That file carried a comment instructing
the next person to hand-edit both copies. They had already drifted once — one
comment still claimed "−4%" months after a retune.

**A diminishing ladder cannot be written as a literal multiply at all**, so the
arrangement had stopped being possible, not merely fragile. Both lanes now call
`tod_upgrades::dr_mult()` — the same shape `sprint_armor_mult` and
`back_armor_mult` have always had, and what `boss_damage_bonus` already did.

> Worth naming: the retune did not just change a number, it removed the *option*
> of storing that number in two places. The fix that should always have been
> there became the only fix available.

### The DR cards cannot carry a number any more — docs/60

Not "the numbers are stale". A rarity band grants **+1/+2/+3 LEVELS**, so a
figure printed on a card is a constant INCREMENT — honest only while the domain
is LINEAR. DR was; it no longer is:

| taken at | ULTIMATE (+3) lands on | actual gain |
|---|---|---|
| Lv0 | 15% | +15pp |
| Lv1 | 18% | +12pp |
| Lv2 | 20% | +9pp |

The cards print −5 / −10 / −15% DMG TAKEN, which is now wrong at every level
except zero. Same trap as LEECH's "+4 HP PER KILL" (docs/48); the test is
`val(l) != l * val(1)`, not "did the number change". All three get the same
numberless line, `TAKE LESS DAMAGE`, and the pause menu keeps the exact figure
(`DETAIL[2].val` → `drPct(l)`, level-aware and server-fed). Pips stay 5 — `max`
did not move. Prompt written, art not yet delivered.

### Multi-session note

Three sessions edited `_tod_upgrades.gsc` and `tod_upgrade.lua` inside the same
minute, including a function RENAME (`push_tier_hint` → `push_panel_hints`), with
no collision. The reason is worth keeping: **nobody held a file in a buffer.**
Every edit was a read-modify-write inside a single script — read, match on TEXT
not line number, write — so each saw the others' work by construction. The danger
is stale editor buffers, not concurrent editing as such.

### One deliberate deviation from the written prompt

The ADRENALINE spec said the value panel must be **empty** ("that line is gone
and nothing replaces it"). The delivered art reads **"MULTI-KILLS GRANT SPEED"**.
Kept, on three grounds: it is accurate for the new trigger (the defect was the
old "KILLS GRANT SPEED"); it carries **no numbers**, which is the actual
constraint, so a percent or cooldown retune still needs no re-bake; and an empty
panel reads as a missing asset — no other card in the set has one, while
`i_tod_card_sprint_regular` is the house precedent for words-without-numbers.
The prompt's own author agreed on review, noting the spec had cited that very
card while demanding "here even the words go", which does not follow.

**Residual risk, logged:** the text goes stale if the *trigger* ever stops being
a multi-kill. That is a far better bet than any number — this domain's cooldown
already doubled once in a single session.

### The rule earning itself in real time

The same night, FULL STEAM's cards — the one card set in the v15 pass that baked
a NUMBER into its value panel, reading **"SPRINT 1.5S FOR SPEED"** — went stale
within hours when the user retuned the arm time 1.5 s → 1.0 s. Every other card
in that pass went generic and none needed re-cutting. **If a card states a value,
a later retune silently makes the art lie**; the same applies to superlatives
("FASTEST ON THE TOWER" on the slasher class card, false since the v14.29 speed
swap). Generic text is not laziness, it is the thing that stops art from
becoming a lockstep dependency of every balance change.

now three, and every one was caught only by

## 2026-09-01 (v16) — ATHLETE: the slasher gets its mobility card back (domain 43)

User: *"Can we add a new upgrade to melee where they can slide faster and jump
higher? Its called athlete ... It can be 5 tiers 10% slide speed each tier and
25% jump height increase each tier"*

**NEW DOMAIN 43 `athlete`** — SLASHER-only, band A, max 5, scope `class`
(survives tier promotions). Mechanic in the new `_tod_athlete.gsc`; only the
slide half touches `_tod_upgrades.gsc`. It fills the mobility slot the retired
CHAIN LUNGE (id 22) left empty.

### The trap this feature is built around

**`SetJumpHeight()` IS GLOBAL TO ALL PLAYERS, AND USING IT WOULD HAVE PASSED
EVERY SOLO TEST.** From `docs_modtools/bo3_scriptapifunctions.htm`, verbatim:
*"Set the global jump height of all players."* — no `<player>` receiver, no
per-player form anywhere in the API. Contrast `AllowJump` / `AllowSlide` /
`AllowLean`, which are all explicitly `<player>`-scoped and all booleans; slide
has no magnitude setter at all. So one slasher buying ATHLETE would have given
the **whole lobby** +25% jump — invisible in solo, because global *is* that one
player. Same shape as the v15 item-20 omni-sprint via the equally global
`player_sprintForwardMinimum`. (Found and quoted by the `-9c` session before a
line was written.)

**The escape is that neither half needs it.** Both are per-player primitives,
all four verified in the same doc — `<player> SetVelocity`, `<player>
IsSliding`, `<entity> IsOnGround`, `<entity> SetMoveSpeedScale`. Map 1 solved
this years ago and left a note aimed squarely at the objection
(`_acc_boss_items.gsc`): *"~2x jump HEIGHT via a per-player velocity multiply
(NOT the global jump_height dvar)"*.

**The general lesson, worth more than the feature:** an API search answers *"does
a per-player setter for X exist"*, but the design question was *"can X be made
per-player at all"*. Those come apart exactly when the capability is reachable
through a **different primitive than the one it is named after**. The shipped map
was the better source than the function list. (The distinguishing question is
"is there another primitive that reaches this" — for the omni-sprint case there
genuinely is not, so the two look identical from an API search and are not.)

### Apex height goes as velocity SQUARED

`h = v² / 2g`, so **"+25% height" is not "×1.25 velocity"** — that would be +56%
height, roughly double the spec at every level. The conversion is
`v = sqrt(h)` and it lives in one function, `jump_vel_scale()`:

| Lv | height | velocity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.25× | 1.118 |
| 2 | 1.50× | 1.225 |
| 3 | 1.75× | 1.323 |
| 4 | 2.00× | **1.414** |
| 5 | 2.25× | 1.500 |

Lv4 landing on √2 is the same landmark map 1 recorded as *"x1.42 velocity =
double height"* — an independent check that the curve is right.

### Why the writes stick, which is also why CHAIN LUNGE died

The player movement code **overwrites a grounded player's velocity every frame**
(map 1's `_acc_movement` finding, recorded in our own `_tod_lunge.gsc:45-46` as
the reason that module never worked and was retired). Impulses survive only while
**airborne or sliding** — and both of ATHLETE's writes land in exactly those two
states: the jump multiply fires on the frame the player leaves the ground, the
slide kick while `IsSliding()` is true. Not luck; move either to a grounded frame
and it silently does nothing.

`IsSliding()` is the only correct slide detector: `GetStance()` never returns a
slide value, a BO3 slide is entered from a standing sprint, and the MP
`slide_begin`/`slide_end` notifies do not fire in ZM at all.

### Slide speed rides the ONE move-speed owner

`apply_move_speed()` is the single writer of the move-speed scale and re-asserts
on a 1s body-loop cadence — **shorter than a slide**, so a direct
`SetMoveSpeedScale` in the new module would be stomped mid-slide, intermittently.
`_tod_athlete` sets only the flag and asks the owner to recompute; the term is
`athlete_slide_bonus()` and it is additive to the scale, matching the v15 doctrine
that speed bonuses are **added** (a flat +0.10/Lv for every class) rather than
multiplied into the base. `TOD_ATH_SLIDE_PER_LV` lives in `_tod_upgrades.gsc` and
**only** there — the module deliberately carries no copy, so this is not a
lockstep pair.

**The flag is slide-only: no grace window, no release ramp.** Both were tried on
map 1 and rejected on feel — a `SetMoveSpeedScale` flag scales *input-driven*
movement, so holding it past the slide just makes the player walk fast. It reads
as ice and leaks a free boost after every slide.

A slide-start forward impulse (`SetVelocity`, 50/Lv, topping out at map 1's
tuned 250) supplies the distance the engine's missing slide-duration lever
cannot. That is the half **not** in the spec and the first knob to cut if slides
feel floaty.

### Wiring

New `_tod_athlete.gsc` + scriptparsetree line · `add_domain` + the speed term +
`athlete_slide_bonus()` in `_tod_upgrades.gsc` · `domain_id` case 43 ·
`DOMAIN[43]`/`DETAIL[43]` in `tod_upgrade.lua` · `#using` + `init()` in
`_tod_main.gsc`. **`PAUSE_PLATE_MAX` stays 42** — ATHLETE renders as a TEXT card
and TEXT pause row until art lands (`docs/57`), same as VITALITY/RECOVERY/PERK
SLOTS each did. `DETAIL[43]` uses the `{V}` string form because the domain
carries two different ladders.

Also fixed in passing: `DETAIL[41]` still said DISTRACTION's decoy *"MAX AMMO
refills it"*, which v14.61 made false. Now "MAX AMMO gives +1, carry 3".

Lints green (arity 70 files, lua 42/0, hints 83/190). `-GscOnly`. Shipped in the
`.ff` at 02:26:59; the CURRENT `.ff` to test is **114.38 MB @ 02:28:15**, a
second build from another session that carries ATHLETE plus a CLEAVE audio echo
and whose own freshness diff is clean.

### Postscript: three sessions in one file, and the check that caught it

The post-build freshness diff came back **non-empty** — a third session edited
`_tod_upgrades.gsc` at 02:26:45, **14 seconds before this `.ff` was written** and
22 minutes after this file was claimed. Their change (a CLEAVE audio echo) is
therefore *not* in this `.ff`, while ATHLETE is; verified by full diff plus a
`grep` of the deployed copy, and ATHLETE survived intact (pure additions, no
deletions — arity still reports 70 files).

This is the documented trap, live for the second recorded time: **the build syncs
at the START, so a file edited mid-build is newer than the sync and older than
the `.ff`.** An mtime gate calls that tree clean. Only
`diff -rq scripts zone_source ui` against the deployed tree catches it, which is
why that is the sanctioned check and the only one.

Second lesson, new: **a lane claim only covers the sessions that existed when it
was made.** This file was claimed and announced to every session `ListAgents`
showed at the time; the third session started later and could not have known.
Their build then landed clean at 02:28:15 with an empty diff, carrying both
changes — sequential, not overlapping, and verified on both sides rather than
assumed.

## 2026-09-01 (v14.61) — DISTRACTION: MAX AMMO GIVES +1, NOT A REFILL

User: *"Currently max ammo is giving 3 cymbal/lil arnies for assault and the
spec is that a max ammo will give only 1 but the max that can be held is 3"*

Correct on both counts, and the second half explains the first. The original
spec was +1 per Max Ammo, cap 3. Neither number shipped in v14.59.

**THE CAP WAS RAISED 3 -> 4 ON A CLAIM NOBODY COULD HAVE CHECKED.** The
justification recorded in `_tod_distraction.gsc` was that 4 is "stock parity"
and 3 "would have been a nerf below vanilla". There is no stock weapon-stat GDT
on this box, so the baked cap was not readable — the 4 came from reasoning, and
the file's own comment even said so ("treat 4 as matches stock as far as we can
establish and NOT as a verified engine maximum"). The first armed session
measured it for free: a Max Ammo grab topped the weapon to **exactly 3**, which
is stock's `GiveMaxAmmo` hitting the weapon's own baked ceiling. The spec number
and the engine number were the same number the whole time.
`TOD_DISTRACT_MAX_CARRY` is back to **3**.

**AND BECAUSE THE CAP MOVED, THE +1 LADDER WAS DROPPED WITH IT.** The same
decision concluded "stock behaviour is fine as-is", so the two pieces the
increment needs were deliberately left out and a comment block was written
explaining how to restore them. Both are now in:

- `_tod_distraction::init()` calls `zm_powerups::set_weapon_ignore_max_ammo` on
  **both** weapon names. Stock `full_ammo_powerup` walks `GetWeaponsList(true)`,
  which includes the offhands, and `GiveMaxAmmo`s each. The skip is keyed on the
  weapon **name string**, not the weapon struct. Both tiers are listed —
  registering only Lv1 would make the ladder work with the monkey and silently
  revert to a full refill the moment it became Li'l Arnies.
- `on_max_ammo()` adds `TOD_DISTRACT_MAXAMMO_ADD` (1), clamped, raise-only,
  gated on the DOMAIN LEVEL rather than on inventory — a powerup never hands out
  a grenade the upgrade did not grant.

**AN INCREMENT ON TOP OF A REFILL IS INVISIBLE, NOT BROKEN.** Without the
opt-out, `on_max_ammo()` still runs, still "succeeds", and still changes
nothing, because stock maxed the count 0.05 s earlier and the clamp eats the +1.
That is the check-passes-wrong-question shape again: a working `on_max_ammo()`
is not evidence the ladder is live. The two failure modes are distinguishable in
game — **Max Ammo still filling to 3** means the `set_weapon_ignore_max_ammo`
pair did not take; **Max Ammo doing nothing at all** means the ammo accessor is
reading the wrong store.

**THE AMMO ACCESSORS ARE NOW THE CLIP, NOT THE STOCK.** This was flagged as
unverified in v14.59 ("if the first armed boot shows the count living in the
clip, flip these two bodies") and inherited from map 1, where it could never
have been caught: map 1 handed these grenades out FULL from the box, so a no-op
`SetWeaponAmmoStock` is indistinguishable from a working one. Every stock
tactical-grenade count is a **clip** — `zm_usermap.gsc:185` zeroes the tactical
with `SetWeaponAmmoClip`, and the last-stand stash at `_zm.gsc:3201/3219` saves
and restores it with `GetWeaponAmmoClip`/`SetWeaponAmmoClip`. Three writers,
zero counter-examples, and no stock site anywhere that touches an offhand's
stock. The read only started mattering now: a refill never needed to know the
count, and an increment does.

**WIRING.** `_tod_powerups::max_ammo_clip_watch` calls through a new
`level.tod_distract_max_ammo` pointer — it rides the watcher's existing 0.05 s
"let stock finish" wait and its respawn latch rather than opening a second
`"zmb_max_ammo"` waittill that would race it for the same settle. A direct
`#using` is impossible: `_tod_upgrades` imports `_tod_powerups` and
`_tod_distraction` imports `_tod_upgrades`, so powerups -> distraction closes
the cycle. Same idiom as `level.tod_distract_reconcile`. Guarded, so the module
going away degrades to "no top-up" rather than to a crash.

`docs/armory.html` refreshed (`TOD_DISTRACT_MAX_CARRY 3` + the new rule);
`verify_armory_constants.js` 23/23, `lint_tod_arity.js` clean. `-GscOnly`.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.60) — THE SPIRE PERK FLOOR: a v14.56 regression, found by asking a question

User: *"Also we should make sure that this new system works fine when you get to
endless spire. Cause you get max perks at endless spire but do you get the
upgrade first and then rewarded max perks? We should consider this and think
whether it works or not like that"*

**THE ORDERING WAS ALREADY RIGHT, AND THAT WAS NOT THE INTERESTING PART.**
`_tod_spire::grant_all` maxes every domain at `:589` (`self.tod_levels[d.key] =
cap`) and only then grants perks at `:640`. Same thread, no yield between them,
so nothing can reorder it. PERK SLOTS is universal, so `domain_available()`
short-circuits true and `domain_max()` returns 5 — the cap is 4 + 5 = 9 before
the first `give_perk`, and the nine machines fit exactly.

It would not have mattered anyway: `zm_perks::give_perk` is `SetPerk` +
`num_perks++` with **no cap check**. The ordering is load-bearing only for the
**first re-buy after a down on the spire**, which is precisely where it has to
hold — and does, because `tod_levels` is init-once and survives death.

**BUT THE QUESTION FOUND A REAL REGRESSION, and it was v14.56's.** The cap used
to be `level.perk_purchase_limit = 10` — a **LEVEL** variable, so it covered
every player no matter when they connected. Moving it per-player was right for
the tower and wrong for the spire, because **`_tod_spire.gsc` has ZERO
`callback::on_spawned`**: `grant_all` is a one-shot loop over `GetPlayers()` at
the moment of ascension. A player who joins or reconnects afterwards gets a
fresh entity, `player_upgrade_setup` zero-fills `tod_levels`, and
`perk_slot_limit()` returns **4** while their team-mates sit at 9. Before
v14.56 they would have had 10. **Strictly worse than what it replaced — a
regression, not a missing feature.** And unfixable from inside the run: the
spire suppresses upgrade events, so PERK SLOTS can never be dealt up there.

**THE FIX IS A FLOOR, AND IT IS DERIVED RATHER THAN TYPED.** In
`perk_slot_limit()`: while `level.tod_spire_active`, take the greater of the
player's earned limit and `TOD_PERK_SLOT_BASE + domain_max(self, perkslots)`.
Reading the domain's own max means a retune tracks automatically and no second
copy of "9" enters the tree — the same discipline the v14.56 entry argues for.
Raise-only by construction, so it can never lower a limit anyone earned, and
off the spire the branch never runs.

**A SIDE EFFECT WORTH KEEPING:** with every spire cap now ≥ the roster, the
`PERK SLOTS FULL` refusal becomes **unreachable on the spire** — where its
advice ("take a PERK SLOTS upgrade") was unactionable, since the card cannot be
dealt there. Fixed by the mechanism instead of by a spire-specific string, so
it costs no new triggerstring.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method is the point.** A five-area adversarial
audit of PERK SLOTS × the Spire. 26 agents, 24 completed — **two refuters died
on an API error**, both covering `spire-rebuy` and `cards-and-events`, so parts
of those areas went unrefuted **and this regression was one of them**. It was
hand-verified instead (`get_level` returns 0 for a fresh player; zero spawn
callbacks in `_tod_spire.gsc`), which is why it is in this changelog rather than
in a list of plausible findings. Most of the other 26 dissolved under refutation
— the "bled-out players lose their weapons" theory that three separate auditors
reached independently is refuted by `_zm.gsc:4776-4779`, which returns into
`spawnSpectator` before the `TakeAllWeapons` at `:4798` can run.

**THREE FINDINGS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE**, all pre-existing and none about
perk slots — raised for the user rather than taken unilaterally:
1. `_tod_spire.gsc:568` turns a **transient** `tier_up` refusal into a
   **permanent** tier freeze via `if (!ok) break;`. `tier_up` can return false
   having changed nothing whenever a weapon swap is in flight — and an
   ascension is exactly when `swap_primary` is busy. Zero recovery: events
   suppressed, stations 10,240 units away, teleporters deleted. The comment
   above it names only the permanent cause ("no class picked?"), which is how
   a `break` came to look reasonable.
2. Solo: the grant can burn the third lifetime Quick Revive and ghost the
   pinned arena machine. One-line stock opt-out exists.
3. Dead/spectating players are granted but not teleported (the teleport loop
   filters `!isalive`, the grant loop does not). Cosmetic.

⚠️ **STILL NEVER PLAYED.** Everything above is static analysis of a ladder that
has had no real playthrough (it could not even have run before v14.19 seeded
its navmesh). The cheapest live check for the user's actual question: ascend,
go down once, re-buy. You should reach nine.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.59b) — IMPACT ROUNDS + SPRINT ARMOR retired; seven bands moved

*Renumbered 14.59 -> 14.59b: two sessions independently claimed v14.59 the same evening.
BOTH sets of changes shipped in the SAME fastfile (the 20:41 full build) — this is one
build recorded as two entries, not two builds. The b-suffix follows v14.58/58b.*

User: *"remove impact rounds from assault class. Lets completely retire this
upgrade. No one likes it"*, *"Retire sprint armor entirely"*, and a band pass:
BOUNTY→S, PERK SLOTS→A, BULLET FEED→A, LUCK→A, PENETRATION→B, DRAW CUT→B,
LEECH→B.

**TWO DOMAINS RETIRED, on the CHAIN LUNGE form rather than the MOMENTUM one.**
Both `add_domain` calls become `// Was:` comments carrying the reason; ids 28
and 32 STAY mapped in `domain_id()` and in the Lua tables (key-keyed, so nothing
renumbers and neither id can be silently reused — and note nothing in the build
chain checks `domain_id()` for duplicate returns, so a freed id is a real
hazard). **Unlike MOMENTUM/REGEN, the ART goes**: `CARD_SLUG[28]`/`[32]` and six
zone image lines removed, because an unreachable art slug is dead weight in the
`.ff` where a Lua row costs nothing. PNGs stay in `source_data`.

**THE EFFECTS ARE GONE, NOT LEFT INERT** — `impact_splash()`, the IMPACT ROUNDS
block in `unique_on_hit`, and the four `TOD_IMPACT_*` defines. Leaving them
would have been harmless (`get_level` returns 0 for an unrollable domain) but a
dead lane that still looks live is how the next reader loses an hour.

**ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: `sprint_armor_mult()` survives as a permanent 1.0.**
`_tod_bosses` calls it from both player-damage lanes, and editing that file's
damage chain to delete an already-inert call on the eve of a publish build is a
worse trade than a function whose header states in caps that it always returns
1.0. Delete it and its two call sites together, or not at all.

**`unique_on_hit`'s `swing` parameter is now unused** — IMPACT ROUNDS was its
only reader. Kept rather than dropped: the arg is free, the call site's
two-value note still governs CLEAVE next door, and changing an arity in the
damage chain to delete a name is not worth it. Documented at the function.

**CROSS-CHECK THAT MAKES THIS VERIFIABLE: 33 armory `DOMAINS` rows == 33 live
`add_domain` calls.** `verify_armory_constants.js` reads 23 match / 0 mismatch —
23 rather than 24 because a retired domain took its constant with it, which is
the count dropping correctly, not drift.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.59) — DISTRACTION: THE MAP GETS A TACTICAL SLOT

User: *"Can you look into adding cymbol monkeys and lil arnies to the map. They
will be attainable through the updares and we will have cymbol as tier 1 and lil
arnies as tier 2. Only assault will get these upgrades. And they will persist
through class upgardes. Also tehy will be S tier."*

**NEW DOMAIN 41 `distraction`** — assault-only, band S, max 2, scope `class`.
Lv1 grants the **Cymbal Monkey**; Lv2 replaces it with **Li'l Arnies** (the
`octobomb`). The engine has exactly ONE tactical slot, so the second level is a
REPLACE, not a second grenade — and **the carried count comes with it** (user:
3 monkeys must become 3 arnies; an upgrade may never read as a downgrade).

**IT COST NO ASSETS AT ALL.** Both weapons were already included via the
`zm_levelcommon_weapons.csv` rows this map already ships, and stock `zm_usermap`
already `#using`s `_zm_weap_cymbal_monkey` AND `_zm_weap_octobomb` on **both**
VMs. So: zero clientfield bits, zero `weapon,` zone lines, zero registrations
against the ~230 twin ceiling. **Do not add a `weapon,cymbal_monkey_zm` line** —
no GDT on the box defines it and the link hard-fails "Unable to load weapon".
The tactical slot was empty before this: usermaps never set
`zombie_tactical_grenade_player_init`, and this map has no wallbuys and no box.

**THE EFFECT IS A LEVEL-DRIVEN RECONCILE, NOT A CARD HOOK** — because a grenade
is INVENTORY and three paths write a domain level without touching inventory:
`tier_up`'s reset loop, `tier_up`'s grant field, and `_tod_spire::grant_all`.
A one-shot on the card pick is skipped by all three, and an ascended spire player
would have carried a maxed domain and no grenade. `_tod_distraction::reconcile`
reads the level and makes the slot match; it is idempotent and runs on spawn plus
those three sites via a **guarded level pointer** (`level.tod_distract_reconcile`)
— never a `#using`, since that module imports `_tod_upgrades` for `get_level` and
importing back is the KB cycle rule.

**FOUR ENGINE TRAPS, ALL PAID FOR ON MAP 1** and all handled in the module's
header: (1) `register_tactical_grenade_for_level("octobomb")` is MANDATORY —
stock registers only `cymbal_monkey`, so without it `is_offhand_weapon` is FALSE
and any `weapon_give` of the octobomb runs the PRIMARY flow and trades away the
held class gun (map 1's "box Arnie traded my gun"), silently here because this
map disables the too-many-weapons monitor; (2) raw `GiveWeapon` does not ARM the
grenade — the thrown behaviour is threaded by the registered zombie-weapon
callback that only `weapon_give` dispatches, so we dispatch it by hand or the
projectile lands inert; (3) `get_player_tactical_grenade()` returns `weaponNone`,
never `undefined`, so an `isdefined` guard alone `TakeWeapon`s nothing; (4) the
slot pointer is nulled on EVERY spawn, so `HasWeapon` can be true while the throw
does nothing — re-assert `set_player_tactical_grenade` every time.

**FREE-PaP OFFHAND GUARD (a latent bug this feature would have activated).**
`_tod_powerups.gsc`'s free-PaP drop calls `can_upgrade_weapon(GetCurrentWeapon())`,
and that stock function has **no offhand exclusion** — while the CSV gives
`octobomb` an `octobomb_upgraded`. Grabbing a free-PaP mid-throw would have taken
the grenade and given back an unregistered tactical down the primary path, eating
a class gun. Now guarded with `!is_offhand_weapon(w)`, which belongs at that call
site regardless of this domain.

**CARRY CAP 4, AND MAX AMMO IS DELIBERATELY UNHOOKED.** Specced as "1 at grant,
+1 per max ammo, cap 3 which is normal" — but 3 is **not** stock: map 1 set these
grenades to 4 explicitly, so 3 would have been a nerf below vanilla. User raised
it to 4 for stock parity and ruled that stock Max Ammo behaviour is therefore
fine as-is. So the `set_weapon_ignore_max_ammo` opt-out and the +1 pass **do not
exist**, and Max Ammo refills to the baked cap in one grab like every other
weapon. Consequence, deliberate: the real ceiling is the weapon's own baked cap,
which is **not readable from disk** (no stock weapon-stat GDT exists on this box).
`TOD_DISTRACT_MAX_CARRY 4` only clamps what the module itself writes. Restoring
the +1 ladder is ~6 lines and the module header says exactly which.

*(Unrelated but same evening: v14.56 also moved the PERK purchase cap to 4,
independently and for different reasons. Two caps landing on 4 the same night,
both citing stock parity — they are not the same mechanism and neither drove the
other.)*

**SHIPS ON THE TEXT FALLBACK.** `DOMAIN[41]`/`DETAIL[41]` are in the Lua;
`CARD_SLUG[41]` and `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX` are deliberately untouched until the art in
`docs/54_distraction_card_art_prompt.md` is installed AND zoned — same flow as
VITALITY/RECOVERY/PERK SLOTS. `PAUSE_PLATE_MAX` is 40 after v14.56, so 41 is the
only step left there.

**KNOWN AND DELIBERATE:** max 2 means **no ULTIMATE card can ever be dealt** (the
band-honesty clamp relabels any +3 down), and a SUPER takes a Lv0 player straight
to Li'l Arnies without ever holding the monkey — which `TOD_UPG_GUAR_FIRST`
*guarantees* if it is dealt on the round-1 deal. S band on a max-2 domain also
means `guarantee_rarity` swaps it OUT of deals at bar >= 100, since it can never
absorb the owed +3. It is the rarest card in the deck by construction.

**NOT YET RUN IN GAME.** Boot-verified nothing — this entry describes a build
that has not been played. The two things static analysis cannot settle are the
weapon's real baked cap and whether the count lives in the clip or the stock
(the module routes both through one helper each so it is a two-body flip).

## 2026-08-31 (v14.58) — EVERY PROMPT WAS A WALL WEAPON

User: *"We shoudl say Regulat $2500 and Pack a Punch $5000. We have an issue
with the ammo crate copy. ALl ammo crates should work the same. We also have an
issue where ammo crate and heavenly alter say wall weapon. I think we may have
this issue all through the map... for a bunch of the triggers we see
HoldXAMMOCRATE. There is no spacing between things."*

**THE USER WAS RIGHT THAT IT WAS EVERYWHERE.** `ZMCursorHintNew.lua` picks which
prompt card to draw by pattern-matching the hint TEXT, and its wall-buy arm was
*"the text contains `[Cost:`"* **AND** `getCursorHintImage() ~= ""`. The image
guard was believed to make that route safe for our `HINT_NOICON` triggers — two
GSC files carry comments reasoning explicitly from that premise
(`_tod_ammo_crate.gsc:155`, `_tod_upgrades.gsc::station_hint_loop`). **The
premise was false.** That model does not read back as the empty string for an
icon-less hint, so the guard never fired and **every PRICED NON-DOOR
interactable in the map drew `PromptWallBuy`** — whose hardcoded description is
the literal text **"Wall Weapon"**. The ammo crates, the Heavenly Gift Altar,
CALL EXTRACTION, every spire buy. Doors were the only ones that looked right,
and only because the door keyword excluded them one line earlier.

**THE ROUTER IS NOW ONE CLASSIFIER.** Nine independent predicates across nine
state arms — several of which could match the same hint, with arm order deciding
the winner — collapsed into `classifyHint()`, which returns EXACTLY ONE state.
WallBuy, MysteryBox and GobbleGum have no arm at all: this map has no wall
weapons, no mystery box and no gobblegum machine, so all three could only ever
misfire. `isMysteryBoxWeapon` was the worst of them, claiming any hint carrying
"hold" and the substring "for" with no cost.

**`TOD_NOUNS` IS THE NEW CONTRACT.** The map's own prompt nouns ("ammo crate",
"heavenly gift altar", "teleporter", "extract", "rampage", "ascend"…) are
claimed BEFORE any generic keyword test. That is what makes the requested copy
safe: **"Pack a Punch $5000" inside an ammo-crate line is no longer dragged onto
the Pack-a-Punch card** by the `"pack"`+`"punch"` test. Any new interactable adds
its noun to that list — and the lint below fails if it does not.

**"HoldXAMMOCRATE" WAS TWO WRITERS ON ONE FIELD.** `PromptDefault` cleaned the
hint (colour codes, the `[{+activate}]` token) in its own subscription — and the
router then overwrote it with `Engine.Localize(RAW HINT)`. The router registers
its callback LATER, so it fired last and won, and every line of that careful
stripping was dead code. The raw string went into a **146px-wide** box. That
writer is deleted; `PromptDefault` owns its text and nothing else may write it.

**`PromptDefault` IS NOW A STRUCTURED CARD**, the shape `PromptDoors` already
uses and the user already reads fine: a title band, up to TWO detail lines, an
optional price row, and a `Hold [F] To Buy/Use` footer that hides itself on a
status line with no button token. It parses one grammar, authored GSC-side:

    Hold [btn] ^5<TITLE>^7 - <detail 1> / <detail 2> ^2[Cost: N]

so the ammo crate reads **AMMO CRATE** over **Regular $2500** and **Pack a Punch
$5000** — two short fields instead of one 44-character line squeezed into a box
sized for the words "Locked Area". Every other prompt was reworded to the same
grammar: CALL EXTRACTION ("opens the road to the crown"), the altar ("take an
upgrade card"), the teleporters' offline/recharging states, RAMPAGE's sealed
states, ASCEND ("one way, no return" on its own line), and the UPLINK pointer.

**ALL AMMO CRATES ARE NOW ONE CRATE.** `_tod_spire::spawn_crate` hand-rolled its
own model, its own trigger dimensions and its own COPY of the hint literal, kept
in step by a "keep in LOCKSTEP" comment and nothing else. It now calls
`tod_ammo_crate::spawn_model` / `spawn_trigger` / `crate_hint`, so the six static
crates and every spire crate are the same object — and the duplicated literal
collapsed from **two permanent triggerstring slots to one**.

**NEW GATE: `tools/lint_tod_hints.js`** (+ `lint_tod_hints_selftest.js`), wired
into `build_map.ps1` on every build **including `-GscOnly`** — a reworded hint is
exactly the GSC-only change that skips every other gate. It proves two things:

* **ROUTING** — every hint lands on the card its module is declared to want. It
  reads `TOD_NOUNS` **out of the Lua**, so GSC copy and the router cannot drift
  apart silently.
* **THE 250 CAP** — it counts **DISTINCT STRINGS**, the only count that proves
  anything (v14.3's "fix" proved its loop had *run* instead). Currently **83
  distinct tod-authored strings**; any hint with an interpolated value must
  declare how many strings it can mint or the lint fails.

The selftest breaks the map eight ways and requires a catch on each plus a clean
control. It earned its keep immediately: it caught the lint reading `TOD_NOUNS`
with a bare `indexOf`, which still matched a *renamed* table — the lint would
have gone green while measuring nothing at all.

**CORRECTION, same evening (v14.58b), because it was briefly written into a file
header and a header is a second source of truth nothing regenerates: THE 146px
BOX IS NOT WHY THE SPACES VANISHED.** Measured, the old copy overflowed it by
~1.38×, and map 1 **shipped this same widget at ~2.48× overflow**. A squeeze at
1.38× leaves spaces at ~73% width — cramped, not absent. The narrow box is a
real layout problem and the structured card fixes it, but the only PROVEN cause
of the report is the two-writer race. The font was independently exonerated
twice (`ltromatic.ttf` defines U+0020 at a wide 550/1024 em, with healthy `hdmx`
at every ppem, and the deployed copy is md5-identical); no Lua `gsub` removes
interior whitespace anywhere in `ui/`. What is left, by elimination and not by
evidence, is an engine-side pass over strings carrying `^N` codes and a
`[{+bind}]` token — unprovable from this machine, since no stock LUI Lua ships
with the mod tools. **So the card's parser was made to survive either answer:**
it splits on `-` and `/` with the surrounding spaces OPTIONAL, and
`lint_tod_hints.js` GATE C enforces the price of that tolerance (a `-` or `/` in
a default-card hint must be written as ` - ` / ` / `, never inside a word).

**Also v14.58b:** `_tod_ammo_crate::use_loop` gains `self endon( "death" )` —
map 1 has it and we did not. Invisible for the six static crates, whose triggers
are never deleted; it matters for the spire, where `crate_window()` re-runs every
2s and `delete_crate` Deletes the trigger the thread is blocked on, over a
100-floor climb, against the map's binding ~1024-gentity budget.

**THE SHAPE WORTH REMEMBERING, and it is bigger than this bug: the Aetherium kit
was vendored into this repo PRISTINE.** Map 1 had *already fixed* this exact
hijack, in the router, with a `hasHoldFor` guard whose comment names the symptom
("show WALL WEAPON") and the cause ("the cursorHintImage model is never
cleared"). CLAUDE.md opens with "do NOT re-learn lessons that map already paid
for" — the doctrine was there; the mechanism was not, because nobody diffs a
vendored kit against its debugged twin. `PromptWallBuy.lua` is byte-identical to
map 1's, so map 1 never fixed the widget either — it fixed the ROUTER. Every
map-1 fix to that kit is absent here unless independently re-derived, and this is
one confirmed instance with no evidence it is the only one.

**THE ALTAR'S OWN PAD, ON YOUR CARDS.** An ULTIMATE now brings the heavenly
altar's aura with it, panned to the side it landed on: `tod_upg_aura_l` /
`_r` / `_both`. All three are cuts of the existing `tod_altar_aura.wav` — no new
authored audio.

**SAME LANE AS THE OVERCHARGE ZAP, which the user pointed out was already
proven.** `self PlayLocalSound()` on a repeating driver
(`_tod_luck::overcharge_driver`, v14.9b) is 2d and reaches exactly one player.
`PlayLoopSound` on an entity would broadcast to the whole lobby, so the
retrigger is not a workaround — it IS the per-player mechanism. 2.0s unit, 0.2s
fades both ends, retriggered every **1.8s** so each pass crossfades over the
seam. ⚠️ That 0.2s overlap is the trick; move one number and move the other.

shortcut.** The units are pre-panned stereo (11 dB channel separation, verified
per-channel) and the aliases are **2d**, so the image is pinned to the SCREEN.
A 3d emitter would re-derive direction from world position and swing the aura
around as the player turned — and the upgrade panel does **not** lock the
camera, so "the card on the left" would drift off it.

**DOUBLE ULTIMATE waits for the second card** and plays one bigger centred
variant instead of two overlapping halves — louder in the wav (mean −15.2 vs
−19.9 dB) *and* at the alias (88 vs 80). It arrives exactly as the choice
becomes the thing worth agonising over.

disconnect, a solo down at the station, and a round event seizing the panel from
a station buy — because when those aborts fire, `present_choice` dies mid-flight
and its cleanup never runs, so the driver cannot rely on being told.
`TOD_AURA_MAX_PASSES` is the last resort: even with every endon missed it stops
on its own. A stuck aura would be a permanent noise in a run.

**A floor-gated tier card summons no aura** — `reveal_deal` reads
`reveal_rarity()`, not raw rarity, so the card that carries rarity 3 but cannot
be taken does not get the "this is yours" sound.

city, relay, eclipse and spire 95 → **90**; boss and finale 100 → **95**.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.54) — CARD REVEAL: the super sting lands early too

User: *"Can you start the super sfx a bit earlier too. Like 0.2s earlier."*

**And 0.2s is the measured right answer, not a round number** — `tod_super_sting`
opens on silence and swells for ~0.20s before its body arrives (measured at
install: −54 dB at t=0, −3.7 dB by 0.20s). Its punch was therefore landing a
fifth of a second AFTER the card. The lead cancels the wav's own onset delay, so
the hit now lands *on* the card.

**THE LEAD IS PER-ASSET, NOT PER-RARITY** — `TOD_REVEAL_LEAD_SUPER 0.20` is
LARGER than `TOD_REVEAL_LEAD_ULT 0.10`, which looks backwards until you measure
the two files: the ultimate's impact is at its own t=0 (no swell-in), so its
0.10 is a genuine early warning that summons the card, while the super's 0.20
merely re-aligns a sound that was arriving late. ⚠️ **Regenerate either wav and
its lead must be re-measured and reset** — the hard-transient super rebuild
already under discussion would need this back near 0, or it will fire a fifth of
a second early and read as broken.

`reveal_slot` now carries one `sting`/`lead` pair instead of branching on rarity
at two separate points, and the first wait is guarded (`if hold > lead`) because
a lead is allowed to equal or exceed its hold — which super's now does exactly.

**CONSEQUENCE WORTH HEARING FOR:** with lead == hold, the super's sting fires on
the same frame the socket starts charging, so the riser and the sting overlap for
the super's entire hold (the ultimate still gets 0.20s of riser alone first). The
snapshot guarantee is untouched — it rides the full hold regardless of where the
sting falls inside it — but if that reads as muddy, dropping the riser for super
is one line.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.53) — CARD REVEAL: half the delay, and the ultimate lands early and loud

User, after playing v14.52: *"The game is fast paced. I like the delays we have
added in the display of upgrades but can we cut all the delays in half."* and
*"for ultimate we need to start the sound effect a bit earlier and it needs to
be louder ... this earlier sfx timing needs to be built on top of that."*

**ALL SIX TIMINGS HALVED, TOGETHER.** open 0.35→0.175, holds 0.10/0.40/0.60 →
0.05/0.20/0.30, gap 0.28→0.14, tail 0.30→0.15. Moving them as a set is the point:
every ratio and the whole rarity ladder survive the cut, so the choreography is
unchanged and only its tempo moved. Double-ultimate deal 2.13s → **1.07s**;
two regulars 1.13s → **0.57s**.

**THE HALVING HAD A NON-OBVIOUS COST, and it is the kind that ships silently.**
The client's flip tween must stay under the server's shortest gap between two
field pushes or a later push's `Render()` snaps the card to its end rect — and
that floor is *derived* from the gaps, so halving them moved it from 140ms to
**70ms**. The existing 120ms flip would have stayed legal on a round event
(140ms gap) and **snapped at the personal station** (70ms), i.e. the flip would
have quietly stopped existing in one of the two places it runs, with nothing
failing and no error anywhere. Flip 120→60ms, socket 110→55ms.

**THE ULTIMATE'S STING NOW FIRES 0.10s BEFORE ITS CARD** (`TOD_REVEAL_ULT_LEAD`).
Built ON TOP of the halving as asked — it is a new constant, not half of an old
one, and it exists precisely because the shorter hold left the sting less room to
announce anything. The wav's impact is at its own t=0 (measured, no swell-in), so
the hit now leads the card and reads as the sound summoning it. Ultimate only.
The split cannot threaten the snapshot guarantee: what the client's `0 -> N` edge
needs is that the RARITY and DOMAIN pushes land in different snapshots, and the
distance between *those* is the whole hold regardless of where the sting falls.

**LOUDER, by the only honest levers left.** The wav is peak-limited, so there was
almost no gain to take: re-rendered from the original at −0.2 dBFS instead of
−1.0 (mean −5.5 → −4.7), alias 96 → **100**, and the riser ducked 90 → **86** so
the sting punches through its own build-up instead of competing with it. Super
left alone — the ask was a louder ultimate, not a quieter super.

**The burst was deliberately NOT halved** (320/460 → 200/**380**ms). It blocks
nothing and is not bound by the flip floor, and shrinking it in proportion would
have pulled against the second request. 380ms still finishes before slot B lands.

⚠️ `REVEAL_HOLD_MS` in the Lua moved in lockstep with `TOD_REVEAL_HOLD_*`.
Full record: **docs/52**.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.52) — THE CARD REVEAL: cards are DEALT now, not displayed

User: *"add an animation and cool sound effect when you pull a super or
ultimate ... like when you pull a super cool camo in csgo or something like apex
legends crates ... if a slot is ultimate it can be empty for 0.5s and then grow
into its ultimate card and then make an epic noise like you are doing something
rare and epic."*

Every deal used to appear **finished** — the panel faded up with two completed
cards already on it, and pulling an ULTIMATE differed from pulling a regular
only by the frame colour on a card that was already there.

**THE HOLD IS THE FEATURE.** The panel now opens on two EMPTY SOCKETS and each
slot lands on its own beat, and the empty wait is **longer the rarer the card**
— 0.10s regular / 0.40s SUPER / **0.60s ULTIMATE** — so the delay itself is the
tell: you know something good is coming before you can see what it is. A riser
SFX rides the same wait, then the socket blows apart into the card's spine and
the face **flips open out of it** (`CoD.TweenType.Bounce`, so it overshoots and
settles — Linear read as the card sliding rather than being dealt), throwing a
rarity burst and leaving a lingering aura. **REGULAR IS DELIBERATELY DULL**: no
riser, no burst, no aura, a dry tick. If every pull flashes, no pull is special.

**ZERO NEW CLIENTUIMODEL BITS** — the pool sits at 60 of its proven 61, so a
field was not affordable, and none was needed. The reveal is derived from three
facts the panel already carried: `show == 1 && focus == 0` **is** the reveal
state (a server contract — every other path that raises `show` sets focus in the
same breath, so it is unreachable otherwise); `R >= 1` with `D == 0` is an empty
socket charging toward rarity R; `D` going `0 -> N` lands the card. The
previously-unused rarity **0** became "no card is coming to this slot", which is
how a one-card deal draws one socket instead of two.

**RARITY AND DOMAIN ARE PUSHED IN TWO WAVES SEPARATED BY A REAL WAIT.** Model
callbacks fire in clientfield REGISTRATION order (`todUpgAD` before `todUpgAR`),
so pushed together a card would land wearing the *previous* deal's rarity for a
frame. The gap is load-bearing, not pacing.

**`self:completeAnimation()` MOVED TO THE TOP OF `Render()`.** LUI's
`completeAnimation` is documented nowhere in this tree and may snap CHILD
animations too — left at the bottom it would have ended each card tween on the
frame it began, silently, with the code still looking correct.

Also: the station runs the whole show at **half speed** (its world is not
paused, so un-pickable card time is real danger); a floor-gated CLASS TIER card
reveals as a REGULAR (it carries rarity 3, but full fanfare into a refused pick
is a tease, not a reward); countdown and tier-gate badge are suppressed until
input actually opens.

**SOUND: 5 aliases, THREE of them authored** — trimmed from 7 on the user's
*"can we do the minimal while keeping the experience?"*, and four of the seven
turned out to be ceremony. **The two risers became one**: the HOLD already
separates the rarities, so a single 0.6s riser completes exactly as an ULTIMATE
lands and is cut off mid-sweep by a SUPER's shorter hold — the ultimate is the
only build you ever hear resolve, which *is* the tell, for one asset instead of
two. **The double-ultimate fanfare is gone**: two ultimate stings 0.9s apart is
already a combination no other deal can produce. **Panel-open and regular-land
stopped being placeholders and became final**, pointed at `reactor_online` (what
`tod_class_open` plays — the *other* choice panel opening) and `glass_cling`

**NEW GATE: `tools/lint_tod_lua.js`** (+ `_selftest.js`, 7 checks), wired into
