## 2026-08-31 (v14.50) — DOWNED TEAMMATES turn the tower gauge red

User: *"players dont know where their tm8s are when they go down. Can we add
some indicator on the tower asset ... that makes a section light red if a player
is down at that location ... Or at least pick the closest section to turn red
depending on where the player went down. Just want to catch the edge cases where
they may be in between section or something."* And, mid-implementation: *"There
is always a possibility that multiple players are down at different areas so we
need to be prepared to have multiple squares red when that happens. I dont want
the system to break cause it doesnt expect 2,3 players down at once."*

**Any cell of the tower gauge holding a downed teammate swaps to a red tile.**
Not an overlay — the lit cyan rung / gold breather underneath is blanked, so the
section reads as one solid red block whether or not you have climbed that high.
A teammate down ABOVE your own trail lights a red cell in the unlit region,
which is the case that actually needed solving.

**BUILT AS A BITMASK, so the count is never a thing the code knows.** Bit
(cell-1) is set for every cell with at least one downed teammate; the Lua walks
all 25 bits on every update and sets 25 alphas. Zero, one, two or three reds are
the same code path with the same cost, and there is no "the" down cell anywhere
in the feature to be wrong about. Two players down on the SAME cell is the case
a naive sum gets wrong (bit 4 + bit 4 = bit 5, a red cell one floor above where
anybody is); `|` is idempotent, so the collision is correct by construction
rather than by a guard somebody has to remember. Verified by exhaustive
round-trip over every single, pair and triple of cells plus the duplicate,
empty and all-25 cases — 16,278 encodes/decodes, all exact.

**THE MASK IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO ARGS AND RIDES ITS OWN `tod_down` EVENT.** 25
cells is 25 bits, up to 33,554,431 as one number, and these values land in the
LUI model system, which the client Lua reads back through `tonumber()` /
`math.floor` — as a Lua number, with no promise anywhere in this tree or in
stock that it survived as an exact 32-bit int. A float32 carries integers
exactly only to 16,777,216; above that the spacing is 2, so *"cell 25 and cell 1
are both down"* would have quietly lost cell 1. Split 13 + 12, every transmitted
value is ≤ 8191 and the question cannot arise. The second event (rather than a
third arg on `tod_floor`) also avoids being this tree's first 4-arg
`LuiNotifyEvent` caller — stock MP ships 4-, 5- and 7-arg calls, so it is very
likely fine, and *"very likely fine"* is how a silent no-fire gets shipped. It
decouples the feeds as a bonus: a climbing party pushes floor events all match
without ever touching the down lane.

**THE EDGE CASES THE USER ASKED ABOUT ARE THE TWO ENDS, not the middle.** Every
z between the base deck and the roof already lands in a cell — `floor_of` has no
gaps, so "in between sections" cannot happen. What can is a down BELOW cell 1
(the base arena, z < 0) or ABOVE cell 25 (roof, causeway, crown), and a mask bit
for either would draw nowhere at all — reading as *"nobody is down"* at the
exact moment somebody is. `down_cell_of` clamps both ends onto the nearest real
cell, the same fix and the same reasoning the boss pip already paid for.

**LAST STAND ONLY, and never your own body.** `IsAlive` stays TRUE through last
stand and goes FALSE once a player has bled out, which is exactly the line this
marker wants: a bled-out player cannot be revived, so pointing the party 30
floors at their corpse would be a lie. `player_is_in_laststand()` reads the
revive trigger's existence, so the red clears itself the frame a revive
completes — nothing watches for the revive. The mask is built per viewer with
their own bit excluded, so red means one unambiguous thing ("a teammate is there
and needs you") and solo never sees one at all.

**Forced off during the finale**, alongside the boss pip: the bar is the song
clock by then, every cell is a chunk of the track, and a red one would read as a
timer event rather than a person.

**Added to the per-life re-arm** in `_tod_upgrade_ui::player_lui_life`. This feed
needed it more than any other on that list — a player who just bled out and
respawned is precisely the one whose teammates are likely to be down right now,
and a change-gated mask would otherwise show a fresh HUD nothing until somebody
else went down.

**ART: `i_tod_gauge_down`,** the `i_tod_gauge_breather` tile with its amber
family hue-rotated into alarm red (255,70,51 — the file's existing WARN_COLOR
band). Derived from the shipped tile rather than baked fresh, so the silhouette,
frame, antialiasing and alpha mask are byte-identical to the rest of the set:
verified 0 alpha-differing pixels against its source. The breather silhouette is
the widest in the set, which is why it is the base — it covers a cyan rung and a
gold breather alike with no fringe.

Files: `_tod_gauge.gsc` (the `tod_down` feed, `down_mask_for`, `down_cell_of`,
`TOD_GAUGE_MASK_SPLIT`), `_tod_upgrade_ui.gsc` (re-arm), `tod_upgrade.lua`
(`GaugeDown` layer, `gaApplyCells`, `GA_SPLIT`), `zone_source` + `tod_ui_images.gdt`
+ the new PNG. `lint_tod_arity.js` clean.

**LOCKSTEP:** `TOD_GAUGE_MASK_SPLIT` (GSC) and `GA_SPLIT` (Lua) must stay equal.
A mismatch does not error — it puts red cells in the wrong places.

**FULL build** (new image asset). Not `-GscOnly`.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.49) — Rampage: seal at 9, banner only, smaller and pinned to the top

User: *"Lets move that to round 9 ... we have lingering UI when its triggered. I
had asked to remove all copy UI when Rampage is on ... i turned it on and saw
some text UI in center of screen I dont want any of that. All i want is that when
you turn it on and it gets to round 9 that the image shows. The Rampage Banner.
Also its too big and needs to actually move up on the screen a bit."*

**1. SEAL ROUND 8 → 9.** `TOD_RAMPAGE_LOCK_ROUND`. The header's earning-window
reasoning (a round-5 seal was unreachable for trio and quad) is unaffected — a
later seal only widens the window it was protecting.

**2. THE TOGGLE NO LONGER PRINTS ANYTHING.** `announce()` is deleted outright,
both the ON and OFF lines. That was the "text UI in center of screen": three
`IPrintLnBold` lines fired on every flip of the breaker.

**The feedback is not lost, which is why deleting it outright is safe** — the
toggle still gives four non-text channels: the `zmb_cha_ching` on every flip, the
breaker's own hint re-stamping to its ON/OFF form, the breaker sparking
continuously while armed, and the luck bar swapping to the red art set. **The seal
banner is now the only thing this module ever puts on screen**, which makes it a
signal rather than a formality.

**3. BANNER 20% SMALLER: 600×300 → 480×240.** Exactly 20% off *both* axes, which
is the only legal way to shrink it — the art is 1024×512 = 2:1 and scaling one
axis renders it squashed (the finale banner one element down already paid for
that lesson). 480×240 is still exactly 2:1, verified.

**4. MOVED TO THE TOP: y 90..390 → 24..264.** 24px on a 720-tall canvas is ~3% of
screen height — clearly pinned to the top, clearly not touching it. Combined with
the smaller size it has also stopped reaching into the middle of the screen at
all, which was half of what made it feel oversized.

**Three stale comment blocks corrected**, because the round number appears in
prose in four places and the code in one. The header's *"At round 8 it SEALS"* and
*"WHY ROUND 8 AND NOT ROUND 5"* both now point at `TOD_RAMPAGE_LOCK_ROUND` as the
live value rather than restating it.

**One of those was load-bearing and is worth stating.** `seal_banner()` waits out
the upgrade pause, and its comment justified that by "round 8 **is** a scheduled
upgrade round" (events land on multiples of 4). **Round 9 is not** — so the
justification evaporated while the code stayed correct for a *different* reason:
a personal station pick can pause any round. The wait is kept and the comment now
gives the reason that is actually true. A comment that argues for the right code
from a premise that has silently become false is the kind of thing that gets the
code deleted later by someone who checks the premise.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.48) — Finale spawns: three road bands, and nothing inside the crown

v14.47 shipped and the user play-tested it. **Two defects, both real**, plus a
better design to replace mine.

### 1. WE WERE SPAWNING THEM INSIDE THE CROWN

User: *"are you spawning them inside the crown. The furthest they should spawn is
right at the crown gate."*

Yes, we were. `finale_far_spots()` took the **furthest candidate riser** and
accepted anything within 1,400 units of it. The **hall** risers at y≈8600 are the
furthest, so the band swallowed the crown room.

⚠️ **THE CAP IS NOW A FIXED WORLD Y FROM `gate_org()`, NOT A DISTANCE FROM THE
CANDIDATE SET.** That distinction *is* the bug: anything expressed relative to
"the furthest riser" drifts the instant a riser is added anywhere new. My first
draft of this fix repeated the same relative form and a peer caught it before it
shipped. The cap is applied ahead of **both** the band pick and the
nearest-ahead picker, so neither path can reach the hall during the road run.

### 2. THE ROAD READ EMPTY FOR MOST OF ITS LENGTH

User: *"I basically ran 85% of the way there before I saw any of them ... it
seemed they were waiting for me to start getting close."*

A **consequence of (1)**, not a separate bug. The wall existed and it was building
from the moment extraction was bought — but it was inside a building the player
cannot see into, so the road read as empty until he was on top of it. Fixing the
cap fixes the symptom; the three bands then guarantee contact along the way.

### 3. THE USER'S DISTRIBUTION REPLACES MINE — and it is better

*"I would say 40% crown gate spawn 30% middle of bridge and 30% beginning of
bridge."*

Continuous contact along the whole road instead of one clump at the end. The
binary far/near split is gone; **all** finale road spawns now roll one of three
bands, which are **thirds of the road derived from the two authoritative gate
constants** (`causeway_gate_org` y≈492 → `gate_org` y≈7860), never literals.

| players | rampage | gate | middle | beginning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | off | **40%** | **30%** | **30%** |
| 4 | off | 49% | 30% | 21% |
| 3–4 | on | 52% | 30% | 18% |

Solo with rampage off is **exactly the 40/30/30 that was asked for** — the
condition it was specified in. The earlier scaling ask is preserved as a
deliberately small shift out of *beginning* and into *gate*, so harder settings
make the objective harder to reach rather than the road uniformly busier.

**Elites follow the same roll** (`finale_roll_band` is shared, so trash and elites
cannot drift apart) with **one deliberate exception: band 0 keeps the
player-relative anchor.** A trash zombie spawned at the road's start while the
party is at the crown costs nothing — it walks, and the spawner makes another. An
elite is not fungible: the finale roof is **four**, so a Panzer anchored ~7,000
units behind the party would spend one of four slots on something that cannot
reach the fight. Band 0 therefore keeps that share of elites near and behind the
player, which *is* the beginning of the bridge early in the run.

**Dead code removed rather than left lint-green:** `finale_far_pct()`,
`finale_far_spots()` and the five `TOD_FINALE_FAR_*` defines are gone, and the
v14.47 header block that described the binary split was rewritten — it now
contradicted the code directly beneath it, which is worse than no comment.

⚠️ **Untested.** The user has said they will not re-test before publish. This is
gameplay tuning; reading it cannot verify how it feels.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.47) — THE CROWN-END WALL: the last mile can no longer be outrun

User: *"the biggest issue with the final run for the crown is that zombies are
spawning as you run so if you are fast enough you can just run by all of them ...
most of them and elites should spawn at the end of the path towards the crown.
The issue we are trying to prevent is a fast player running through and not
seeing a single zombie."* Plus: *"this should scale appropriately depending on
players and depending if rampage is on."*

**THE HOLE, NAMED PRECISELY.** `finale_spawn_selection` spawned at the *nearest
riser ahead of a rolled player*. Nearest-ahead is a **trailing** pressure model —
always relative to where you are *now* — so a player moving faster than the spawn
cadence outruns his own wave, and every zombie behind him is one he never meets.
The road is ~8,220 units; at sprint that is under a minute.

**THE FIX IS AN ABSOLUTE ANCHOR, NOT A BIGGER RATE.** (The rate was never the
problem — the finale already runs at a 0.1s spawn floor, the fastest in the map.)
Most spawns now go to the **crown end of the road regardless of where the party
is**, so the horde accumulates between the runner and his objective and walks
*back* at him. Run fast and you meet the wall sooner; walk and you meet it in the
middle. It cannot be outrun because it is not chasing.

The remainder stays on the nearest-ahead picker — the user asked for both ("they
can spawn near you and behind as you run"), and it is what stops the road
becoming one static wall with dead ground behind it.

**SCALING — one function, `finale_far_pct()`, shared by horde and elites** so the
two can never drift apart ("most of them AND elites" is a single design intent,
and two copies of this arithmetic would be two things to retune and one to
forget). Counts only **upright** players, matching every other player pick in the
finale:

| players | rampage off | rampage on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 65% | 77% |
| 2 | 69% | 81% |
| 3 | 73% | 85% |
| 4 | 77% | **88%** (capped) |

Capped at 88 deliberately: **never 100.** A road with nothing at your back stops
being an ambush and becomes a wall you walk into once.

**THE BAND IS MEASURED, NOT HARDCODED.** `finale_far_spots()` takes the furthest
candidate riser and accepts anything within 1,400 units of it, so it tracks
whatever the road actually is — the v12 rebuild moved every lane, and a literal
`y >=` would have rotted. On a ~7,360-long road that is the final fifth: a
cluster with depth, not a point.

**ELITES — one seam, `pick_spawn_point()`.** Every elite type resolves its spawn
through it (Panzer with a front-offset, Protector/Reaver/hounds from the player's
origin, the last two from their own modules), so hooking the anchor there covers
all four **and cannot be forgotten by a fifth added later**. The Panzer's
front-offset is intentionally discarded on a far roll — "in front of the player"
is exactly the trailing model being moved away from.

**Two interactions checked rather than assumed:**
- **The stray relocator does not undo the wall.** `_tod_stray` already stands
  down for the whole finale (`tod_finale_aggro`), so crown-end zombies are not
  yanked back to the player.
- **Far-end spawns are not stranded.** `crown_door_init` leaves the crown door
  `Hide/NotSolid/ConnectPaths` for the entire road run — it only seals on
  arrival — so hall risers inside the far band path straight out through it at
  the player. That is the intended drama, not the stranded-actor trap. Worth
  stating because biasing *toward* the far end would have amplified a rare
  version of that trap into a common one had the door been shut.

**Both halves stand down once the crown seals.** The hold-out wants the room
evenly; "the far end of the candidates" would then just mean the hall's north
wall — a bias with no meaning — and a crown-end elite anchor would point every
navmesh query at a wall `pick_spawn_point` is required to reject, burning both
passes and falling through to "spawn on the player".

No cycle: `_tod_bosses` now imports `_tod_endless_rounds`, verified one-way — the
latter imports only shared modules and generated leaf data modules.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.46) — Music obeys the volume slider; no boss track on the spire; silent OFF seal

### 1. THE MUSIC SLIDER NOW WORKS — the volume group, not the bus

User: *"is it possible to wire up our music to the actual game music lever...
I can go to my settings and lower music volume but the in game music doesnt
lower"*

**It was already on `BUS_MUSIC`. That was never the problem.** All seven music
aliases use `Template = UIN_MOD`, and `UIN_MOD` is a **user-interface** template
(`share/raw/sound/templates/template_mod.csv`): it sets `grp_menu` and `bus_ui`.
Our rows override the *bus* to `BUS_MUSIC` but left **`VolumeGroup` empty**, so
every one of them silently inherited **`grp_menu`** — a menu group the Music
slider does not touch. The bus routed the audio correctly and the mixer grouped
it as UI.

`VolumeGroup` is now `grp_music` on all seven (`tod_ambient_music`,
`tod_music_city`, `tod_music_relay`, `tod_music_eclipse`, `tod_boss_music`,
`tod_music_finale`, `tod_music_spire`).

**Precedent, not a guess:** map 1's own music aliases (`acc_round_sounds.csv`)
set `BUS_MUSIC` **and** `grp_music` together, and its music responds to the
slider. Ours set only the first half.

`DuckGroup` deliberately left at `snp_never_duck` rather than map 1's
`snp_music` — the ask was about volume, and never-duck is load-bearing here (the
finale track is the run's clock and must not be ducked by gunfire).

⚠️ Needs the **sound banks rebuilt**, and these are `STREAMED` aliases, so the
proof is the `.all.sabs` mtime moving with the `.ff` — not a `.ff` grep.

### 2. NO BOSS MUSIC ON THE SPIRE

User: *"No boss music at the spire. Lets keep the music that the spire
specifically has."*

New `boss_music_blocked()` — one predicate read by **both** `boss_track_start`
and `boss_track_end`, so the two can never disagree. It returns true for the
finale latch (unchanged behaviour) and now also for `level.tod_spire_active`.

**Why the spire needed it at all:** the door honour guard spawns up to four
Panzers *per door* across ~100 doors, so up there the Panzer track would not be
an override — it would be the permanent soundtrack, and the spire's own track
would essentially never be heard.

**Both ends, not just the start.** If the boss track was never allowed to take
the channel, the last Panzer death must not "restore" anything either — that
restore would be an audible restart of a stream that never stopped. The refcount
still runs on both paths, so bookkeeping stays correct in every mode. This sits
directly on top of the v14.44 refcount fix; without that, the count would never
have reached zero on the spire anyway.

### 3. RAMPAGE SEALED **OFF** NOW SAYS NOTHING

User: *"when rampage is off and it hits round 8 we display text. lets remove
that. Recently we added a displayed asset when its on but if its off thats fine.
We wont show anything."*

The v14.40 reasoning for keeping a text line was that a mode lock is not routine
chatter. That was wrong in one specific way: **OFF is the default.** A player who
never touched the breaker is not being locked into anything they chose, and
telling them "nothing changed" is precisely the routine chatter the map's own
no-on-screen-captions rule exists to prevent.

The banner is now the only seal announcement, which also makes it a signal rather
than a formality: **if you see anything at round 8, rampage is on.**

## 2026-08-31 (v14.45) — Relocated zombies climb out instead of appearing

User: *"We also have a system where if zombies are too far away from you they
will spawn at you. Its pretty annoying actually cause they just appear. Can we
have them have to spawn back in or is that not possible?"*

Possible, and it is stock's own function. `_tod_stray::relocate` now hands the
zombie to **`_zm_spawner::do_zombie_rise`** at the destination riser: Ghost, move,
face the goal, riser FX, and `AnimScripted` of
`ai_zombie_traverse_ground_climbout_fast` with its notetracks — the identical
climb-out every ordinary spawn plays.

**THE VIEW-CONE TEST WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM**, which is worth recording so nobody
"fixes" it next. Destinations were already stock risers and already outside
every living player's ~80° cone. But a cone test only covers the *instant* of the
move: the player turns around a second later and finds a zombie that was not
there. The giveaway is the **absence of an arrival**, and no amount of visibility
testing can supply one. So the arrival is supplied instead.

**Why stock's function rather than an imitation of it** — verified by reading it,
not assumed: `do_zombie_rise` is fully self-contained. It spawns its own anchor
(`_zm_spawner.gsc:2980`, *inside* the function), links, moves, unlinks and
deletes it. There are no spawn-time preconditions, so a live walking zombie can
be put through it — which is what stock's own board-traversal paths already do to
live zombies elsewhere.

Called **synchronously inside our own thread**, so the goal is set *after* the
climb-out rather than into it. `do_zombie_rise` carries `self endon("death")`,
which therefore ends our thread too — correct, and why no death cleanup is
needed.

**One real interaction, closed:** `in_the_ground` gates only eye-glow timing and
the Giant cleanup manager — **not** the behaviour tree — so nothing stock stops
this map's own 1.5s speed sweep from re-asserting gait and animation rate
underneath a scripted animation. `apply_speed_for_round` now returns early while
`in_the_ground` is set. Stock's field rather than a new tod flag on purpose: it
covers this relocation rise *and* every ordinary spawn-time riser, so nothing new
has to remember to opt in. `_tod_stray` re-asserts the rate the moment the
climb-out finishes, so no zombie is left at the wrong gait.

No import cycle: `_zm_spawner` references no tod module and is already imported
by seven of them.

**AND IT PLUGS A LEAK IN STOCK'S OWN FUNCTION** — found by tracing every exit
after a peer asked whether the clear path was unconditional. It is not.
`do_zombie_rise` opens with `self endon("death")`, spawns a `script_origin`
anchor at `:2980`, and does not delete it until `:3013` — with two `waittill`s
in between. **A zombie killed inside that ~0.1s window ends the thread before the
delete, orphaning the anchor forever.**

Stock carries the same exposure at spawn time and gets away with it: spawn-time
rises are bounded by the round's spawn rate, and a zombie is rarely killed during
its own emergence. **We would not have.** Relocations fire continuously, and on
the **spire** they fire against a 0.18s spawn floor and a saturated elite roof —
the mode where the ~1024-slot gentity table is the binding constraint. A slow
leak of invisible script_origins there is precisely the bug that surfaces hours
later as something unrelated failing to spawn.

`rise_cleanup_guard()` deletes the anchor on death and ends on `"risen"` in the
normal case, so it costs one short-lived thread per relocation and does nothing
the rest of the time.

**THE ONE HOLE THAT REMAINS IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A CURRENT STATE.** The guard
hangs off `"death"`, so a zombie **deleted outright without dying** would still
orphan its anchor. No such path exists today, verified on both sides rather than
assumed: corpse cleanup deletes only after death, `_tod_spire::wipe_all_zombies`
uses `Kill()` (so death fires and the guard runs), and
`_tod_spire::teardown_tower` deletes only tracked script props — door triggers,
slabs, structs, teleporter beams, finale hosts — and touches no AI at all. **The
day someone adds an actor `Delete()` to a teardown sweep is the day this hole
opens.** If you are writing that sweep, `Kill()` first or clear `self.anchor`
yourself.

The companion worry — `in_the_ground` stuck true forever, leaving a zombie at
stock gait — **is moot, checked rather than assumed**: the zombie is dead, gait is
irrelevant, and fields cannot leak between zombies because every spawn is a fresh
actor rather than a pooled one. Cleared in the guard anyway so a corpse never
reads as mid-rise.

⚠️ **Unproven until played.** `_tod_stray` has only ever been boot-verified — its
sweep and pump lanes have never had a real run — and this change puts a live,
walking zombie through a scripted animation, which is the part that most wants
eyes on it.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.44) — Boss music stuck on; armored sprinters slowed

Two live-run bugs from the user, both one-site fixes.

### 1. THE BOSS TRACK NEVER RELEASED THE CHANNEL

User: *"On rampage mode the music gets stuck on boss music even after killing
both panzers."*

**A refcount that only ever decremented once.** `boss_track_start()` is called
**once per Panzer spawn**, so two Panzers push `tod_panzer_music_count` to 2. But
the matching `boss_track_end()` was wrapped in `if ( level.tod_panzer_alive <= 0 )`,
so only ONE end call was ever allowed through — the count landed on 1, never
reached 0, and the boss track owned the channel for the rest of the match.

**The guard was solving a problem the refcount already solves.** Its comment said
it existed because "the first death cut the boss track while others were still
hunting you" — but `boss_track_end()` only swaps back when the count hits zero,
so the first of two deaths takes it 2 → 1 and correctly changes nothing. A
second, cruder gate stacked on top of a working counter is what produced the bug.
Removed; the contract is now **one start, one end, always**, and anything that
spawns a Panzer inherits it for free.

**It was never rampage-specific, and the spire had it worse.** Rampage is simply
the mode where two Panzers are reliably alive at once. `_tod_spire`'s door honour
guard spawns up to `TOD_SPIRE_GUARD_MAX` (**4**) per door — four starts against
one end — so the music would have stuck permanently after the *first* spire door,
on every spire run. That path had not been played yet.

### 2. ARMORED SPRINTERS: `TOD_SPRINT_SPEED_ADD` +10 → **−10**

User: *"The armored sprinters should actually move -10 round speed instead of +10
round speed."*

A sign flip on the existing offset — they now run **slower** than the round they
appear in rather than faster. The armor and the 20× health are what make them a
threat; a heavy thing that lumbers reads as heavier than one that outruns you.
Still an offset rather than a rate multiplier, for the reason that block has
always given.

Computed against the live constants rather than estimated:

| round | plain | old (+10) | new (−10) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 0.965 | 1.020 | **0.847** |
| 20 | 1.006 | 1.034 | **0.906** |
| 30 | 1.034 | 1.062 | **1.006** |
| 40 | 1.062 | 1.090 | **1.034** |

The gap narrows with altitude because the curve flattens past round 18 — a big
early nerf, a small late one, the same shape the +15 → +12 retune had.

**No degenerate values in a ship build**, checked rather than assumed: sprinters
unlock on the floor-30 door, so the earliest realistic appearance is ~round 15 and
the floor is **0.847** — above the live-tested round-1 rate of 0.8. (A dev build
with every door forced open at round 1 reaches ~0.68: visibly slow, not broken,
and unreachable in a real match.) **Under rampage the table does not apply** —
`full_round()` returns 10 there, so the ramp is steeper and −10 bites harder
early: round 15 reads 0.889.

**Three stale comments corrected** in the same pass — the file header, the retune
block, and `_tod_zombie_speed`'s offset note all still asserted `+15` or `+12`,
and one told the next reader not to "fix the offset upward without a fresh ask"
without recording that a fresh ask had since taken it negative. The offset is
signed now, and nothing in `apply_speed_for_round` assumed otherwise.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.40) — SKY REVERTED TO MIAMI: the spire is the dark place, so the tower must not be

User, on seeing v14.37 darken the whole map: *"But its only in the spire
correct? Thats the whole point."* Right, and v14.37 got it wrong in a way worth
recording rather than quietly undoing.

**THE SKYBOX IS A BAKED WORLDSPAWN KEY — it cannot be spire-only.** So darkening
it to serve the spire necessarily darkened the tower too, and that works
*against* the feature: arriving somewhere black is a smaller moment if you were
already somewhere black. The contrast IS the effect.

**And the revert costs the spire nothing**, which is the load-bearing fact:
at `TOD_SPIRE_FOG_OPACITY 0.90` with `TOD_SPIRE_FOG_HALFDIST 1400`, anything at
sky distance is fully fogged, so **the skybox is invisible from the spire
regardless of which one is baked**. The baked sky therefore only ever decides
how the TOWER looks — so it should be picked for the tower, and the spire's own
fog does all the work up there.

* `gen_tower_map.js` `SKYBOX_MODEL`/`SSI` and the zone `xmodel,` line all back
  to `skybox_t9_mp_miami` + `acc_ssi_miami_night`, in lockstep (the ssi carries
  its own `skyboxmodel` key — the pair must move together or they fight).
* **Tower fog STAYS ON** at `TOD_FOG_OPACITY 0.38` — separately requested
  ("lets add fog on the tower") and unaffected by this revert.
* The dark pairing is documented in place, not deleted: `acc_ssi_dark_night` +
  `skybox_t9_zm_silver_dark` is proven-good and is a safe one-line swap if a
  darker tower is ever wanted (the two ssi entries are identical apart from
  their skybox, so it touches neither the sun rig nor the bake).

FULL build required — worldspawn keys live in the BSP. Gates: geometry lint
green no-regression, arity green across 68, regen coherent.

## 2026-08-31 (v14.39) — CLASS TIER: the locked card

User: *"What about a design where you get the card but you cant select it and we
use this asset to show that during the upgrade menu"*

v14.35 hid the tier card when the player was below its floor gate. Now the card
is **dealt and shown, locked** — you see the exact gun you are climbing toward,
dimmed, with the gate badge as its caption. Seeing the thing beats inferring an
absence.

**THE COST, STATED UP FRONT AND ACCEPTED.** The user was offered a third
"preview" slot that keeps both real cards, and chose the locked card in its
normal RIGHT slot instead. So on the deals where the tier card rolls below the
gate floor, the deal is effectively **one card, not two**. It is bounded — the
same ~20% `TOD_TIER_CARD_PCT` roll as always, and very few upgrade events happen
below floor 10 — but it is a real cost and it is deliberate, not an oversight.

**THE ROLL MOVED, THE GATE DID NOT.** `roll_options` now asks
`tier_card_ready_but_for_floor()` instead of the full `tier_card_eligible()`, so
a floor-blocked player draws the promotion. The floor now decides whether a dealt
card is *takeable*, not whether it *exists*. `tier_up()` still asks the full
question, so nothing can actually promote through this.

**THE REFUSAL LIVES AT ONE PLACE.** `wait_for_choice` gained a `locked` slot
index, enforced at the single point where every input lane commits `want -> sel`
— not in each of the seven lanes that can produce a `want` (d-pad, movement
stick, four action buttons, KBM). A lane added later cannot bypass it. **Audible**
(`zmb_no_purchase`), because a control that silently does nothing reads as a
broken trigger; it can only fire on an input edge, so holding a direction into
the locked card cannot machine-gun the sound.

**TWO WAYS THIS COULD HAVE PRODUCED A DEAD PANEL, both closed:**
1. *Only the right slot is ever lockable.* Focus starts on the left card and a
   timeout locks whatever is focused, so an unselectable panel is impossible by
   construction rather than by care.
2. *A lone locked card is never dealt.* With the domain pool empty and the
   promotion out of reach, `roll_options` returns nothing rather than freezing
   the world for a panel with no answer — that is the leaver-stall bug's shape
   with a different cause. The round event's participant filter already declined
   this player; the guard covers the station path, which does not go through it.

**NO NEW DATA CHANNEL.** The client infers the lock from what it already has:
`bd == TIER_DOMAIN` (a tier card is in the right slot) **and**
`CoD.TodTierNeed > 0` (this player is floor-blocked) can only mean the dealt card
is the locked one. A tier card dealt to a player who has cleared the floor
arrives with `need == 0` and stays takeable. The card's own `cur` field already
carried `tier_card_code`, so the Lua was already drawing the correct per-class
tier art — nothing had to be added for it to name the gun.

**THE BADGE HAS TWO HOMES, NEVER BOTH.** STAMPED ACROSS the locked card when one
is dealt; in the top-left gutter otherwise. Same asset, repositioned per paint —
the v14.35 art needed no re-bake.

The stamp band is MEASURED off the 768x1152 card art, not eyeballed: the card is
dense with text that must survive (the `TIER 2` header, the class banner, the gun
name and the `GUN UPGRADES RESET` warning), so the badge lands on the gun
ILLUSTRATION only — screen y 336..396 — and never on a word. Being able to read
what you are climbing toward is the whole reason the card is dealt instead of
hidden.

**Z-ORDER BUG CAUGHT BY MOVING IT (user: "with these new images over the top of
it" — it was UNDER).** `TierGateImg` was added to the menu BEFORE `CardA`/`CardB`,
and LUI draws in addElement order — so a badge stamped over the card would have
rendered BEHIND it and been invisible. Harmless while it sat in the empty gutter,
fatal the moment it moved onto the card, and the symptom would have read as "the
new art did not pack" — sending the next reader to audit the GDT and the zone
lines for a pure draw-order mistake. Construction is now deferred until after both
cards; the declaration stays early so the render closure still captures it.

**Look:** a normal unfocused card already sits at 0.4 alpha, which is not enough —
"unfocused" and "unselectable" would look identical and the player would keep
trying to reach it. The locked card drops to 0.22 **and** takes a cold grey-blue
tint no live card ever has. Both directions of that tint are written every paint;
`setRGB` persists on the element, so skipping the restore would make the *next*
deal's live card look dead.

**THE DIM WAS RETUNED IN THE SAME PASS: 0.22 -> 0.55.** Alpha and tint MULTIPLY,
and 0.22 x ~0.5 lands near 0.11 effective — grey enough that the gun name stopped
being readable, which defeats the point of showing the card at all. 0.55 x ~0.6
= ~0.33: below a live unfocused card, still legible. The TINT, not the alpha, is
what carries "dead".

**One near-miss worth recording.** The deny sound was written as
`PlayLocalSound( "zmb_no_purchase" )`. Grepping for a precedent returned exactly
one hit — **my own new line**. Every `PlayLocalSound` in this map pairs with a
custom `tod_*` alias; the only proven pairing for that stock alias is
`PlaySound`, four times in `_tod_ammo_crate`. Switched. A self-citation is not a
precedent, and the failure mode of guessing wrong here is silence — the exact
thing the sound exists to prevent.

## 2026-08-30 (v14.38) — RAMPAGE: a down is a party event

User: *"On rampage if a player goes down everyone loses 50% luck."* The sixth
Rampage lever, and the first that is not about the enemy at all — it attacks the
party's shared **card economy** instead of the horde's stat block, which is the
axis the other five (speed ramp, elite throughput, spawn pacing, elite HP, HUD
tell) never touch.

**MULTIPLICATIVE, not a flat subtraction.** "Loses 50%" reads as *halve the
bar*, and halving is the version that scales: it costs a banked player 50 and a
broke player almost nothing, so the penalty tracks how much you had to lose. It
therefore bites hardest exactly when the party cares most — a full bar, or an
**OVERCHARGE at 150**, halves to 75 and falls out of the guaranteed-ultimate
band. That is the loudest consequence in the system and it needs no new cue.

**IT STACKS ON TOP OF THE EXISTING PERSONAL `TOD_LUCK_DOWN` 25, deliberately.**
The alternative — halving *replaces* the 25 for the downed player — was
considered and rejected: at a low bar it would make a RAMPAGE down cheaper than
a normal-match down (bar 10: halve = −5 versus the flat −25 that floors them).
**A hard mode must never be softer than the base game on any input.** Net at a
full bar: the downed player pays 62.5, everyone else pays 50.

**Every write goes through `set_bar`**, which is the single owner of the 0/150
clamp, the HUD refresh, the segment-pip rule (downward crossings are silent — so
a halving makes no ding, and the bar dropping *is* the read) and the overcharge
state. `overcharge_driver` polls its own exit, so a 150 → 75 halving ends the
zap animation and its 3 s deep-zap within one 0.15 s tick with nothing to clean
up at the call site.

**No cycle.** `_tod_luck.gsc` field-reads `level.tod_rampage_on` with `IS_TRUE`
and does not `#using` `_tod_rampage` — the same contract as
`_tod_zombie_speed::full_round`. With RAMPAGE off the function is never called,
so behaviour is byte-identical to before.

Scope notes: `GetPlayers()` is the whole connected party — players who are
themselves down or spectating are included on purpose, or a wiped teammate walks
back in with an untouched bar. In **solo** "everyone" is one player, so the lever
still bites (62.5 of a full bar instead of 25). **No debounce**, per the spec:
two downs inside one 0.5 s `down_watcher` tick fire twice and quarter the bar —
correct for "if a player goes down", and named in the code as the first knob to
revisit if co-op wipes feel unrecoverable.

One file (`_tod_luck.gsc`): `TOD_LUCK_DOWN_PARTY_MULT 0.5`, `party_down_drain()`,
and one gated call inside the existing laststand edge test in `down_watcher()`.

## 2026-08-30 (v14.37) — THE MAP HAS NEVER RENDERED FOG: the 8-arg SetVolFog has no opacity argument

User: *"I want to make the map darker and foggier when the endless spire starts.
And we did some interesting stuff with fog on abandoned cybercity. We moved it
around because just on and off didnt work."* Following that pointer found a
defect older than either map.

**THE BUG.** `SetVolFog`'s **8-argument overload has no opacity parameter** —
its 8th slot is **`<transition time>`**. Both this map and map 1 have passed an
"opacity" there since they were authored, so `TOD_FOG_OPACITY 0.55` was a
0.55-second fade, and max opacity stayed at whatever the fog settings asset
booted with. Ours boots `"fsi" "default"`, and `<modtools>/source_data/fog.gdt`
ships that entry with **`"fogopacity" "0"`**. Verified three independent ways
before acting:
1. `<modtools>/docs_modtools/bo3_scriptapifunctions.htm` — the 8-arg form ends
   `<red>,<green>,<blue>,<transition time>`; `<fog max opacity>` exists ONLY in
   the 18-arg form, as arg 17.
2. Stock's only call site, `load_shared.gsc:807`, passes `0.4` there — a
   0.4-second blend for a fog-volume trigger. **This is the very cite our own
   file header used to claim proved the opposite; it had been misread.**
3. `fog.gdt` `default` → `fogopacity 0`, unreachable from any 8-arg call.

**USER CONFIRMED LIVE: "Yes this map has never rendered fog."** So the cold
purple-blue city smog, the height-as-progress design ("climb out of the smog by
mid-tower"), and the finale's ember sky turn have all been invisible for the
life of the map — every one of those values was tuned against `preview_crown.js`
and never once seen in game. It also retro-explains map 1's blood-paid
"zeroing opacity does NOT clear it" (`_acc_atmosphere.gsc:51-52`): correct
symptom, wrong mechanism — it was setting a 0-second fade. Map 1's two famous
workarounds, sinking `baseHeight` to fade out and pushing `startDist` past the
world to switch off, were both compensating for a lever it never had.

**THE FIX** — every write in `_tod_atmosphere.gsc` now goes through the 18-arg
form (`set_fog` / `spire_set_fog`), the only one carrying `<fogMaxOpacity>`:
* **TOWER FOG IS ON** at `TOD_FOG_OPACITY 0.38` — deliberately RETUNED DOWN
  from the authored 0.55, because 0.55 was picked by eye against an offline
  tool and the first build where fog actually draws should not also be the one
  that buries the neon look nobody has seen it interact with. Raise it once it
  has been looked at.
* **`fogColorScale` (arg 8) is the real DARKNESS knob** and the 8-arg form
  could never reach it: it multiplies the fog colour, 1 = darkest, 10000 =
  blown out (mp_apartments ships 290). Tower holds 1; the spire pins 1
  deliberately, which is what makes it dark rather than merely hazy.
* Sun-fog RGB is pinned to the fog colour and its cone squeezed to 0-1°, so
  even if the engine applies the sun term it cannot introduce a hue we did not
  choose.
* **SPIRE:** real opacity 0.90, near-black red, halfDist 1400, halfHeight
  42,000 (density still 53% at the 38,592 summit — the red holds the whole
  climb and there is no horizon). Rises 0 → 0.90 over ~6s on ascension, then
  re-asserts. `baseHeight` deliberately does NOT track players: fog is one
  server-wide global and a moving base would pulse as the party spreads out.
* Ported map 1's proven emergency off as `spire_fog_kill()` (push the fog
  beyond the world — there is no fog-off builtin). Unused, deliberately.

**DARKER SKY — a FULL-BUILD change** (user: *"make the map darker or change the
sky box to something dark"*): worldspawn `skyboxmodel`/`ssi` swapped
`skybox_t9_mp_miami` + `acc_ssi_miami_night` → **`skybox_t9_zm_silver_dark` +
`acc_ssi_dark_night`**, plus the zone's `xmodel` line in lockstep (the ssi
carries its own `skyboxmodel` key — move the pair together or they fight).
Diffed in `acc_nastian_t9_skyboxes.gdt`: the two ssi entries are **identical
except for the skybox** (same colorSRGB, ev 6, evcmp 2.5, evmax/min, stops
−2.2, pitch 130, bounceCount 4, dynamicShadow), so this changes the sky IMAGE
and nothing about the sun rig — the lighting solve is unchanged. Darker still
available if wanted: `skybox_t9_mp_black_sea`, `skybox_t9_mp_moscow`.
NOTE the skybox can only change at BUILD time — it is a baked worldspawn key,
which is exactly why the spire's *dynamic* sky is done with fog instead.

Gates: geometry lint green no-regression, arity green across 68 files,
regen clean. **Nothing here is play-verified — this is the first build in the
map's history where volumetric fog can draw at all, so every value above is a
first guess and the tower's 0.38 is the one most likely to need moving.**

## 2026-08-30 (v14.36) — SPIRE DOORS: one per FLOOR, tower-matched (100 doors restored)

User: *"each door is 4 set of stairs between each where the normal tower is 2...
I want the endless spire to match that 2 set of stairs per door. Please
implement. Its existing so i dont see a need to wait."*

v14.23's 50 doors were one per LAP-PAIR — a compromise taken while the entity
budget was suspect. This restores the original v14.0 cadence: **100 doors, one
per floor, alternating faces by parity** exactly like the tower's own DOORS
table (odd floor → E face y=−256, even floor → W face y=+256, because odd
flights climb E+N and even flights W+S). v14.23's doors were all E-face
precisely BECAUSE they only sealed odd floors; a per-floor door that ignored
parity would hang on the wrong side of the core every other floor.

**THE v14.0 CRASH DIAGNOSIS WAS NEVER ISOLATED — and this build is the test.**
The received wisdom is that 100 resident spire slabs exhausted the ~1024-slot
gentity table at init and cost the crown altar its trigger. But **v14.1 shipped
TWO fixes for that ONE symptom in a single release**: the slab cut (100→2) AND
`_tod_upgrades::station_place` reordering so the trigger manager launches first
instead of behind four unguarded `Spawn()` calls. Either alone could have been
the cure; nothing separated them, and the changelog then asserted the
entity-pressure cause as fact. Measured today: the `.map` contributes **166
runtime-gentity entities at 50 doors, 216 at 100** (160 script_brushmodel + 53
trigger_use + 3 misc) against a ~1024 table — a 21% delta on a budget with 5×
headroom, which is not a plausible crash mechanism on its own, whereas "four
unguarded Spawns upstream of the trigger manager" is a concrete ordering bug.
**THE EVIDENCE FOR THE ENTITY-PRESSURE STORY IS NOW NEGATIVE** (user, live,
2026-08-30, via the session auditing the altar): *"So the crown altar has never
had the buy prompt and still doesnt. We never solved that."* The v14.0
diagnosis rested entirely on the inference *we cut the slabs and the altar came
back* — **the altar never came back.** It has been trigger-less in every build
before and after v14.1, at 100 slabs, at 2, and at 50. So the slab cut is not
merely unisolated from the `station_place` reordering; the symptom that
motivated BOTH fixes was never resolved by either, and the altar is a separate
open bug that cannot be used as a canary for anything. **A canary that was
already dead cannot tell you the air is bad.**

**The empirical check is therefore the DIRECT measurement, not a proxy:** the
dev headroom probe in `_tod_spire::init` spawns throwaway `script_origin`s
until the pool refuses (capped 150), frees them, and prints the count. That
number — not the altar, not any downstream symptom — is what decides whether
100 resident slabs are affordable. This build is ARMED specifically so it
prints.

Separately, this build can also finally DIAGNOSE the altar, because dev is on
and `_tod_upgrades` already carries the instrumentation: a print of
`"altar 5: trigger up at <org>"` means the trigger exists and the bug is
reach/visibility; `"altar 5: TRIG SPAWN FAILED (pool)"` means G_Spawn is
refusing; NO print at all means the manager never ran. That discriminates
three long-suspected causes in one boot, and only the middle one would be
genuine entity-pressure evidence.

Sites (all lockstep — a mis-key here is the out-of-playable INSTAKILL, since a
chunk whose flag never fires is a DISABLED zone and stock answers that with the
Samantha laugh and an unrevivable kill):
- `gen_tower_map.js` — `SPIRE_DOORS` one per floor with parity; `.map` emits
  100 slabs; `_tod_spire_data` gains `spire_door_count() = 100`, parity-aware
  `get_spire_door_info`, `spire_door_z(n) = (n−1)·384`, and a parity-aware
  `guard_spawn_org` (odd → NE +336/+336, even → SW −336/−336).
- `zm_tower_of_doom.gsc` zone chain — back to the direct keying
  `enter_spire{5k+1}` (v14.23's `int((5k+2)/2)` lap-pair arithmetic existed
  only because a door covered two floors); summit rides `enter_spire100`.
- `_tod_spire::door_manager` riser gate — `door_z + 400`, one floor (was +784;
  leaving it would wake risers a full floor above the highest bought door —
  the stranded-actor trap the gate exists to prevent).

Knock-on, deliberate: the climb doubles to **300,000 points** (100 × flat 3000)
and the v14.31 honour guard now fires **100 times**, so a full climb is ~100
Panzer fights and ~100 × 30s of sealed holds. That is the intended answer to
"its just run simulator", but it is a large swing and the first thing to
revisit if the climb reads as long rather than hard.

Gates: geometry lint green no-regression, arity green across 68 files,
generator coherence proven (regen is a byte no-op). Spire 7109 brushes / 594
entities. **ARMED build (dev+god per the measurement plan) — NOT a publish
candidate.**

## 2026-08-30 (v14.35) — CLASS TIER: a FLOOR GATE on top of Pack-a-Punch

User: *"You must also reach floor 10 to get 2nd tier class upgrade and floor 20
for 3rd tier. I dont want players able to be tier 2 or 3 before even opening the
first door to the tower."*

The TIER card now needs TWO things, not one: the class gun Pack-a-Punched **and**
the player's own climb high-water at **floor 10** for the promotion into tier 2,
**floor 20** for tier 3.

**WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN.** The PaP requirement was doing this job by accident:
the first Pack-a-Punch reachable while climbing IS the floor-10 breather vendor
(the crown machine sits above all 50 laps), so the normal route already implied
floor 10. The hole was the **FREE-PAP POWERUP** — it sets `player.tod_pap_owned`
wherever it drops, so one lucky drop in the base arena made a tier-1 player
eligible with no doors bought. Tier 3 had a second, quieter hole: you could PaP
the T2 gun at the *same* floor-10 machine and promote again without climbing a
step.

So for the intended route this costs nothing — floors 10 and 20 are exactly the
first two breathers, which is where the PaP machines are — and it closes both
shortcuts.

**THE HIGH-WATER** (`_tod_gauge`). `real_floor_of()` is `floor_of()`'s ungrouped
sibling: the gauge folds two floors into one art cell and pins the roof to cell
26, both answers about the BAR; this one answers about the TOWER, so the gate is
written against the floor numbers the player reads on their own HUD. The 0.35 s
gauge poll keeps a per-player maximum in `player.tod_floor_best`:

* **It only ever rises.** The gate asks "have you been there", not "are you there
  now" — you can take the promotion at a base station or on a teleporter pad once
  you have earned it. It is also why nothing re-checks the floor after a card is
  dealt: a card that was legal when dealt stays legal.
* **Alive + playing only.** A dead player spectates a teammate and their
  `.origin` rides that camera — sampling spectators would have handed a body in
  the base arena the climber's floor, which is the exact free ride being closed.
  Last stand still samples (`sessionstate` stays `"playing"`, `isalive` TRUE): a
  downed player really is on that floor.
* **8-unit epsilon**, because a player standing on a landing has their feet at
  the exact z boundary between two floors and one ground-trace hair under it
  reads as the floor below. Half a stair riser — it cannot promote anyone who has
  not arrived, and cannot demote anyone who has.
* Clamps at floor 50, so the crown, the causeway and the Endless Spire all report
  the top floor instead of running off the end.

**WHERE IT BITES.** `tier_floor_ok()` sits inside `tier_card_eligible()`, which
`tier_up()` re-asks before every promotion — so the gate holds on the round
event, the personal station's deferred cards, and the redeal paths alike, with
one edit. `has_upgrade_headroom` inherits it too: a maxed player below floor 10
correctly reads as having nothing to spend, and the overcharge cue comes back on
its own when they climb (that test is polled live, never latched).

**THE SPIRE GRANT is stamped, not exempted.** `grant_all` calls
`tod_gauge::mark_top_reached()` before its `tier_up` ladder. Anyone ascending has
stood in the citadel far above floor 50 so the high-water already clears the
gate — but the grant runs in the same breath as the teleport out, and a grant is
not a thing that may lose a race with a 0.35 s poll.

While reading that grant, note it now answers to **two independent per-class
rules from two different passes**, and both are correct: this floor gate decides
*whether* `tier_up` fires (satisfied unconditionally by the stamp), and v14.33's
`domain_max()` decides *how far* each domain climbs — so an ascended skirmisher
takes DR to **5**, not 10, exactly as they would have on the tower. A "maxed"
grant is per-class maxed, not universally maxed. Neither is a bug; they are just
no longer readable from one place.

**NOT waived by `level.tod_dev`.** A dev session that skips its own gate cannot
test it, and the dev build already gets up there fast.

No card art changes: the eight baked tier cards name the gun each promotion hands
out and never carried the requirement. Files: `_tod_upgrades.gsc` (the gate +
`TOD_TIER2_FLOOR`/`TOD_TIER3_FLOOR`), `_tod_gauge.gsc` (`real_floor_of` /
`floor_reached` / `mark_top_reached` + the poll), `_tod_spire.gsc` (the stamp),
`_tod_powerups.gsc` (comment).

### Part 2 — TELLING THE PLAYER (user: *"how can we add some clue"*)

A withheld tier card is silent, and a rule nobody can discover is just an
unexplained absence. Two displays; **no rule moves**.

**THE PaP PROMPT WAS THE OBVIOUS PLACE AND IT IS A DEAD LANE.** `ZMCursorHintNew.lua:205-213`
routes any hint containing "pack" AND "punch" to a STATIC Pack-a-Punch card that
renders its own fixed title/blurb/cost and never looks at the string — the map
already paid for this once (`_tod_powerups.gsc:855`, where a "REQUIRES POWER"
overwrite was both invisible *and* a regression over stock's working card).
Banners and floaty text are out by earlier user calls. That left two lanes, and
both are used:

1. **A badge on the upgrade panel** reading `TIER 2 AT FLOOR 10`, in the
   top-left gutter — the exact mirror of the luck badge slot (280x60 at
   x 50..330 against its x 950..1230, same row), so the panel now carries what
   BOOSTED this deal on one side and what is being WITHHELD from it on the
   other. Shown **only when the floor is the sole blocker** (`tier_floor_pending`:
   PaP already done, not top tier, asset linked, no powerup gun). It stays silent
   for every other reason on purpose — a line that fires for everything teaches
   players to stop reading it, and telling a player who has not Pack-a-Punched to
   go climb would be true and useless. New eventstring `tod_upg_tier_need` on the
   **zero-bit int `LuiNotifyEvent` lane**, so the clientuimodel pool stays at its
   proven 61-bit ceiling; precached, because the silent-no-fire trap is already
   two-for-two on this map. Pushed unconditionally (0 included) before **every**
   deal, which is what keeps a stale value from surfacing later and why nothing
   has to clear the line when the panel closes.
2. **The pause-menu CLASS TIER row now sends from tier 1** (was tier 2 on), and
   its detail line states what the *next* promotion costs — `tier 2:
   Pack-a-Punch + floor 10`, then `tier 3: ... floor 20`, then `final tier`. This
   is the idiom the user already chose for the tier-reset badge. `DETAIL[24].act`
   became a **function of the level** — the only such row — behind the same
   `pcall` guard `val` uses.

**Checked rather than assumed:** the pause panel's `atTopTier` test is `lvl >= max`
with an explicit nil path documented "ABSENT MEANS TIER 1", so sending 1-of-3
takes the same branch the nil path took and every other row's reset badge is
unaffected. `AetheriumStartMenu.lua` needed **no change at all** — the line
arrives through `CoD.TodDomainDesc`.

**IMAGES OVER LUI — THE ART IS IN.** The badge is two baked PNGs
(`i_tod_tier_gate_2` / `_3`, 420×90 on the luck badge's own canvas) behind
`USE_TIER_GATE_ART`, now **true**. The user picked explore direction 3 — steel
pill, amber stacked double chevron, reading as *climb* rather than *refused*.
Verified before install: 420×90 / colortype 6 read from the PNG headers, and
legibility checked by **downscaling to the on-screen 280×60 and looking at it**
rather than trusting the spec. The delivered type is lighter than the luck
badge's heavy outlined face — a deviation from the chassis brief that survives
the reduction cleanly, so it was kept. The LUI text survives as the no-art
fallback. Prompt, chassis specs, five explore directions and the install
order: **docs/50**. **A `.gdt` edit makes this a FULL build**, not the `-GscOnly`
the script half would have been. The design call worth recording: the badge must **not** be
gold — the luck badge already is, 620px away on the same row, and a second gold
pill gets pattern-matched and skipped by exactly the player this exists for. It
is a dimmed steel pill with an amber padlock, so the pair reads as *earned* vs
*withheld*. The pause row needs no asset at all: `i_tod_pause_r24` already
exists, and that panel draws all ~30 rows' detail lines as text by design —
baking level-aware lines that move on every retune is the opposite of what the
images-over-LUI rule is for.

**THE FIRST PLACEMENT WAS WRONG AND MEASUREMENT CAUGHT IT.** This began as a
strip under the cards. The free band there is 38px — card hints end at 612,
`SwitchHintImg` occupies 650..693, the countdown 697..717 — so anything legible
would have landed on the switch hint. Read the neighbours' coordinates before
placing a HUD element, not after.

`tier_card_eligible()` split into `tier_card_ready_but_for_floor() && tier_floor_ok()`
so the hint can ask "is the floor the *only* blocker" without a second copy of
the other four conditions drifting. One implementation of each rule, still.
`tier_up()` and the spire's `grant_all` are behaviourally identical.

⚠ **LOCKSTEP:** the floor numbers now also live in `tod_upgrade.lua`'s
`DETAIL[24].act` — the client cannot ask the server for them (61-bit ceiling), so

## 2026-08-30 (v14.33) — SKIRMISHER: DR capped at 5, primaries −10% again

User: *"Skirmisher damage resistance can only go to 5 levels instead of 10.
Also reduce damage for skirmisher primary by another 10%."*

**1. DR CAPPED AT 5 FOR THE SKIRMISHER.** DMG REDUCTION (id 2) is a SHARED
domain at max 10; the slasher was already held to 5 in v14.11 through the
`bonus_class`/`bonus_max` pair used as a downward override. **`bonus_class` now
accepts an ARRAY** (`array( "slasher", "skirmisher" )`) so one domain can cap
two classes — extending the array is the way to add a third, never cloning the
domain. `domain_max()` handles both forms and stays the single authority.

Audited rather than assumed: every per-player cap consumer already routes
through `domain_max()` — make_option, roll_options, both guarantee paths, the
redeal clamps, `tier_up`'s sync, `refresh_upgrade_list`, `player_has_domains_left`
and the spire grant — and `sync_max()` (the pause menu / pip count / reset badge)
calls it too. So the cap reaches the UI with no Lua change; the static max in
`tod_upgrade.lua` remains a nil-fallback only.

Assault and heavy still reach −50% incoming. Skirmisher and slasher now stop at
−25%.

**2. PRIMARIES −10% AGAIN.** `CLASS_DAMAGE_MULT.skirmisher` 1.19025 →
**1.071225**. That is ×0.9 twice = **×0.81 of where the class started the day**,
not ×0.8 — the second cut is 10% of the already-reduced number, which is what
"another 10%" means.

| | base | PaP | vs start of day |
|---|---|---|---|
| MAC-10 | 167 → **150** | 209 → **188** | ×0.81 |
| MP5 | 338 → **304** | 423 → **380** | ×0.81 |
| MP7 | 483 → **434** | 604 → **543** | ×0.81 |

**Secondaries held with NO second edit**, because v14.32 pinned
`CLASS_SEC_CAP_MULT` to an ABSOLUTE 1.3225 rather than a ratio. Bulldog / SG12 /
SPAS-12 all byte-identical again. Blast radius 48 damage lines across exactly
three stems.

**Compounded survivability note, worth having before this is play-judged:** the
skirmisher's effective HP drops from **400 to 267** (150 ÷ 0.5625, sprinting with
SPRINT ARMOR) — second-squishiest in the map, while also being the fastest — in
the same pass that cut its damage by a further 10%. Four separate reductions
landed on this class today across the two versions; nothing in either request
was wrong, but the total is larger than either implies.

Armory updated for both, plus two staleness fixes the audit surfaced: the
skirmisher survivability row (37.5% → 56.3%) and the heavy's jugg e-HP, which
still assumed the broken 200 that v14.28 fixed (now 300 max HP → ≈857 e-HP).
`tools/verify_armory_constants.js` green: 23 constants, 0 mismatches.

## 2026-08-30 (v14.31) — SPIRE DIFFICULTY: 4x elites, a Panzer honour guard per door, and a 30s seal

User, after the first genuinely playable spire run (the v14.19 navmesh seeds +
v14.23 doors made it a real mode): *"The endless spire is too easy. We need to
add way more eliets and think about how doors open... 4x the elites of what we
currently have... Maybe after every door buy a panzer will spawn. 1-4 depending
on players in game"* and *"we need a 30s delay per buying each door. So you need
to stay and fight for a bit and cant just run through each door if you have lots
of money."* The diagnosis behind all three: the spire was a **run simulator** —
round-scheduled elite waves decayed between rounds, and a rich party could buy
50 doors back-to-back without ever holding ground.

* **4x ELITES ON THE SPIRE** (`TOD_SPIRE_ELITE_MULT 4`, consumed by
  `elite_mult()` — the ONE throughput lever every elite type already reads).
  Composes multiplicatively with the rampage inducer: **1 base / 2 rampage /
  4 spire / 8 both.** Obeys the existing doctrine exactly — it scales DEBT and
  the DEBT CLAMP, never a concurrency roof, so `TOD_ELITE_ROOF_ALL 12` still
  bounds what may STAND. What 4x actually buys is **saturation**: the roof
  refills the instant a slot frees instead of being touched once a wave. The
  8x case is not 8x the actors — past saturation it buys backlog, i.e. the
  roof never gets a gap. One-line revert documented at the function.
* **THE HONOUR GUARD**: every door buy drops **one Panzer per living player,
  capped 4**, onto the floor just opened (`guard_spawn_org()`, generated — the
  NE mid landing of odd floor 2n-1, proven-open ground), staggered 3.5s.
  Spawned DIRECT via `spawn_panzer()` because both existing paths would
  silently deliver one instead of four (`finale_beat_panzer` carries the
  ending's hard 4-elite ceiling; the director gate reads `panzer_max_alive()`
  = 1/2). Going direct means this function owns the bookkeeping the director
  normally does — hence `TOD_SPIRE_GUARD_MAX` doubling as the STANDING cap:
  a party that leaves guards alive gets fewer, never more (TOD_ACTOR_LIMIT 60
  is the real ceiling and a Panzer is expensive). Skip, never queue.
* **GUARD PANZERS PAY THE ELITE RATE** (new `boss.tod_spire_guard` lane in
  `panzer_life`, polled-latched like `killer`/`org` because the caller stamps
  it after `spawn_panzer()` returns): 500 to the killer instead of 1000
  team-wide + a guaranteed full_ammo. At ~50 doors x up to 4 the boss lane
  would print roughly **200,000 team-wide points** and carpet the climb in max
  ammo — the flat-3000 door economy would stop existing. Scheduled boss-round
  Panzers are untouched and keep the jackpot. The luck grant is deliberately
  NOT split: last-hitting a Panzer should always be worth the bar.
* **THE 30-SECOND SEAL**: doors 2-50 open SEALED and flip to the price after
  `TOD_SPIRE_DOOR_SEAL_SECS 30` — which is exactly the window the honour guard
  drops into, so the fight is the price and the points are the receipt. Door 1
  is exempt (the party arrives into an empty arena; a seal there is 30s of
  nothing). Refusals during the seal PLAY THE DENY SOUND — a mute refusal reads
  as a dead trigger (the 2026-08-26 teleporter lesson). Implemented as its own
  `seal_window` thread so `door_manager` keeps exactly ONE waittill; a second
  wait there would have swallowed the bypass watchdog's notify.
* **TRIGGERSTRING COST: TWO constant strings for the whole mode** — the SEALED
  literal and the price literal, neither interpolating anything (flat 3000).
  Re-stamping the same two across 50 doors mints no further slots. The price
  hint is factored into `spire_door_hint()` so the stamp and the re-stamp can
  never drift into two distinct strings.

Gates: arity green across 68 files, geometry lint green no-regression,
regenerated .map has **ZERO geometry delta** (spire still 7059 brushes / 544
entities — the generator change emits a GSC helper only).

**NOT LIVE-VERIFIED.** Ships in -aa's v14.32 artifact (disarmed). Still owed:
an ARMED boot to read the v14.23 entity-headroom probe, which is the gate on
the user's approved *"measure, then 100 doors"* decision — restoring a door
every floor (100 doors, 300k climb) if the margin allows.

## 2026-08-30 (v14.30) — Slasher pass: melee damage −20% · THOR'S THUNDER −20% all round

Two user asks, one class. *"We need some class nerfs. We need to nerf thors
thunder all around by 20%. And we need to nerf damage on melee by 20%."*
**FULL BUILD** — the melee half moves `MELEE_TIER_DMG`, which is baked into
`tod_weapon_twins.gdt`, so this is not a `-GscOnly`. No geometry, no card
re-bake (the THUNDER card carries no numbers; docs/33 line 111).

**1. MELEE DAMAGE ×0.8, EVERY RUNG, BASE AND PaP.**
`MELEE_TIER_DMG` (tools/gen_tod_twins.js) and its script-side mirror
`register_melee_dmg()` (_tod_classes.gsc) move together, as the lockstep
comment on both requires:

| blade | was (base / PaP) | now |
|---|---|---|
| Combat Knife (T1) | 2000 / 4000 | **1600 / 3200** |
| Wakizashi (T2) | 4000 / 8000 | **3200 / 6400** |
| Stormbreaker (T3) | 6800 / 13600 | **5440 / 10880** |

The ladder's SHAPE is untouched — every rung takes the same 20%, so the ×2
step and the one accepted 2026-08-24 break in it (a PaP'd katana still
out-hits a fresh axe) are exactly as they were, one notch lower. Against this
map's HP curve (~×1.1/round) a ×0.8 cut is worth **~2 rounds of one-hit
reach** per form: the PaP Stormbreaker stops one-hitting around r33 instead
of r35.

**BACKSTAB FOLLOWED FOR FREE**, which is the payoff of the 2026-08-24 decision
to DERIVE it rather than author it: `BACKSTAB_MULT` ×1.5 of the frontal number
re-emitted as 2400/4800, 4800/9600, 8160/16320 — verified in the regenerated
GDT. The map's backstab ceiling drops 20400 → 16320 with no second edit.

**3. MELEE vs THE BOSS/ELITE TRIAD: 0.5 → 0.33** (user, same pass). A melee
hit on a Panzer, a Rogue Protector or a Reaver now pays **one third**, not a
half, applied multiplicatively to the final number through `melee_boss_mult()`
(three call sites: the actor chain, cleave splash, the RP damage feed — none
re-spell the constant). Compounded with the −20% above, a blade swing against
the triad lands at **0.264×** its pre-2026-08-30 value; against ordinary
zombies it is the −20% alone.

**2. THOR'S THUNDER −20% ON EVERY LEVER.** "All around" read as: strength down
20% *and* frequency down 20%, applied so the level curve keeps its shape:

| lever | was (Lv1 … Lv5) | now |
|---|---|---|
| damage (% of victim max HP) | 20 / 35 / 50 / 65 / 80 | **16 / 28 / 40 / 52 / 64** |
| radius | 80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 u | **64 / 96 / 128 / 160 / 192 u** |
| cooldown | 3.75 / 3.13 / 2.50 / 1.88 / 1.25 s | **4.50 / 3.75 / 3.00 / 2.25 / 1.50 s** |

The cooldown is scaled on **all three** constants (MAX, MIN and STEP), for the

`max(MIN, MAX − (lvl−1)·STEP)`, so touching MAX/STEP alone lets the floor

## 2026-08-30 (v14.29) — Sprinter armor vs ALL damage · skirmisher/slasher speed swap · pad = d-pad only

Three user asks in one pass. `-GscOnly` (scripts + one Lua string); no `.map`,
no `.gdt`, no geometry, no card re-bake.

**1. THE ARMORED SPRINTER IS ARMORED AGAINST EVERYTHING.** User: *"Armored
sprinter should be resistant to all damage not just bullets. Melee is too
strong against it so we need this buff on them."* The v13.7 armor gated on
bullet MODs + `MOD_HEAD_SHOT`, leaving melee, explosives and the blades at full
damage as deliberate counter-play (map 1's Shielded contract). Effective HP was
therefore **×60 to a gun and ×20 to a knife** — the slasher killed a sprinter
three times faster than the class the enemy was tuned against. The MOD test is
gone; every source that reaches the damage callback is now scaled by the same
1/3. `TOD_SPRINT_BULLET_FRAC` → **`TOD_SPRINT_DMG_FRAC`** and
`level.tod_sprinter_bullet_frac` → **`level.tod_sprinter_dmg_frac`**, so the
name can't go on claiming a gate that no longer exists.

**The hole this exposed, which the MOD test was hiding:** *splash never paid
the armor at all.* CLEAVE splash and IMPACT ROUNDS splash both mark the victim
with `tod_cleave_hit` and take the callback's early `return -1` — "the splash
already carries the final damage". True of the **attacker's** multipliers;
false of the **victim's** armor, which was never in the splash figure. The
pass-through now returns the armored value instead of `-1` when the victim is a
sprinter. New `sprinter_armor_frac()` is the one owner for both lanes.

**The two lanes were in different states, and the distinction matters to anyone
recomputing balance from this entry** (corrected here after a first pass
blurred them): **IMPACT ROUNDS** carried a genuine *pre-existing* 3× bypass — a
direct bullet was armored, its own splash was not, so the splash out-damaged
the shot that spawned it by 3× for the whole life of v13.7. **CLEAVE** did not:
melee was unarmored on both paths, so splash and swing agreed. Cleave becomes a
3× leak only *the moment melee is armored* — i.e. it was created by this change
rather than revealed by it, which is why the splash fix had to ship in the same
build and not as a follow-up.

RICOCHET + RED NUMBERS now fire on melee and explosive hits too: they *are* the
"your damage is being deflected" read, and a hit quietly cut to a third with no
feedback is the version players report as a bug. Splash hits ricochet but draw
no number (splash never drew one).

**Deliberate carve-out, flagged to the user:** the **WISP TEA** pass-through is
*not* armored. The wisp deals a fraction of the victim's **max health**
(`WISP_TEA_*_SEGMENTS` is literally hits-to-kill), so it already pays the ×20
in full and kills a sprinter in the tier's advertised tick count. Armoring it
would triple that and make the sprinter more wisp-proof than the Panzer, off a
knob never meant to touch percentage damage. One call to `sprinter_armor_frac()`
reverses this if wanted.

**2. SKIRMISHER AND SLASHER BASE SPEED SWAPPED.** User: *"Melee is too fast and
skirmisher should be the fastest."* `class_speed_base()`: skirmisher
**1.0 → 1.1**, slasher **1.1 → 1.0**. A straight exchange — the pair keeps the
same two rungs, so the spread and every relative gap are unchanged and only the
labels moved. New order, slowest to fastest: heavy 0.75 · assault 0.9 · slasher
1.0 · **skirmisher 1.1**. SPRINT (+5%/Lv, max 10) is scoped to both classes, so
the ceilings follow: skirmisher 1.50 → **1.65**, slasher 1.65 → **1.50**.
`class_speed_base()` is the single source and no UI or card art prints the
number (the class cards were opened and checked, not assumed) — the skirmisher
card's existing *"fastest fire rate + speed"* copy is now true for the first
time. Stale doc surfaces (`docs/armory.html`, the Steam workshop description's
"Slasher … fastest on foot") are owned by the peer session that wrote them.

**3. UPGRADE PANEL: CONTROLLER = D-PAD ONLY.** User: *"can we make the upgrade
menu d pad only on controller. Its akward to move around and still set an
upgrade."* This directive already shipped once (v10.21) and was then undone
piece by piece by v10.19/v10.20, which put the stick, RT, LT, R3 and X lanes
back so a keyboard — which has no d-pad — could navigate at all. Rather than
re-picking one directive over the other, the extra lanes now sit behind a
**per-player device latch**.

**How the latch knows the device.** There is no server-side gamepad read in T7
— no such builtin appears anywhere in `share/raw`, and CSC/LUI cannot answer the
server (clientfields are one-way; `Engine.IsGamepadEnabled` exists but only
client-side, which is why the LUI hint text can already switch and the GSC
cannot). What the map *does* have is an input only one device produces:
**ActionSlotThree/Four are the controller d-pad and BO3 PC binds no keyboard key
to an action slot in zombies** (the v10.20 research). So the first d-pad press
proves the device and sets `self.tod_input_pad` for the match — a plain player
field, so it survives respawns, and no import (the cycle rule).

**ONE-WAY on purpose:** the d-pad is never gated on anything, so a player who
*has* bound a key to an action slot still navigates, and a player who never
touches the d-pad keeps every lane they had before. **Nothing regresses for the
keyboard.** `_tod_class_select` sets the same field during the 30 s draft — the
earliest point in a match a device can prove itself — so the round-1 event is
already d-pad-only rather than learning one menu too late; the draft's own lanes
are untouched (pre-spawn panel, no weapon in hand, never the awkward ones).
`atk/ads/mel/rld` are seeded to 0 outside the gate so the dev input probe can't
be handed uninitialised variables. The Lua pad hint drops "/ STICK"; the **baked**
`i_tod_hint_switch_pad` plate already drew a d-pad glyph alone and needs no
re-bake (opened and checked).

## 2026-08-30 (v14.28) — VITALITY vs JUGG: stock's health reboot was discarding both

User, mid-test: *"Vitality upgrade breaks when you get jugg. I have 210 but
level 3 vitality"*, then *"I just went back down to 200. Also jugg on this map
will get you to 200 not 250."* All three numbers are one bug.

**ROOT CAUSE.** Stock rebuilds a player's max HP **from scratch** via
`perk_set_max_health_if_jugg("health_reboot")` — on **every round transition**
(`_zm.gsc:4521`), on laststand revive (×2), and on jugg loss — computing
`player_base_health (+jugg)`. The map never overrode that zombie_var, so it was
stock **100**: every reboot produced 200 for a jugg holder, discarding the 150
base *and* every VITALITY level.

**Why it read as "breaks when you get jugg":** the body-loop maintain floor
(150 + 10×VIT, raise-only) was **jugg-blind**. Without jugg the rebuilt 100 sat
*below* the floor and was silently repaired within a second — invisible. With
jugg the rebuilt 200 sat *above* a Lv3 floor of 180, so the raise-only floor
was satisfied while 80 real HP were missing. The user's **210** was a vitality
card bought while jugg was up (`apply_upgrade`'s additive +10, healed in),
eaten by the next round's reboot back to **200**.

**THE FIX, two halves with one owner each:**

1. **Entry `main()` pins `level.zombie_vars["player_base_health"] = 150`**
   (post-`zm_usermap::main()`, same timing contract as the melee-score var
   above it; stock seeds 100 at `_zm.gsc:1229` during the bootstrap). Blast
   radius audited before changing a stock var: it is read **nowhere** except
   `perk_set_max_health_if_jugg`'s health_reboot and jugg-upgrade-without-jugg
   branches — both mean exactly "base max HP", which on this map is 150. Stock's
   own rebuild now lands at **250 with jugg**, agreeing with the additive
   purchase path by construction. LOCKSTEP: `TOD_UPG_BASE_HP` (150) in
   `_tod_upgrades.gsc` — file-local `#define`, cannot be referenced across.
2. **`max_hp_floor()` — new ONE OWNER of the minimum-max formula**
   (`150 + 10×VIT + active-jugg bonus`), used by both the spawn grant and the
   body-loop maintain; neither re-spells the sum. The jugg term (via
   `zombie_perk_juggernaut_health`, isdefined-guarded) is what makes the floor
   able to *see* a post-reboot deficit: a jugg holder at VIT 3 floors at
   **280**, so any stock clobber is repaired within a second. Still raise-only,
   still no free heal; a PAUSED jugg deliberately reads false (stock already
   restored the pre-jugg max, and raise-only never fights the resume re-add).

The `#define`'s old "JUGG-SAFE BY THE SAME MECHANISM" comment — whose premise
this bug disproved — is rewritten at the site to describe the real mechanism.

**Expected numbers now:** base 150 · VIT 3 = 180 · jugg = 250 · jugg + VIT 3 =
**280** (was 200/210) · jugg + VIT 5 = 300, matching the armory's VITALITY note,
which was aspirational until today. Survives round flips, revives, and jugg
loss→rebuy. `-GscOnly`; no constant changed, so no card, Lua, or armory edits.

## 2026-08-30 (v14.23) — SPIRE LIVE-TEST BATCH: 50 resident doors (mover retired), the instakill root, shelf holes, crate flips

The user's first real spire run (dev+god, .ff 16:35:56) reported 7 issues.
One root explains most of them: **the v14.1 two-slab parity MOVER never
re-seated a slab after its first serve.** Doors 3+ never physically existed
("running through the spire for free"), the live door's buy prompt floated in
an empty doorway ("no doors on some entrances but I see the trigger"), the
never-bought doors never set their flags, so every zone past spire_c1 stayed
DISABLED — and stock's out-of-playable monitor (laugh + unrevivable
`lives=0` + `health+1000`) instakilled anyone past ~floor 6. That is the
Samantha laugh the user heard at "the 7th floor" (god mode blocked the kill)
and the death Ped_UK reported from the Workshop build. The riser gate stuck
at door ~3's height is also why nothing followed the climbers. The mover used
two mechanisms this map never proved live (`.origin` assignment on a
brushmodel; `Show()` after `Hide()` on one) — which one failed is unproven
and now moot:

* **50 RESIDENT DOORS, NO MOVERS** (user's own proposal: "What about changing
  the spire to 50 doors?"). Door d seals odd floor 2d-1 (all on the E face)
  and opens floors 2d-1 + 2d; even floors have no barrier. Slabs are .map
  residents on the tower's proven 53-door contract (Solid at load, opened
  ONCE on buy, never moved/re-shown). Entity cost +48 at the init peak vs
